author: realmarcin
body:
Closes #200.

## The gap

Before #196, **every** workflow in this repo sat behind a `paths:` filter. A PR touching only `docs/**`, `README.md`, `NEXT_TASKS.md`, or a brand-new workflow file matched none of them and ran **nothing**.

`gh pr checks` prints `no checks` for that case. It reads like "nothing to verify". It means "nothing was verified".

PR #194 is a live instance — two files, zero checks — which is pointed, since #194's own description is about agent workflows that silently do not run.

#196 gave the repo a floor: `vendored-sync` has no filter, so every PR now gets at least one real check. But it verifies *vendored files*, not the diff in front of it. This verifies the diff.

## What it checks

Four checks, stdlib + PyYAML, no network, **~0.5s**:

| check | catches |
|---|---|
| `WORKFLOW_INVALID` | a workflow that does not parse, or has no `on:` / `jobs:` |
| `NO_UNFILTERED_CI` | no workflow triggers on `pull_request` without a `paths:` filter |
| `CONFLICT_MARKER` | an unresolved merge-conflict marker in a tracked file |
| `BROKEN_LINK` | a relative Markdown link pointing at a path that does not exist |

`WORKFLOW_INVALID` matters more than it looks: GitHub does not fail loudly on a malformed workflow, it silently never runs it — the same bug class as the rest of this PR.

`NO_UNFILTERED_CI` is **self-referential on purpose**. It is #200's invariant expressed as a test: if someone later adds a `paths:` filter to the last unfiltered workflow, this fails loudly instead of quietly returning the repo to "some PRs run nothing". There is also a test asserting the *live* repo satisfies it.

## Testing, given what is being fixed

The failure mode here is "a check that silently verifies nothing", so a vacuous check would be self-defeating. Every check is therefore tested in **both** directions — it fires on the real defect, and stays quiet on the legitimate lookalike:

- `<<<<<<< HEAD` flagged; `=======` **not** flagged, because a bare `=======` is a Markdown setext heading underline and matching it would false-positive on ordinary prose.
- broken relative link flagged; resolving links, `#anchors`, `https://`, `mailto:`, and root-relative `/docs/x.md` all clean.
- all-filtered workflows trip `NO_UNFILTERED_CI`; one unfiltered workflow satisfies it.
- CLI exit codes asserted end to end (0 clean, 1 with findings).

I also confirmed against the live repo that the link check is **not vacuous**: it resolves **31 real relative links across 44 markdown files**, all currently passing. A "0 findings" result that came from matching nothing would be exactly the disease.

14 new tests, 166 total.

## Also

Wired into `just qc` as well as its own unfiltered workflow, so it runs locally. The duplicate CI run on qc-matching PRs costs half a second and buys local coverage.

Two pre-existing gates caught my own mistakes while building this, which is a good sign for them: `audit-justfile-paths` failed until `scripts/pr_sanity.py` was tracked, and the same untracked-file condition failed a test.

author: ibanner56
body: Follow-up from the beta.6 release: make the landing page's version pill self-updating only, so cutting a release never requires editing a non-Markdown file. ## The problem `site/index.html` hardcoded `v0.1.0-beta.6` as a pre-hydration fallback, and `releasing.md` instructed maintainers to bump it each beta. That has two costs: 1. **It runs the full build matrix for a cosmetic string.** `ci.yml` uses `paths-ignore: ['**.md']`, which only skips CI when *every* changed file is Markdown. `site/index.html` isn't, so the beta.6 docs PR (#755) — otherwise Markdown-only — triggered all five platform builds to change one line. 2. **A hand-bumped fallback is stale by design.** It's correct only between the bump and the next release, and a *wrong* version reads worse than no version. ## The fix Use a version-free placeholder, exactly like the downloads line (`#dl-version-line`) **already did in this same file**: ```html Latest beta ``` `site/app.js` fetches `beta.json` and overwrites `hero-version`, `hero-status` and `dl-version-line` with the live version on load, so **the rendered page is unchanged**. Only the pre-hydration flash differs — and it now reads "Latest beta" instead of a number that may be wrong. There is now **no version string anywhere under `site/`**, so a release needs no edit here at all. ## Docs - `docs/dev/releasing.md` — the "Version fallbacks" bullet said to bump the pill; it now says there's nothing to do, and explains why the file should stay untouched (the `paths-ignore` interaction). - `docs/dev/release-checklist.md` — dropped "version fallbacks" from the landing-page item for the same reason. ## Verification - `grep -rn "0\.1\.0" site/` → no matches. - All three ids `app.js` targets still exist and are still version-free in the markup. - No behaviour change once JS runs; the live page already sources its version from `beta.json`, which the release pipeline publishes.

author: asdscv
body:
Work in progress on this branch — opening early so CI exercises **migration 181** (DDL cannot be validated through the management API; Cloudflare rejects it).

Four commits so far:

1. **Knowledge kernel** — the app shipped two disagreeing definitions of mastery, one of which (`ease_factor > 2.5`) counts a card after a *single* correct review. One criterion now, pluggable via a single `ACTIVE_CRITERION_ID`.
2. **Workload projection** — the goal form asked "하루 몇 분?", which the learner cannot know. Now computed, peak included. Two earlier versions of the model were 26-38% low; caught only by comparison against a card-level simulation of `lib/srs.ts`.
3. **Goal form 6 fields → 3** — 과목 was a provable no-op, 중요도 was a question the app can answer, 하루 몇 분 is now an output.
4. **List → detail** — `/learning` lists plans, `/learning/:goalId` opens one. The hidden "진단" screen is absorbed and deleted.

Why "완료" is not a goal metric: simulating this repo's own scheduler over 10,000 cards at a 10% lapse rate settles at **99.1%** for a 21-day threshold and *worse* for stricter ones (97.7% at 56 days, 89% at 365). A progress bar on any interval threshold can never fill. "Will I know it on the target date" reaches 100% — verified at 10,000 cards / 180 days / ~78 min per day.

Still to come on this branch: mobile restructure, study history + achievements (the `mastery_*` family still counts `ease > 2.5`), dashboard summary, then device testing on web/iOS/Android.

author: jdolson-88
body:
`unzbd rc anim` currently fails on the US retail release of Recoil. This adds the release-specific constants it needs.

Every anim def in all six missions failed at the same assertion:

```
Expected `anim def reset time` == -1.0, but was 0.0 (at 95472)
```

The `seq_defs_ptr` values on this copy aren't in `RESET_TIME_BORK`. I collected the full set by temporarily replacing the assertion with a log line and running all six missions in one pass: **12 pointers, exactly 2 per mission**.

Mission 6 then hit a second one, in `rc_m6_fixup`:

```
Expected `fog state type` == Linear (1), but was Off (0) (at 460576)
```

Same `vtol1` / `m6_start_animation` event, but at `read.prev` 460540 rather than 460748, so I turned the offset check into a small list.

I first tried dropping the offset entirely and keying on the name pair alone, on the theory that names are stable across releases. That's too broad — the same anim def contains a later fog state event that legitimately *is* `Linear`, so the assertion just inverts. The comment records this so the next person doesn't repeat it.

### Results

| Mission | anim defs | before |
|---|---:|---|
| m1 | 464 | failed at 51 |
| m2 | 422 | failed at 51 |
| m3 | 332 | failed at 51 |
| m4 | 579 | failed at 51 |
| m5 | 418 | failed at 51 |
| m6 | 839 | failed at 50 |

### Known limitation — not fixed here

Round-trip is **4 bytes** short of byte-identical on each mission. `rezbd` writes `0xDEADBEEF` for the anim defs pointer, matching the `Unknown defs pointer 0x02F1B484, ZBD translation may be inaccurate` warning.

The six defs pointers on this release are:

| | m1 | m2 | m3 | m4 | m5 | m6 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| US retail | `0x02F1B484` | `0x02F52F3C` | `0x02F7AC60` | `0x02ED29F0` | `0x02EF2BF0` | `0x034DF8DC` |
| current | `0x02F1D378` | `0x02F53FD8` | `0x02F830F0` | `0x02ECD990` | `0x02EDD314` | `0x034DEF64` |

I haven't included these, because `Mission::defs_ptr` is the exact inverse of `Mission::from_defs_ptr`, so a variant can only carry one pointer — supporting both releases needs a design decision that's yours to make (per-release variants, or carrying the raw pointer through the API type). Happy to open a separate issue, or implement whichever you'd prefer.

Locally I verified that overriding the six values does give byte-identical round-trip on all six missions, so the parse itself appears lossless.

### Aside

While tracing this I noticed that on the RC path, `BORKED_UNK044` (`nodes/src/rc/lod/info.rs`) and the `DEFAULT_FLAGS_M2` check (`nodes/src/rc/world/info.rs`) look unreachable since GameZ node reading moved to dispatching on `NodeClass` — `assert_variants` is now only called from `pm/node.rs` and `mw/node.rs`. Not touched here, just flagging it. (Both had blocked this copy under v0.6.1; on rc3 all six GameZ files convert and round-trip byte-identical unmodified.)

### Testing

- `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy`, `cargo build --release` all clean
- All six missions parse; 3,054 anim defs total
- Existing constants untouched and unreordered

I don't have the copy the original constants came from, so I can't check for regressions there — though the changes are purely additive.

author: cleerox-svg
body:
Follow-up enhancements to the **Guess the Tune** mini-game (the three deferred items from #138, plus the requested dual listen-links). Additive — no D1 migration (reuses `game='tune'` rows).

## What's new

**1. Genre chips** — `TUNE_SEEDS` is now bucketed into `TUNE_GENRES` (Pop, Hip-Hop, Rock, R&B, Electronic, Country, Latin) plus **Any**. The Tune menu shows a genre chip row; `buildTuneRound` draws seeds from the chosen bucket.

**2. Title / Artist mode** — a menu toggle chooses whether the player guesses the **track title** or the **artist**. Artist-mode distractors are other same-genre artists (backfilled from the seed pool). The reveal shows both title and artist in either mode.

**3. Random clip start-offset** — previews now begin at a random point rather than always the intro, so replays of a track differ. `secondsHeard` measures elapsed listening *from the offset*, so time-based scoring is unchanged; the stop backstop now tracks real playback (re-armed on `playing`, cleared on `waiting`) so a post-seek rebuffer can't cut a clip short.

**4. Reveal "listen to the full song" links** — after each guess the reveal screen links out to **Apple Music** (the track's iTunes `trackViewUrl`, newly surfaced by the worker proxy) and **Spotify** (a client-built search deep-link `open.spotify.com/search/<title artist>`). Both open externally with `rel="noopener noreferrer"`. Text-only labels — no third-party logos, to avoid trademark issues.

> Spotify uses a **search** deep-link (zero-auth, opens the app/web to the track). An *exact* Spotify track link would require the Spotify Web API with a client-credentials secret in Wrangler — happy to add that as a follow-up if you want precise links.

## Review fixes (from `code-reviewer`)

- **Scoring bug fixed:** artist-mode distractor dedup now folds diacritics, so an accented answer (e.g. "Beyoncé") can't also appear as its ASCII twin ("Beyonce") — previously the twin was a visually-identical choice that scored as wrong.
- **Audio hardening:** the clip-cutoff backstop now follows actual playback instead of wall-clock, so buffering after the random seek can't end the clip early.

## Verification

- `pnpm typecheck` — clean (both packages)
- `pnpm --filter @relay/worker test` — 30/30 (tunes projection test extended for `trackViewUrl`)
- `lint:migrations` + `test:migrations` — clean; **no new migration**
- `pnpm --filter @relay/worker build` + `pnpm --filter @relay/ui build` — clean

Built via the sub-agent fleet (media + frontend-pwa) and gated through `code-reviewer` + `qa-verify`; the two flagged issues above were fixed on this branch before commit.

author: bjscha03
body: ## Production failure being fixed On mobile, the customer can select artwork and see a local preview, but the original upload can fail before a permanent Cloudinary asset exists. The page then leaves the local preview on screen, shows `Upload failed`, and Buy Now incorrectly reports `Upload still processing`. Because no permanent source exists, the cart/checkout thumbnail is also blank. ## Root cause The current browser sends the full original file through a buffered Netlify Function multipart request. The product UI advertises files up to 50 MB, but that transport cannot reliably carry files of that size—especially after binary/Base64 request overhead. The current client-side compression helper is not a safe fix because it would alter customer print artwork and does not solve PDF uploads. ## Repair - Upload original PDF/JPG/PNG bytes directly from the browser to Cloudinary using a short-lived server-signed ticket. - Keep the Cloudinary API secret exclusively server-side. - Retry interrupted direct uploads automatically up to three times. - Retain a conservative same-origin fallback only for small files that fit safely inside the Netlify request envelope. - Preserve the customer's original bytes without recompressing the production source. - Keep the local preview visible while the permanent upload completes. - When Buy Now is clicked during or after a failed upload, wait for the active upload and retry the already-selected file automatically—no second file selection required. - Remove the misleading `Upload still processing` dead-end. - Route Yard Sign originals and generated positioned thumbnails through the same persistent transport. - Replace Yard Sign's raw `` row thumbnail with the stable decoded fallback renderer. - Preserve checkout, pricing, PayPal, Admin layout, Resend templates, original artwork handling, and print-PDF behavior. ## Validation added - Secure signature-ticket tests, including secret non-disclosure. - Direct browser-upload unit tests with exact signed parameters and progress. - Static guards proving Design, Google Ads, Yard Signs, and generated previews no longer post large originals through the Netlify function. - Existing thumbnail, expanded-preview, checkout, email, Admin, TypeScript, function syntax, and production-build suites. A one-time Actions workflow applies the focused source patch, runs all checks, removes the patch script, and commits the validated application source back to this branch. Do not merge until that source commit, normal CI, and Netlify Deploy Preview are green.

body:
## 起因

Round 232 部署后 Railway 日志 03:15:21 出现 20+ 条 Helius 429 flood：
```
Server responded with 429 Too Many Requests. Retrying after 500ms delay...
... 500ms → 1000ms → 2000ms → 4000ms exponential backoff x 20 条
```

Autopilot 03:16 reseed 80 单，`openOrders` 一直 0 → 80 单起单全部失败。

同时 lastError = `pollFills → trades-history rate_limited`（Phoenix API 侧 429）。

## 根因

Web bundle 探过：Phoenix 没有 `place-multiple` / batch endpoint。
80 单 seed 让 `sendRawTransaction` + `confirmTransaction` 内部轮询打爆 Helius。

具体：`confirmTransaction` 每 500ms poll `getSignatureStatuses`，Helius 429 → web3.js 内部 exponential backoff → 单个 tx 卡 30s 才超时 → 排队 80 单全部堵住。

## 改动 `src/exchange/ph/phoenix.js`

**1. `_signAndSubmitInstructions` 串行化 + 500ms gap**
```js
const chain = this._solanaSubmitChain || Promise.resolve();
this._solanaSubmitChain = chain.then(() => gate).catch(() => {});
await chain.catch(() => {});
const wait = Math.max(0, (this._lastSubmitAt || 0) + 500 - Date.now());
if (wait > 0) await new Promise(r => setTimeout(r, wait));
```

**2. `confirmTransaction` 8s Promise.race timeout**
```js
await Promise.race([
  this._solanaConn.confirmTransaction(sig, 'confirmed'),
  new Promise((_, rej) => setTimeout(() => rej(new Error('confirmTimeout8s')), 8000)),
]);
```
超时不 throw —— 只 log。tx 已经 broadcast，sig 已有，`trades-history` 90s 内会补记账。

**3. `_pollFills` 30s → 90s**
`% 3` → `% 9` (10s tick × 9 = 90s)。缓解 Phoenix API `trades-history` 429。

## 预期

- 80 单从 burst → 匀速 500ms/单 = 40 秒起完
- confirmTransaction 卡不住下一单起单
- Phoenix `trades-history` 429 消失

## 验证

- `node --check` OK
- `npm test` → 16/16
- Deploy 后 Railway 日志应看 429 flood 停止 + `[Phoenix] confirmTransaction 8s 超时` 出现（正常，可接受）

author: kenhia
body:
Proposal [korg:893](https://korg.kubs.casa) (rank 4.7). The lifecycle cluster T3 exposed, taken with the question it belongs to.

korg had two endings in the code — `archived` on nodes and projects, hard `DELETE` for comments, plan items and edges — and **no rule** saying which applied to what. #855 names the cost precisely: using one status for three different claims is how a corpus drifts. So this decides it once, writes it down, and then builds only the mechanics that decision implies.

## The rule

Now in [`docs/api.md`](docs/api.md) § *Disposal semantics*, with a per-kind table:

- **`archived` means "real, but not a target for new work."** Lossless, reversible, the ending for anything with identity.
- **A hard delete means "this was never real."** Irreversible, and it **refuses when the row is referenced**.
- **Test residue is a `category`, not a disposal.** `EVAL` (migration 0018) already makes harness leakage findable as a group.

The refuse-if-referenced clause is the load-bearing half. Without it the schema answers the question instead, and answers it wrongly in both directions: `relationship` and `comment` both cascade from `node`, so deleting a link would take its edges and its whole thread with it; `workitem.area_id` is `ON DELETE SET NULL`, so deleting an area would silently unfile every item under it. Neither is a decision a caller made.

## What shipped

### #855 — no `delete_project` verb

## ⚠️ OWNER DECISION FLAGGED — the founding cap

Two public counters disagreed about how scarce founding is:

| surface | endpoint | source | live reading |
|---|---|---|---|
| homepage pill | `/api/v1/founding-customers/count` | `founding_customers` cohort table | **14**, cap **25** (`FOUNDING_CUSTOMERS_CAP` env) |
| pricing seats meter | `/api/founding-members` | `users WHERE plan='founding'` | **9** of hardcoded **10** → "1 remaining" |

**One more sale** would have flipped /pricing to "All founding licenses claimed" and set `pointer-events:none` on the primary money CTA — while Stripe shows **11 active \$99 founding subs**, the renewal watcher just logged **three abandoned \$1,188 annual-Founding checkouts in 3 days**, and the first renewal wave lands **Aug 3–20**.

**This PR defaults to the larger cap (25)** so the CTA cannot self-disable mid-renewal-wave. After deploy the meter reads "Only 11 of 25 founding licenses left."

**To lower it (e.g. back to 10, or anything else): set `FOUNDING_CUSTOMERS_CAP` on Railway — no code change.** Setting it at or below `claimed` closes the program (meter shows sold-out, CTA disables). Note at cap 10 the program shows sold-out immediately, since the cohort already has 14 rows.

**Count semantics also unified** — flagging since the numbers differ:
- cohort table (now canonical): **14** — every paid signup auto-tagged until cap (any plan, incl. \$9/\$49)
- `users.plan='founding'`: **9** — known-stale class (`users` lags Stripe)
- Stripe active \$99 founding subs: **11**

The cohort table is what the webhook auto-tag writes and what the cap logic already read, so both public surfaces now serve it. If you'd rather the meter count only \$99-founding-plan buyers, that's a one-line change in `founding_status()` — say the word.

## What

- `routes/founding_customers.py`: new `founding_status()` — single source (cohort count + `FOUNDING_CUSTOMERS_CAP`, default 25). `/count` response now also carries `cap`/`remaining`/`program_active`. DB failure → program stays active (an outage must never render as "sold out" on a money surface).
- `public_endpoints.py`: `/api/founding-members` delegates to `founding_status()`; legacy inline count kept only as a never-500 fallback. Response schema unchanged (`total/claimed/remaining/price/regular_price/program_active`).

## Companion

Frontend azmartone67/dchub-frontend#1111 (merged): pill → `/pricing#founding`, pill cap read from this API, expired date-countdown removed (it had **already disabled the pricing CTA for every visitor since Aug 1**), map layer-modal CTA relabeled to founding.

Local: `3992 passed, 40 skipped, 23 xfailed` (full suite, clean worktree off origin/main).

author: copilot
body:
Comprehensive repair of build, runtime, and configuration issues across the repo. No functional content changes.

## JavaScript (runtime bug)
- **`assets/js/_main.js` + `main.min.js`**: `userPref` was never defined — `ReferenceError` on every page load, breaking dark/light theme detection entirely. Fixed to `window.matchMedia(...)`.

```js
// before — ReferenceError at runtime
return (userPref && userPref("(prefers-color-scheme: dark)").matches) ? "dark" : "light";

// after
return (window.matchMedia && window.matchMedia("(prefers-color-scheme: dark)").matches) ? "dark" : "light";
```

## Gemfile / bundle
- Removed `gem 'jekyll'` from `:jekyll_plugins` group — conflicts with `github-pages` which manages its own Jekyll version.
- Added missing `jekyll-gist` and `jekyll-paginate` (referenced in `_config.yml` `plugins:` but absent from Gemfile).
- Relaxed `connection_pool` from exact pin `'2.5.0'` → `'~> 2.5'`.

## Dockerfile
- `gem install connection_pool:2.5.0` — colon syntax is invalid, breaks the image build immediately.
- Removed pinned `bundler:2.3.26` (incompatible with Ruby 3.2).
- Changed CMD to `bundle exec jekyll serve` (bare `jekyll` fails for non-root user without gem path).

## package.json
- All three URL fields pointed to `academicpages/gsalgadoma.github.io` (non-existent). Corrected to `gsalgadoma/gsalgadoma.github.io`.
- Replaced `uglify-js` with `terser` — `uglify-js` does not parse ES module `import` syntax used in `_main.js`; `npm run build:js` would fail.

## CI workflow (`.github/workflows/scrape_talks.yml`)
- Updated `actions/checkout@v2` → `@v4` and `actions/setup-python@v2` → `@v5` (v2 uses deprecated Node 16).
- Added `permissions: contents: write` — `git push` was silently failing without it.

## Configuration
- **`_config.yml`**: Removed deprecated `whitelist:` block (superseded by `plugins:`; duplicate and causes warnings in modern Jekyll).

## Broken links
- **`_includes/footer.html`**: AcademicPages link pointed to `academicpages/gsalgadoma.github.io` → corrected to `academicpages/academicpages.github.io`.
- **`_pages/talkmap.html`**: Notebook link had same wrong org/repo.

## Scripts
- **`scripts/update_cv_json.sh`**: Removed `read -r answer` interactive prompt + `jekyll serve` — would hang indefinitely in any non-interactive context.
- **`markdown_generator/publications.py`, `talks.py`**: Removed bare DataFrame expressions (Jupyter display artifacts; no-op and misleading in standalone Python execution).

author: kashmithnisakya
body:
standup already automated the *"what happened"* half of a standup, because the board writes the log. This does the other half: **synthesis** and **entry**.

## What you get

- **Ask about your own board.** "What's blocked?", "Who has the most open work?" — answered with real names, real counts, and the actual blocking reason.
- **The standup note writes itself.** A structured card (shipped / in flight / blocked / needs attention) with a Copy button, ready to paste into a channel.
- **Describe a task, confirm a task.** "Add a high priority task for Nadia on Docs site to write the API reference page" becomes a proposal card with the project and person resolved to real records. Nothing is written until you press Apply.

A floating dock, mounted in the layout next to `<Toaster />`, so it is reachable from the board and the log rather than being a sixth nav tab.

## How it is built

`walkers/insights.jac` builds one `Snapshot` with **no LLM at all**: blocked items with the reason taken from the log row that recorded the move, the review queue with days waiting, aging and overdue work, per-person and per-project counts. It is the context for every model call, and it is useful on its own.

`walkers/assistant.jac` is the byLLM surface: three `by llm()` functions with `sem` prompts, returning a `str`, a `StandupNote`, or a `ProposedAction`.

### Four decisions, each forced by something verified against the runtime

- **No tools, no ReAct.** The whole org fits in one prompt, and a graph-reading tool comes back *empty* under streaming, while a nested `root spawn` returns empty `.reports` and leaks its rows into the outer walker. Both fail silently, and the model then answers fluently from nothing. Context is assembled eagerly in plain `def`s that traverse `[root-->]`.
- **No streaming in v3.0**, for the same reason. A spinner beats a wrong answer.
- **No `:pub`.** Every assistant walker is bare, so it requires a JWT and runs on the caller's own root. A `:pub` walker would let an anonymous caller burn the provider key against the shared guest graph — and it would look perfect in a demo, because a caller who *does* send a token works fine.
- **The model never writes.** `ProposeAction` returns a suggestion; the client applies it through the ordinary `CreateTask` / `MoveTask`. This is also the prompt-injection mitigation: task titles and notes are user-authored and land in the model's context, so an injected instruction can at worst produce a bad *suggestion* that a person declines.

## Verification

Driven end to end in a real browser against a real model: ask, standup note, propose, apply, and the board refreshing immediately via a `standup:refresh` event.

An 18-assertion API gate suite (in the scratchpad, per repo convention) covers:

| | |
|---|---|
| no token | `Digest` / `AskAssistant` / `WriteStandup` / `ProposeAction` all 401 |
| forged token | same four, all 401 |
| tenant isolation | account A creates a task; B's `Digest` and B's `AskAssistant` answer cannot contain it, and B's snapshot is genuinely empty |
| empty input | a blank question or instruction reports nothing, so no call reaches the provider |

**Degradation is graceful, and tested.** With no `OPENAI_API_KEY` or a bad one, the server starts and the entire deterministic app still works (`ListTasks` 200, `Digest` 200); only the assistant reports that it is unreachable, naming `.env` as the place to look.

## Two more Jac landmines, now in CLAUDE.md

Both cost real debugging time here:

1. **A name first assigned inside an `if` is block-scoped in the compiled JS** and is a `ReferenceError` after the branch. The whole handler died before its first walker call, silently, with the spinner left spinning.
2. **A `has` read after `await` is the pre-call snapshot.** Appending the question and then the reply as two separate `turns = turns + [...]` statements dropped the question every time. Build the list in a local and assign once.

## Config

`.env.example` is added (names only, no values). `jac.toml` gains `[byllm]` with a grounding system prompt, `default_model = "${LLM_MODEL:-gpt-4o-mini}"`, and `temperature = 0.2`. byLLM passes the key down to litellm, which reads `OPENAI_API_KEY` from the environment, so no secret goes in `jac.toml`.

author: ephbaum
body:
Evaluates the project, rewrites the README to match reality, files the defects found as labelled issues, and fixes all of them.

## Why

The README described an aspiration — "accept, and prompt for missing, values and then output the missing variable" — that was never implemented. Meanwhile the code had five real defects, all reproducible from a terminal, plus no tests, no CI, and no way to run it without typing at a prompt.

## What changed

**README** — rewritten to document what the program actually does: takes principal, rate and term, solves for the monthly payment. It cannot solve for a missing variable, and now says so. Adds build/run instructions with verified example sessions, the amortization formula, and the Unlicense, which the old README never mentioned.

The known-defects section links to the [`bug`](https://github.com/Bombing-Around/loan_calculator/labels/bug) and [`enhancement`](https://github.com/Bombing-Around/loan_calculator/labels/enhancement) label views rather than enumerating issues inline, so it stays accurate as issues open and close without needing an edit.

**Bug fixes (#1–#5)**

- `monthly_payment()` extracted as a pure function with an explicit zero-rate branch. A 0% loan returned `NaN` (the formula computes 0/0); it now returns `principal / months`.
- `get_input()` takes a constraint description and a predicate, so principal and term must be > 0 and the rate >= 0. Previously nothing was range-checked and a negative principal produced a negative payment. Non-finite input is rejected too — `"inf"` and `"nan"` both parse successfully as `f64` and would otherwise slip past a range check.
- `get_input()` retries in a `loop` rather than by recursion, and `read_line`'s `Ok(0)` is treated as end of input. Piping a closed stdin previously recursed until `fatal runtime error: stack overflow`; it now exits non-zero with a message.
- The `read_line` `Err` branch is handled instead of `.unwrap()`ed.
- `main` returns `ExitCode` so those paths exit cleanly instead of panicking.

**Enhancement (#6)**

- `--principal`, `--rate` and `--months` flags, in both `--flag value` and `--flag=value` forms, plus `-h`/`--help`. Anything not supplied is still prompted for; supply all three and the program never reads stdin, so it can be scripted.
- Flag values go through the same validation as interactive input, but a bad one is a hard error to stderr with a non-zero exit rather than a re-prompt — a script should not hang waiting on a prompt it cannot see. Unknown flags, missing values and repeated flags are errors too.
- Parsing lives in a pure `parse_args()` over an argument iterator, so it is testable without touching the environment.
- CI workflow running fmt, clippy, build and test on push and pull request against `main`.

Still zero dependencies, still Rust 2021. Closes #1, #2, #3, #4, #5, #6.

## Verification

`cargo fmt --all -- --check` and `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` both clean; `cargo test` 15 passed, 0 failed. Behaviour re-checked against the rebuilt binary:

| Input | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `10000 / 5 / 60` | `188.71` | `188.71` (unchanged) |
| `10000 / 0 / 60` | `NaN` | `166.67` |
| `10000 / 5 / 0` | `inf` | re-prompts |
| `-10000 / 5 / 60` | `-188.71` | re-prompts, then `188.71` |
| `< /dev/null` | stack overflow, abort | `Unexpected end of input.`, exit 1 |
| `abc` / `inf` / `nan` | — | rejected, then `188.71` |
| `--principal 10000 --rate 5 --months 60` | n/a | `188.71`, exit 0, no stdin read |
| `--principal 10000` + piped `5`, `60` | n/a | prompts for the rest, `188.71` |
| `--principal -5` | n/a | error to stderr, exit 1 |
| `--bogus` / repeated flag / missing value | n/a | error to stderr, exit 1 |

200,000 consecutive invalid lines now complete in ~0.9s with flat memory, confirming the recursion fix rather than just a raised limit. The `188.71` figure was independently re-derived from the formula.

author: keirsalterego
body:
"The request timeout is 30s" and "the request timeout is 60s" are both in the store, both real rows, and both handed to every agent that connects — with nothing anywhere saying which one the project settled on.

The near-duplicate pass keeps both **on purpose**. #28 added the figure guard precisely so a differing number is not collapsed as a restatement, because collapsing them loses a decision. What that left behind is two contradictory facts presented as equals, and an agent picking between them by luck.

### The pass

`superseded_mask` is a read-time pass, sibling to `near_duplicate_mask`, writing nothing. Two facts are two readings of one when:

- they have the same shape with the digits blanked out (`figure_blind`), **and**
- they name figures that differ.

Both sides have to name one. "the timeout is 30s" against "the timeout is configurable" leaves the second alone — a fact that dropped the number is not a newer reading of it.

### It labels. It does not drop.

This is the design, not a shortcut.

- `30s` → `60s` is a project changing its mind.
- `us-east-1` → `us-east-2` is a project with two regions.

The two are **lexically identical**. Any rule that picks a winner will sometimes hide a true decision, silently, which is the one failure a memory layer must not have.

So the older reading is still sent — sent saying it is the older one, and naming what replaced it:

```
- The request timeout is 60s
- The request timeout is 30s (an earlier note; a later one says: The request timeout is 60s)
```

An agent told a fact is out of date and *not* told what is current has less than it started with. A few tokens against never losing a decision is the right side of that trade.

### The panel says the same thing

Amber, where a restatement is plain italic, because the two mean different things: a restatement is one fact said twice and costs nothing to ignore; this one says the row above contradicts this row **and both are going out**. Nothing is filtered from the list — a row nobody can see is a row nobody can correct.

---

### One real bug fell out of writing the test

`recent` sorted on `created_at` alone. That is unix seconds, so two facts from one extraction pass over one session stamp identically and came back in scan order.

Every reader downstream takes that list as newest first — `drop_near_duplicates` keeps the first wording it meets, and this pass calls the first reading current. So a tie gave the **exact opposite** answer: the agent told the old timeout is the new one. It happens precisely when two facts land together, which is what one session's extraction does.

Now ordered by id within a second, with a test that fails on the reversal.

---

Five unit tests on the pass (including the two silent-failure cases: unrelated facts that both carry numbers, and revision chains resolving to the newest reading), one end-to-end test that the connect payload carries both facts with the older one marked, and one on the ordering tie.

`cargo fmt`, `clippy --all-targets`, 42 core + 40 mcp tests, `tsc`, `bun test` and the frontend build are clean.

author: mad4bdigital-ai
body:
## Scope

Implement the next concrete Durable Tenant Runtime Bridge capability: one parent-aware async execution engine over the canonical durable Tenant repository facade and the canonical non-provider synthetic adapter.

## Execution lifecycle

The engine:

1. verifies the canonical synthetic protocol and digest;
2. validates exact protocol/preparation/run/lease/plan-item bindings before durable preparation;
3. prepares plan-item and run parents through the durable facade;
4. appends deterministic `prepared → result → readback` child evidence for every item;
5. advances Run and Operation through `readback_pending → reconciling` using checkpoint CAS, exact versions, and canonical transition policy;
6. appends one reconciliation bound to protocol, preparation, journal, readback, and item-accounting digests;
7. finalizes Run and Operation to outcome-bound terminal states.

## Facade extension

The facade now exposes `advanceExecutionState`, a high-level governed operation. It performs a fresh read, checks exact version/current state, validates the transition through `transitionHostingerStorageOperation`, invokes the private repository transition, and verifies readback. Raw `transitionOperation` remains unexposed.

## Non-provider boundary

The engine accepts only the canonical synthetic memory adapter. It has no filesystem, shell, network, Hostinger, or Provider access. The deterministic execution epoch makes child evidence and checkpoints replay-bindable.

## Safety boundary

No route, server, worker, migration, live database access, Hostinger access, provider dispatch, deployment, `main` merge, or Production mutation occurs.

`async_only: true`
`synthetic_only: true`
`live_provider: false`
`filesystem_access: false`
`shell_access: false`
`runtime_mounted: false`
`route_mounted: false`
`worker_mounted: false`
`provider_dispatch_allowed: false`
`production_ready: false`
`secrets_included: false`

author: fortysixand2-t
body:
Final slice of 4 (order: topic bank → faster STT → diction → **lazy audio**).

## Why
The examiner turn ran **STT → LLM → TTS in sequence**, so the HTTP response — and thus the visible reply text — waited on speech synthesis. TTS is the tail latency the learner didn't need to wait for.

## What
- **`POST /speech/turn`** no longer synthesizes (`want_audio=False`). It returns the transcript + reply text as soon as the LLM responds, and advertises `reply_audio_url` whenever TTS is configured and there's something to speak.
- **`GET /speech/audio/{id}`** now synthesizes on the **first play** (lazy) and persists the WAV, so repeat plays are served from cache. If TTS isn't configured (or there's no reply text), it 404s.
- Frontend needs no change: the Play / 🐢-slow buttons already fetch audio on click (no autoplay), so the reply renders immediately and audio is produced only if/when the learner taps play.

## Verification
- Backend: **232 passed, 1 skipped**; `ruff check` clean.
- Rewrote the eager-synthesis test → asserts lazy behavior: POST does not call TTS and stores nothing; first `GET /audio` synthesizes once + caches; second play is served from cache (no re-synth); R10 upheld (uploaded audio never stored). New test: no-TTS → `reply_audio_url` null and `/audio` 404s.
- No web changes.

## Notes
- Ownership check preserved (a turn's audio is only served to its owner).
- Takes effect on app restart (no migration).

author: moschionigabriel
body:
## Summary

This release cuts `main` forward with `move()`'s full **extract** side implemented — the "E" of "EL" — across three feature PRs, plus a review-driven cleanup/fix pass done at release time.

### #6 — [feat: implement move() extract for Sheets, Drive, BigQuery, and API sources](../../pull/6)
Adds `move({ source })` with an internal `extract()` dispatcher covering all four planned v1 source types: Google Sheets, Drive files (CSV/XLSX/JSON), BigQuery (whole table), and external APIs. Every source type returns the same shape — a 2D array, header row plus data rows — the same shape `getValues()` already gives you for a Sheets range, so any source can eventually feed any target once loading lands. XLSX support works around Apps Script having no native XLSX parser by converting the file to a temporary Google Sheet via the Advanced Drive Service, reading it, then deleting the copy.

### #7 — [feat: allow move() to extract a BigQuery query, not just a whole table](../../pull/7)
Extends the `bigquery` source with `query` (inline SQL) and `queryFileId` (a `.sql` file in Drive) as alternatives to `table`. Adds a keyword-based read-only guard (`assertReadOnlySelect`) so a `move()` BigQuery source can only run a `SELECT`/`WITH` — write/transform SQL stays `model()`'s job. Documented explicitly as a footgun-preventer, not a security boundary, since the query always comes from the pipeline author's own config, not external input.

### #8 — [feat: allow move() to extract from a user-defined custom function](../../pull/8)
Adds a `custom` source type: `source.fn` is a direct reference to a function already defined in the caller's own Apps Script project (not a name to look up — see CLAUDE.md's "eval scoping gotcha" for why that distinction matters here). `move()` calls it as `fn(source)` and validates the return shape, same as every other extractor.

### Release-time fixes (this branch, on top of the three PRs above)

Per this repo's workflow, `simplify` and an independent fresh-agent review ran once, batched, against the whole release diff instead of once per PR. That pass found a few real issues spanning the three combined PRs, now fixed:

- **Data loss**: `objectsToRows()` (used by `drive`/`json` and `api` sources) only read the *first* object's keys as the header row, silently dropping any key that only appeared on a later object. Now unions keys across all objects.
- **Silent truncation**: `extractBigQuery()` never checked `queryResults.pageToken`, so a result set spanning more than one response page was silently cut off. Now pages through results.
- **Guard gap**: the read-only SQL guard only checked the leading keyword, so a semicolon-separated multi-statement script (`SELECT 1; DROP TABLE foo`) passed untouched. Now also rejects extra `;`-separated statements.
- **Missing validation**: a `table` BigQuery source missing `dataset` or `projectId` previously interpolated `undefined` into the generated SQL instead of failing clearly; `sheets`/`drive`/`api` sources now validate their required fields upfront too, matching the pattern `bigquery`/`custom` already used.
- **Unchecked HTTP errors**: `extractApi()` didn't check the response code, so a non-2xx error body (e.g. with `muteHttpExceptions`) got parsed as if it were data.
- **Drive API version mismatch**: the XLSX temp-file copy only set the v3 `name` field; on a project whose Advanced Drive Service defaults to v2 the identifying name was silently dropped. Now sets both `name` and `title`.

Plus a cleanup pass: deduped three separate Drive-file-text-reading call sites into one helper, dropped a wasted `DriveApp.getFileById()` call on the xlsx path, dropped a redundant `sleep()` before each BigQuery poll, switched manual row-building loops to `.map()`, and unified the "extractor must return a 2D array" check into one place applied to every source type instead of just `custom`.

## Test plan

Each of #6/#7/#8 already has hand-verified GAS test coverage described in their own PRs (see linked PRs above for the full `notsobigdata-example/` test functions and checklists) — not re-litigated here.

The release-time fix commit changes runtime behavior in ways not covered by the original per-PR testing, so these specific scenarios should be re-verified by hand before merging:

- [ ] Drive JSON / API extract with a payload where a later record has a field the first record lacks — confirm the header row now includes it.
- [ ] BigQuery query extract with a result set large enough to span multiple pages — confirm no rows are missing. Also re-confirm a normal small query still works.
- [ ] BigQuery query/queryFileId with a trailing `;` — confirm it's still accepted; with an actual second statement (`SELECT 1; SELECT 2`) — confirm it's now rejected.
- [ ] BigQuery whole-table extract — confirm it still works now that `dataset`/`projectId` are validated upfront.
- [ ] API extract against an endpoint returning a non-2xx status — confirm it now throws a clear `move():` error instead of parsing the error body as data.
- [ ] Drive XLSX extract — confirm extraction and temp-file cleanup still work with the `name`/`title` change.

author: pfelrodrigues
body:
The port makes finalizing part of the contract rather than something an adapter
has to remember:

```swift
public protocol AudioCapturing: Sendable {
    func start() async throws -> AsyncStream<Segment>
    func stop() async throws -> [Segment]
}
```

`stop()` returns the segments that were still open. Not writing them loses their
audio, and both tracks are open when capture ends, so it returns one partial
each. This is what #48 decided.

`FakeAudioCapture` replays a recording of a known length, rotating on the same
interval as real capture, so the pipeline can be driven without audio hardware
or granted permissions.

The first test is the #48 bug turned into a test: a recording ending before the
first rotation yields its audio and measures 40 seconds rather than zero.

The other three passed on their first run, which `AGENTS.md` calls a red flag,
so each was confirmed against a mutation of the fake it is supposed to catch —
rotation removed, zero-length partials returned, and the two tracks pulled off a
shared clock. All three failed as they should.

Still open from this issue's acceptance: running the whole pipeline end to end
on the fake needs transcription to exist, so it lands in M5.

Closes #9

author: s243a
body:
Items 1 and 2 of the three you asked for, in **one PR straight to the feature line** — no stacking, nothing to strand (see the merge-order note at the end). #4090 was merged, but into `whole-record-str-cmp` *after* #4088 had already taken that branch to the feature line, so its work needs carrying anyway; this branch is rebased on top of it and includes it.

## 1. `&&` / `||` in ternary conditions

```awk
x = ($1 == "a" && $2 > 1) ? 1 : 0     DECLINED
```

Because the condition is now **one emitter** (`plawk_ternary_cond_ir/8`) with three callers, combinators added there land for i64 branches, string branches and the `$0` form **simultaneously** — asserted, not assumed.

**Parser:** `&&`/`||` layered with `&&` tighter, mirroring `while_condition//1`. A single comparison still parses to the bare `cmp/3` term, so nothing downstream changes unless a combinator is written; a parenthesised sub-condition is recursive, so precedence can be overridden.

**Codegen:** `and i1` / `or i1`, no short-circuit — a ternary condition has no side effects and both arms are already evaluated for the `select`. The two differ only in mnemonic, so one helper recurses through `plawk_ternary_cond_ir/8` and inherits every condition form. **SSA placement** is the subtle part: operand setup in the operand half, condition lines in the condition half, so the caller emits `setupA, setupB, [branches], condA, condB, combine`.

**Gates:** `plawk_ternary_condition_ok/1`, with all three admitting gates routed through it, so a comparison can't be admitted at top level but rejected inside an `&&`.

## 2. Scalar-variable operands

```awk
{ n++; x = n > 1 ? 1 : 0 }        DECLINED
```

A scalar compares fine in a rule pattern and an `if` guard; the ternary operand resolves to the slot's SSA value the same way. Works in the condition, in a branch (`$2 > 1 ? n : 0`), and on both sides (`n > m`).

## What this pair actually surfaced

Item 2 initially introduced an **asymmetry** — i64 branches compiled, string branches still declined:

```awk
{ n++; x = n > 1 ? 1 : 0 }        compiled
{ n++; x = n > 1 ? "a" : "b" }    DECLINED
```

A string-valued ternary is carried by a `set_str` operation as **`ternary_str/3`** — a different functor from `ternary/3` — and `plawk_substitute_scalar_reads/4` had a row for the latter only, so the scalar read in the condition was never substituted.

That is the shape the shared condition emitter exists to prevent, reappearing one layer up in the *substitution* pass. Counting them, **four traversals of one term** each had to learn the same lesson independently, and the last had no row at all:

| walker | assumption | fixed |
|---|---|---|
| `plawk_ternary_cond_ir/8` | `cmp`-only | item 1 |
| `plawk_expr_uses_nr/1` | `cmp`-only | item 1 |
| `plawk_substitute_scalar_reads/4` (`ternary/3`) | `cmp`-only | item 2 |
| `plawk_substitute_scalar_reads/4` (`ternary_str/3`) | **absent entirely** | item 2 |

The `plawk_expr_uses_nr/1` one is the dangerous kind: without it `x = (NR == 2 && …) ? 1 : 0` emits an undefined `%current_nr` and clang fails. Fixed *before* probing this time, having cost a debug cycle earlier.

## Verification

**gawk 5.2:** 13 probes (item 1) + 11 (item 2). **Tests:** `test_plawk_ternary_bool.pl` **23/23**, `test_plawk_ternary_scalar_cond.pl` **14/14**.

Structural tests pin the arguments: the gate recurses; the NR walker sees NR through both combinators; substitution covers **both** payload spellings and reaches through combinators; and the i64/string symmetry pair moves together.

### Test-quality note

Item 1's IR tests were wrong first time, in both directions — they asserted bare `= and i1`, but every driver's read loop contains `%line_bad = and i1 …`, so the positive assertions passed vacuously and the negative one failed for an unrelated reason. Now pinned on `_bl_cond`/`_br_cond`. **Third time** in this campaign a driver-wide grep for a common instruction produced a test that couldn't fail (previously `@strcmp`, `@wam_intern_atom`). The rule: pin the construct's own variable names, never a shared mnemonic.

## Item 3, and a merge-order suggestion

**Item 3 (unifying the duplicate string-scalar comparison emitters) is not here.** It's a byte-identity refactor whose whole value is that emitted IR stays identical while one caller's temp names change — that needs a before/after golden dump to confirm, and I'd rather hand it over than ship it unverified. Brief: unify `plawk_if_cond_ir/8`'s two string clauses (~5935, ~5958) with `plawk_pattern_guard_ir/5`'s `scalar_str_cmp_resolved` clauses (~18751, ~18764); they differ **only** in temp naming (`lit`/`slit`, `empty`/`sempty`, `scmp`/`sscmp`) and cond-var source, so one emitter parameterised by a name flavour reproduces both byte-identically. The four-walker count above is the strongest argument yet for doing it.

**Merge order:** with a stack `A → B → C`, merging A to the feature line before B merges into A strands B. That's cost four bookkeeping PRs now. Either merge innermost-first, or retarget the dependent PR before merging its base.

**Targets:** `dscr loan` / `dscr loans` — **60,500/mo, KD 1–8** — plus `what is a dscr loan` (6,600/mo, KD 13). **1,431 words.**

## Positioned against the actual SERP, not a template

That SERP returns **only seven organic results, with Reddit at #2**. On a commercial-intent money term, a forum thread ranking second says Google isn't satisfied with the commercial pages available — it's rewarding candour over marketing.

So the page is built that way:

- **Leads with the answer**, carrying citable numbers for the AI Overview sitting above those seven results
- **States the cost plainly** — 1–2 points above conventional, 1–2 points origination, and the 5-4-3-2-1 prepayment structures nobody leads with
- **Has a "when this is the wrong product" section** that tells qualified borrowers to use a cheaper conventional loan, sends renovation deals to bridge/fix-and-flip, and routes 5+ unit buyers to commercial

A broker page that argues against itself where true is the differentiator on a SERP where Reddit is winning.

## Content

How underwriting changes when the *asset* qualifies instead of the borrower — no DTI, no financed-property cap, LLC-friendly title, each property standing alone. A requirements table (DSCR minimums, down payment, credit, reserves, LTV, property types, the Form 1007 rent schedule). Real costs. The process and what actually delays it — almost never credit, usually the appraisal, the rent schedule, or missing LLC documents. Why these get declined.

## Cannibalization handled up front

The two existing DSCR articles already cover pricing tiers, BRRRR, and the conventional comparison. The hub deliberately stays off those and links to them instead. **Hub owns the head term; supporting pages link up.** That's the rule from the plan, applied at build time rather than discovered later — this site has already had three duplicate pairs suppress clusters.

## Wired in

Sitemap at priority 0.9, visible breadcrumb synced to schema, and inbound contextual links from the calculator, both DSCR articles, and the investor guide.

## One judgment call worth recording

I swapped the hero to the fix-and-flip asset since it's residential rather than commercial — then reverted. It shows an **active construction site**, which would have directly contradicted the page's own point that a property needing work before it rents is exactly when DSCR is the wrong product. Kept the stabilized-building image.

## QA

- **0 real failures.** The one flag is the article-template sibling-link check, which doesn't apply to root pages.
- **Voice:** no banned phrases, no AI-tell structures, sentence stdev **11.2**, **6.5 numbers per 100 words**.
- Three schema blocks valid; **FAQ 7 visible = 7 in schema**; **53 internal links verified 200** in a live render; breadcrumb confirmed rendering.
- `npm run audit`: 835 pages, broken:0 thin:0 filler:0.

| #155 | 1.1 — calculator expansion | open |
| **#156** | **1.2 — this hub** | open |

body:
💡 What:
Implemented parallel data fetching using a `ThreadPoolExecutor` (concurrency) in `main.py` and thread-local HTTP connection pooling (`requests.Session` using `threading.local()`) across all scraper modules (`rootdata.py`, `cryptorank.py`, `okboost.py`, and `notifier.py`). Also added a safe extraction helper in `rootdata.py` and a comprehensive unittest mock suite in `test_main.py`.

🎯 Why:
Sequential network-bound HTTP queries create a cumulative latency bottleneck in multi-API aggregators. Naive multi-threading, however, can introduce concurrency conflicts if sharing HTTP client sessions.

📊 Impact:
Significantly reduces total execution time for the daily aggregation job from ~3.9 seconds to ~0.9 seconds (roughly a ~75% speedup in high-latency simulated network environments).

🔬 Measurement:
Run `python -m unittest test_main.py` to verify the thread-local connection pooling and concurrent execution behaves exactly as expected.

author: pexisgle
body:
## Summary

Started from "can a custom image speed CI up?" — measured it, and the answer was no. What this actually does:

- **Remove the disk cleanup step.** The runner does not need the space. The old `jlumbroso/free-disk-space` report showed `/dev/root 145G 37G 109G 25% /` *after* reclaiming 21GiB, so the job would have started with ~88G free. The `~25GiB free` figure the step guards against does not match what the runner image leaves. #575 already took its wall-time cost off the critical path by detaching the delete, so what remains here is dropping work that was never needed rather than a speedup.
- **Run apt detached, joined after the cache restore.** Nothing between the install and cargo needs those packages, so the install overlaps `Swatinem/rust-cache`. `LIBCLANG_PATH` still resolves because the wait step derives it from `clang --version` after joining.
- **Collapse the three identical setups into `.github/actions/rust-build-env`** instead of a fourth copy of the same twenty-line apt list.

`fmt` is untouched (no native deps, ~10s).

## Measured effect — smaller than first claimed

An earlier revision of this description projected `~250–390s → ~195s`. That was wrong: it compared against a pre-#575 baseline that no longer exists, and it used a 41s clippy timing taken from a job that had **failed fast**, not completed.

Against the real like-for-like baseline — main run `30731204700` (post-#575, warm cache) vs this PR's run `30731382147`:

| job | setup: main | setup: this PR | cargo: main | cargo: this PR |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Clippy | 47s | 62s | 371s | 288s |
| Tests | 54s | 42s | 428s | 508s |
| Doc build | 85s | 37s | 250s | 349s |

Total run: 8m19s (main) vs 8m34s (this PR). **The setup saving is roughly 10–25s per job and is swamped by run-to-run variance in the cargo step.** apt turns out to cost 28–70s rather than the 22s measured earlier, so a 10–20s cache restore only partially hides it.

So this stands on being less configuration and one less unnecessary step, not on a wall-clock win.

## The actual bottleneck, left for follow-up

`llama-cpp-sys-4` rebuilds on every run despite `Restored from cache key … full match: true`, costing 4–6 minutes per job — in the clippy log it runs from 03:54:09 to 03:58:37 out of a 4m48s step. Main does the same, so it predates this PR. That, not setup overhead, is where CI time goes.

### Other rejected alternatives

- **Custom container image** (the original idea): only removes the apt step, and a ~1.5GB GHCR pull costs about as much.
- **cargo-nextest**: total test *execution* is 19.2s across 64 binaries / 2081 tests (summed from the `test result: … finished in Xs` lines). The rest is compile+link, which nextest does not touch.
- **Merging clippy/test/docs into one job**: cuts billed minutes to ~1/3 but serializes, so wall clock gets worse. Billed minutes are free on a public repo.
- **Sharding tests by package**: `-p a -p b` resolves features differently from `--workspace`, so each shard re-builds dependencies with its own feature set.
- **Larger runners**: not free for public repositories.

## Test plan

- [x] Composite action's start/wait mechanism exercised locally with a stubbed apt: success path, apt failure (log surfaced, step exits 1), and status-file timeout all behave as intended
- [x] `LIBCLANG_PATH` derivation verified → `/usr/lib/llvm-18/lib` in the real run
- [x] CI Format / Clippy / Tests / Docs green on this branch
- [x] Cache keys unchanged — the run logs `Restored from cache key "v0-rust-clippy-Linux-x64-db7c195c-b2e9e542" full match: true`
- [x] No job ran out of disk without the cleanup step

author: tibirot
body:
## What & why
**Phase 0 · Week 1 (messaging slice)** — the transactional outbox from ADR-0006: modules publish
integration events reliably, with **no dual-write**. This is the reliability primitive the whole
system reuses (cross-module events now; the sync push path later).

## Scope
- **Implements:** delivery-plan **W1** (messaging) / **ADR-0006**.
- **Module(s):** `BuildingBlocks` (`AggregateRoot`), `Infrastructure` (outbox).
- **Not in this PR (next slices):** the **hosted polling service** (`OutboxProcessor` is the tested core; the always-on `BackgroundService` wires up with the first module/host); **per-tenant row-version stamping**; a handler-level **inbox** ledger (the outbox row's processed-marker gives at-least-once today; handlers must be idempotent).

## How it was tested
- **Real-Postgres integration test** (Testcontainers): an `AggregateRoot` raises `WidgetCreated`; on save it's written to the module's `outbox_message` **in the same transaction** (1 pending row); the `OutboxProcessor` claims it (`FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED`), delivers it to the handler (**exactly-once effect**), marks it processed; a **second run is a no-op** (idempotent).
- 19 tests pass (12 unit + 3 arch + **4 integration**); `BuildingBlocks` stayed pure (arch test green).
- [x] Unit · [x] Architecture · [x] Integration (Testcontainers)

## Docs updated (in this PR)
`roadmap.md` Phase 0 and `delivery-plan.md` W1 — outbox marked done, row-version stamping + hosted service called out as the next slices. (The outbox design was already specced in ADR-0006 / data & persistence.)

## UI
n/a.

## Risk & rollback
- **Blast radius:** additive infra; nothing produces events yet (no modules), so no runtime behavior changes. `ModuleDbContext` now also maps an `outbox_message` table per schema.
- **Revert:** delete `Infrastructure/Outbox/*` + `AggregateRoot.cs`, undo the `ModuleDbContext`/`AddModuleDbContext` wiring.
- **Migration/flag:** none (model exercised via `EnsureCreated` in tests; real migrations come with the first module).

## Reviewer notes
- Start at `OutboxProcessor.cs` (the claim `FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED` + reflection dispatch) and `OutboxIntegrationTests.cs`.
- The write path is a `SaveChangesInterceptor` that drains aggregate events into `OutboxMessage` rows **before** save, so they commit atomically with the state change — the standard outbox pattern.
- Events are stored by `AssemblyQualifiedName` + JSON; fine within a single-process monolith (types are loaded). Cross-service extraction would swap this for a broker (per ADR-0006), not change the domain.
- ~313 lines of C# (within the ~400 budget).

---
### Definition of Done
- [x] One purpose; within budget
- [x] Behavior covered by a real-Postgres integration test (write-in-tx, deliver-once, idempotent)
- [x] Arch-test gate green (BuildingBlocks stayed pure); no banned patterns
- [x] Docs-in-lockstep (roadmap + delivery plan)
- [x] Scope + non-scope stated; W1 / ADR-0006 cited
- [x] No migration; no feature flag
- [x] Self-reviewed; builds clean; 19 tests green locally
- [x] No secrets, no unrelated files, no gate weakened

Unable to satisfy `pubspec.yaml` using `pubspec.lock`.
```

`pubspec.lock` has pinned `vm_service 14.2.5` **since the initial commit**, but `release.yml` pinned `FLUTTER_VERSION: '3.24.0'`, whose bundled `vm_service` is `14.2.4`. Honouring the lock would require a *downgrade*, so `--enforce-lockfile` aborts.

That flag isn't something odd about our build — it's in F-Droid's canonical Flutter template (`templates/build-flutter.yml`), so the bot-generated build-13 entry picked it up and turned a long-latent inconsistency into a hard failure.

**Why CI never caught it:** `ci.yml` ran plain `flutter pub get`, which silently re-resolves. The lockfile was only load-bearing in F-Droid's build, so F-Droid was the first place it could fail. Both Flutter jobs now pass `--enforce-lockfile`.

## Why current stable rather than a one-patch nudge

F-Droid imposes **no ceiling** on the SDK — `srclibs/flutter.yml` is an unpinned clone of `flutter/flutter`, and the recipe checks out whatever tag `FLUTTER_VERSION` names. Apps published on F-Droid today:

| App | Flutter |
|---|---|
| `cz.mod42.diktafon` | 3.44.5 (published, versionCode 93) |
| `InlitX/streak` | 3.41.9, `compileSdk 36` |
| `UXAVIA/bag` | 3.41.5 |

So instead of nudging to 3.24.5, this moves to current stable **3.44.8**, which resolves `vm_service` to 14.2.5 and satisfies the existing lock.

## Migration required by the two-year jump

| Breakage | Fix |
|---|---|
| Synthetic `flutter_gen` package removed; gen-l10n emits into the arb-dir | 15 files → `package:nfc_archiver/l10n/app_localizations.dart`; generated output gitignored since every build path regenerates it |
| `ThemeData.cardTheme` now takes `CardThemeData` | renamed at both call sites |
| `file_picker` 6.x references the removed v1 embedding — cannot compile | → 11.0.3; `FilePicker` is now an `abstract final class`, so `.platform` is gone |
| `android/build.gradle` forced **plugin subprojects** to `compileSdk 34` → `checkDebugAarMetadata` fails once `androidx.core` requires 35+ | app and subproject override both → 36, Java 17 |
| AGP 8.1.0 is below Flutter 3.44's 8.6.0 minimum | → 8.13.2, deliberately **not** 9.x: AGP 9 reads only the new DSL and these are Groovy scripts. Flutter's migrator added the matching `newDsl`/`builtInKotlin` opt-outs |

## Docs and mirror

`CLAUDE.md`'s **"compileSdk must stay at 34"** rule is removed. It was written for a JDK 21 `jlink`/`JdkImageTransform` bug, but the builder is now `buildserver-trixie`, the recipe forces JDK 17, and published F-Droid apps ship on `compileSdk 36`. The `fdroid/` mirror is resynced to fdroiddata master — ours had builds 8 and 13, upstream has 8–12.

## Verification (Flutter 3.44.8 / Dart 3.12.2)

- `flutter pub get --enforce-lockfile` → exit 0 (**the original failure**)
- `flutter analyze` → 0 errors
- `flutter test` → **250/250 pass**
- `flutter build apk --debug` → built
- `flutter build apk --release` → built, 56.4 MB (this is what F-Droid runs)
- Cross-language interop cross-decode → passes **both directions** under the new Dart SDK, so the on-tag byte format is unaffected
- F-Droid's exact `sed` still extracts a single clean value: `3.44.8`

## Not verified

**NFC and BLE behaviour on real hardware.** The plugin bumps and `targetSdk 36` touch exactly the areas only a device can confirm. Worth a device pass before tagging.

**This does not clear build 13 on its own** — that entry is pinned to tag commit `4567440`, so F-Droid needs a new tag to build successfully.

author: zxgshawn
body:
## Why

The Docker workflow takes ~5 min wall clock per push, and #97 made it 6 legs. In the slowest leg, 242s of 265s is a from-scratch 319-crate release compile. Root causes:

- The repo's 10 GB Actions cache is saturated (~137 entries), so buildkit `mode=max` cache exports get LRU-evicted and the `/src/target` cache mounts restore empty.
- `runtime.Dockerfile` had no cache mounts at all — every runtime leg was a guaranteed cold build.
- The 6 matrix legs each compile the same dependency tree independently; the three images on one arch share nearly all deps.

The repo is public, so minutes are free — this targets pure wall clock.

## What

- **One multi-target `docker/horsie.Dockerfile`** (targets `server`, `runtime`, `velos`) with a single cache-mounted cargo invocation building all three binaries; replaces the three per-image Dockerfiles. Adds mold as the linker.
- **Workflow matrix 6 legs → 2** (one per arch): each leg runs three `build-push-action` steps on the same builder, so the runtime/velos steps resolve the shared build stage CACHED locally.
- **One gha cache scope per arch** instead of six, with a single `cache-to` writer per run; PR validate builds all three targets with `cache-from` only, so PRs can no longer evict main's cache.

## Callouts

- The `merge`/`compose-validate` jobs are untouched; digest artifact naming (`digest-<key>-*`) is preserved, and the keys stay mutually non-prefixing.
- Only `horsie-runtime` has default features, so one `--no-default-features` invocation builds all three correctly (drops runtime's `sandbox`, as today). Runtime build also gains `--locked`.
- Verified locally on aarch64: all three targets build, later targets reuse the shared stage (CACHED), and all three mold-linked binaries pass `--help` smoke tests.
- Expected: ~3 min wall clock warm (vs ~5+), cold ~4.5–5 min but rare once the cache stabilizes. First post-merge push will confirm.

body:
## Summary

Root-causes and fixes the mobile/tablet E2E signup timeout flagged as pre-existing on `main` during PR #272's CI run (confirmed failing at base commit `4242e58`, unrelated to that PR's diff).

## Story

No story doc — this is a config bug fix, not a feature.

## Type of change

- [x] fix (bug fix)
- [ ] feat (new feature)
- [ ] refactor (no behavior change)
- [ ] docs (documentation only)
- [x] test (adding or fixing tests)
- [ ] chore (tooling, deps, build)

## Root cause

`playwright.config.ts`'s `chromium-mobile` and `chromium-tablet` project names were a lie. Both spread `devices["iPhone 13"]` / `devices["iPad (gen 7)"]` directly into `use`, and both of those Playwright device presets set `defaultBrowserType: "webkit"` (they're modeled on real Safari/iOS). Nothing overrode it, so despite their names, both projects have always launched **WebKit**, not Chromium — only `chromium-desktop` (via `devices["Desktop Chrome"]`, which correctly sets `defaultBrowserType: "chromium"`) was ever actually testing Chromium.

Reproduced locally (spun up a local Postgres, built the app, ran the suite): under WebKit, clicking the signup form's submit button never triggers navigation at all — the page just sits on `/signup` until the test's 15s `toHaveURL(/dashboard)` assertion times out. Under Chromium at the identical viewport/touch profile, the same test passes in under a second.

## Fix

Explicitly set `browserName: "chromium"` (clearing the inherited `defaultBrowserType`) on both projects, so they test what their names claim — Chromium at a mobile/tablet viewport and touch profile, not real WebKit/Safari behavior, which was never the intent (nothing else in the repo — CI config, docs, other test files — suggests Safari/WebKit compatibility was ever an explicit target).

author: deco354
body:
## TLDR
Adds some experimental github workflows that will set claude to fix issues with the claude-fix label using a predefined workflow of /plan mode then auto mode using a model that was determined appropriate by the issue.

## Description (claude generated)

Adds the automated pipeline that turns code-quality findings into reviewed PRs, built on `anthropics/claude-code-action@v1` and the existing `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` secret (subscription auth — quota exhaustion is handled as a first-class state, never conflated with task failure).

**Flow:** `scripts/kickoff.sh` files tiered issues from `code_quality/findings_v2` (high-severity only by default) and labels them `claude-fix-ready`. A human arms one issue at a time with `claude-fix` (the throttle). The fixer plans (read-only plan mode), posts the plan as an issue comment, gates on risk (HIGH → `needs-human`, fail-closed), implements on `claude/issue-<n>` with incremental pushes, and opens a PR only when `compileall + pytest` is green. The existing auto-review approves or requests changes; `claude-review-fix.yml` addresses change requests (3-cycle cap). A 30-minute cron requeues quota-killed runs, which resume from the plan comment + branch state instead of re-spending.

| Tier | Phases | Plan | Implement |
|---|---|---|---|
| `tier-light` | single | — (plan comment first, in-prompt gate) | sonnet / medium |
| `tier-standard` (default) | two-phase | opus / high | sonnet / high |
| `tier-heavy` | two-phase | opus / xhigh | opus / high |
| `tier-max` (human-only escalation) | two-phase | claude-fable-5 / high | opus / high |

Design decisions worth knowing when reviewing:

- **PR identity:** PRs are created by a plain step with `GITHUB_TOKEN` (author `github-actions[bot]`) because GitHub blocks approving/requesting-changes on your own PR and the auto-reviewer posts as `claude[bot]` — the action's default identity. Since `GITHUB_TOKEN` events don't trigger workflows, the job then close/reopens the PR with the App token so `smoke` + the auto-review fire.
- **Cron re-triggers use `workflow_dispatch`**, not label remove/re-add — `GITHUB_TOKEN` label events don't fire workflows; dispatch is exempt from that rule.
- **Repo-wide 2-job cap is a busy-gate step** (counts in-progress runs of all four claude-code-action workflows, defers fixer runs with `claude-busy-wait`), not sharded concurrency groups — GitHub cancels the *older pending* run in a group, which silently drops items. Busy deferrals never consume the 8-retry quota budget.
- **tier-max plan-phase quota failures are frozen** (never auto-retried): a Fable planning run draws heavily on the rolling allowance. tier-max *implement* failures run on Opus and retry normally — resume skips the Fable plan step since the plan comment exists.
- **Trust boundaries:** plan comments and quota markers are only honored from the pipeline's exact bot identities (`github-actions[bot]` / `claude[bot]`); the review-fix trigger only fires for reviews from `claude[bot]` or accounts with repo standing; git in the fixer steps is scoped to explicit subcommands.
- **`--disallowedTools "Task"` on every action step** (the PR #73 stall lesson).

Labels (`claude-fix`, `claude-fix-ready`, `needs-human`, `claude-quota-wait`, `claude-busy-wait`, `tier-*`) are already created in the repo; `scripts/kickoff.sh` re-bootstraps them idempotently.

## How to test

Everything below happens **after this PR merges** — the `issues:` and `schedule:` triggers only run workflow files that are on `main`. There is nothing else to set up first: the `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` secret and all 9 labels already exist.

Run the stages in order. Each stage says what it costs; "free" means no Claude call is made. Watch runs either in the **Actions tab** (workflow "Claude Fix") or with:

```bash
gh run list --workflow=claude-fix.yml --limit 3   # newest first
gh run watch <run-id>
```

If any stage goes sideways, look at the run's **"Classify failure"** step log and the issue's newest comment — every deliberate stop leaves a comment saying what happened and how to re-trigger.

---

### Stage 0 — rehearse kickoff without creating anything

*Cost: one small Claude run (it reads and clusters the findings, creates nothing).*

```bash
scripts/kickoff.sh --dry-run
```

**Expect:** a markdown table of the 4 high-severity findings it *would* file — issue title, files, tier + one-line reasoning, batch order — and no new issues in the tracker afterwards.

### Stage 1 — the smallest real end-to-end loop (tier-light on issue #54)

*Cost: one tier-light fixer run (sonnet).*

```bash
gh issue edit 54 --add-label tier-light
gh issue edit 54 --add-label claude-fix      # this is the trigger
```

**Expect, in order** (the whole run takes a few minutes):

1. A "Claude Fix" run starts on the Actions tab.
2. A **plan comment** appears on #54, starting with `<!-- claude-plan issue=54 tier=tier-light risk=LOW -->` — and it appears **before** any commit exists on branch `claude/issue-54` (compare the comment's timestamp with the branch's first commit time).
3. The branch fills with small commits, pushed incrementally.
4. A PR opens, **authored by `github-actions[bot]`**, containing `Closes #54`, `## Plan`, `## Risk class`, `## How to test`, and a 🤖 Claude-generated callout.
5. The PR is briefly **closed and reopened** — that's deliberate (the "kick" that makes GitHub run checks on a bot-created PR). Right after it, the `smoke` check and `Claude Code Review` start.
6. claude[bot] posts a review verdict on the PR.

Merging that PR is your call, as always.

### Stage 2 — two-phase handoff + proof the planner can't write

*Cost: one plan run (opus) + one implement run (sonnet).*

```bash
gh issue create \
  --title "Canary: clarify resolve_run_dir docstring" \
  --body "Add one sentence to shared/utils.py resolve_run_dir's docstring explaining what happens when --run-id is given but no such run exists. (Pipeline canary — safe to close.)" \
  --label tier-standard
gh issue edit <N> --add-label claude-fix     # <N> = number printed by the create
```

**Expect:**

1. Plan comment on the issue with first line `RISK: LOW`, files to touch, steps, verification.
2. **Write-block proof:** while the "Plan (read-only)" step is running, `git ls-remote origin claude/issue-<N>` returns nothing — the branch only appears once the "Implement" step starts. (Bonus: the "Post plan comment" step's log says whether the plan arrived via `structured_output` or the `RISK:` line fallback — either is fine, this is the one behavior we could only verify live.)
3. Implement → green gate → PR opens, same shape as Stage 1.

### Stage 3 — risk gate stops a HIGH-risk plan

*Cost: one plan run (opus). No implementation happens — that's the point.*

```bash
gh issue create \
  --title "Canary: change how publish_hf reads the HF auth token" \
  --body "Rework the HF token handling in evals/publish_hf.py. (Pipeline canary — safe to close. Touching credential handling should classify as HIGH risk.)" \
  --label tier-standard
gh issue edit <N> --add-label claude-fix
```

**Expect:** plan comment with `RISK: HIGH` → the issue gets `needs-human` plus a comment explaining the block → **no branch `claude/issue-<N>` is ever created** → the workflow run ends green (a deliberate stop, not a failure).

### Stage 4 — quota failure → classifier → cron → resume

*Cost: 4a and 4b are free; 4c spends one implement run.*

**4a. Fake a quota death** (no Claude call — the run fails fast with a simulated usage-limit error). Use the Stage 2 canary's number:

```bash
gh workflow run claude-fix.yml -f issue_number=<N> -f simulate_quota=true -f simulate_phase=implement
```

**Expect:** the run fails within ~1 minute; the issue gains the `claude-quota-wait` label and a comment starting `<!-- claude-quota issue=<N> phase=implement ... count=1 ... -->` saying it's quota retry 1 of 8

author: hyuntohoon
body:
FEAT-album-review-authoring **Step 2 — 쌓인 것을 본다**. Workspace side: the merged contract for one new read, the implementation record in the RFC, and the plan.md row.

Merges **first** so the backend's notify-contract dispatch is a no-op (workspace contract merge order).

## What is in here

- `docs/contracts/openapi.json` — regenerated via `tools/merge_openapi.py`. **Purely additive**: `GET /api/me/review-candidates` + two schemas, 120 insertions / 0 deletions. No pydantic version drift.
- `docs/rfcs/FEAT-album-review-authoring.md` — Step 2 implementation record + 3 rows in the decisions log + 충돌 #8 closed.
- `docs/plan.md` — row updated: Step 2 implemented, next = Step 3 (with OQ3 잔여 still open).
- `infra/apigateway.tf` — **comment only**, no resource change.

## Decisions recorded (made while implementing)

1. **평가 이력 통계에는 백엔드 변경이 없다.** `GET /api/members/{handle}` already returns the member's whole rating feed unpaginated, and 개수·평균·분포·정렬 are all folds over rows the page already holds — exactly what OQ7 predicted. Noted the condition that would invalidate this: if the feed is ever paginated, the stats must move server-side, or a fold over one page reports that page's average as the member's.
2. **"평론 쓸 것" is its own read, not a filter over `/api/me/album-states`.** `review_candidate IS TRUE` is the entire definition of the list — in the query it can't be forgotten, in the caller it can. And a mark can sit on an album that is in no bucket with no rating, so the row has no other source of a title.
3. **Extending `MyAlbumStateResponse` was considered and dropped.** It is also the PUT write response, so album fields nobody reads would land on the write path and `upsert` would have to return the album too.
4. **별점 ties break by 이름.** Two 4.5s in arbitrary order read as a glitch while scanning by score.

충돌 #8 (dead `computeStats`) is closed as **delete**, and the reason is kept: it was not merely dead, it folded the wrong type — `MemberReview[]`, i.e. 평론 posts from the build-time collection, excluding 칼럼 and de-duplicating by a `"title|artist"` string. None of that applies to a rating history.

## The empty states are written down as decisions

## The problem

The overlay from #6 was summoned by a three finger touch or F3, deliberately hidden so no control sat in the tactical view. That was the wrong trade. The machine it exists to measure is a phone, a phone has no F3 key, and an instrument nobody can find on the machine it was built for is not an instrument.

## The change

A `DBG` button in the bottom left corner, on screen at all times, including during a battle.

- **Bottom left** because a landscape grip puts a thumb there, the overlay opens on the right so the two never collide, and it is the one corner of the battle view carrying nothing a player reaches for under fire.
- **Dimmed to 55%** until touched, so it reads as bolted to the outside of the screen rather than as something the game is offering.
- The CanvasLayer now stays visible and `$Panel` hides, rather than the whole layer hiding, because the button lives on the layer the toggle used to switch off.
- The gestures still work and cost nothing, so nothing is lost by keeping them.

## Verified

Driven in the exported web build under Playwright: the button renders bottom left during a battle, tapping it opens the panel, and the counters read live. Tests pass, style check passes.

## What changed

- Added a threat-model worksheet for assets, principals, boundaries, threats, controls, tests, and residual risk.

- Added adversarial fixtures for tool poisoning, SSRF, cross-tenant access, destructive actions, and safe reads.
- Added a runnable capstone policy implementation.
- Added scenario-based questions to the interactive quiz.

### CI and deployment
- Consolidated Pages deployment into the canonical `publish-pages.yml` workflow.
