author: yukon-autoresearch[bot]
body:
Yukon submission `6e930ece-a903-4514-a1b8-19c5ee530c4c` against https://github.com/Layr-Labs/mlxfast-challenge at `7702fab8a41fe2f4ff2ae281beeb1548b31e3406`.

Current best score: 2.4549506212825. This PR's own benchmark run scores the head commit;
the PR is merged automatically if the submission is accepted, and closed with the result otherwise.

---

**Submitter note**

Model: OpenAI Codex (GPT-5)

# Context and objective

This submission is an incremental optimization on top of the promoted challenge leader at commit 7702fab8a41fe2f4ff2ae281beeb1548b31e3406. Before changing code, I verified both origin/main and the public benchmark record pointed at that commit, ran setup, built the participant worker and Metal library, and recorded a same-machine local leader baseline. The objective was to find small, architecture-general savings in serial one-token decode without changing any accepted model representation or observable behavior. This was deliberately scoped to two orthogonal ideas: remove duplicated MoE routing work from the sparse-layer decode path, and simplify the exact NVFP4 scale decode arithmetic used by the quantized kernels.

The ranked acceptance window rewards controlled incremental changes, so I avoided combining unrelated experimental work. In particular, this submission does not change attention requantization, tail norm or QKV scheduling, the leader split-K design, the routed/shared down R1 kernel, layer-zero asynchronous attention behavior, KV semantics, or any harness code. It also does not introduce prompt specialization, speculative execution, future-token work, cross-request state, model-output memoization, network or file access, or a new quantized representation.

# Baseline and hypotheses

The fresh leader local-iterate measurement at 7702fab8 passed all 130 checked steps with max_abs_diff 0. It measured prefill at 0.0006124408359375 seconds per token, charged decode at 0.0072108466796875 seconds per token, and a steady one-token decode-step mean of about 0.004542 seconds. Local absolute values are directional because this host is not the official M5 Max and the local estimate compares against pinned constants, but same-host cool-gated brackets are useful for deciding whether a change is worth submitting.

The first hypothesis concerned the sparse MoE router. The leader path already has a fused residual, RMS normalization, and router-score producer, followed by the large packed routed gate/up QMV plus SwiGLU kernel. The standalone router selector then consumes the same score information to produce eight expert indices and normalized expert weights. Since the packed routed QMV already visits the expert slots, I hypothesized that publishing the exact pre-bias sigmoid score bits from the producer and returning the top-eight route alongside the packed activation could remove the separate selector dispatch and dependent post-processing. The main tradeoff was extra output plumbing and a very small amount of work in one designated SIMD lane; the implementation therefore preserves the old fallback path and keeps route publication to a single writer.

The second hypothesis concerned NVFP4 group scales. The existing loader reconstructs the FP8 scale as a half value and then applies the FP8 exponent decode and FP4 renormalization through separate exact powers of two. IEEE binary multiplication by these powers does not require a lossy numerical reassociation for the finite scale-byte domain. I hypothesized that carrying the sign bit while constructing the half bits, followed by one float multiply by the combined power of two, would preserve every decoded scale exactly while removing staged multiply work. This was implemented in both AOT and JIT sources, including the M5 NAX variants, so the source used on the ranked machine cannot diverge from the checked counterpart.

# Router implementation

The router change is confined to Sources/MLXFastModel/LagunaRuntimeModel.swift. It adds a default-on DARKBLOOM_PACKED_ROUTER_OUTPUTS feature switch so that the exact previous path remains available for controlled ablation and unsupported configurations.

When enabled, the fused residual/RMS/router producer stores the existing ordinal keys unchanged in words 0 through 255 and publishes each exact pre-bias FP32 sigmoid score by bitcast in words 256 through 511. The payload shape is 512 words only for the enabled path. The disabled path retains the original 256-word shape, source, and keys_v1 JIT identity. The enabled source uses a distinct keys_scores_v1 identity to avoid stale JIT cache aliasing.

A three-output version of the packed routed QMV plus SwiGLU kernel returns the original BF16 activation, UInt32 expert indices with shape 1 by 1 by 8, and FP32 normalized expert weights with shape 1 by 1 by 8. Slot 7, tile 0, SIMD group 0, lane 0 is the only route-output writer. It uses the same repeated-min top-eight selection, ordinal comparison, stable expert-index tie break, score-plus-total fold order, and division order as the prior standalone route selector. Scores are recovered through bitcast, not recomputed. This is important because even a mathematically equivalent sigmoid or a different reduction order could alter a near-tie token.

The sparse-MoE forward path constructs the packed route only under exhaustive guards for the exact supported flags, batch shape, token count, expert geometry, dtype, group size, and quantization mode. When every guard passes, it reuses the packed activation and returned route. When any guard fails, it invokes the previous gate path exactly once and retains all pre-existing behavior. The attention g_proj is unrelated to this MoE router and is untouched. The current-token-only serial contract is unchanged: one supplied token produces one logical and physical KV advance, with no future logits or cache rows.

# Exact NVFP4 scale implementation

The scale fold changes four synchronized kernel sources:

- Vendor/mlx-swift/Source/Cmlx/mlx-generated/fp_quantized.cpp
- Vendor/mlx-swift/Source/Cmlx/mlx-generated/fp_quantized_nax.cpp
- Vendor/mlx-swift/Source/Cmlx/mlx/mlx/backend/metal/kernels/fp_quantized.h
- Vendor/mlx-swift/Source/Cmlx/mlx/mlx/backend/metal/kernels/fp_quantized_nax.h

The helper adds the sign bit to itself before shifting the byte by seven, which carries the sign into half bit 15, reinterprets the resulting ushort as half, converts it to float, and multiplies once by 4194304.0. That constant is exactly 2 to the power 22, combining the previous 2 to the power 8 FP8 decode and 2 to the power 14 FP4 normalization. The scale-byte domain is finite, and both stages are exact binary powers. Negative zero behavior is preserved. No weight, packed nibble, group boundary, scale byte, or quantization parameter changes. The leader fused split-K loader inherits this helper without otherwise changing its body.

The plain and NAX AOT/JIT implementations were compared for textual equivalence. The patch also matches the previously audited scale-fold patch identity. The Metal library was rebuilt after each checkout in the A/B bracket so the AOT artifact always matched the source being measured; the benchmark rebuilt the JIT-effective participant worker when necessary.

# Reproducible workflow

The main validation commands were:

    git fetch origin main
    git switch laguna-leader-router-scale
    ./setup.sh
    ./benchmark.sh --local-iterate
    DARKBLOOM_PACKED_ROUTER_OUTPUTS=0 ./benchmark.sh --local-iterate
    ./tools/build-mlx-metallib.sh
    swift build -c release --scratch-path .build-worker --product mlxfast-runtime-worker --force-resolved-versions
    swift test --force-resolved-versions
    BASE_SHA=7702fab8 HEAD_SHA=HEAD .github/scripts/enforce-modifiable-surface.sh
    ./benchmark.sh --local-submit

All local benchmark runs used the normal thermal gate. I did not disable cooling or the run guard. Only one model-holding process ran at a time. A/B controls used the feature switch or the router-only commit, not

author: cbirkbeck
body:
`exists_circle_toUnitDisc_eq_of_nonneg` (in `Poincare/Betweenness.lean`) was
proving two separable things in one 47-line body:

1. the forward orbit of an origin-fixing isometry lies on a Euclidean ray
   through `γ 1` — i.e. `γ t` is a *nonnegative multiple* of `γ 1` for `t ≥ 0`;
2. normalising `γ 1` names the direction `u`, and the norm formula pins that
   multiple to `tanh t`.

Step 1 is a statement about betweenness alone. It is now the private lemma
`exists_nonneg_mul_toUnitDisc_one`, which needs only `hγ` and `h0` — the
collinearity setup (`hmem`, `hdist0`, `hne`, `hbetween`) moves with it and is
no longer in scope for step 2. It is stated **pointwise** in `t` rather than as
a `∀`-family, since that is the form the caller consumes.

Bodies: 47 → 19 (`exists_circle_toUnitDisc_eq_of_nonneg`) + 25
(`exists_nonneg_mul_toUnitDisc_one`).

To be explicit about scope: the original body was **under** the 50-line bar, so
this is not a decompose-queue item. The case for it is the interface — the
extracted statement is a named mathematical fact with two hypotheses, not a
mechanical slice. No public signature changes; both lemmas stay private.

Gates run locally: `lake build`, `lake exe axioms` (20182 decls in allowlist),

author: simplykryssie-blip
body:
## Three independent, currently-live production bugs

All found while validating PR #9's preview — none are related to that PR's feature work, all already exist on `main` right now.

### 1. Production build is currently broken (main's own CI confirms it)

`main`'s HEAD commit (`3560e3e`, PR #8) added `getAppOrigin()` to `lib/auth/portal.ts` and imported it from the Client Component `app/(auth)/sign-up/page.tsx`. That file also imports `next/headers` for its other (legitimately server-only) exports, so the whole module gets pulled into the client bundle — a hard Client/Server Component boundary violation.

**This isn't a hypothesis** — `main`'s own CI run for `3560e3e` has `conclusion: failure` (checked directly via the GitHub Actions API), and I reproduced the identical error locally with both `npm run build` and `npm run build -- --webpack`.

Fix: moved `getAppOrigin()` into a new client-safe `lib/auth/app-origin.ts` with no server-only imports, and improved it to prefer `window.location.origin` in the browser (this also fixes signup confirmation emails redirecting to production instead of the current Vercel preview). Same fix independently arrived at in `feature/guided-client-engagement` (PR #9) — reused verbatim here.

### 2. Invisible buttons/text (white-on-white or transparent)

`tailwind.config.ts`'s `theme.extend.colors` (primary, secondary, destructive, card, popover, sidebar, input, ring) and `backgroundImage.brand-gradient` are Tailwind v3-style JS config with no `@config` directive bridging them into Tailwind v4's CSS-first `@theme` system — so none of those tokens ever generated any CSS. `bg-brand-gradient text-white` (the most common CTA button style, including the dashboard hero and its "Add client"/"New engagement" buttons) rendered as just `text-white` with no background: literally invisible white text.

Confirmed via the actual compiled CSS output before/after the fix. Also sets `color-scheme: light` in `:root`.

### 3. No way to edit a client, and add-client was missing SSN/EIN/DOB

The client detail page (`/clients/[clientId]`) was entirely read-only — there was no edit button, no edit page, and `createClientAction` had no update counterpart. Added `updateClientAction`, a new `/clients/[clientId]/edit` page, and an Edit button on the client detail header (gated to the same `STAFF_ROLES` the create flow already requires).

Also extended both create and edit to capture date of birth, SSN last 4, EIN last 4, preferred contact method, and source — those columns already exist on `clients` and the fuller validation schema already existed in `lib/validation/clients.ts` (via an orphaned, never-rendered `ClientFormDialog` component) but were never wired into the actual live add-client flow.

## Validation

- `npm run type-check` — clean
- `npm run lint` — 0 errors, 48 pre-existing warnings (unchanged count — no new warnings introduced)
- `npm run build` (Turbopack) — clean, `/clients/[clientId]/edit` present in route output
- `npm run build -- --webpack` — clean

## Scope

Deliberately separate from PR #9 (`feature/guided-client-engagement`) — that's a large feature branch still pending manual QA. This is a minimal, isolated fix for bugs already live on `main`/production.

author: fomotsar-commits
body:
The last two residues from the 78-agent review.

## 1. `outcomesReader.ts` — the port had diverged from its own source of truth

`LauncherDataFetcher.fetchMarket` returned `TokenMarket | null`, so *"GeckoTerminal answered and there is no pool"* and *"GeckoTerminal never answered"* were the same value. #216 fixed that in `api/_lib/launcher-outcomes.js` — the JS port that actually runs — and left a note saying to **port it upward rather than resync it away**. This is that port.

**Honest scope: this is not a live defect.** I checked before writing it — `buildOutcomeRecords`, `buildLaunchSummary` and `LauncherDataFetcher` are referenced **only by this file's own test**. Every other module imports just the `LaunchBaseline` type, and the production path is the JS adapter. The value is that the documented source of truth now matches shipped behaviour, so the next person porting between them doesn't reintroduce the collapse.

Only the **boundary** needed widening. The liquidity-null half of #216 belongs to the adapter — the thing that parses GeckoTerminal attributes. The reader is handed an already-built `TokenMarket` and never sees them.

`buildLaunchSummary` deliberately does **not** get a `read === false` branch. `marketIsObserved(null)` already covers it, an unranked launch is the right answer either way, and the explicit guard **survived its own mutation** — so it wasn't doing work. Removed rather than kept for symmetry.

## 2. `ethereumAdapter` — rows in, nothing out

Rows arriving but none being attributable still derived an empty holder set and landed on `ScanError('empty')` — *"No holder data for this token — double-check the address is a token."* The payload wasn't empty; we just couldn't use any of it.

#213 closed this on the route (*non-empty in, empty out, is drift*). This is the client half of the same guard, so a drifted payload from any other source can't launder either.

## Verification

| Mutation | Tests killed |
|---|---|
| drop the adapter's non-empty-in/empty-out guard | 1 |
| collapse the reader's unreadable state back into "no pool" | 4 |

`172 files / 2477 tests` pass, `tsc -b` clean, eslint 0 errors.

author: eunolabs
body:
## Summary

Three follow-ups from the `schemaVersion 0.2` publication, each closing a place where a guarantee stopped at the edge of one enforcement point, one token, or one file: single-use declassify approvals, task-anchored enforcement state, and signed attestations on registry entries.

**Delegation attenuation (#140) has been split out** into its own branch and PR. It was originally here because it composes with #139 — a quarantined sub-agent is only quarantined if it shares the task's taint — but it touches far more of the decision path than the other three (the engine's `evaluateMatched`, the flow-label sink rule, obligation collection, three list filters, two PDPs, the token boundary) and unlike them its defects deny traffic rather than failing closed. Two review rounds found outage-class bugs in it while these three had been stable since the first. It should not gate them.

## Why

Closes #139
Closes #141
Closes #142

Each issue names a boundary the current implementation stops at:

- **#142** — `DeclassifyApproval.Covers` scopes a grant on `(labels, target)` only, so an approval minted into a long-lived token is a *standing* declassification when the intent is almost always "approve clearing this once".
- **#139** — flow taint, `sequenceBlock` antecedents, and the effect/quota counters are keyed by `sessionID`. A sub-agent delegated to a second PEP, or the same task re-entering through a fresh session, starts with a clean label set and a full budget. Information-flow control's "for all flows" claim spans one enforcement point, and no more.
- **#141** — the corpus trust model was package-signing-by-content-digest only: an entry is provably what it says it is (integrity), but nothing established *who* is asserting it or let a second party countersign or dispute it.

### #142 — single-use approvals (`once`)

A `mcp.declassify` grant marked `once: true` is burned on the first call that clears with it; every later presentation is refused `approval_consumed`.

- The burn is keyed by the grant's **`id`**, which `once` therefore makes **mandatory**. A content key would collide two genuinely distinct human decisions, and a grant with nothing to burn would silently behave as a standing one — so it rejects the token instead.
- It is burned **even when the clear is a no-op**, or the grant would be replayable by ordering: present it once while clean, acquire the taint, present it again to the clear that matters.
- The burn is written **before** the clear. A fault can then leave a grant spent for a clear that did not happen (over-refusal, the safe direction) but never a label dropped by a grant still marked live. There is deliberately **no refund** — the un-burn an earlier revision performed was itself a fail-open, because the antecedent-fault deny it fired on is soft and an `--audit` route forwards it.
- A token carrying a spent grant *and* a live one uses the live one rather than refusing on the first match.
- The ledger lives in the **call counter**, not the flow store, and the reason is atomicity: a Get-then-Add against the flow store is a check-then-act two concurrent callers both win, which double-spends exactly the approval this makes single-use. A counted bucket with a limit of 1 through `AdmitAll` is precisely "admit once, ever". It is **unanchored** — a burn belongs to the approval, not to a session or a task, so reconnecting does not restore it. The cost of a windowed backend is a **seven-day** retention bound, stated in the threat model rather than wished away.

### #139 — cross-PEP task anchoring (`taskAnchoredState`)

Keys flow taint, `sequenceBlock` antecedents, and `maxCalls`/cumulative `blastRadius` budgets on the validated `mcp.task_id` claim rather than on the session.

Three properties, each structural rather than conventional:

1. **Opt-in** — it changes what every budget in the policy *means* (a `maxCalls` of 20 becomes 20 per task, not 20 per connection). That is not a change to make on an operator's behalf.
2. **The anchor is a validated claim** — `task_id` is one of the reserved `input.claims` keys a custom claim cannot shadow, so an agent cannot pick which task's budget it spends.
3. **It falls back to the session only where that is safe, and never to a shared bucket** — a request with **no token** is anchored exactly as it is today, so turning this on cannot make two unauthenticated callers share anything. A request that **presented a token carrying no `task_id`** is hard-denied `MISSING_CONTEXT` instead: on an HTTP host each request carries its own `Authorization` header, so falling back there would let one caller split its own taint, budgets and antecedents across two buckets by alternating tokens, and every direction of that split is a fail-open.

A task-anchored key carries the anchor kind as its own length-prefixed component, so a task and a session with the same name address different buckets; a session-anchored key is **byte-for-byte** what it was before, so an operator who does not enable this cannot be affected by it, including mid-rollout against a shared Redis backend. `anchor.go` owns the choice and every key builder routes through `Engine.anchoredKey`.

`maxCalls` follows the same anchor as the states the issue names. It falls out of one rule rather than a per-feature split, and it is the same argument: a per-session quota is a per-*reconnect* quota once a task can re-enter.

### #141 — registry attestation and community review

Corpus entries may carry Ed25519 `signatures` over their content digest, verified locally against an operator-supplied trust store.

- **Role and statement are inside the signed payload**, so a reviewer's signature cannot be re-presented as a vendor's and a `disputes` cannot be edited into an `attests`.
- **An untrusted signature is inert; a trusted one that fails is an error.** A corpus may carry signatures from keys an operator has never heard of, and refusing to load over one would make every entry's usability depend on collecting every publisher's key — those report as `unverified(n)`, a materially different state from unsigned. A signature by a key the operator *did* configure that does not verify means the entry was edited after signing, and that stops the command.
- **A dispute is not an error exit.** It leads the summary, is repeated below the table, and warns on both single-entry commands (`--ref` and `--attest-payload`, the two moments an author commits to an entry) — but someone who looked disagreeing is a community-advisory signal, not a verdict eunox is in a position to issue.
- Signatures sit **outside** the digest (each is over the digest, so including them would be circular and every countersignature would invalidate every manifest pin).
- `eunox contracts --attest-payload <id>` prints the exact bytes a publisher signs. eunox verifies attestations and never mints them — it holds no signing key, for the same reason it consumes IdP tokens and never issues them.
- The trust store is opened with `O_NOFOLLOW` under a size bound, and a contract id may not contain a line break: it is the one free-form field inside the signed payload, and keeping it newline-free makes the payload's field boundaries a property of the format rather than of an argument.
- No shipped entry is signed: the format and the verifier are what was missing; the signatures are the part only publishers and reviewers can supply.

### Shared: a strict decoder for claim-borne grants

Every grant carried on a verified token now decodes through one path that refuses the three JSON shapes which produce something **wider** than the grant reads, none of which a struct decode catches:

- an **unknown member** (`lables` decodes to an empty label set — a grant that covers nothing while looking like it covers something);
- an explicit **null** (`"once": null` decodes to `false`, i.e. a *standing* grant — exactly the replay window `once` exists to close);
- a **duplicate or case-variant key** (`target` beside `Target` is on

🟠 **2ª rejeição do Wagner** — trava a v0.36.0.

> "Ao editar o horário de uma série, a mesma não atualizou."

## Causa
O caminho "editar série" mandava **sempre** `somente_campos=true`. No `graph.rs` (`evento_json`), `somente_campos` **omite start/end/isAllDay/recurrence** (pra não mover o schedule ao editar só assunto/local). Resultado: mudança de **horário** na série nunca aplicava.

## Fix (front, sem Rust)
Ao editar a **série**, detecto se o usuário mexeu no schedule (início/fim/dia-inteiro) comparando a assinatura atual com a **semeada ao abrir o form**:
- **Mexeu no horário** → `somente_campos=false` → PATCH no seriesMaster com `start/end` → o Graph desloca a série inteira.
- **Não mexeu** → `somente_campos=true` → preserva o schedule, altera só os campos (comportamento que o S2 queria).

Reusa o `somente_campos` que já existia — **sem mudança Rust**. Editar ocorrência e criar seguem idênticos.

- `tsc -b` ✅ · `vite build` ✅ · `oxlint` (0 warnings) ✅ · `node --test agenda-slice.test.ts` sem regressão.
- Revalidação (Wagner): editar a série e **mudar o horário** → todas as ocorrências deslocam; editar só o título da série → horário preservado.

author: araq
body:
Two additions to the template-plugin protocol, and typetraits ported onto them. Nothing in std/typetraits is known to the compiler anymore.

A plugin runs in its own process, so it cannot resolve a symbol. Structural types (ptr, array, tuple, ...) already reach it expanded, but a nominal one -- object, enum, distinct, generic instance -- arrives as a bare Symbol and is opaque. It now asks: returning `needTypes(syms)` as the whole output makes the compiler append those declarations to the second input and run the plugin again. Nothing is shipped unrequested, so a plugin that never inspects types pays nothing. Asking again for something already provided is an error, which bounds the exchange; a symbol that turns out to be a type variable is answered with its `(typevar ...)` declaration rather than silence, so a plugin can recognize `T` positively instead of inferring it from absence.

An eager transitive closure was tried first and dropped: for `distinctBase(Wrapped)` over an object holding a `Table[string, seq[Inner]]` it shipped 16 declarations / 3.9 KB, and force-loaded foreign modules, where 2 declarations / 454 B were what the trait needed.

Inside a generic body a plugin still runs once, on the typevar -- correct and cheaper for a symbolic transform like `pointerBase(ptr T)` -> `T`. A plugin that must decide something from the concrete type says so with `deferExpansion()`. The call is then kept as `(at <template> <args>...)` -- nimony's existing unresolved type application, the shape `Foo[T]` already takes in a generic body, so it is validator-legal in a type slot, sameTrees-comparable and substituted by subsGenericProc for free. Instantiation re-checks it and `semInvoke` asks the plugin again with concrete arguments. Deferring is rejected when no argument holds a generic parameter, since nothing would be substituted before the next round.

`semInvoke` has to recognize the plugin head before the head is sem-checked: `InInvokeHead` turns a template symbol into an error node.

Also fixes a crash reachable from the new shape: sigmatch's TypekindT constraint branch called `typeImpl` on an `(at ...)` head, asserting on a non-type declaration.

Ported: distinctBase, distinctBaseShallow (Nim 2's `recursive = false`), genericHead, stripGenericParams. A generic instance's declaration carries `(at <head> <args>...)` in its typevars slot, which is where genericHead comes from -- genericParams is the rest of that same slot.

A deferred type is exactly as capable as a bare type variable: declarable, passable, convertible, returnable, but operations needing to look through it fail in the generic body just as they do for `T` itself.

## What this PR does

Adds first-class Kimi and Xiaomi MiMo presets to `/auth` → **Third-party Providers**. Kimi appears as one provider with **Coding Plan**, **API Key (China)**, and **API Key (International)** access choices; Xiaomi MiMo appears as one provider with pay-as-you-go plus China, Singapore, and Europe Token Plan endpoints.

Carries endpoint-specific model metadata through the CLI, ACP, daemon/SDK, VS Code, Web Shell, and desktop setup flows so each selected endpoint receives the correct default models and environment key. The third-party provider registry is displayed alphabetically, and the `/auth` lists now paginate according to the available terminal height with visible scroll arrows.

## Why it's needed

Kimi and Xiaomi MiMo previously required users to recreate supported endpoints through **Custom Provider**, which was repetitive and made subscription-specific endpoints difficult to discover. Kimi also uses different credentials and model catalogs for Coding Plan versus its regional APIs, so a single flat model list would install invalid choices for some endpoints.

The provider list also became taller than the dialog after these additions. Its previous logical limit was ten items, but every descriptive item consumes multiple terminal rows, so the outer height constraint clipped content without activating list pagination.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

1. Launch the repository CLI and open `/auth` → **Third-party Providers**. Verify the displayed provider labels are alphabetical, DeepSeek remains first, and `▲`/`▼` appear when the list exceeds the available height. Continue pressing Down and verify Kimi and Xiaomi MiMo become visible without clipping the footer.
2. Open **Kimi**. Verify the access choices are **Coding Plan**, **API Key (China)**, and **API Key (International)**. Coding Plan should recommend `k3-256k`, `k3`, `kimi-for-coding`, and `kimi-for-coding-highspeed`; either API option should recommend `kimi-k3`, `kimi-k2.7-code`, `kimi-k2.7-code-highspeed`, and `kimi-k2.6`.
3. Open **Xiaomi MiMo API Key**. Verify the endpoint choices are pay-as-you-go, Token Plan (China), Token Plan (Singapore), and Token Plan (Europe), followed by `mimo-v2.5-pro` and `mimo-v2.5` model recommendations.
4. Cancel each flow before entering real credentials. Optionally repeat endpoint selection through VS Code, Web Shell, or desktop and confirm endpoint-specific default models remain consistent.

Automated validation: 157 core provider tests passed; core build and typecheck passed; 413 focused CLI tests passed; 10 VS Code auth-handler tests passed; SDK and VS Code typechecks passed; changed files passed ESLint and Prettier.

**Before:** Kimi and Xiaomi MiMo were absent from Third-party Providers and required Custom Provider setup. The descriptive provider list could exceed the constrained dialog height while still reporting that all logical items fit, leaving later providers and the footer clipped.

body:
## Summary
`npx expo-doctor` flagged two real problems:
- Missing peer dependency `expo-font` (required by `@expo/vector-icons`), which its own advice warns can crash the app **outside of Expo Go**
- Two different `expo-font` versions being resolved at once: `57.0.1` (top-level) and `14.0.12` (nested under `expo/`)

Two versions of the same native module loaded at once is a well-known cause of an immediate native-level crash on a real device on launch, even when an emulator happens to tolerate it — which matches the reported symptom (app opens then is killed immediately, no error screen, only on a physical Android device).

## Fix
Pinned `expo-font` at the version Expo SDK 54 expects (`~14.0.12`, matching what's nested under `expo/`) and let its config plugin get added. `expo-doctor` now reports 18/18 checks passing (was 16/18).

## Test plan
- [ ] Install the updated dependencies (`npm install`) and rebuild/reload on the physical Android device that was crashing
- [ ] Confirm the app opens normally to the welcome/login screen instead of closing immediately

author: martin-henz
body:
Re-opens #835, which was automatically closed (not merged) when its base branch `conductor-migration` was deleted after being merged into `master` via #680. This branch cherry-picks the original commit from @11suixing11 unchanged, onto current `master`.

## Summary
- validate the rune channel before calling the base plugin constructor
- make rune initialisation idempotent so primitive rune exports are not duplicated
- load the host tab by the shared Rune tab name instead of by the first tab entry
- share rune deserialisation through the bundle protocol and cover serialize/deserialize round trips

Addresses #827

## Motivation
This PR follows #827, which came from checking which CSG conductor-migration review findings also apply to Rune. It is scoped to the four Rune items from that issue and intentionally does not address the separate duplicate-delivery or js-slang error-shape issues tracked in #823 and #825.

## Concrete Cases
- Constructor guard: the old constructor passed `[undefined]` into `BaseModulePlugin` before throwing Rune's own missing-channel error. Moving the guard before `super(...)` keeps invalid channel state out of the base plugin.
- Initialisation idempotency: calling `await plugin.initialise()` twice re-ran `super.initialise()` and re-pushed method and primitive-rune exports. The new guard wraps the full method so repeated initialisation leaves the export list stable.
- Tab lookup: `__loadRuneTab()` previously used `tabs[0]`. Looking up `RUNE_TAB_NAME` keeps the tab contract explicit if the host ever provides more than one tab.
- Protocol round trip: the tab previously had its own local `deserializeRune`. Sharing it from `protocol.ts` lets the bundle test the same serialization/deserialization path used by the tab.

author: ziyu4huang
body:
Closes the **intervention** half of the live-visibility arc (#988 → #993 → #1008). Today the only mid-flight control is whole-turn **Esc**, which kills *every* in-flight child. This adds **per-child abort** from the `/subagents` viewer.

## Fog → reframe (charted in `.planning/2026-08-02-subagents-mid-flight-intervention/`)

The frontier label *"parent-model live visibility"* is **ill-posed** under the synchronous dispatch model — the parent LLM is blocked on `await spawn` for the whole run, so it can neither see nor act mid-flight. Live **visibility** is already shipped (Ctrl-O trace, Running section, always-on widget). The valuable, tractable core is the missing **intervention** lever: the user watching the TUI can see one child failing/looping but can only Esc the whole turn. Per-child abort fixes that.

## What landed (3 TDD tasks)

- **T1 — lever + singular-tool detection.** `SubagentInFlightRegistry.abort(id)` fires a per-child abort lever. The singular `subagent` tool owns a per-child AbortController that **fans in the parent turn signal** (so Esc still works) and is independently triggerable. User-abort is detected **post-hoc** (childAc aborted but parent signal not) → new `aborted` status + "Subagent aborted by user." Whole-turn Esc and timeout paths are **unchanged** (regression-pinned).
- **T2 — batch tool.** Each `subagents` batch child gets the same per-child controller + lever, so aborting one child leaves its siblings running. Side improvement (tested): batch children now also respect whole-turn Esc (previously they ignored the turn signal entirely). `renderBatchResult` gains an `aborted` line + distinct header count — **byte-identical** when no aborts.
- **T3 — viewer UX.** `/subagents` list view: cursor on a Running entry + `x` → "Abort this subagent? y/N" confirm; `y` aborts that one child, `n`/Esc cancels. The confirm sub-state gates nav/enter/printable. Aborted runs surface in **Completed** with the ⊘ glyph (additive — reconstruct already carries the status).

## Verification

- `pi-agent-ext-subagent`: **400 pass / 0 fail** (12 new tests across 4 files).
- `tsc --noEmit` clean (incl. `pi-agent-ext-workflow`, the type consumer).
- `biome check` clean (0 errors; the 9 warnings are pre-existing on main).
- No new tool params / promptSnippet / schema → schema-cost canary unaffected.

## Decisions (grilled + confirmed)

- **D0** per-child user abort (Reframe A) — rejected non-blocking dispatch (Reframe C, engine-level, separate arc).
- **D1** `/subagents` list + `x` key.
- **D2** new `aborted` status, surfaced in Completed.
- **D3** y/N confirm before abort.

Spec/plan/map in `.planning/2026-08-02-subagents-mid-flight-intervention/`.

author: noron12234
body:
## What

`_create_cdp_connection_browser` is `async def`, but waits for the spawned browser with a synchronous sleep:

```python
browser_process = subprocess.Popen([...], stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.PIPE)
# Add small delay to allow browser to start
time.sleep(1)
if browser_process.poll() is not None:
    raise Exception(f"Failed to open browser. browser_path: {browser_path}")
```

A blocking sleep inside a coroutine stalls the **entire event loop**, not just this call. For that second nothing else on the loop runs — every other task in the process is frozen, however unrelated.

`await asyncio.sleep(1)` waits the same wall-clock second while letting the loop keep working. `asyncio` is already imported in this file (line 3).

## Change

```diff
  # Add small delay to allow browser to start
- time.sleep(1)
+ await asyncio.sleep(1)
```

This was the only `time` usage in the file, so its import goes with it — that is the second line of the diff and the reason it is two lines rather than one.

No behaviour change beyond the loop staying responsive: the same delay, the same `poll()` check after it.

## Verification

```console
$ ruff check skyvern/webeye/browser_factory.py        # ruff 0.14.1, pinned in .pre-commit-config.yaml
All checks passed!
$ ruff format --check skyvern/webeye/browser_factory.py
1 file already formatted
$ python -m py_compile skyvern/webeye/browser_factory.py
```

Found with an AST scan for blocking calls (`time.sleep`, `requests.*`, `subprocess.run`, `urlopen`) inside `async def` bodies, excluding anything passed to `run_in_executor` / `to_thread` and anything in a nested sync `def`. This was the only hit in the repo.

author: umputun
body:
⌃A then C over a session lists what the Claude Code run inside it was working on, newest first, in a floating overlay. Each item is a relative age, a short title, a one-sentence detail and a status of done, in progress, blocked or abandoned.

**What ships**

`claude-recap.zsh` resolves the session's directory through `agtermctl tree --json`, finds that session's transcript, condenses it with `jq`, and asks a second Claude Code invocation on haiku for the list, pinned to a json schema.

`pane-map-statusline.sh` is the other half. Claude Code files transcripts under a slug of the working directory, which names the wrong run twice: two panes of a split in one repository share a cwd, and a run that moves into a git worktree is filed under the worktree while the pane's shell stays put. The status line receives the live `transcript_path` and runs as a child of the pane's shell, so it can record which transcript belongs to which pane. Claude Code takes exactly one `statusLine` command, so the README gives both the block to paste into an existing status line and this minimal one for readers who have none.

**Worth knowing**

Two flags decide whether the summary is usable. `MAX_THINKING_TOKENS=0` keeps the model from spending thousands of thinking tokens on six one-line items, which is the difference between seconds and a minute and a half. `--safe-mode` drops CLAUDE.md, rules, skills, plugins, hooks and MCP, leaving a few hundred tokens of harness context instead of tens of thousands.

The list is sorted by parsing the age strings back into seconds rather than trusting the model's "newest first", which it ignores often enough that the ordering has to be mechanical.

**Limits, stated in the README**

Read-only, but each press sends up to 120 KB of transcript to the model. Without the pane map the recap can name the wrong run, and the map itself misses a `claude` started under tmux, which inherits the `AGTERM_*` of whichever session started that server.

Requirements are agterm 0.10.0 or later, for `{AGT_PANE}` and `overlay open --background-color`, plus zsh, jq and the Claude Code CLI.

author: jasperblues
body:
Updates the normative OAuth2 section for pack authors. The host's `admin/oauth-apps.yml` and the per-workspace `config/oauth-apps.yml` override are both retired — credentials now live in an org-scoped WorkOS Vault (encrypted host-side before the vault sees them) and in each user's wallet.

**Lookup order is now:**

1. the user's own **wallet** (per-user override)
2. the deployment's **org vault** (the default everyone gets)
3. `${VAR}` from the pack's `oauth2` block (power-user escape hatch)

The per-workspace file tier is **removed rather than renamed**. The wallet replaces it and is strictly better for the same use case: encrypted, self-service, and needing no filesystem access.

Two properties pack authors can now rely on are stated explicitly:

- **Nothing is read from the filesystem**, so a pack must never instruct an operator to write credentials to a file.
- **A user can override the org's client app with their own**, which matters for any pack doc explaining how to test against a personal provider project.

Docs only — no schema or runtime change. `apis.yml` entries are unaffected.

### Motivation

- Reduce total health-check latency by running independent SSH probes in parallel and provide interactive callers visibility into which checks are still pending.  
- Ensure the bootstrap script installs the same CLI revision used by the launcher and verify the installed package matches the expected version.

### Description

- Added a concurrent `_remote_group` helper using `ThreadPoolExecutor` to run SSH probes in parallel while preserving probe order and bounded worker count.  
- Reworked `remote_health` to consolidate probes into a single list, execute them via `_remote_group`, and map results back into `HealthReport` categories.  
- Extended `wait_until_healthy` to accept an optional `on_pending` callback argument and invoke it with the current `HealthReport` when a polling pass finds pending checks.  
- Updated the launch flow to provide a `report_pending` callback that logs which checks are pending and passed it into `wait_until_healthy`.  
- Templating: `userdata.render` now injects `Config().version` into the embedded bootstrap script via the `__LCW_VERSION__` placeholder, and the packaged `bootstrap.sh` was adjusted to install the CLI from the `main` branch and assert the installed `workstation version` matches the expected value.
- Tests updated to cover the new behavior, including `wait_until_healthy` pending callbacks, bounded parallel worker usage for `_remote_group`, and bootstrap/userdata rendering of the version and install source.

### Testing

- Unit tests were run (`tests/test_core.py`) exercising `render()`, `wait_until_healthy()` with `on_pending`, and `_remote_group()` behavior and they passed.

author: asadbekme
body:
This pull request addresses the caching issue encountered on the Kanban board when dragging and dropping tasks. 

### Changes made:
- Updated the API calls in `lib/api.ts` to prevent cached responses:
  - **fetchTasks**: Added `Cache-Control`, `Pragma`, and `Expires` headers, along with a timestamp query parameter (`t`) to ensure fresh responses.
  - **saveTasks**: Moved `apiKey` to axios parameters and included a timestamp parameter and no-cache headers for the PUT request.

### Reason for changes:
The previous implementation was returning a cached 200 response for the GET request immediately after a PUT, causing the task to not appear in the new column. By adding explicit no-cache headers and a cache-busting timestamp, we ensure that the GET and PUT requests are treated as fresh, allowing the dropped task to display correctly.

author: uncletomscabi
body:
## Summary

Add support for embeddable question types inside table question columns.

Instead of knowing about specific plugins, the table question now delegates rendering to any question type implementing the new embeddable interface.

## What is implemented

- support for embeddable question types;
- dynamic column configuration loading;
- embedded administration rendering;
- embedded end-user rendering;
- server-side rendering for dynamically added table rows;
- validation and preparation of embedded question extra data.

## Why server-side row rendering?

Originally, additional table rows were created entirely in JavaScript.

This approach worked for built-in question types because their client-side configuration was sufficient to recreate the controls.

With embeddable question types, this is no longer enough. Embedded question types are responsible for rendering and initializing their own controls, which may include server-generated markup, unique identifiers and initialization logic.

To keep this responsibility inside each question type and avoid duplicating rendering logic in JavaScript, newly added rows are now rendered on demand by the server through a dedicated controller. The controller simply exposes the existing row rendering logic already used for the initial table rendering, ensuring that dynamically added rows behave exactly like the initially rendered ones.

## Motivation

The table question previously only supported built-in question types.

With this change, any question type implementing the embeddable interface can be used inside a table without introducing plugin-specific rendering logic into Advanced Forms.

## Backward compatibility

Existing built-in question types continue to work exactly as before.

Plugins that do not implement the embeddable interface are unaffected.

## Related

Depends on:

- GLPI Core PR: https://github.com/glpi-project/glpi/pull/25065

Example implementation:

- Fields PR: https://github.com/pluginsGLPI/fields/pull/1235

author: wenyikuo
body:
## ⚠️ Blocked by the backend PR — do not merge first

This documents and relays an endpoint Core must serve first, and publishes `entryYear` as required on the strength of a Core `@NotNull` that ships in that PR. Merge order: **backend → bff → frontend**.

## Summary

**The substantive change here is a header-fidelity bug fix, not a schema tweak.** Please do not read it as one line of zod.

Core computes `Cache-Control: public, max-age=<n>` for the enrolment-year rules, where `n` counts down to the next 1 January UTC (capped at 24 hours), precisely so a cached copy expires when the year window it describes stops being true. The bff was destroying that: the proxy's response leg copied only `content-type` and dropped every other header, and a separate hard-coded set imposed a flat `public, max-age=300` that explicitly overrode anything upstream. Either way the computed age never reached the browser, so a client could validate against last year's window for up to a year.

This was invisible to any test looking at one side of the proxy — Core set the header correctly, the browser simply never saw it.

The fix adds a deliberately separate pass-through set: `CACHEABLE_STATIC_META` is the set the proxy *owns* a policy for, and `UPSTREAM_CACHE_CONTROL_PATHS` is the set it must have no opinion about. `/meta/tour-topics` and `/meta/tour-features` keep their proxy-owned flat 300; every other path still receives no `Cache-Control` at all.

Alongside that, three contract corrections: `entryYear` becomes required on the guide-onboarding request schema; `GET /v1/meta/enrollment-years` is registered in the bff's OpenAPI document (the first `/v1/meta/*` path documented here) with its `Cache-Control` header described on the 200; and the guide profile's per-school `entryYear` stops advertising itself as nullable, since Core now stores it `NOT NULL`.

## Related issue

Relates to CTL-97. Blocked by the backend CTL-97 PR.

## Type of change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)

The `Cache-Control` relay is the fix. The schema changes are contract corrections that align this repo's published document with what Core already enforces; no bff runtime behaviour changes with them.

## What is deliberately NOT here

- **No range validation.** The bff has never validated `classYear`'s range and must not start. Core owns the rules; a third copy is a third thing to keep in sync. A reviewer seeing "no validation added" should read that as intentional.
- **No runtime request-body validation.** This repo's zod request schemas are documentation-only — the route chain is `csrfGuard → withMutation(handler)` and the handler forwards `req.body` to Core untouched. So making `entryYear` required changes the published contract and nothing else: a body missing it is still forwarded, Core returns 422, and that problem+json is relayed verbatim. Introducing a guard for one field would leave two conventions with nothing covering the rest.
- **No real rule numbers in the OpenAPI example.** The example is deliberately synthetic (`1900`–`2100`, `example-degree-keyword`, uniform `1`s). Nothing in this repo can pin a copy of Core's numbers, so a realistic-looking example would rot silently and invite a frontend developer to hardcode a fallback against it.

## Testing

`npm run lint && npm run typecheck && npm test && npm run openapi:lint` — **48 suites, 618 tests, 100% coverage** on statements, branches, functions and lines; Spectral reports no errors.

The proxy change ships with six tests, and four of them guard things that must NOT change: `tour-topics` still gets the proxy-owned 300, an ordinary meta path still gets no header at all, the rules endpoint still serves anonymously with no session cookie, and — the fail-closed one — when Core sends no `Cache-Control` the bff invents none. That last guard exists specifically to catch a future `?? "public, max-age=300"`, which would read as a harmless default while quietly restoring the bug this PR removes.

The OpenAPI contract test asserts the nested shape, not merely that a path was registered: a `data` object with the right three keys and wrong innards is exactly the drift it exists to catch.

Also verified live end-to-end after a database rebuild — `Cache-Control: public, max-age=86400` arrives unchanged at backend `:8080`, bff `:4000` and frontend `:3001`.

## Screenshots

**Before:**

```
$ curl -i localhost:4000/v1/meta/enrollment-years
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Content-Type: application/json
        ← no Cache-Control; Core's computed max-age dropped by the proxy
```

**After:**

```
$ curl -i localhost:4000/v1/meta/enrollment-years
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Cache-Control: public, max-age=86400
Content-Type: application/json
```

## Checklist

- [x] Tests added or updated (or explained why not)
- [x] No secrets, tokens, or `.env` files committed
- [x] `.env.example` and API contract updated if config or request/response changed — no config change; the API contract (`src/openapi/`) is updated
- [x] If a BFF endpoint changed, `src/openapi/` (schemas + examples via the `apiRoute` DSL) was updated and `npm run openapi:lint` passes (see `docs/openapi-conventions.md`) — `/v1/meta/enrollment-years` is a proxied path, registered via `apiRoute` with `protected: false`
- [x] Docs / README updated if needed

## Downstream

The frontend PR is blocked by this one. Frontend must read the rule numbers from `GET /v1/meta/enrollment-years` rather than hardcoding them, must apply the degree match exactly as documented (trim, lowercase, plain substring `includes`, **array order as received** — do not sort or re-key), and must respect the served `max-age` rather than caching the body indefinitely.

Size override: accumulated CTL-97 branch — several coordinated changes (deferred provisioning, the `provisioningStatus` session rename, enrolment years) share one API contract with backend and frontend, and the three repos must merge in a fixed order. Splitting now would mean re-sequencing merges across all three and shipping intermediate states where the contract is half-applied.

author: fajarhide
body:
#241 removed skeleton grouping from `CollapseMode::Generic` and left the other
four falling through to `normalize_structural`, which rewrites every digit run to
`#`. That is most real commands: `cat`, `grep`, `rg`, `tail`, `head`, `curl` and
any command string containing `.log` resolve to `Log`, and `docker`, `kubectl`,
`helm`, `terraform`, `aws`, `gcloud` and `az` resolve to `Infra`.

Reported by @keefar against 0.6.8 and reproduced. Nine Portainer stack paths
differing only in an ordinal came back as

```
[9 similar lines collapsed] (pattern: "/var/lib/docker/volumes/portainer_data/_data/compose/#/v#")
```

with forty container rows as one more marker, and a footer claiming 93%
compression over 49 rows of data. A count that identifies nothing leaves
re-running with distillation bypassed as the only recovery, which is the
token-negative outcome collapse exists to avoid.

The four modes group on the whole line now. Their named special cases still fold
what they were written for, because each names a shape where something
established the varying token is noise: a crate version after `Compiling`, a test
name before `... ok`, a layer hash after `--->`, a severity prefix on a log line.
Anything they miss established nothing, which is the argument #241 already made.
Identical lines are still repetition and still collapse.

`normalize_structural`, its 2,048-entry LRU cache and `is_git_hash_line` have no
callers left, so they are deleted rather than kept warm for a rule the project
has now decided against twice. Net 99 lines removed against 57 added.

## Verification

Toolchain 1.97.0, the pinned one, `OMNI_DB_PATH` isolated.

The regression test covers all five modes, and the first version of it did not
work: 9 rows sits under `MIN_LINES_FOR_COLLAPSE = 10`, so `collapse` returned
early and the test passed against the unfixed code. At 14 rows it has teeth:

```
break (skeleton restored in Log mode)  keeps_rows_that_differ_only_in_a_number  rc=101
```

Fixed:

```
18 suites, 1,278 passed, 0 failed
cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings   rc=0
```

`still_collapses_identical_lines` is the counter-case, so this is not "never
collapse": 30 identical `npm WARN` lines still fold.

## Not in this change

@keefar's note that `omni exec` reported 0.0% on an equivalent payload while the
post-hook collapsed it. The two take different routes, so that is route selection
rather than collapse, and it needs its own measurement.

Closes #267

author: pzaisystems
body:
PZA-291 (reopened PZA-285): handleOpenThread stored the clicked message's own id as openThreadHeadId, but get_thread_replies filters thread_metadata WHERE root_event_id = $2 -- an exact match against the true root, not the clicked event. The main channel window shows root messages plus broadcast replies, so a broadcast reply can be a genuinely nested (2+ hop) message; clicking one queried by the wrong id and returned zero rows, rendering the thread panel blank.

Fix: open threadHeadId = message.rootId ?? message.id (TimelineMessage already computes rootId via getThreadReference). threadReplyTargetId still targets the exact clicked message.

Verified against live production Postgres: published a real root -> replyA -> replyB (2-hop nested) via buzz-publish.mjs, then ran get_thread_replies''s exact SQL filter directly. Querying by replyB's own id returns 0 rows (the bug, reproduced); querying by the resolved root id returns both replies (the fix).

body:
## Summary

The repo had no tests and no test tooling, so every module sat at 0% coverage. This adds PHPUnit (PHP) and Jest + jsdom (JS) with tests targeting the modules that carry the actual logic: `includes/functions.php`, `includes/auth.php`, the `includes/*.php` templates, and `assets/js/app.js`.

Coverage after this PR (`composer test:coverage`, `npm run test:coverage`):

| file | lines |
| --- | --- |
| `assets/js/app.js` | 100% (96% branch) |
| `includes/functions.php` | 33/35 |
| `includes/header.php` | 32/32 |
| `includes/footer.php` | 9/9 |
| `includes/auth.php` | 2/8 |
| `config/db.php` | 0/19 |

100 tests total (47 PHPUnit, 53 Jest).

Two things worth knowing before reading the diff:

1. `app.js` is a classic script with no exports, so nothing was reachable from a test. It gains a browser-inert CJS shim at the bottom — no other source change:

```js
if (typeof module !== 'undefined' && module.exports) {
  module.exports = { money, toast, cardData, addToCart, updateQuantity, renderCart,
                     saveCart, openProductModal, filterProducts, initTheme,
                     getCart: () => cart, getWishlist: () => wishlist };
}
```

`tests/js/helpers/loadApp.js` re-`require`s the module per test with `jest.resetModules()`, seeding `localStorage` and the DOM first (the module reads both at load time) and unregistering the `document` listeners left behind by the previous load.

2. `redirect()` is `: never` — it calls `header()` then `exit`, so `require_login()` / `require_admin()` cannot be asserted in-process. `PhpScriptRunner` runs those snippets in a child process: the CLI binary for "execution stopped + flash message set", and `php-cgi` (skipped if absent) for asserting the actual `Location:` header. This is why `auth.php`'s line coverage stays low despite the behaviour being covered — child-process lines aren't attributed by pcov. `config/db.php` is likewise 0% because it executes at test-file include time, before per-test coverage starts; its MySQL-unavailable fallback (`$pdo = null` + `$dbError`) is asserted in a child process too.

The template tests render `header.php` / `footer.php` through `ob_start()` + `include`, covering guest/customer/admin nav variants, `basePath` prefixing, HTML escaping, session cart count, and flash consumption.

author: hyuntohoon
body:
FEAT-album-review-authoring **Step 2** — the harvest side of the Step 1 mark. Step 1 shipped placing and clearing `review_candidate`; this is the read that gathers the marks into a list.

Merge **after** the workspace contract PR (hyuntohoon/myblog-workspace#775) so the notify-contract dispatch is a no-op.

## The change

`GET /api/me/review-candidates` → the caller's marked albums, most recently touched first, each joined to its album identity.

**Why a new read instead of a client-side filter over `/api/me/album-states`:**

1. `review_candidate IS TRUE` is the whole definition of this list. In the query it cannot be forgotten; in the caller it can.
2. A mark can sit on an album that is **in no bucket and carries no rating**, so the row has no other source of a title — hence the album join and the batched primary-artist resolve. `album-states` needs neither; its callers key by `album_id` alone.

**Why not extend `MyAlbumStateResponse`:** it is also the PUT write response. Album fields nobody reads would land on the write path, and `upsert` would have to start returning the album as well. A read with a different purpose is cleaner as its own shape, and this way the diff is purely additive.

`rating`/`comment` ride along so the queue can distinguish "marked, not heard yet" from "heard and rated, still to write" without a second read.

## Privacy

Same class as the mark itself (RFC C6 — a mark others can see becomes a promise, and a promise can't be made lightly):

- JWT-only, scoped to the caller's own member id. **There is no handle parameter** — no way to ask for someone else's.
- Verified from the browser on the frontend side: a visitor viewing someone's profile requests only `/api/me`, `/api/members/{handle}` and `.../now-playing`. This endpoint is never called.

## Infra

**None.** An authed GET rides the edge_guard catch-all (`GET /api/{proxy+}`) with the JWT verified here at the Lambda — same as `GET /api/me` and `GET /api/me/album-states`. No API Gateway route, no `terraform apply`. (The workspace PR adds a comment in `apigateway.tf` recording that this is deliberate.)

## Tests

Route level (`tests/api/test_album_states.py`) — scoping, row shape, an already-rated candidate keeping its rating, an empty queue being an empty list, and the auth guard. The guard test **lifts the suite-wide `ENV=local` bypass**, which would otherwise happily return 200 and hide a missing dependency; it also sets a pool id so the answer is a plain 401 rather than the (correct) fail-closed 503.

Real engine (`tests/integration/test_rating_service_db.py`) — four regressions for the two WHERE-clause failure modes this read can have: listing an unmarked state, or listing someone else's. Plus clearing a mark dropping it from the queue **without** touching the 평가 it sat on, and an unrated mark still arriving with its album (the inner join).

```
647 passed, 98 skipped in 2.76s
```

⚠️ The 4 new real-engine tests are `TEST_DB_URL`-gated (`SKIPPED: TEST_DB_URL not set (Neon test branch)`) so they **skip locally and run here in CI** — the skip count, not the pass count, is the thing to read on this repo.

`openapi.json` regenerated (`make export-openapi`): +120 / -0, no version drift.

author: dominikwozniak
body:
`git worktree add` checks out tracked state only, so everything else in a working tree is missing in
a fresh worktree — and every gap fails silently rather than loudly. Claude Code's `.worktreeinclude`
covers one third of the problem, and only for the worktrees it creates itself (`--worktree`,
subagent worktrees, desktop); `worktree.sh create` uses plain `git worktree add` and got nothing.

Found while dogfooding: a `/dw-start` worktree had no local config, no `CLAUDE.local.md` — so the
agent fell back to generic git conventions — and no `.husky/_/`, which meant **git found no hooks at
all and every commit there silently skipped prettier, agnix and the manifest version check**. That
last one produces bad commits instead of errors, which is why the change grew past its original
scope.

## What changed

Untracked files now get one of four treatments, chosen by what the file *is*
([`0003`](docs/decisions/0003-worktree-carry-classes.md)):

| class | example | treatment |
| --- | --- | --- |
| local config / secrets | `.env`, `config/secrets.json` | **copy**, via `.worktreeinclude` |
| personal agent memory | `CLAUDE.local.md` | **symlink** — one source of truth |
| installed deps, generated tooling | `node_modules/`, `.husky/_/` | **regenerate** — reported, never carried |
| build cache, scratch | `.next/`, caches | **leave absent** |

- `worktree.sh create` copies the `.worktreeinclude` matches, applying the documented rule exactly:
  a file is copied only when it matches a pattern **and** is gitignored. Matching is delegated to
  git — the intersection of two `ls-files` runs — so it cannot drift from what `claude -w` does.
- Hard refusals for `node_modules/`, `.claude/worktrees/` and `.git`, independent of what the
  include file says. A bare `*` matches 421 files in this repo, 394 of them dependencies, and
  copying the worktrees directory would nest worktrees inside a worktree.
- `CLAUDE.local.md` is symlinked at create time rather than left to the `SessionStart` hook, which
  never fires for a session that enters a worktree mid-flight.
- A readiness report on stderr names what still has to be installed, and says plainly when commit
  hooks are inactive.
- `dw-init` ships a `.worktreeinclude` template, every line commented out.
- `dw-start` makes the install a required step rather than an offer, and says why.

`stdout` still carries the path and nothing else — `dw-start` parses it, and a test pins it.

## Verification

- `scripts/tests/worktree.test.sh`: 32 cases, green under the bash 3.2 macOS ships.
- Full gate green: `lint`, `format`, `validate:manifests`, `validate:artifacts`, `validate:docs`.
- End-to-end on this repo: 1 file copied, 394 refused, `CLAUDE.local.md` linked, report naming
  `pnpm install` and `COMMIT HOOKS ARE INACTIVE`.

## Follow-ups parked in `.ai/BACKLOG.md`

Four, the first of which is vendored from `dw-skills` and has to be fixed in both repos:
`block-env-access.sh` inspects commit messages, so writing about a dotenv file blocks the commit.

author: ankit373
body:
Phase 23 cleanup. Three things existed in triplicate, four were dead.

## #167 — deduplication

### 1. The admin gate

`requireAdmin` (admin.go) was re-implemented inline in `capabilities` (server.go) and `quality`
(quality.go). Both now call the helper — one authorization decision, one place.

No behaviour change: the inline copies used `writeError(w, http.StatusForbidden, …)`, which
`statusToCode` classifies to `codeForbidden` — exactly what `requireAdmin` already emits. Same
status, same `{type, code}`, same message.

`TestManagementRoutesRequireAdminRole` (from #178) **passes unchanged** — it was not touched,
weakened, or rewritten. All ten subtests (eight `/admin/*` routes plus `/capabilities` and
`/v1/quality`) still assert 403 for an `inference` tenant and not-403 for an `admin` tenant.

### 2. `esc()` — and the double-escaping bug behind it

Three copies in two flavours (`internal/metrics`, `internal/breaker`, `internal/server/gate.go`).
Two of them (metrics, gate) were called *inside* `%q`, so a model id containing `"` or `\` emitted
a double-escaped, corrupt label. Demonstrated before the fix:

```
mainspring_requests_total{model="we\\\"ird\\\\model",status="200"} 1     # was
mainspring_requests_total{model="we\"ird\\model",status="200"} 1         # now
```

A scraper read the old label back as `we\"ird\\model` — not the model id.

**Decision: keep one shared escaper (`util.PromLabelValue`), drop `%q` at every call site.**
Deleting all three and relying on `%q` alone was the tempting fix, and I checked it against the
exposition format before rejecting it. `%q` is Go string-literal quoting, not Prometheus label
quoting; the two coincide only for `\`, `"` and newline. Verified against Go's actual output:

| input | `%q` emits | Prometheus |
|---|---|---|
| `a"b` | `"a\"b"` | valid |
| `a\b` | `"a\\b"` | valid |
| `a` + LF + `b` | `"a\nb"` | valid |
| `a` + TAB + `b` | `"a\tb"` | **invalid escape** |
| `a` + CR + `b` | `"a\rb"` | **invalid escape** |
| `a\xffb` (invalid UTF-8) | `"a\xffb"` | **invalid escape** |

The text exposition format defines exactly three escapes (`\\`, `\"`, `\n`) and the reference
parser errors on anything else — which fails the *whole scrape*, not one sample. So a named
helper that emits only those three, used as `{model="` + `PromLabelValue(id)` + `"}`, with the
reasoning written down next to it.

New tests, one per emitter, with a model id containing both a quote and a backslash:
- `metrics.TestPrometheusEscapesLabelValueOnce` — **fails on develop** (double-escaped)
- `server.TestGatePrometheusEscapesLabelValueOnce` — **fails on develop** (double-escaped)
- `breaker.TestWritePrometheusEscapesLabelValueOnce` — passes on develop (breaker never used `%q`;
  this is a regression guard so the correct copy stays correct)
- `util.TestPromLabelValueEscapesExactlyTheThreeSpecialChars` — pins tab/UTF-8 pass-through

### 3. One error-body writer

`internal/auth` hand-rolled its 401 and 429 JSON literals, duplicating the server's taxonomy. The
taxonomy moves to a new `internal/apierr` — it has to sit *below* both, because the auth middleware
rejects requests before any handler runs, and `auth` cannot import `server`.

`internal/server/errors.go` keeps the short in-package spelling with a type alias and const aliases
(`type errorCode = apierr.Code`, `codeForbidden = apierr.Forbidden`, …), so the ~60 call sites in
that package are untouched. Aliases are names, not a second copy. The three places that read
`codeMeta` directly (`recordRejected`, `sseError`, `streamError`) now use `apierr.Meta` /
`apierr.Body`.

Wire shape is unchanged: auth's 401/429 already matched the taxonomy by hand, and the new
`auth.TestMiddlewareErrorsUseSharedTaxonomy` pins that (it passes on develop too — it exists so the
two cannot drift again). Taxonomy tests moved from `server/errors_test.go` to
`apierr/apierr_test.go` and gained a `Meta` fallback case, a 405 mapping case, and a check that
`Body` and `Write` agree; the server keeps the two shim-level assertions.

## #168 — dead code

Each verified uncalled with `grep -rn` across non-test Go before deleting:

| Item | What I found |
|---|---|
| `config.Save` | Zero callers anywhere — non-test *and* test. Deleted. The package doc still said "loads and saves"; corrected. |
| `Recorder.TTFTp50` | Zero non-test callers. Its comment claimed it was "kept for existing callers" — those callers do not exist; `/v1/quality` uses `LatencyPercentiles(model).TTFTP50`. Deleted, along with the back-compat assertion in `TestRecordAndPrometheus`; `TestTTFTp50` is rewritten as `TestLatencyPercentilesTTFT` so the no-samples-⇒-0 case stays covered. |
| `contextOverage` | Confirmed dead: the only non-test caller (`admit.go`) calls `contextOverageDetail`. Deleted the wrapper; the tests are repointed at `contextOverageDetail` through a small local `estimated()` helper that mirrors what `admit` passes. |
| `adminConfig`'s `r.Method` check | Confirmed: route is `GET /admin/config`, and net/http serves HEAD for a GET pattern, so the branch fired only for HEAD — where 405 is the wrong answer. `adminUsage` had no such check. Deleted; the mux is now the only method gate for both. |

**New coverage the issue asked for:** `contextOverageDetail`'s `exact=true` reason branch had *no*
test at all. `TestContextOverageExactPromptCountIsLabelledExact` now covers it — asserts the exact
wording (`prompt (4000 tokens)`), asserts it is *not* hedged with "estimated"/"~", and asserts the
same numbers with `exact=false` produce the hedged form, so the two stay distinguishable on the
wire. `TestContextWithinLimit` also gains an exact-count-that-fits case.

## Behaviour changes

Two, both intended, both tested:

1. **`HEAD /admin/config` now returns 200 instead of 405** — the #168 fix.
   `TestAdminEndpointsLeaveMethodGatingToTheMux` **fails on develop** (`HEAD /admin/config = 405,
   want 200`). It also asserts `POST` to both endpoints is still 405, now from the mux.
2. **Prometheus labels for a model id containing `"` or `\`** are no longer double-escaped.
   Ordinary model ids produce byte-identical output.

Nothing else changes on the wire.

## Docs

No change needed. `docs/llms.txt` documents `GET /admin/config` and never mentioned HEAD or 405 for
it; the "all errors are OpenAI-shaped `{message, type, code}`" claim was already true (auth matched
the shape by hand) and is now true by construction; label escaping is not documented anywhere.

## Verification

```
go build ./...   OK
go vet ./...     OK
go test -race ./...   all 18 packages ok, 0 failures
```

`gofmt -l` reports only `internal/install/install.go`, which already fails on `develop` and is not
touched here.

Closes #167
Closes #168

author: azmartone67
body:
Adversarial audit of the shell's own lanes. Three defects — all the exact class the shell exists to catch, all shipped inside it.

## Lane 4 — harmful red (worst)

It compared public surfaces against `canonical_stats["facilities"]`, chosen from a candidate list **headed by `facilities_tracked`**. `/api/v1/stats/canonical` says outright:

> `facilities_distinct` = COUNT(DISTINCT canonical_slug) — distinct **BUILDINGS, and the field to cite**. `facilities_records` = `facilities_tracked` = COUNT(*) — raw source records, ~1.5x the buildings

So the lane demanded your surfaces quote the **~23.7k raw discovery pile**. Acting on that red would have published a false facility count everywhere — the precise over-claim `canonical_stats` exists to prevent.

Now: reads only `facilities_distinct` / `facilities_verified`, names the raw keys as forbidden, and renders `?` rather than compare against one. Since public figures are floors that **round DOWN**, over-claim and staleness are scored separately — a surface *above* canon fails hard, one >500 behind is flagged stale.

## Lane 7 — self-count + dead branch + overclaim

The file contains its own grep needle, so **it always matched itself**. One of the reported "15 independent implementations" was the needle literal (L542) and the `"no site found"` string (L549). The shell holds zero agent-count SQL.

Because it always self-matched, the no-hits branch was **unreachable** — an `os.listdir` failure rendered the confident *"no COUNT(DISTINCT agent_id) site found"*, asserting a fact about the repo from an IO error.

And a grep hit is not a distinct counter: some hits were a `COUNT(...) FILTER` variant, while the fixed string missed `SELECT DISTINCT agent_id` and everything outside `routes/` — including `flask_mcp_endpoints.py`, which produces one of the two numbers the detail string blames.

Now a case-insensitive regex over the repo, self excluded, reported as **candidates** and explicitly not scored as proof of drift. The measured drift (portal 62 vs reach 99, same day) is named as the real evidence.

## Lane 3 — red by construction

It compared a shared-DB open-findings count against **this process's** in-memory `dchub_self_heal` caches. A web dyno never runs the scans, so `merged == 0` forever — the lane could never go green no matter what anyone fixed. A permanently-red lane is noise.

Now structural: *does the triage handler read `brain_findings` at all?* That is fixable, so the lane is greenable — and it still correctly fails today, because triage reads only the per-process caches.

## Verification

22 pins pass. Three must-fail controls verified — reverting lane 4 to the raw key, restoring lane 7's self-count, and restoring lane 3's count-comparison each fail their pin. The obsolete lane-7 needle-case pin was replaced with one asserting the regex is case-insensitive and matches the real spellings.

author: kevinlourd
body:
Primeforge exposes no billing surface — `/subscriptions`, `/billing`, `/invoices`, `/plans`, `/prices`, `/orders`, `/usage` all 404 — so its **10 domains and 35 mailboxes** were the largest hole in `/internal/infra/spend`.

The rate now comes from the vendor's published page, and the page itself is **mirrored into bronze** (`provider_account_raw`, scope `pricing-page`) alongside the rate rows. That is the point of the migration: a rate card typed straight into a seed is unauditable the moment the vendor changes it, whereas a bronze row lets any figure on screen be traced to the page and the date it was read.

Published terms (primeforge.ai/pricing, read 2026-08-02):

| Unit | Rate | Note |
|---|---|---|
| domain | $14/year | .com; the page states explicitly there is **no** annual discount on domains |
| mailbox | $4.50/month per **slot** | minimum 10 slots, billed monthly |
| mailbox | $3.75/month per slot | effective rate on annual billing (2 months free) — **captured in bronze, not seeded** |

Two calls worth stating:

- **Seeds the monthly list rate, not the discounted annual one.** Nothing we can reach says which billing period the subscription uses. Overstating a cost is the safe direction; understating it flatters every cost-per-email derived from it. If it turns out to be annual, that is a new row with a new `effective_from` — the table is non-retroactive by design, so no row is ever edited.
- **The unit is a slot, not a live mailbox.** Primeforge bills capacity: a deleted mailbox keeps costing until the slot is released.

After this, the only unpriced domains left are the 2 Gandi ones whose renewal quote failed, which are kept null on purpose rather than guessed.

Refs #555

author: kyure-a
body:
## Summary

- Move the global and project-local synchronization logic out of `lib/default.nix` into a shared, static `scripts/sync.sh` runtime.
- Add `mkSyncProgram` and `mkLocalInstallProgram`, with a versioned JSON configuration boundary between Nix and the runtime.
- Keep `mkSyncScript` and `mkLocalInstallScript` as compatibility wrappers so existing consumer flakes retain their current call patterns and return types.
- Route the root flake apps, Home Manager activation, `mkShellHook`, and examples through the shared runtime.
- Add destination ownership markers, path-containment checks, preflight validation, safe limited global path expansion, and literal handling of shell metacharacters.
- Add integration coverage, consumer API compatibility coverage, and a ShellCheck flake check.

## Why

The synchronization behavior was duplicated as large inline shell fragments inside `lib/default.nix`. That made the Nix file difficult to review, allowed the local and global implementations to drift, and mixed destination data with generated shell source.

A single runtime with a JSON boundary makes the synchronization contract explicit and testable while reducing `lib/default.nix` from roughly 790 lines to 615 lines.

## User impact

Existing Home Manager configuration, flake app names, package names, and direct helper call patterns remain valid.

Tree destinations are now marked with `.agent-skills-managed.json`. An existing non-empty destination created by an older release has no marker, so users should inspect it and use `AGENT_SKILLS_FORCE=1` once to adopt it.

Runtime expansion is intentionally limited to `$HOME`, `~`, and `${VAR:-$HOME/...}` forms; destination strings are no longer evaluated as general shell code.

## Validation

- `nix flake check "path:$PWD" --print-build-logs`
- sync integration coverage for copy/link/symlink trees, markers, force takeover, read-only resync, exclusions, traversal, symlinks, overrides, metacharacters, and multi-target preflight
- consumer API compatibility build/run test
- ShellCheck
- `bash -n scripts/sync.sh`
- `git diff --check`

Lets members in from a **browser** (installable to home screen) while the app-store listings are pending — the same Expo app via `react-native-web`, wrapped as a PWA. **Verified in a real browser: the sign-in and full RN app render with zero runtime errors** (screenshotted during dev).

- **env.ts fix (the enabler):** reference `EXPO_PUBLIC_*` statically so Expo inlines them at bundle time on every platform. The old dynamic `process.env[key]` wasn't inlinable → empty object at runtime → crashed the web export. Also makes native EAS env resolution work via the documented path.
- `web/manifest.webmanifest` + `web/service-worker.js` (network-first navigations → cached shell offline; cache-first hashed assets; cross-origin API left to the network so data is never stale).
- `scripts/build-pwa.mjs` + `npm run build:pwa`: `expo export` → layers manifest / SW / icons / iOS meta onto `dist-web/`. Adds `react-dom` + `@expo/metro-runtime`.
- `web/README.md`: build & host steps (HTTPS, SPA fallback, `CORS_ORIGINS`).

Degrades gracefully on web: native push + offline video *downloads* no-op; video plays via the web player. **No server/admin/contract change**; native builds unchanged. mobile `tsc` clean. Merging with --admin.
