author: claudespice
body:
## Summary

`Cayenne auto-tuned config: …` is emitted from `get_vortex_config_with_footer_cache`, which runs on every `create_external_table` / `create_cayenne_table_provider`. Nothing deduped on the resolved configuration, so the line was a function of *how many times a provider was built* rather than *how many distinct configurations exist*.

Dataset initialization retries with unbounded Fibonacci backoff (`crates/runtime/src/init/dataset.rs`) and only `Error::PermanentDatasetFailure` short-circuits, so a dataset that fails a deterministic check is rebuilt for the life of the process — and re-emits its ~1.1 KB config line with every attempt. The reported case produced 33 emissions for 3 tables (3 unique configurations) in the first 4.5 minutes and kept going. The cost is not the bytes: the repeated line buries the `WARN` that explains why the dataset is unhealthy, which is the one line an operator is looking for.

Fixes #12330

## Changes

- `auto_tuned_config_fingerprint` hashes everything the line prints for one table. It hashes the *rendered* values rather than a hand-listed tuple of typed fields, so `{config:?}` covers every `VortexConfig` knob and a knob added to the line later cannot silently fall out of the key and start hiding re-tunes. The calibration measurements on the hardware profile (`data_perf`, `metastore_perf`) are excluded — the line does not print them, and they still reach the fingerprint through the knobs they resolved.
- `auto_tuned_config_is_newly_resolved` records the last fingerprint seen per table and reports only when it is new or changed. Keying on the resolution rather than logging once per table keeps the two cases worth seeing: the first resolution, and a genuine re-tune (adaptive tuning moving a knob, or a configuration edit after a hot reload).
- The `config_warnings` loop moved inside the same gate. Those warnings are a pure function of the same `config` and `hw.cores`, so they repeated in exactly the same storm — and a misconfigured dataset is precisely the one that retries forever, so the reported scenario emits both. One fingerprint covers both emits.

Behaviour on a healthy runtime is unchanged: every dataset still reports its resolution exactly once at startup.

## Scope

Two adjacent emits are deliberately left alone and are not part of this fix: the `cayenne_goal_* set: enabling adaptive tuning` INFO and the `cayenne_tuning: adaptive is in preview` WARN. Both fire only under the adaptive-tuning preview opt-in, and both are emitted from inside the tuning-resolution branch *before* the configuration is final, so they cannot share this fingerprint — gating them needs a different key and is a separate change.

The reporter also raised, as context rather than as part of this report, whether a deterministic configuration error should be retried unboundedly at all. That is the amplifier rather than the duplication, and it is filed separately as #12339.

Existing `warn_once!` / `OnceTracer` was considered and does not fit: it emits a bare `warn!` with no structured fields or custom target, it retains every distinct message string forever, and its never-repeat semantics would suppress the re-tune this line exists to record.

## Test plan

- `make lint`
- `make test`

New unit tests in `crates/runtime/src/dataaccelerator/cayenne/mod.rs`:

- `auto_tuned_config_is_reported_once_per_resolution` — first resolution reports, identical re-resolutions do not, a changed resolution reports again and then settles, reverting to an earlier resolution still reports, and tables are independent.
- `auto_tuned_config_fingerprint_covers_the_logged_values_only` — the fingerprint is deterministic; a knob, the host basis, the inferred workload signals and the table name each change it; a knob the line does not print still participates (over-reporting is the safe direction); a measured storage rate does not.
- `auto_tuned_config_line_survives_a_provider_rebuild_storm` — the regression test. Three provider constructions for one dataset, through the production `get_vortex_config` path with the emitted output captured, must produce exactly one config line and one configuration warning; a subsequent re-tune must report both again.

The regression test was verified load-bearing: reverting the gate to always-emit fails it deterministically with `left: 3, right: 1`, which is the reported failure mode.

## Checklist

- [x] Regression test fails on the old code and passes on the new
- [x] Edge cases covered: re-tune, revert to an earlier resolution, per-table isolation, unprinted knobs, excluded measurements
- [x] No behaviour change on a healthy runtime
- [x] No new dependency
- [x] Deferred item filed separately and linked

author: tessie1993
body:
A fidelity and safety pass back over the work that landed in #64. Three findings — two fixed, one recorded.

## Layers bypassed `VisualSafety` entirely

The blend happens in the composite, **after** `apply()` has clamped every parameter, and its magnitude is set by the mix and the mode — neither of which `apply()` can see. Two of the eight modes are genuine full-frame luminance events at high mix:

- **`ADD`** nearly doubles frame brightness, and does so whenever the two layers peak together — which for two beat-driven scenes is *on the beat, at the track's own rate*.
- **`DIFFERENCE`** drops the frame to black wherever the layers agree, so two scenes drifting in and out of agreement swing the whole frame with nothing setting the rate.

That is exactly the hazard the rest of that file exists to bound, and it was reachable without the user doing anything unusual.

`VisualSafety.layerMix` now clamps those two to `maxFlashDepth`. `DIFFERENCE` additionally rides `allowInversion`, because identical layers producing black is a contrast reversal in the same sense Invert and Solarize are.

The **mix** is clamped rather than the mode substituted, because the mix *is* the magnitude control and `apply()` bounds full-frame events by magnitude rather than by forbidding them. `transitionStyle()` gets away with substituting only because a cut and a fast fade read the same; swapping someone's blend mode would not.

The other six modes are deliberately untouched — none can produce a value outside the range its two inputs already occupied, so clamping them would ruin Screen and Multiply for no safety gain. Tests pin both halves of that split.

## Two refractory counters could overflow and kill their gate

`DrumChannels.Channel` rested at `Int.MAX_VALUE / 2` and incremented once per silent frame; `BeatGate` does the same from 100. Unbounded, both eventually wrap to negative — after which `sinceHit > refractoryFrames` is false **forever** and the gate is silently dead until something calls `reset()`.

Only reachable on a wallpaper left running for months, so this is latent rather than live. But the starting value I picked in #64 made it twice as likely as the existing idiom, which is my error. Both now clamp; the ceiling sits far above the 72-frame maximum refractory, so nothing reachable changes.

Tested by asserting the property rather than stepping a billion frames: a channel idle for 200,000 frames fires identically to one idle for 200.

## Layers do not survive a video export — recorded, not fixed

`FxCompositor` builds this same `composite_frag` but hardcodes `uStyle = CUT`, and `VideoExporter` renders exactly one `Scene`. An export of a layered view shows the active scene alone: nothing corrupt, the layer simply absent.

Worth stating because every other visual control in the renderer is mirrored on the export path deliberately. Closing it means a second `SceneFactory`, a second FBO and a second update loop in the exporter — a feature, not a patch — so it is documented on `layerSceneId` rather than half-done.

## Verification

- 86 pure-JVM tests green (one new), run outside Gradle with a standalone `kotlinc` — this environment still cannot reach `dl.google.com` for AGP or the SDK.
- ktlint clean on every touched file, checked locally this time rather than discovered by CI.
- The preview harness's composite audit still passes at 53/53/53, with `DIFFERENCE` still cancelling identical layers to exactly 0.
- `VisualSafetyTest` additions are **not** locally runnable — `VisualSafety`'s dependency closure reaches `CyclicPalettes`, which needs an Android `Context`. This PR's CI is the first thing to compile them.

body:
## Description

On the non-streaming endpoint a Gemini candidate can arrive carrying only a `finishReason`, with no `content` key at all — Gemini does this when it aborts before producing anything. `UNEXPECTED_TOOL_CALL` reproduces ~9 times out of 10 against `gemini-2.5-pro` with no tools declared, and `MALFORMED_FUNCTION_CALL` turns up there too.

That shape matched neither content-bearing clause in `convert_google_to_openai_format/1`, so it fell through to the catch-all and was reported as `finish_reason: "stop"`: a provider abort was indistinguishable from an empty but successful answer, and the raw reason was discarded before any caller could see it.

This adds the missing clause so the reason is normalized like every other, and carries `finish_reason_raw` (plus `finish_message` when present) in `provider_meta` — the non-streaming counterpart of `put_raw_finish_meta/3`. The streaming path has preserved the raw value since #936; this closes the same hole on the path tool-less requests actually use.

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change fixing an issue)
- [ ] New feature (non-breaking change adding functionality)
- [ ] Breaking change (fix or feature causing existing functionality to change)
- [ ] Documentation update

## Breaking Changes

None in the API surface. Behaviour changes for the specific case that was previously mis-reported: a content-less candidate with a `finishReason` now yields the normalized reason (`"error"`, or `"content_filter"` for the policy stops from #939) instead of `"stop"`. Candidates that carry content are untouched.

author: sburdges-eng
body:
Follow-up to #600. That PR fixed one suite falling through to `data/lariat.db`; this sweeps the remaining 374 and fixes the four others it found.

## Why these matter

`getDb()` falls back to `<dataDir>/lariat.db` whenever no `setDbPathForTest()` override is active, and **every open runs `initSchema()`** — a migration pass. `node --test` runs a lane's files concurrently, one process each. So a fall-through isn't just reading the wrong database; it's running DDL against a file its siblings hold cached prepared statements on. That's the `SQLITE_SCHEMA` signature from #599.

None of the four went red. All four were silently doing this on every CI run.

## The four

| Suite | Lane | Mechanism |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `test-unconfigured-install-fails-closed` | core | No DB setup at all — asserts install state *from* the shared DB |
| `test-haccp-audit-atomicity` | foodsafety | `setImmediate` fires after teardown released the override |
| `test-pin-defense-in-depth` | core | Same |
| `test-coverage-weekly` | infra | Importing the script under test ran the whole weekly job |

**The security one is the reason to read this diff.** `pinConfigured()` is `managerPinGateConfigured` → `hasActiveManagerPinUsers` → `getDb()`. So *"reports the install as unconfigured"* was reading `manager_pin_users` out of the production database, passing only while that table happened to be empty. A sibling suite inserting a manager PIN flips it; on a machine with one configured, the surrounding PHI / pay-data assertions stop describing the state they name. It now gets its own empty in-memory schema, so the premise is true by construction rather than by luck.

**The `setImmediate` pair** isolate correctly and then hand the database back while work is still scheduled — the receiving and compute-status routes fire `triggerComputeEngine` on an immediate that lands after `after()` called `setDbPathForTest(null)`. The trigger swallows its own errors, so both exited 0 while migrating `data/lariat.db`. They now drain pending immediates and leave the override alone; the process is exiting, and the reset was the only thing opening that door.

**`coverage-weekly`** ended in a bare `main().catch()` at module scope, so importing it for two pure helpers ran the entire weekly job: a `getDb()` against the shared file, a CSV and summary written into `data/coverage-reports/` — `REPORT_DIR` resolves from `__dirname`, so no test could opt out via `LARIAT_DATA_DIR` — and a `process.exit(1)` fired from inside the test runner. Now runs only when invoked directly, comparing **real** paths, since Node realpaths `import.meta.url` but not `argv[1]` and a symlinked component would otherwise silently stop the launchd job.

## Verification

- Sweep re-run against this tree: **0 of 375** suites open `<cwd>/data/lariat.db` (was 5).
- `npm run verify` green end to end, including `next build`.
- `regression-core` 517/517 · `regression-foodsafety` 665/665 · `regression-infra` 532/532, no `data/lariat.db` left behind.
- Both `coverage-weekly` paths checked: `npm run coverage:weekly` still produces a report; importing it does nothing.

Method, per-finding evidence and the stack traces are in `docs/audit/2026-08-01-shared-db-isolation-audit.md`.

## Note for the reviewer

CI already knew about this. `.github/workflows/ci.yml` prefixes the python step with `rm -f data/lariat.db …`, commented *"An earlier node:test suite can leave a stray schema-only data/lariat.db"* — and two steps above asserts the regression lanes "all use in-memory/tmp DBs (no data/lariat.db)", which was untrue for five of them until now.

**Left in place deliberately** — this branch changes only the four suites it names. Removing that workaround and replacing it with a one-line post-lane guard (`data/lariat.db` must not exist) is the natural follow-up, and can go green now.

body:
## Summary

Implements enterprise-grade cookie-based authentication with email verification, comprehensive security features, and full test coverage.

## Key Features

### Backend Authentication
- **User model** with UUID PKs, unique/indexed/NOT NULL email constraints
- **Bcrypt password hashing** (12 rounds) with constant-time comparison
- **Email verification system** with 24h token expiry and rate-limited resend
- **Logged-out token detection** (dual Redis+PostgreSQL storage) with security alerts for stolen tokens
- **Soft delete** for account deletion with login prevention
- **JWT access tokens** (15 min) with token blacklisting on logout
- **Rate limiting** on all auth endpoints (SlowAPI: 5 login, 3 register per hour)
- **Security headers middleware** (X-Frame-Options, CSP, etc.)
- **Audit logging** for all auth events including suspicious activity
- **Access control**: Unverified users blocked from enrichment/DSAR, opt-out remains public

### Frontend UI
- **Auth pages**: login, register, email verification flow
- **AuthProvider context** with login/logout/register/delete-account
- **AuthGuard component** for protecting app routes
- **VerificationBanner** for unverified users with resend functionality
- **UserMenu** with verification status indicator
- **BFF API routes** with cookie forwarding and auto-refresh on 401

### Security Features
- **HttpOnly cookies** (XSS protection)
- **SameSite=Lax** (CSRF protection)
- **Token blacklist** on logout (dual Redis+PostgreSQL)
- **Security alerts** for stolen token detection
- **IP-based rate limiting** on all auth endpoints
- **Constant-time password comparison** (timing attack prevention)

### Database Changes
- **Alembic migrations** for all auth tables (006, 007)
- **user_id foreign keys** on JobRecord and DsarRecord
- All indexes and constraints properly configured

### Tests
- **Password hashing** with timing attack resistance (331 lines)
- **Email verification** flow with token expiry (225 lines)
- **E2E authentication** (register → verify → login → logout) (271 lines)
- **Unverified user access control** (250 lines)
- **Logged-out token detection** (194 lines)
- **Account deletion** (soft delete) (328 lines)

### Documentation
- **Comprehensive authentication guide** (1000+ lines) with troubleshooting
- **Google OAuth setup guide** (173 lines)
- **ADR 0009** for architecture decision (236 lines)
- **ARCHITECTURE.md** updated with auth implementation status
- **README.md** updated with authentication prerequisites

## Testing Checklist

- [ ] Backend unit tests pass (`pytest backend/tests/test_auth_*.py`)
- [ ] Frontend TypeScript compilation passes
- [ ] Manual E2E test (register → verify → login → logout)
- [ ] Email verification flow works with SendGrid
- [ ] Rate limiting enforced on auth endpoints
- [ ] Unverified users blocked from enrichment/DSAR
- [ ] Opt-out remains publicly accessible
- [ ] Logged-out token detection triggers security alerts
- [ ] Soft delete prevents login for deleted accounts

## Architecture Decision

This PR implements ADR 0009 (Cookie-Based OAuth Authentication). See:
- `docs/adr/0009-cookie-oauth-authentication.md`
- Related plan: `cookie_oauth_authentication_5055b3c4.plan.md`

## Breaking Changes

None. All existing functionality preserved. Authentication is opt-in until environment variables are configured.

## Migration Guide

1. Run Alembic migrations: `alembic upgrade head`
2. Configure environment variables (see `.env.example`)
3. Set up SendGrid for email verification (optional)
4. Configure Google OAuth (optional)
5. Generate SECRET_KEY: `openssl rand -hex 32`

## Performance

System designed to scale to 10k+ concurrent users:
- Token validation: ~1ms (Redis lookup)
- Login: ~120-330ms (bcrypt intentionally slow for security)
- Horizontal scaling ready (stateless API servers)

## Security Review

All security best practices followed:
- ✅ HttpOnly cookies
- ✅ Bcrypt with 12 rounds
- ✅ Constant-time comparison
- ✅ Token blacklist
- ✅ Rate limiting
- ✅ Security headers
- ✅ Audit logging
- ✅ Stolen token detection

author: jenner-analytics
body:
[Jenneranalytics.com](https://jenneranalytics.com) provides an API that runs SAS code, with support for more than 200 SAS procedures. You can also use it with AI assistants in a collaborative workspace. It's available for Mac on the Apple App Store, and by license for Windows and Linux.

We support the larger community by
(1) increasing access to SAS-compatible systems,
(2) by providing test coverage and a test coverage framework to public SAS repos in order to encourage the use of best practices in software engineering.

Your project.sas runs on Jenner unmodified — this PR adds a small compatibility bundle so you can see for yourself. It's the test we wrote for your project, shared in case it's useful, and was assembled with AI assistance as is most code in modern businesses today.

The concentration-versus-rooted regression in your PROC REG step is a nice touch: rather than fit the model on the raw binary rooting outcomes, you aggregated up to rooted counts per K-IBA level first, so the linear model is estimated on the same 7-row summary table your PROC FREQ output produces. That two-stage move (individual-level frequency tables, then an aggregate-level regression) is exactly the right call for a designed experiment with only seven concentration levels, and it's why your fitted line matches the numbers in your slides so cleanly.

`jenner-check/` holds three bundles, each a byte-identical (or near-identical, where noted) copy of a stage of project.sas, its captured Jenner run, and a small runner:

```
jenner-check/
├── run_jenner.sh
├── README.md
├── t001_freq_root_conc/       # dummy-variable derivation + both PROC FREQ tables
├── t002_univariate_histogram/ # PROC UNIVARIATE NOPRINT histogram by root
└── t003_reg_rooting/          # the PROC REG model, byte-identical to your script
```

t001 and t002 swap your PROC IMPORT of a local azalea.csv for an inline sample matching the conc/rooted frequency counts from your own slide deck, since the runner submits script text only. t003 needed no changes at all — your inline DATALINES step and PROC REG model ran as-is.

To try it yourself: check out this PR's branch and run from the repo root, then POST one of the bundles straight to the hosted API —

```bash
# Check out this PR (puts you on its branch); then run from the repo root:
gh pr checkout <PR_NUMBER>
curl -sS --data-binary @jenner-check/t003_reg_rooting/script.sas https://api.jenneranalytics.com/v1/quick
```

or run `cd jenner-check && ./run_jenner.sh --all` to re-run all three and verify them against their pinned results. The API is free to try, no signup required — full reference: [the docs](https://docs.jenneranalytics.com/api/).

Only the SAS source text of whatever script you run (plus a two-line autoexec) is sent to api.jenneranalytics.com, which runs it and returns the log and listing — no data files are read or uploaded, so anything sitting next to a script stays on your machine, and nothing is transmitted unless you run a command yourself. It's the same exposure as pasting a snippet into any hosted tool, so it's worth a glance at a script's own source first if it embeds anything sensitive inline.

Merge it, close it, or ignore it — no response expected either way, and we won't open further PRs in this repo. To opt out for good, leave `no-more-prs` in any comment here, or open an issue titled `jenner-check: opt out`.

author: rocketman-21
body:
## Why this PR exists

A member asked Murph to search their email. The provider answered `200 OK`, but the response body exceeded the web tier's raw wire ceiling and was discarded, and the runtime tool reported the failure to the assistant as the single string `connected apps API is unavailable`. Murph then told the member their account was fine, called it a temporary service bug, and offered a retry that could only fail the same way.

Both halves are defects: a mailbox read is large because of markup, not because of content, and a rejected request is not an outage.

## User goal / user-visible behavior

Asking Murph to search connected email returns the result instead of an apology. When a request genuinely returns too much, Murph says so and narrows the search rather than reporting an outage and offering a doomed retry.

## User experience

Entry point is an ordinary chat message ("search my email for X"). Murph runs a connected-app search and read; the read now succeeds where markup-heavy mailboxes previously failed. Timing class is unchanged — the same single provider round trip, bounded by the existing 30s client timeout.

Failure paths change:

- Too much data returned: Murph receives `CONNECTED_APPS_RESULT_TOO_LARGE` with the instruction to ask for fewer results, a narrower time range, or one item at a time. It narrows and retries within the same turn instead of ending the conversation on an outage claim.
- Genuine provider outage: Murph receives `retryable: true` and the "one retry is reasonable" posture, matching the retry it already offers.
- Rejected request (bad arguments, revoked access, inactive account): Murph receives the code and the reason and can tell the member what is actually wrong.

No asynchronous continuation and no new screen. Not a frontend change, so there is no rendered evidence to record.

## Invariants the PR must preserve

- No untrusted provider or proxy body text reaches the model through an error path. Only a well-formed error code (`^[A-Z][A-Z0-9_]{0,63}$`) admits its paired control-plane message; anything else reports status alone. Covered by `withholds an unstructured transport failure body from the model`.
- The assistant result stays bounded. The compacted result is capped at 120 KB before the web tier responds, and the runtime keeps its own identical budget as a second gate.
- Oversized results fail closed, never truncated. A silently half-read mailbox is undetectable to the model; both budget checks return an explicit narrow-the-request instruction.
- Compaction never deletes member content. It runs once, in the web tier, and is safe to repeat: angle brackets stay escaped so an email quoting markup cannot be re-read as structure by a second pass. Covered by `survives a second pass so mixed-version callers cannot corrupt content`.
- Raising the raw read ceiling remains a memory guard, not an assistant budget. 4 MB bounds what the web tier buffers; it is never what the model receives.
- Calendar-create failures keep their existing non-retryable ambiguous-outcome wording, which takes precedence over the new generic failure description.

## Non-obvious affected surfaces

- `HostedWebControlPlaneResponseError` gains a `detail` field (`apps/cloudflare/src/runtime-platform/web-control-transport.ts`). Necessary because the class formats `message` as `"<description> failed with HTTP <status>. <body message>"`; quoting that to the model would duplicate the status and leak the internal transport description. `detail` keeps the control plane's own message verbatim. Additive only — every existing field and the formatted `message` are unchanged. Proof: `keeps the control-plane error code, status, and message readable by the caller` in `apps/cloudflare/test/connected-apps-web-control-policy.test.ts`, which drives the real class through the real port.
- Failed dynamic and MCP tool-call runtime issues now record the sanitized tool name (`packages/assistant-engine/src/assistant-codex/action-diagnostics.ts`). Necessary because `hosted_assistant_runtime_issue` previously recorded only action kind and duration/output buckets for these failures, so a failed call could not be attributed to a surface without the web tier's request logs. Reuses the existing `resolveToolDiagnosticIdentity` allowlist, so only an identifier-shaped name is stored — never arguments or output. Proof: the extended `builds privacy-safe runtime issues for failed Codex action events`, whose existing assertions still verify no prompt, stdout, stderr, or output text is encoded.
- `executeHostedConnectedAppsRequest` now compacts every operation's result, including `manage`. Compaction is a no-op walk on markup-free payloads; the existing management tests cover the unchanged shapes.

## Architecture and reuse

- **Existing systems reused:** `@murphai/hosted-execution/connected-apps` already had both consumers as dependents, so it became the compaction owner without a new package or dependency edge. The oversize failure reuses `hostedOnboardingError` and the existing `{error: {code, message, retryable}}` body that the transport already parses into `code`/`retryable`; no new error channel was introduced.
- **New logic:** Web-tier compaction and budget enforcement before responding (`boundHostedConnectedAppsResult`); a control-plane failure description that reports code, status, and retry posture; the `detail` field carrying the unformatted control-plane message.
- **New abstractions:** None. The compaction function moved from the runtime tool into the shared contract package it already imported; the runtime tool now calls the same function instead of a private copy. The structural failure reader is a local function, not a shared abstraction, because the runtime tool is its only consumer and the error class lives in an app the package cannot import.
- **Complexity intentionally avoided:** No retry, queue, chunking, pagination layer, or streaming path was added — the fix is a budget applied at the layer that owns the assistant's context, plus an error that already existed being allowed through. Compaction runs in exactly one place rather than defensively at both tiers, and deploy-window safety comes from making the transform repeatable instead of from version negotiation.

## Hot reply path impact

`Not applicable.` The change is confined to connected-app tool calls made during a provider turn. It adds no database call, network call, or awaited operation to durable acceptance of a current conversation message, provider start, or durable reply handoff. Compaction runs in the web tier on a payload already buffered in memory; it replaces a byte-length check that ran on the same payload.

## Murph initial provider input impact

`Not applicable` for both individual and group Murph. No prompt file, tool description, argument schema, tool availability, deferral metadata, Codex version, or provider-request assembly changed. The three connected-app tool definitions in `dynamic-tools/connected-apps.ts` are byte-identical to base; the diff in that file touches result and failure handling, which is tool-call output within a turn, not provider input.

## Preliminary specialist lenses

- **Product experience** — `applicable`. Intended outcome: a member asking Murph to search their email gets the result, and when a request truly returns too much, gets a narrower search instead of a false outage report and a doomed retry offer. Direct journey evidence: the production incident is reproduced as a test — `delivers a markup-heavy mailbox read that the raw wire ceiling used to discard` builds a mailbox payload over the old ceiling and asserts the voucher code and its link survive; `reports the control-plane failure code, status, and retry posture` asserts the assistant no longer sees "unavailable" for a rejected request. Gap: no live end-to-end run against the provider, since the Composio credential is production-only.
- **Prompt** — `not applicable`. No prompt text, tool description, o

```
attempt 1/3 hit a transient network error; retrying in 5s
attempt 2/3 hit a transient network error; retrying in 15s
still failing after 3 attempts; the last one hit a transient network error
```

Docker Hub was not blipping, it was degraded: `Client.Timeout exceeded` then `context deadline exceeded` twice, across the whole twenty seconds the budget allowed. The classification was right and the outcome was still a red job, which is the outcome the retry exists to prevent.

- Defaults move to five attempts with the pause tripling from five seconds and holding at `RETRY_MAX_DELAY` (sixty): pauses of 5, 15, 45, 60, about two minutes in total.
- The cap is what keeps the tail bounded as attempts grow; without it a fifth attempt would wait 405 seconds.
- `RETRY_MAX_DELAY` is validated like the other two: a non-numeric value returns 2 rather than misbehaving.

author: manuxv3-dev
body:
## Summary

`GET /api/v1/public/og/:type/:slug.png` returned 500 for **every** resource type
(event/poll/expense/todo/list) — Open Graph preview images were completely broken, both
locally and in production, killing link previews across ADR-010's public-link sharing.

## Root cause

`og-renderer.ts` loaded the variable font `Inter.ttf` and referenced the same buffer twice in
Satori's `fonts[]` config (once per weight). Satori's pinned dependency
`@shuding/opentype.js@1.4.0-beta.0` throws in `parseFvarAxis` while parsing that font's `fvar`
(variation axes) table — the crash happens in Satori's constructor, before any template is
touched, hence "all types, not just expense/todo/list".

```
TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading '256')
  at parseFvarAxis (@shuding/opentype.js@1.4.0-beta.0/.../opentype.js:10285:25)
  at Object.parseFvarTable [as parse] (…)
  at zt.addFonts (satori@0.10.14/dist/index.js:5:55244)
```

I confirmed bumping Satori doesn't help: **every** release up to the current latest (0.29.0)
pins the exact same `@shuding/opentype.js@1.4.0-beta.0`.

## Fix

Switch to two **static** Inter TTFs (Regular 400 / Bold 700, no `fvar` table — verified by
inspecting the sfnt table directory) instead of the variable font. This is actually a return
to ADR-018's original wording ("Fonts Inter Regular + Bold embarquées dans le bundle") — the
variable-font approach was an implementation drift, not a deliberate decision, so no new ADR.

The fonts are now **committed** directly (`packages/backend/assets/fonts/*.ttf`, ~66 KB each)
instead of downloaded at setup time via `scripts/download-og-fonts.mjs` (now deleted, along
with the `setup:fonts` pnpm script). This removes a network dependency from onboarding/CI and
is what let this bug ship silently in the first place: the CI test suite never ran
`setup:fonts`, so the render path was never actually exercised — `og-renderer.js` was mocked
out entirely in `public-og.test.ts` (added for MAN-16) specifically to sidestep this
already-known-broken path.

**Production blocker found in review:** the `Dockerfile` runner stage never copied
`packages/backend/assets/` into the final image — so even with fonts committed, prod would
have stayed on 503 forever. Fixed alongside (one `COPY` line).

## What changed

- `packages/backend/assets/fonts/Inter-Regular.ttf`, `Inter-Bold.ttf` — committed static fonts (Google's official CDN, `latin` subset — see note below), plus `OFL.txt` license.
- `og-renderer.ts` — `LoadedFonts` is now `{ regular, bold }` instead of `{ variable }`; `renderTemplateToPng` is exported for direct testing (no Redis needed); `loadFonts()` resets its memoized promise on failure so a transient read error doesn't permanently poison the exported render path.
- `index.ts` — 503 body no longer leaks the internal asset path (moved to the Pino log only).
- `Dockerfile` — runner stage now copies `packages/backend/assets`.
- `scripts/download-og-fonts.mjs`, `setup:fonts` script, `.gitignore`/`.gitkeep` font-download plumbing — removed (dead now that fonts are committed).
- `.gitattributes` — `*.ttf binary`.

## Testing

New `og-renderer.test.ts` — unlike `public-og.test.ts` (mocks `og-renderer.js` entirely), this
exercises the **real** Satori + resvg pipeline with the real committed fonts, no mocking:

- Confirmed RED before the fix: fails with the exact `parseFvarAxis` TypeError from the ticket.
- GREEN after: renders all **5** template types (event/poll/expense/todo/list) to a valid PNG — magic bytes + IHDR 1200×630 dimensions asserted.

`just verify` (lint + format-check + typecheck + test) green locally, Postgres+Redis up
(`107 backend tests passing, 0 failures`).

## Known trade-off (flagged, not blocking)

The committed static fonts are Google's `latin` subset (~230 glyphs) — covers French/English
fully, but drops Latin-Extended/Greek/Cyrillic glyphs the old variable font had (silent
fallback to notdef, not a crash). Acceptable since French is the primary locale and this was
previously 100% broken either way; noted on the ticket as a follow-up if broader script
coverage is ever needed (ties into MAN-30 i18n).

## Related Issues

Closes MAN-36

author: z915084508
body:
## Resumen

Corrige los fallos repetidos de despliegue `P1002` causados por varias compilaciones de Vercel intentando adquirir al mismo tiempo el advisory lock de Prisma Migrate.

## Cambio

El build normal ya no ejecuta automáticamente:

- `prisma migrate deploy`
- `staff:bootstrap`

Estas operaciones pasan a ser explícitas:

- `AOC_RUN_MIGRATIONS=true`
- `AOC_RUN_STAFF_BOOTSTRAP=true`

Todas las compilaciones siguen ejecutando:

- `prisma generate`
- `next build`

## Motivo

Los cambios recientes no contienen migraciones. Ejecutar `migrate deploy` en cada Production Deployment provoca contención entre despliegues concurrentes y hace fallar builds sanos.

## Seguridad

- no se desactiva el advisory lock
- no se usa `PRISMA_SCHEMA_DISABLE_ADVISORY_LOCK`
- no se cambia el schema
- no se ejecuta ninguna migración
- las migraciones futuras siguen disponibles mediante `npm run db:deploy` o el flag explícito

Incluye un contrato de prueba para impedir que `VERCEL_ENV=production` vuelva a activar migraciones implícitamente.

author: trick77
body:
Follow-up to #304.

`App.tsx` and `views/Player.tsx` each opened their own connection to `/api/downloads/stream` — and App was already decoding the very `summary` events the Player subscribed for, since it builds `summaryPhaseByVideoId` out of them. The second connection existed to re-decode bytes the first one had decoded a moment earlier.

That was mildly wasteful before. The now-playing dock made it structural: the Player is mounted for the whole session now, so its stream stays open for the whole session with it, and a summary page adds a third connection decoding the same bytes a third time.

## How much this actually mattered

Less than I first suggested, and I checked rather than left it as a guess. Production is behind Traefik on the `websecure` entrypoint with TLS terminated there, so browsers speak HTTP/2 and these are streams on one connection, not separate ones — the 6-per-origin limit is an HTTP/1.1 rule. The backend hub has no client cap either.

Against an HTTP/1.1 origin it is real but modest: three of six connections spent on one feed, which is the local dev server through Vite's proxy.

So this lands as a **simplification**, not a fix for a production problem. The reason to do it is that the subscriber count had started scaling with a design decision — how many Players are mounted — that has nothing to do with SSE.

## The change

- App forwards the newest `summary` event to the open video's page as a prop. **A new object per event, deliberately:** two consecutive events can carry the same `status` while only the `phase` moves, so the page has to react to the second one too. What matters is that an event *arrived*, not that its value changed — the effect is keyed on object identity for exactly that reason.
- `Player`'s `streamDownloads` effect goes. Its `done` branch keeps the same `getVideo` refetch and the same stale-`videoId` guard; the non-`done` branch keeps the same in-place `summary_status` patch.
- The payload type moves next to the stream it arrives on as `SummaryEventData`. It had been cast inline at both call sites — in two different shapes, one of which under-declared `phase`.
- `streamDownloads` gains a comment stating the one-subscriber rule, so the next thing that wants an event off this stream asks App for it.

## Verification

1004 UI tests pass. The old test drove the SSE mock directly; it now drives the prop, and two cases were added that the previous shape could not express: an event for a *different* video is ignored (no refetch, no repaint), and a repeated event with an unchanged status still lands. The dead `streamDownloads` mock scaffolding is removed from the Player tests, since the Player no longer calls it.

body:
Adds `messages/vi.json` — a complete Vietnamese translation of `messages/en.json`. One file, no other changes; locale registry wiring is handled separately.

**Key parity:** 4,577 / 4,577 leaf keys. Zero missing, zero extra, zero placeholder mismatches, zero type mismatches (verified with a full key-path diff against `en.json`).

**Checks:** `bunx tsc --noEmit` clean; `bun run test` 1282/1282 passing (unchanged from baseline).

**Conventions used**
- `tệp` for "file" throughout (`tập tin` appears zero times).
- Northern-standard register, impersonal phrasing (second-person pronouns avoided except where the English genuinely needs one), bare verb phrases for buttons.
- `hoá / xoá / khoá / huỷ / tuỳ` tone-placement style, applied consistently.
- `bảng nhớ tạm` for "clipboard" (normalized across the file).
- Full diacritics: 4,294 of 4,577 strings carry diacritics. The 283 that do not are format lists (`PNG, JPG, WebP`), protocol tokens, city and country names, and canonical HTTP reason phrases.
- No `\u` escapes — raw UTF-8 throughout.

**What a native speaker should review**
- HTTP status codes: all 51 `codes.*.text` reason phrases were left in English (`Not Found`, `Internal Server Error`) since developers match on them; descriptions and use cases are translated. Confirm this is the desired split.
- Trailing exclamation marks were removed from 57 toast strings that have them in English, to keep the register uniformly plain. Revert if the source punctuation should be preserved.
- Number formatting was localized to the Vietnamese convention (`10.000`, `0,01`) in a handful of strings, deviating from the English digits.
- `PomodoroTimer` splits a sentence across five fragments (`workFor` / `thenTake` / `shortBreakMin` / `sessions` / `longBreakMin`). Vietnamese word order forced a different cut, so this needs eyeballing in the running UI.
- `HabitTracker` weekday initials became `T2`–`T7` / `CN` (two characters instead of one) — check column widths.
- Meme generator placeholder `VĂN BẢN TRÊN` / `VĂN BẢN DƯỚI` is longer than the English and renders as caps on the image; may need a font-size check.
- `TextCaseConverter` case labels were made self-demonstrating in Vietnamese (`IN HOA`, `in thường`, `xEn Kẽ`) rather than left as English ASCII samples.
- Terminology worth a second opinion: `Media` and `Dev` kept as loanwords in `categoriesShort` (Vietnamese equivalents are too long for nav chips); `opacity` rendered `Độ mờ` / `Độ đục` depending on whether it collides with `blur` in the same panel; `rollover`, `dithering`, `inset`, `Chevron`, `Story` left untranslated.
- Privacy wording was deliberately kept at source strength — model-download strings preserve "tải xuống một lần từ CDN trong lần dùng đầu tiên, sau đó ... trên thiết bị", and the TOTP offline claim stays scoped to "khi trang này còn mở". These should not be flattened into blanket offline claims during any copy-editing pass.

body:
## UI updates: home page tiles, match-day banner, live match screen

### Home page
- **Tiles are fully clickable.** Each card is now the navigation target (`role="button"`, `tabindex="0"`, click + Enter/Space), and the four "Naar …" buttons are gone. New `.home-tile` class carries the affordances the buttons used to: pointer cursor, hover lift, focus ring, with a `prefers-reduced-motion` opt-out. Same behaviour on mobile and desktop — the tile fills its grid cell.
- **Squad tile title** `Spelers beheren` → `Selectie`.
- **Tile subtitles are admin-only.** Anonymous visitors see label, icon and title; the descriptive line is wrapped in `<AuthorizeView>`.

### Match-day banner
- `LiveMatchService.GetInProgressAsync` → **`GetTodaysMatchAsync`**. A match in progress still wins outright (it can have kicked off before midnight); otherwise today's fixture is picked, preferring one not yet finished when there are two on the same day.
- The banner now runs the whole match day instead of only between kick-off and the final whistle:

  | State | Label | Score | Opens |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | Not started | `VANDAAG` | — | `/games/{id}/live` |
  | In progress | `NU LIVE` (pulsing dot) | live | `/games/{id}/live` |
  | Finished | `EINDE WEDSTRIJD` | final | `/games/{id}/result` |

- Before and after the match the banner drops the loud live gradient for the card gradient with a club-coloured outline, and swaps the pulsing dot for a ball icon — the live treatment stays reserved for a match actually being played. Added a focus ring the banner was missing.
- The live page is reachable from the banner **before kick-off and for non-admins**, so a spectator can get in early.

### Live match screen
- **Players off the roster are no longer offered as subs.** `OnBench` filters through `Game.IsInRoster`, so a saved substitute who has since been marked unavailable or dropped from the squad disappears from the bench — and, because `SubCandidates` builds on it, from the substitution sheet too.
- **Score buttons are hidden before kick-off** (previously shown greyed out above the start button) and relabelled `Doelpunt` / `Tegen doelpunt`.

### Resource strings (`Strings.nl.resx`)
- Added: `Selection`, `Today`, `Goal against`.
- Removed (now unused): `Manage Players`, `Go to Squad`, `Go to Games`, `Go to Stats`, `Go to Settings`, `We scored`, `They scored`.

### Notes
- Non-admin formation colours needed no change — `PitchOverview.HidePositionFit` already collapses every chip to the default green, and both call sites (live match, formation overview) already pass it.
- The squad tile now shows `SELECTIE` as its eyebrow label *and* `Selectie` as its title; worth deciding whether to drop or rename the eyebrow.

Syncs the shared agent-instructions block from `automations/agent-standards/` into this repo's `AGENTS.md`, and ensures `CLAUDE.md` imports it.

Content outside the managed markers is preserved. Edit shared standards in the `automations` repo. Anything changed here is overwritten by the next sync.

This sync carries the 2026-08-01 ablation, which cut the shared block from 151 lines to 47, together with the corrections made since. Every deleted, demoted, and restored line is recorded in `automations/agent-standards/ABLATION-LEDGER.md` with the reason and the current counts. Read the diff rather than rubber-stamping it, and open an issue if a deletion turns out to be load-bearing in this repo.

Three deletions have been reversed, all because the thing believed to cover them did not. The rule against pushing directly to the default branch is back, since no repo in this org has branch protection and nothing rejects such a push. The rule against committing packaged `.plugin` and `.skill` artifacts is back, after a briefly attempted move to `automations` rested on a search that could not match the paths it was looking for. Several writing-style rules are back, because the block pointed at a skill that only exists on machines running the nstack bootstrap.

The writing-style section is rewritten. It was previously stated four times across four files in four different wordings, and it is now stated once, in `automations/agent-standards/writing-style.md`. The section you see here is lifted verbatim out of that file by this script, so the two cannot drift apart. The rules themselves moved from a list of prohibitions to a short set of principles, and they now say what to do about audience and about the opening summary of a document. The banned-word list is deleted and is not coming back in this form. It blocked ordinary words including `can`, `may`, `it`, and `that`. Em dashes and semicolons are no longer banned outright, and are instead reserved for the rare case where nothing plainer carries the meaning.

author: al-rabbani
body:
## GDS Agent OS Kernel — True Agentic Operating System Foundation

This PR implements the 4-phase transformation from Agentic Platform → Agentic OS.

### Phase 1: Active Kernel Runtime
- AgentProcessControlBlock (APCB) with 7 lifecycle states (NEW→READY→RUNNING→BLOCKED→SWAPPED→TERMINATED→CRASHED)
- Priority-based preemptive scheduler (P0-P4, P0 preempts P1)
- LLM Compute Arbitrator with per-process token budgets and model routing (GPT-4.1/mini/nano)
- Kernel daemon with boot/run/shutdown lifecycle and crash recovery via checkpoints

### Phase 2: Virtual Context Paging Engine
- MemoryManager treating LLM context window as RAM (128K tokens)
- Redis as swap (recent working memory), Qdrant as disk (persistent), PostgreSQL as archive
- Automatic page fault handling — cold segments evicted when context overflows
- LRU-based eviction, context compression (summary generation)

### Phase 3: Isolated Tool Driver Sandbox
- ToolSandbox with timeout enforcement, capability-based security
- Panic isolation — crashed tools do NOT crash the kernel
- Health tracking + auto-disable after 5 consecutive failures
- 10 pre-built tool drivers (nmap, nuclei, semgrep, trivy, cisa_kev, etc.)

### Phase 4: System Call Interface
- 18 syscalls: agent_create, agent_terminate, mem_alloc, mem_page_in/out, tool_call, llm_request, ipc_send/recv, approval_request/grant, kernel_status, process_list
- Full audit trail — every syscall logged with caller PID, args, result, latency
- IPC message passing between agent processes
- Human-in-the-loop approval gates for high-risk actions

### Integration
- `GDSUnifiedKernel` class combines all 4 phases
- All tests passed: process creation, priority scheduling, dependency blocking, memory allocation, page fault handling, tool sandboxing, IPC messaging, syscall audit trail

### Stats
- 7 Python files, 2,614 lines of kernel code
- 10 tool drivers pre-registered
- 18 system calls available

GDS Co-Pilot — Sovereign AI Security Analyst

| ① | `[split 주택, 단순 주택]` | 409,060,000 | 432,060,000 | **과소 23,000,000** |
| ③ | `[split, split]` | 379,060,000 | 396,060,000 | **과소 17,000,000** |
| ② | 부분 비사토 + 사업용 | 240,000,000 | 240,000,000 | 0 (단일세율 호라 floor만) |
| ④ | 파트 없는 자산만 | 432,060,000 | 432,060,000 | 0 (세액·`appliedRate` 모두) |

⭐ **도출값은 추정이 아니다** — ①의 432,060,000은 **파트 없는 동등 입력**(과세표준 합계·해당 호
동일)에 대해 현행 엔진이 **이미 내던 값**이다. 「**split이라는 이유만으로** 23,000,000이 빠진다」.

## 근거 (신규 해석 없음)

§104⑤ 본문 **후단** 「한 필지의 토지가 … 구분되는 경우 **각각을 별개의 자산으로 보아**」 +
예규 「"자산별" = **각 호별로 합산한 자산**」(「기획재정부 재산세제과-536」 2018.6.19. ·
국세청 「기준-2018-법령해석재산-0098」). **P12가 누진 호 분기에서 이미 쓴 근거 그대로**다.

## 설계 — 3안 비교 후 B안

- A(두 분기 완전 통합): ❌ 회귀 케이스 ④의 **표시가 바뀐다**(실측 `appliedRate` 0.72→0.70 ·
  `surchargeRate` null→0.3)
- **B(버킷 멤버만 교체 · 표시 계산 유지)**: ✅ ④ 세액·표시 **완전 불변**, ①은 파트 없는 동등
  입력과 **세액·`appliedRate` 둘 다 일치**
- C(`isAssetLevelClause5` 제거해 자산 단위 합산): ❌ D-12 회귀

⇒ **§104⑤ 합산 단위가 전 그룹에서 「파트」로 통일**됐다 — 두 분기가 키 함수 · 인자 축 ·
멤버 단위 셋 다 같다.

## Do 중 고아 제거 3건 (Surgical — 내 변경이 만든 것만)

- `isAssetLevelClause5` — **마지막 소비처가 이 분기**였다
- `assetTaxOf`의 `splitParts`·`partialNbl` 반환 (취지는 `parts` 주석으로 보존)
- `hasPartialNonBusinessLand` import (lint가 잡음)

## anchor

**7건 신설** — 세액 4 + 회귀 2 + 구조 1. **P13-3**이 핵심이다:
`[S,B]`와 파트 없는 동등 입력 `[B2,B]`의 세액이 같음을 직접 고정하고,
전제로 `groupTaxBase` 일치도 함께 잠근다(비교가 성립하는지부터 고정).

## 검증

tsc 0 · lint 0 · 신규 7건 + GREEN 조건 64건 = **71건**
· 전체 **1,159파일 12,997건 · 회귀 0**

author: zhoulf1006
body:
Closes #27

## 问题

仓库此前**没有任何 workflow 跑 typecheck 或 test**:

| workflow | 触发 | 做什么 |
|---|---|---|
| `build.yml` | `push: tags: v*` / 手动 | 打包、签名公证、发 Release |
| `download-statistics.yml` | 定时 | 抓下载统计 |

合进 master 的代码在 GitHub 上从未被检查过。质量完全依赖本地自觉,review 时看不出跑没跑;分支保护也无从设起(没有任何 required check 可选)。

## 改动

新增 `.github/workflows/checks.yml`,在**每个 PR 与每次进 master** 时跑:

1. `pnpm typecheck`
2. `pnpm test`(根 vitest 的 include 已覆盖 `src/**` 与 `site/src/**`,两侧一次跑完)
3. `pnpm build`(electron-vite —— 模块解析、插件配置这类构建期错误 typecheck 看不见)
4. `site` 的 `astro build`(site 有独立 package.json / lockfile / node_modules,不在根 workspace 里,故单独 install)

加了 `concurrency` + `cancel-in-progress`:同分支连续 push 时取消旧运行,不排队跑陈旧提交。

## 一个必须踩准的点:Node 版本

**不能沿用 `build.yml` 的 node 20。** 测试会经 `src/main/db/messages.ts` 加载 `node:sqlite`,该模块 Node 22.5 才有:

```
$ grep -rln "node:sqlite" src/
src/main/db/messages.ts
$ grep -rl "from './db/messages'" src/main/*.test.ts | head -3
src/main/app-core.alias.test.ts
src/main/app-core.offline-keep.test.ts
src/main/app-core.resolve-peer.test.ts
```

`build.yml` 用 20 一直没出事,是因为它只打包不跑测试——打包产物里跑的是 Electron 自带的 node,与 CI runner 的 node 无关。本 workflow 钉 22,与本地开发环境(v22.22.0)一致。

## 验证

四条命令已在本地按 CI 的顺序实测跑过(含 `--frozen-lockfile` 两次 install),全部通过。workflow 本身的真实验证就是这个 PR —— 它的 `pull_request` 触发会让 checks 在本 PR 上跑一次,绿了才说明门禁真的立住了。

## 后续(不在本 PR)

workflow 稳定跑绿后,在 GitHub 仓库设置里把 `checks` 设为 master 的 required status check。那是设置项不是代码改动,需要手动操作。

author: gen16k
body:
## Why

Claude Code populates its `/model` picker from the gateway's `GET /v1/models`,
but the fetch is **credential-gated**: skipped entirely unless
`ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN` or a resolved API key is configured. waired deliberately
writes no credential — that is what keeps the claude.ai subscription the active
auth (#488) — so on a subscription-OAuth host discovery has **never run**, the
cache has never been written, and the three reserved directive ids from #52 have
never once appeared in the picker. #332 established that with a live
reproduction; it is reproducible on any OAuth-only machine (no
`~/.claude/cache/gateway-models.json`, ever).

The read side has no matching gate: the picker falls back to whatever cache is
on disk (upstream `llm-gateway-protocol`'s documented fallback-to-cache). So the
agent writes it.

Last of three PRs for waired-ai/waired#1002 L26: canary pins (#419) → window
derivation (#425) → **this**.

## What

**A user-scope writer** (`internal/integration/claudecode/gatewaycache.go`).
The file is user-owned while the routing it complements is machine-wide and
written as root, so it rides the existing sudo hop: a hidden
`waired claude _models-cache write|remove` re-entered as the invoking user via
`runLinkAllAsUser`, exactly as the `/waired-route` skill and the statusline do.

**The base URL travels as an argument**, not re-derived in the child. The reader
compares `baseUrl` against the live `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` by **exact string**, so
re-deriving it in another process with another state-dir view is precisely how a
trailing slash or a stale port gets in and silently disables the whole cache.

**`modelsCacheGuard`** re-checks in the user context that this machine really is
routed at that URL. Not redundant with `applyClaudeRoute` having just written
managed settings — the subcommand is reachable on its own, and every case it
refuses fails *silently* otherwise: Claude Code neither validates the file nor
reports on it, so a cache naming an unconfigured gateway leaves a picker full of
entries that go nowhere and a file nothing told the user about.

**Removal is wired as carefully as the write.** `waired claude disable` and the
model-route-directives opt-out both clear it, for the same reason.

## The measured shape, not the sketched one

`fetchedAt` is epoch **milliseconds**, a JSON number — #419's schema assert
caught that on its first run against a real client, correcting this issue's
original schema sketch. The type matters more than it looks: the reader
schema-parses the whole document, so a string there yields `null` and the picker
falls back to the built-in list — indistinguishable from the bug this fixes.

## Id consolidation

Rather than adding a fourth copy of the directive ids, they move into
`claudecode.DirectiveModels`, which `cmd/waired` now also uses for #408's
local-id lookup. The gateway keeps its own copies (the CLI must not link the
gateway package, and through it the router and the inference stack, for three
strings — the same trade `internal/proxy/intercept` makes).

`TestDirectiveModelsMatchPickerCache` asserts the table against the **advertised
`/v1/models` response**, not against the constants, so display names — which are
user-visible picker copy — are covered as well as ids. The weaker cmd/waired-side
pin added in #425 is dropped as redundant.

## Deliberately not implemented

The opportunistic statusline/Stop-hook refresh this issue floats. The document
only changes when the directive id set or the base URL changes, and the read side
applies no TTL, so a per-turn rewrite would be pure cost.

## Verification

**Our writer's output vs. the real client's**, both against the same stub gateway
on this host — identical keys, identical types, identical values for all three
directive entries (the client additionally keeps the stub's `claude-sonnet-5`,
which waired does not advertise; timestamps differ by the second between runs):

```
=== THEIRS (real claude 2.1.220) ===        === OURS ===
{                                           {
  "baseUrl": "http://127.0.0.1:34709",        "baseUrl": "http://127.0.0.1:34709",
  "fetchedAt": 1785662506086,                 "fetchedAt": 1785662507181,
  "models": [                                 "models": [
    {"id": "anthropic-waired-auto",             {"id": "anthropic-waired-auto",
     "display_name": "Waired auto (…)"},         "display_name": "Waired auto (…)"},
    {"id": "anthropic-waired-local", …},        {"id": "anthropic-waired-local", …},
    {"id": "claude-waired-cloud[1m]", …},       {"id": "claude-waired-cloud[1m]", …}
    {"id": "claude-sonnet-5", …}]}            ]}
```

- `go test ./cmd/waired/ ./internal/integration/... ./internal/gateway/` — green.
  `gofmt`, `go vet`, `golangci-lint run` — 0 issues.
- `npm run i18n:check` — 31 pairs in sync; `npm run build` — 63 pages, and both
  new anchors render (`#the-waired-entries-are-missing-from-model`, EN and ja).
- New tests: the on-disk schema (exact key set, `fetchedAt` as a number and as
  epoch ms, per-model keys), mode 0600, cache-dir creation on a fresh tree,
  `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` honoured *and* `~/.claude` left alone when it is set,
  refusal on an empty base URL / empty model list, overwrite-not-merge, removal
  (including "absent is success"), the `^(claude|anthropic)/i` filter every
  written id must survive, and a 7-case table over `modelsCacheGuard` — including
  the trailing-slash case, which the reader treats as a mismatch and so must we.

## Owner check requested

The docs copy (three-entries paragraph, the new troubleshooting section) and the
`/model` entry labels are user-visible; happy to revise the wording.

Still worth an on-device pass on an OAuth-only host: `sudo waired claude enable`
→ restart Claude Code → the three entries render in `/model` and each routes per
directive → `sudo waired claude disable` removes the file. The comparison above
is as close as this gets headlessly — the picker render itself has no headless
surface.

Fixes #407
Fixes #332
Refs waired-ai/waired#1002

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

### Live guard check on this host (unrouted, OAuth-only)

```
$ waired claude _models-cache write --base-url http://127.0.0.1:9472
waired: waired claude _models-cache write: /etc/claude-code/managed-settings.json is not present — run `waired claude enable` first
exit=1                       # and no file created

$ waired claude _models-cache write
waired: waired claude _models-cache write: --base-url is required

$ waired claude _models-cache remove
exit=0                       # absent is success

$ waired claude --help | grep -c _models-cache
0                            # hidden
```

### Known edge, not fixed here

`scrubbedChildEnv` (`cmd/waired/init_integration.go`) drops `HOME`,
`WAIRED_STATE_DIR` and `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` before the sudo hop but passes
`CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` through, so `sudo -E` with that variable set would place the
cache under the operator´s chosen tree rather than the target user´s `~/.claude`.
Reachable only via `sudo -E` (plain sudo env_resets it) and arguably what an
operator who exported it meant; left alone rather than widening a shared scrub
list from this PR.

author: copilot
body:
`bump_version.py` only read the local `app/VERSION` file, so two parallel PRs branching from the same base commit would independently produce the same next patch version. When the first PR merged, the second's bump became stale—equal to the new base—causing the version-guard push check in `docker-publish.yml` to fail (root cause of check run 91480277439, PR #473/#474 collision at `26.7.36`).

## Changes

- **`app/scripts/bump_version.py`**: Added `--base-ref` argument (default: `release/v26-beta`). After computing the local patch bump, the script reads the target branch's current VERSION via `origin/<base-ref>` (with a best-effort fetch) and raises the floor if the bump would be ≤ that value:

  ```
  # Before: always bumped from local file
  26.7.35 (local) → 26.7.36  ← collision if branch tip already at 26.7.36

  # After: raises floor to branch tip when needed
  26.7.35 (local) + 26.7.36 (branch tip) → 26.7.37
  ```

  Network/auth failures are swallowed silently so the hook can never block a commit.

- **`app/scripts/tests/test_bump_version.py`**: 13 new tests covering the collision-prevention path, graceful fallback when the ref is unreachable, explicit `--base-ref ""` opt-out, and no-double-bump when the local version already exceeds the branch tip.

- **`app/VERSION`**: `26.7.35` → `26.7.36`

author: pollo3470
body:
Closes #1530

## 背景更正

issue 正文说 step1 拆分侧「还没有这层联动，LLM 可能为带引用的 unit 拆出执行时申请不到的时长」。代码事实相反：step1 传 `generation_mode="reference_video"`，`uses_reference_images` 缺省即 `True`，所以拿到的是**整集一律按「带参考图」收窄**的单一集合（Veo 3.1 @720p 即 `[8]`）。真实缺陷是**过度收窄**——无引用 unit 本可申请的 4/6 秒被整集收掉——且这层保证并非逐 unit，只是恰好取了最窄的那套。

本 PR 按验收标准的字面落地：让每个 unit 的时长落在**其引用状态对应**的生效档位内。

## 改动

- **两套档位 + 并集枚举 + 派生后逐 unit 判**。拆分工具注入 `with_references` / `without_references` 两套档位（`sdk_tools/_context.reference_unit_duration_tiers`），response_schema 枚举与 prompt 候选取二者**并集**，落盘前在 `references` 从正文机械派生**之后**按该 unit 的引用状态判档位成员性、fail-loud。放弃的替代方案是让 LLM 自报引用状态——引用是从正文派生的，模型没有直接写它的余地，自报只会引入新的漂移面。
- **并集显式求，不拿其中一套当上界**。`constrain_durations` 在交集为空时回退到未收窄候选，型号同时声明「带图仅 8s」与「1080p 仅 6s」时带图那套反而更宽。注册表现状没有这种型号，但代码与 CONTEXT.md 都不写这条包含关系假设。
- **prompt 在两套档位不同时把两套都写全**，并在项目默认时长只对一种引用状态合法时点明其适用范围（如带图仅 8s 而项目默认 4s，避免模型把默认值套到带引用的 unit 上）。两套相同时整条不写——多数型号如此，多写一条无效约束只挤占注意力。
- **`get_video_capabilities` 补 `reference_unit_durations` 字段**。`split-reference-video-units` 的「手工改 step1」分支此前被指引按 `supported_durations`（**未**收窄的型号全集）取值，是既存的契约漂移；改后把服务端拆分工具用的同两套档位一并返回，让改写方与生成方对同一份数字。ad 项目不补该字段——其 unit 是从 `shots[]` 派生的轻量索引、镜头时长不受档位枚举管辖。
- **原 `duration > max_duration` 检查被档位成员性判定取代**：`max_duration` 现在派生自并集最大值，不可能小于任一并集成员，那条检查已不可达；档位成员性是更强的判定。

## 待决设计项定论：剧集脚本侧档位收敛 —— 保持现状

与 #1518 既有口径（存量走取档保护 + warning、从不静默改写用户编排真相）同构，不构成新取舍。论证写进 `lib/reference_video/duration_migration.py` 模块 docstring，四条依据：

1. 落盘时刻已必然在档——`ScriptGenerator._add_metadata` 按最终 references 逐 unit 取档，出档直接报错；偏移只可能来自事后改模型 / 改分辨率。
2. 偏移后没有脏值能到供应商——预检与执行都会重新取档并出 warning，执行期实际申请的秒数写回 task payload 供 resume 读取，脚本本身不动。
3. 回写与全仓策略冲突——出档一律「fail-loud 或 warning + 引导重选」；且预检是 GET 读路径，在其上写盘不可接受。
4. 加载期回写另有硬阻——`load_script` 同步、无 DB 会话，拿不到档位表。

即：结构区间 clamp 负责脏数据兜底，档位级偏移由消费点取档保护承担，两者分工是终局。

## 验证

- `uv run ruff check .` / `ruff format --check` 通过
- `uv run basedpyright` 0 error
- `uv run python -m pytest` 7343 passed
- 新增测试覆盖：两套档位的求取与不假定包含关系、并集枚举、按引用状态的逐 unit 校验（含带引用 unit 取到仅无引用合法的秒数时 fail-loud）、非包含情形下 prompt 写全两套、默认时长的适用范围限定、ad 项目不返回该字段
- 未起 server、未写数据库，全程单测

## 已知薄弱点

- step2 被明确允许给 unit 新增 `@` 引用。一个 step1 无引用、取了较短档的 unit 若在 step2 获得引用，会在 `_add_metadata` 的逐 unit 取档处失败。该失效路径不是本 PR 新引入的——`_unit_duration_off_every_tier` 的 docstring 已声明这是既定取舍（提前判死会拦掉本会成功的生成），手工编辑 step1 同样可构造。
- 联动约束在注册表里只有 Veo 3.1 系列声明，且只在 720p 下与不带图档位不同；新 prompt 措辞的真机效果（模型是否真能按引用状态选档）未验收。
- `reference_unit_durations` 是新字段，subagent 是否照新 doc 改用它只能实跑才知道；旧 `supported_durations` 仍在返回值里（它是型号声明，不能删）。

## 改动面

只动 step1 拆分侧的档位注入与后校验，外加 `get_video_capabilities` 的字段增补。与 #1499 的同函数分工：本 PR 在 `split_reference_video_units` 内只碰 caps 解析段、prompt 构造段、`_build_reference_units_from_flat` 的校验器本体；`except` 失败分支与 `pm.file_lock` / `atomic_write_json` 写盘段一行未动。后合并者需注意的唯一接触点是 `_build_reference_units_from_flat` 的调用参数由 `max_duration` / `max_refs` 两个标量改为单个 `caps: ReferenceSplitCaps`。

author: sugarkrap
body:
`mb_menu_remove_menu()` open-codes the same per-item cleanup that `mb_menu_item_free()` does a few lines above it, and dropped exactly one line: the item's decoded icon image was never released. Every item with an icon leaked one `MBPixbufImage` each time a menu was torn down.

```c
      if (item->title)   free(item->title);
      if (item->info)    free(item->info);
      if (item->icon_fn) free(item->icon_fn);
+     if (item->img)     mb_pixbuf_img_free(mb->pb, item->img);
      free(item);
```

### Why this is safe

The item owns that image — every assignment to `->img` is a fresh `mb_pixbuf_img_new_from_file()` or `mb_pixbuf_img_scale()`, and the menu's shared default icons (`img_default_app` / `img_default_folder`) live on the `MBMenu` and are freed there, never handed to an item. So this is not a double free. `mb_menu_item_free()` has always done exactly this.

### Why it surfaced now

A menu is normally built once and torn down at exit, where the leak costs nothing. It stops being invisible as soon as something rebuilds a menu repeatedly — matchbox-panel's launcher now rebuilds on every open so the menu can't go stale (sugarkrap/matchbox-panel#3), which turned this into a steady leak on a 64 MB machine.

### Measured on hardware

Sharp Zaurus SL-C760, 64 MB, no swap. Panel menu opened 45 times, RSS of `mb-applet-menu-launcher` sampled every 15:

| | 0 | 15 | 30 | 45 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **before** | 4800 | 4976 | 5208 | 5384 KB |
| **after** | 4676 | 4740 | 4784 | 4816 KB |

Before: ~13 KB per rebuild, linear. After: ~3 KB per rebuild with shrinking increments (64, 44, 32). A further 45 rebuilds post-fix reached 4928 KB — the residual keeps decaying instead of tracking the rebuild count, i.e. a heap arena settling on its working set rather than this leak.

Cross-compiled for `arm-unknown-linux-uclibcgnueabi` and deployed to the board; the menu renders and operates normally with the freed images (icons still draw correctly across many rebuilds, including after a cold reboot).

author: ly4m
body:
Résout #21.

## Le constat

Sur desktop, la barre latérale précède le contenu dans le DOM : quatre liens de nav, quatre liens sociaux et le bouton de thème — **neuf arrêts au clavier avant le premier mot**, à chaque page, sans moyen de sauter. Sur mobile, le logo et le hamburger en font deux.

## Le traitement

Trois maquettes ont tourné sur le site réel (les deux layouts, les deux thèmes) : un panneau surgissant au coin, un bandeau pleine largeur, et celui-ci. Le lien d'évitement classique est une boîte en haut à gauche ; **le site n'utilise cette forme nulle part**.

Le retenu se lit comme le **premier item de la barre latérale** — rail laiton compris, calé sur la nav (rail à 1.5rem, texte à 2.25rem, juste au-dessus d'ACCUEIL) — et reste replié à zéro tant qu'il n'a pas le focus. Rien d'étranger n'apparaît jamais sur la page. Sur mobile, où la barre latérale n'existe pas, il se range sous l'en-tête fixe.

Replié via `line-height` et `opacity`, jamais `display:none` ni `visibility:hidden` — ces deux-là le sortiraient de l'ordre de tabulation, et le lien n'existerait plus pour personne.

## La cible

`<main id="contenu" tabindex="-1">` dans les deux layouts. Le layout est le seul endroit qui garantit le `<main>` sur les sept pages depuis c8979f4. Le `tabindex="-1"` est nécessaire : sans lui, Safari déplace la vue mais laisse le focus en haut de page, et la tabulation suivante repart dans la nav.

## Deux effets de bord réglés au passage

- **Pas d'anneau `:focus-visible`** sur le lien — il n'est à l'écran que *parce qu'*il a le focus, l'anneau ferait doublon avec le rail — ni sur `<main>`, où il encadrerait toute la colonne de contenu.
- **`scroll-behavior: auto` sous `prefers-reduced-motion`** : le `scroll-smooth` posé en dur sur `<html>` animait aussi le saut.

## Vérifié

- Tabulation réelle dans Chrome : premier arrêt = le lien ; `Entrée` → focus sur `MAIN#contenu` ; arrêt suivant = le premier article, dans `<main>`. Neuf arrêts ramenés à un.
- `pnpm build` vert ; les 15 pages portent le lien, un seul `<main>` chacune.
- `astro check` : 0 erreur. Prettier : propre.

## Pas vérifié

Safari et VoiceOver — le `tabindex="-1"` est posé pour Safari mais je ne l'y ai pas testé.

author: harikeshav-r
body:
## What & why

Adds `atlas.ai.api`: the **LiteLLM-backed API provider** and Atlas's default API
failover backend, **OpenRouter** (PROJECT.md §5.1a; the config + keyring work in
PR #9 unblocked this). A single `LiteLLMProvider` implements `LLMProvider` for
every hosted model backend, so adding a vendor is configuration, not code.

This completes both Phase 0 AI backends behind `LLMProvider` (Claude Code CLI +
OpenRouter API). What remains in the AI-provider roadmap item — the failover
chain, capability probing, and `atlas doctor` — is a separate follow-up PR.

## Design

LiteLLM sits behind **two injectable seams** so its heavy import never happens in
the hermetic test suite (AGENTS.md §6.2) and the API path stays swappable:

- **`CompletionFn`** (`client.py`) — the `litellm.completion` call boundary. Its
  default lazily imports `litellm` and hands it the **transport** retry layer
  (`num_retries`) plus `drop_params=True`. This is the transport/content retry
  split the design mandates: transport retries live here; **content** retries
  (bad/truncated JSON) stay in `complete_json()`.
- **`CapabilityFn`** (`capabilities.py`) — per-model schema-support lookup from
  LiteLLM's **registry, not hardcoded**, so `response_format` is requested only
  where the model supports it and `complete_json()` recovers structure from text
  otherwise.

The provider maps `LLMRequest` → chat messages, applies a per-provider **adaptive
timeout**, normalizes `ModelResponse` → `LLMResponse`/`Usage` (tokens + cost) via
defensive `getattr` (no LiteLLM types imported), and classifies failures by HTTP
status/message into `LLMAuthError`/`LLMRateLimitError`/`LLMTimeoutError`/
`LLMBackendError` with generic user-facing messages (no vendor diagnostics, URLs,
or secrets leaked). `build_openrouter_provider` resolves the key via
`resolve_api_key()` (keyring first, `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` fallback), passes it to
LiteLLM **directly, never via `os.environ`**, and prefixes the model for routing.

## Key commits

- `build(deps): add litellm for the API provider`
- `feat(ai): add LiteLLM API provider with OpenRouter backend`
- `docs: record OpenRouter/LiteLLM API backend and advance STATUS`

## Testing

- Reusable offline `FakeChatCompleter`/`FakeModelResponse`/`FakeLiteLLMError` test
  doubles in `conftest.py`; **no network and no `litellm` import in the suite**
  (it still runs in ~0.3s). An end-to-end seam test drives the provider through
  `complete_json()` via the text-recovery path.
- Sanity-checked the duck-typed response parser against a **real** `litellm`
  `ModelResponse` (via `mock_response`, no network) to confirm the fakes match.
- Gates green: `ruff format --check`, `ruff check`, `mypy --strict` (incl.
  `--platform win32`), `pytest` at **100% line + branch coverage**. Two justified
  `# pragma: no cover` on the real lazy-import boundaries.

## Notes

- No DB/schema changes; no migration needed.
- `docs/STATUS.md` + `docs/PROJECT.md` roadmap ticked; `CHANGELOG.md` updated.

author: jonaslagoni
body:
Closes #448 (split out of #447).

## The problem

An AsyncAPI document containing a recursive schema fails generation outright:

```
Could not dereference $ref in input, is all the references correct?
```

Three design points collide:

1. `@asyncapi/parser` inlines every non-circular `$ref`, but deliberately leaves a cycle as a literal `{"$ref": "#/components/schemas/Node"}`.
2. The CLI extracts a *fragment*, not the document — a message payload is re-rooted as a standalone draft-07 document, and the `components` section the pointer aims at is not carried along.
3. Modelina re-dereferences that fragment, resolves `#/components/schemas/Node` against something that has no `components` key, and throws.

Nothing needs to change in Modelina — `circular: true` is already set in its dereference options. The pointer target is genuinely absent from the fragment.

## The fix

A new pure helper, `src/codegen/inputs/asyncapi/refs.ts`, applied at each extraction site immediately after the fragment is assembled. Every surviving `#/components/schemas/X` is resolved one of two ways:

- **`X` is already inlined in this fragment** → rewrite the pointer to that copy's local JSON pointer (`#` for a single-message root, `#/oneOf/<i>` for a union member, `#/properties/<id>` for a v2 parameter).
- **`X` is not inlined anywhere** → rewrite to `#/definitions/X`, convert the component, stamp `$id: X`, hoist it into `definitions`, and recurse so transitive targets come along.

Both halves are load-bearing, and this was determined empirically rather than by preference:

| Document shape | Transform | Result |
|---|---|---|
| Self-recursion | `definitions` only | ❌ 2 models — `Node` *and* `NodeChildrenItem` |
| Self-recursion | local pointer → `#` | ✅ 1 model `Node { children?: Node[] }` |
| Mutual recursion | local pointer only | ❌ target misnamed `Ab` after the use site |
| Mutual recursion | local pointer + `definitions` + `$id` | ✅ 2 models `A`, `B` |
| Union w/ recursive member | `definitions` | ❌ 4 models, one name duplicated |
| Union w/ recursive member | local pointer → `#/oneOf/N` | ✅ 3 models, no duplicates |

Duplicate class names in one output file are broken code, not cosmetic noise — hence the two-way split.

The walk is **copy-on-write**. The extraction sites rebuild only the top level of a fragment; nested nodes stay shared with the parser's document tree, so an in-place rewrite would corrupt every other extraction site and `filter.ts`. There is a dedicated regression test for this.

## Sites covered

| Site | Inlined-target map |
|---|---|
| `payloads.ts` single message | `{<root x-parser-schema-id> → '#'}` |
| `payloads.ts` `oneOf` union | `{<member id> → '#/oneOf/<i>'}` |
| `headers.ts` single message / channel union | same two shapes |
| `parameters.ts` (AsyncAPI v2) | `{<param schema id> → '#/properties/<id>'}` |

The plan left headers and parameters as open questions. Both were checked against the parsed model and **both reproduce the failure**, so both are wired rather than documented as non-reproducing. v3 Parameter Objects carry no `schema`, so only v2 documents can reach that path.

## Not a breaking change

The transform is gated on the presence of a surviving `#/components/schemas/` pointer; without one the fragment is returned *by identity*. Documents that hit this bug currently produce no output at all, so there is no working output to break.

Verified rather than asserted: `git diff --numstat` over every snapshot file shows **0 deleted lines** — only new snapshots from the new fixtures, no pre-existing snapshot modified.

## Verification

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `npm test` | 72 suites, 911 passed, 96 snapshots |
| `npm run test:blackbox` | 230/230 (was 215 — the new fixture × 15 configs) |
| `npm run runtime:typescript` (recursive spec) | 5/5 |
| `npm run prepare:pr` | passes end to end |
| Pre-existing snapshots modified | none |
| Issue reproduction | generates `children?: NodeMessage[]` on a single model |

Coverage added across all three tiers:

- **Unit** — `refs.spec.ts` (local-pointer rewrite, `definitions` hoisting with `$id`, transitive collection, cycle termination, unknown component left alone, copy-on-write, no-pointer gate), plus recursive describe blocks in `payloads.spec.ts`, `headers.spec.ts` and a new `parameters.spec.ts`. The integration tests assert **exact model counts and no duplicate names**, since the duplicate-class failure mode shows up only as an extra model with a repeated name.
- **Blackbox** — `recursive-asyncapi.yml` carrying self-recursion, mutual recursion and a recursive union member in one document, so the output has to type-check.

author: infohata
body:
Compounded from a staged rollout of a matching-rule change against a third-party datastore.

## Added — `skills/deployment/references/DARK_DEPLOY_KILL_SWITCH.md`

The **dark → shadow → live** ladder and what each rung actually proves.

**The headline trap: a kill switch's OFF position must be faithful PER CALL SITE.** Three call sites were collapsed behind one helper — but two matched records on a single field and the third matched on that field *plus two others*. A single `legacy` path in the helper would have silently **loosened** the third site, in the direction that fuses distinct records, while presenting as:

- switch says `off`
- "no behaviour change"
- tests green — they were written against the *helper's* notion of legacy
- dark deploy quiet, because the paths are low-volume

Nothing would have surfaced until data was already wrong. Fix: make the legacy selector an explicit per-site argument.

Also covers: rollback stops future writes but **cannot unwind past ones**; never leave two hosts running different write policies against one datastore (dark/shadow are safe everywhere at once, live is per-dataset with all its hosts together); and shadow-that-logs-only-disagreements makes silence ambiguous between *never ran*, *ran and agreed*, and *logging broken*.

## Changed — `skills/shell/references/MAINTENANCE_SCRIPT_CONTRACT.md`

Five siblings to the existing fail-closed `--verify` section, each from a real miss:

| Lesson | The miss |
|---|---|
| **Break the TARGET, not the input** | Breaking the input tripped pre-flight, so the restore path never ran — and the test was reported as a pass |
| **Error paths obey the happy path's contract** | A stage-lint-rename installer restored with a plain `cp` over the live file |
| **Verify the file you edited, never a glob** | A glob hit an unrelated file broken since 2021; `&&` short-circuited and the real check never ran |
| **A zero needs a positive control** | "No matches" is worthless unless the same method demonstrably produces a hit |
| **Prove a log line LANDS first** | Default log destination is a property of the *host config*, not the language |

That last one nearly cost the most: one host recorded, the other discarded — and the discarding host carried ~98% of the traffic, so silence would have read as *"no differences found"*.

## Changed — `skills/compound/` branch policy

**"Stay on the feature branch" now requires that branch to still have an open PR.**

A checkout left on a branch whose PR merged weeks ago is the normal resting state — the merge happens on GitHub and nothing moves local HEAD back. Committing onto it is worse than branch spam: dead ref, stale base for the self-mode version bump, and it reads as success.

**This run hit exactly that** — the checkout sat on a branch merged 2026-07-27. Reuse the *review surface*, not the branch name.

## Housekeeping

Self-mode patch bump to **v5.4.8**; manifest and CHANGELOG asserted equal, and the diff adds a new `## v` section rather than appending into the released one.

## Summary
- The `path` subtest of `test_worktree_target_snapshot_detects_byte_mode_and_path_races` recreated its target with byte-identical content and asserted the worktree identity guard would detect it — a property no host guarantees, so it failed on hosts with coarse inode timestamps and ext4 inode reuse (e.g. WSL2) while passing on CI.
- The guard genuinely cannot discriminate an unlink+recreate that reuses the inode within one coarse timer tick with identical content — but such a replacement is harmless, because the analyzed bytes are unchanged and the loader's payload compare is what guarantees them.
- Resolution: accept that limitation as by-design and document it at the guard, and rewrite the subtest to recreate with *different* content, a real path race the payload compare catches deterministically on every host.

## Changes
**`lib/test/pin-corpus-lint.py`**: Added a docstring to `_worktree_path_identity` stating exactly what the `(st_dev, st_ino, st_mode, st_size, st_mtime_ns, st_ctime_ns)` identity tuple detects, and a "By-design limitation" paragraph explaining why a same-inode, same-coarse-tick, byte-identical recreate is indistinguishable and harmless — the payload compare in the loader's `verify()`, not the identity tuple, is the guarantee that the analyzed bytes are the on-disk bytes.

**`lib/test/test_pin_corpus_lint.py`**: The `path` subtest now recreates the target with different content (`"REPLACED\n"` instead of the identical `"TOKEN\n"`), so `verify()` catches the race via the payload/`st_size` compare regardless of the host's inode-reuse or timer-tick behavior.
