author: chaedirdwiantara
body:
Menambahkan PPN pada Rental Monitoring dan invoice.

## Keputusan pajak
- **DPP = sewa + biaya tambahan.** Biaya tambahan yang ditagihkan ulang di faktur yang sama secara pajak adalah bagian dari **Penggantian** jasa sewa, bukan transaksi terpisah. Memisahkannya hanya sah untuk reimbursement murni atas nama pelanggan — syarat yang praktis tidak terpenuhi untuk tol/bensin mobil sendiri.
- **Deposit di luar PPN** — itu jaminan, bukan penggantian.
- **11%** adalah beban efektif untuk JKP non-mewah. Sejak PMK 131/2024 tarif nominalnya 12% atas DPP nilai lain 11/12 dari harga jual, yang hasil rupiahnya identik. Dokumen kita adalah invoice komersial (bukan faktur pajak), jadi menulis "PPN 11%" sudah tepat.

## Perubahan
- `partners.is_pkp` + `npwp` — hanya PKP boleh memungut PPN. **Default FALSE**, jadi tidak ada partner yang mendadak memungut pajak sebelum sengaja dinyalakan.
- `rentals.ppn_rate_bps` **ditangkap saat baris ditulis**, bukan dibaca dari konstanta: perubahan tarif atau status PKP tidak boleh menulis ulang apa yang sudah ditagihkan. Rental yang belum dibayar membaca ulang status terkini; yang sudah dibayar membeku pada tarifnya.
- Rupiahnya tetap **diturunkan** seperti angka uang lain, sehingga PPN mengikuti pemotongan per bulan persis seperti `gross`.
- **`omset` dan `nettProfit` tidak memuat PPN** — itu titipan negara, bukan pendapatan. Dilaporkan terpisah lewat `paidPpn` / `paidTotalBilled` / `unpaidPpn`.
- Invoice PDF: baris DPP + PPN + Total, terbilang mengikuti total **setelah** pajak, NPWP penerbit di kop.
- Endpoint baru `GET|PUT /partner/portal/rentals/tax-settings`, dan kolom PPN + Total Tagihan di rekap xlsx/pdf.

## Verifikasi
- 8 unit test baru (DPP termasuk biaya tambahan & tanpa deposit, terbilang pasca-pajak, pembulatan ke rupiah bulat, non-PKP, PPN di luar omset/nett, PPN ikut clipping bulan).
- e2e: PPN hanya berlaku pada rental yang ditulis **setelah** PKP dinyalakan; `paidGross` tetap bersih dari PPN; NPWP bervalidasi.
- Migrasi aditif dengan default — aman untuk rolling deploy.
- Suite penuh hijau kecuali `test/import.e2e.spec.ts` yang sudah gagal di `master` sebelum perubahan ini.

round — 9 curated games with hotlinked provider covers, 5 tags, 4 seats and 2
finished sessions with votes — so a fresh clone has a real app to look at
instead of a blank Regal, an empty Chronik and empty Pokale.

```
seed-dev: seeded .devdata/data.json
  round     "Spieleabend (Demo)" — 9 games, 4 seats, 5 tags, 2 finished sessions
  account   dev@spielwirbel.invalid / spielwirbel-dev (local only)
  run       preview_start "dev-temp-data", or: DATA_DIR=.devdata npm start
```

## Why it is a wrapper, not a second seeder

`lib/demo.js`'s `seedTenant()` already builds exactly this round through the
ordinary repo mutators. Reimplementing those steps in the script would give the
dev seed its own copy to rot — the failure mode
`.claude/rules/shared-constants-across-the-stack.md` is about — so the script
wraps the real thing and inherits any change to the demo's shape for free.

The issue suggested composing the repo calls directly instead, on the grounds
that `seedTenant()` assumes an accounts-mode tenant. That turned out not to
hold: it takes the tenant and owner id as arguments and works unchanged against
`'default'`.

## The dev account (a decision the issue left open)

The round belongs to the `'default'` tenant, which an unauthenticated caller
resolves to in open mode — but the committed `dev-temp-data` launch config runs
with `ACCOUNTS_ENABLED=true`, where `/api` is Bearer-only, so there the seed
would sit invisible behind the auth UI and registering would mint a *fresh empty*
tenant.

So the script also creates one local account whose own `tenantId` is `'default'`
(the legacy pre-tenancy user shape `lib/tenant.js` already supports). Logging in
as it resolves to the very same round — no second copy of the data, no
re-tenanting. Its credentials are deliberately worthless: they exist only inside
a gitignored throwaway dataset.

## Guards

Both refuse **before** requiring the store (which would `mkdir` the target and
read its file), and both are asserted to exit non-zero:

- the repo's default `data/`, which on a maintainer's machine can hold a real
  instance's private data — compared on the **resolved** path, so
  `DATA_DIR=data` and the absolute form are both caught;
- a target that already holds rounds or accounts, which would otherwise
  duplicate the round and collide on the dev account's e-mail.

## Tests

`test/seed-dev.test.js` drives the script as a child process (its whole contract
is what it does with `DATA_DIR`, which the JSON store resolves once at require
time). Six specs: the seeded shape, the account/tenant relationship, both
refusals, and the locale argument.

Each was seen **red for its own reason** — four deliberate breaks, each
reddening exactly one named test:

| Break | Red test |
|---|---|
| `data/` guard disabled | *refuses to seed the default data/ directory* + *…given as an absolute path* |
| already-holds-data guard disabled | *refuses a target that already holds data* |
| dev account gets a fresh tenant | *the seeded dev account can reach the seeded round in accounts mode* |
| sessions never finished (`lib/demo.js`) | *seeds a filled round into an isolated DATA_DIR* |

`npm test` (1320 pass), lint, syntax and `coverage:ci` all green. Verified
end-to-end in a browser on the `dev-temp-data` config: logged in through the real
form, and Shelf, History and Trophies all render populated (live rating averages
Ø 4.8–3.8 from the seeded votes, History attributed "by Du", Hall of Fame podium).

## Docs

`docs/configuration.md` (new subsection), `docs/architecture.md` (tree),
`CONTRIBUTING.md` (a "before you start" step) and one README line.
`scripts/resolve-demo-covers.js` was missing from the architecture tree — added
while editing that block.

Closes #530

author: konsong
body:
Closes #26. Closes #27.

Two tickets, one dependency between them: the card is what an operator reads about an address, and resolving what the address *is* is what stops the card being asked the wrong question.

## The account card (#26)

Every directory fact about the selected address, from **one** account read — a JVM start costs the same for five attributes as for twenty-five, so the card asks for everything it shows at once.

Absence is rendered as absence, in three different words because absence has three causes: `tanimsiz` (the directory carries no such value), `bilinmiyor` (this program could not read or parse one), `yok` (a list that is genuinely empty). Never a default, and **never zero** — Zimbra writes `zimbraMailQuota: 0` to mean unlimited, and an unknown limit is not no limit.

User-set and administrator-set forwarding stay on separate labelled lines. The administrator-set one is invisible to the account holder in their own client, which is exactly why an operator needs to see it, and why merging the two would hide the only one that is a compromise indicator.

## Address identity (#27)

`zmprov ga` on a distribution list answers `ERROR: account.NO_SUCH_ACCOUNT` — the same sentence, word for word, that an address existing nowhere produces. Measured on TEST-C, not assumed. An operator who reads the first as the second stops looking in the right place.

An address is now resolved when it is chosen, into five outcomes told apart: an account, an alias and the account behind it, a calendar resource, a distribution list, or nothing anywhere in the directory.

- **Bounded at two directory reads, cost class 1, asserted as the number it is.** `ga` already resolves an alias to its account and already returns a resource as the account Zimbra stores it as, so three of the five outcomes cost one invocation. That is why `gcr` is not on the allowlist and `gdl` is.
- **Absence returns 0** — it is something this program learned. A question it could not ask returns why. The list read runs only when Zimbra itself said there is no such account, so a stopped service, an invalid certificate and a refused authentication each keep their own code, and none of them can reach the operator as *"this address does not exist"*.
- **An identity nobody could establish marks nothing.** Marking an entry from a failed resolution would report this program's ignorance as a fact about the server.
- **Menu scope becomes three-valued.** `account` needs the address to *be* an account; `address` needs one of any kind, because mail to a list appears in the transfer agent's log under the list's own address and a trace answers there exactly as it does for a mailbox; `server` needs none.

## Evidence

Every behavioural claim above was captured from TEST-C rather than recalled, including one calendar resource created there because none existed:

- `docs/research/2026-08-02-account-card-attributes.md`
- `docs/research/2026-08-02-address-identity.md`
- `docs/adr/0004-address-identity-before-account-scope.md`

## Known gap

*"A distribution list … routes to the list screen"* is met in its negative half only: the list screen is #30, which this PR unblocks. Until it lands, choosing an account operation for a list address shows what the address is. What it never shows is "no such account".

## Verification

ShellCheck clean across the tree, tests included. 28 files, 2021 assertions, 0 failures under WSL.

author: zechengz
body:
Phase 2 core of the CLI/resource separation: `CLISpec`, one node of a program tree, as a subclass of `CommandSpec` (argparse's parser/subparser as data, click's Group-is-a-Command). A leaf carries `fn`, a group carries `subcommands`, the root may carry `config_model`; grammar fields are inherited, so every tree level parses with the existing spec machinery, and group-level options need no special case.

- Python `mirage/commands/cli/types.py` + TS `commands/cli/types.ts`: the subclass with import-time validation (single-word name, fn XOR subcommands, no positional/rest on groups, unique child names, config_model root-only).
- Leaf handlers receive the installation's validated config instance: `fn(config, paths, *texts, **flags)`. No accessor factory; what the fn does with the config is the author's business.
- TS base accommodations: `CommandSpecInit` widened to instance types so `new CommandSpec({...spec, ...})` mirrors `dataclasses.replace` (fixes the hand-listed `withHelpSupport` rebuild that silently dropped new fields from `--help`), and `Object.freeze` guarded with `new.target` so the subclass can exist.
- `@command`, `RegisteredCommand`, and all builtin specs untouched.

Tests: 9 pytest + 10 vitest covering the tree build, group-level options, and each validation error.

body:
## 概要

セッション 06: AUTH_SPEC の本実装(D1 + Drizzle、GitHub OAuth web/device、セッション / トークン)、チェーン API へのリクエスト認証の結線と認可(AUTH_SPEC §11 として仕様化)、統合テストの認証込み全面改修。

セッション中の AskUserQuestion で所有者裁定 4 件 + 確認 2 件を取得済み(裁定内容は `docs/notes/session-06.md` §2 と AUTH_SPEC §11 に記録)。PR #14 時点の既知の制約(リクエスト認証なし・チェーン取得全公開・org 未連携)は全て解消。

## 仕様 § ↔ ファイル ↔ テスト対応表

| 仕様 | 実装 | テスト |
|---|---|---|
| AUTH_SPEC §2 データモデル | `apps/server/src/db.package/schema.ts` + `drizzle/`(migration) | auth.test.ts(DB 行の直接検証)|
| §1-5 getOrCreateUser / §9-1 パーソナル org | `db.package/repos.ts`(atomic batch + 競合再ルックアップ)| auth.test.ts「creates the user + personal org」「is idempotent」|
| §3 Web ログイン(state 検証・トークン即時破棄)| `api-schema/src/auth-api.ts` + `apps/server/src/handlers-auth.ts` + `auth.package/github.ts` | auth.test.ts「githubStart / githubCallback」(state 不一致・code 交換失敗含む)|
| §4 Device Flow 交換 | 同上(`deviceExchange`)| auth.test.ts「device/exchange」|
| §5 セッション(256-bit・ハッシュのみ・`__Host-`・スライディング 30 日・ログアウト)| `auth.package/session.ts` + logout ハンドラ | auth.test.ts「logout」「期限切れ」「スライディング更新」|
| §5 CSRF(custom header をミドルウェアで一括)| `api-schema/src/auth-middleware.ts` + `auth.package/middleware.ts` | auth.test.ts / membership.test.ts の CSRF 系 |
| §6 トークン(maruhi_pat_ + Base62・SHA-256・タイミング安全・スコープ・自トークン失効)| `auth.package/token.ts` + `packages/core/src/auth.ts`(スコープ表現)| auth.test.ts「token/revoke」、membership.test.ts のスコープ系 |
| §8 サービス構成 | `packages/core/src/auth.ts`(境界)+ `apps/server/src/index.ts`(env 単位の結線)| 全統合テストが実経路を通過 |
| §11-1 actor 厳密一致 | `apps/server/src/authz.ts` | membership.test.ts「actor-mismatch」×2 |
| §11-2 非メンバー一律 404 | `chain-do.ts`(ChainState 導出 + not-member)+ `handlers-membership.ts` | membership.test.ts「conceals …」「removed members …」「スコープ外 404」|
| §11-3 org 連携・冪等修復 | `handlers-membership.ts`(init)+ `db.package/repos.ts`(OrgRepo / ProjectRepo)| membership.test.ts「org 連携」「repairs a missing projects row」|
| §11-4 エンドポイント配置(全部 api-schema)| `api-schema/src/auth-api.ts` / `membership-api.ts` | — |
| CRYPTO_SPEC §6.2 / §9-2(min(スコープ, チェーン role))| `authz.ts`(スコープ半分)+ verifyChain(チェーン半分。変更なし)| membership.test.ts の negative ベクター再生(insufficient-role 系は従来どおり 422)|

## レビューガイド(推奨順)

1. **`docs/AUTH_SPEC.md` の差分(§6 追記 + §11 新設)** — 裁定 4 件の仕様化。以降の実装はすべてここから導かれます
2. **`packages/core/src/auth.ts`** — 認証境界。旧 `apps/server/src/auth.ts` の移動先(HttpApi ミドルウェアの `provides` が参照するため core へ)
3. **`packages/api-schema/`** — AuthMiddleware 契約・auth グループ・401/403/400 エラー型・membership の認証必須化
4. **`apps/server/src/db.package/`** — Drizzle 採用の確定形。effect-d1 不採用の理由はコミットメッセージ / session-06.md §2 参照(rc.4 は transaction / batch 未対応 → getOrCreateUser の原子性が成立しない)
5. **`apps/server/src/auth.package/`** — OAuth ダンス・セッション・トークン・CSRF。GitHub トークンがメモリ外に出ないことを重点確認
6. **`apps/server/src/chain-do.ts`** — メンバーシップ判定を CAS より先に置いた理由(非メンバーへ現ヘッド情報を漏らさない)と ChainState キャッシュ
7. **`apps/server/src/handlers-membership.ts` + `authz.ts`** — 認可の判定順(413 → actor 403 → スコープ → org → DO)
8. **テスト** — actor-not-member 系 negative の期待値が 422 → 404 に変わった点(§11-2 の帰結。チェーン合意規則としての検証は crypto ベクターが継続担保)

## 検証

- `bun run check` 全通過(oxfmt / oxlint / tsc / ImportLint / fallow / React Doctor / テスト 226 件)
- `wrangler deploy --dry-run` 成立(D1 binding / vars 解決)
- 新規依存: drizzle-orm / drizzle-kit 1.0.0-rc.4(完全ピン。理由はコミットメッセージ)

## スコープ外(意図的)

CLI 本体、Web ダッシュボード(トークン管理 UI 含む)、監査ログ実装(AUDIT_SPEC 承認待ち)、リカバリーコード、grant_server、リカバリーブロブのレート制限設計(未着手の optional 項目)、`packages/crypto` の変更(なし)

author: gaoxiaobei
body:
## Summary

Reworks the 23rd DOTO integration from a framework-owned LLM harness loop into a **Codex-orchestrated benchmark built from versioned Skills and deterministic atomic tools**.

Codex now decides which public-training evidence to inspect, what complete `playerAI.cpp` child to create, whether another iteration is justified, and which complete training version to select. AgentBenchFramework no longer owns an API client or automatic LLM iteration loop.

## What changed

### Harness → four Codex Skills

- `doto-benchmark-run`: authoritative Run lifecycle, training selection, one-shot finalization, validation, and export
- `doto-game-rules`: official mechanics, observations, legal macro-actions, action mask, terminal states, and strict KL support
- `doto-agent-authoring`: fixed native SDK contract and safe complete `playerAI.cpp` authoring
- `doto-replay-reader`: replay/trace schemas, events, evidence joins, and diagnosis

The old `llm_client.py`, `loop.py`, `loop_config.py`, `doto loop` command, loop example, and loop tests are removed. Build, match, replay, evaluation, IG, and lifecycle interfaces remain available for Codex to call.

### Human population and evaluation

- freezes 43 complete human-policy identities at benchmark version `doto-human-43-v1`
- deterministic seed-11 split: 15 public training snapshots and 28 sealed hidden-test snapshots
- packages the 15 public source snapshots in one path-safe archive to keep the PR reviewable while preserving complete-source hashes
- evaluates both candidate seats
- public matrix: 30 cells; hidden matrix: 56 cells
- a human counts as defeated only when both seats terminate normally and candidate-oriented mean score difference is positive
- adaptive multiprocess scheduler targets 70% aggregate CPU with an optional worker hard cap; running matches are never cancelled

### Atomic authoritative lifecycle

The `run` and `iteration` commands provide explicit state transitions:

1. initialize and snapshot source, pool identities, and exact Skills;
2. build an iteration;
3. run/resume the complete public matrix;
4. record strict IG or an exact missing reason;
5. close the iteration and align score/IG curves;
6. durably select a training candidate;
7. finalize the sealed hidden matrix exactly once;
8. validate and export the compatibility projection.

Completed cells are immutable. Build failures, timeouts, crashes, protocol errors, corrupt evidence, missing cells, and incomplete matrices remain explicit rather than being converted into ordinary losses or valid scores.

### Metrics and Results

DOTO's continuous joint action space keeps strict deterministic KL semantics:

- identical canonical actions: `0`;
- different deterministic supports: `infinite`, stored with numeric `value: null` and a reason;
- unavailable or invalid comparison: `missing` with an exact reason.

No score gain, coordinate distance, or action-change rate is relabeled as IG.

author: ethenotethan
body:
## Why the mouse still needs click-and-drag after #156

#156 fixed the **host** side: clicks through HUD overlays now capture the pointer, and Escape is two-stage in the expanded overlay. But the symptom persists in fullscreen worlds — you have to click-and-drag to look around — because the **generated page code** implements drag-orbit as its primary camera scheme.

The failure sequence:

1. Host locks the pointer on your first click (working as designed)
2. Cursor disappears, mouse deltas start flowing as `movementX`/`movementY`
3. The world's camera code ignores them — it listens for `mousedown` + `mousemove` drag gestures
4. A locked pointer can never produce a drag, so nothing moves until you Esc out and drag with the visible cursor

No host fix can save a world authored against the wrong input model. The generation has to change.

## The fix

Render contracts live in the client prompt — the gateway teaches the agent nothing about Portal's surfaces (`appFormattingPrompt` is where chart/map/graph envelopes already live). It now documents the input contract interactive `html` artifacts run under:

- **Look/turn** reads `event.movementX`/`movementY` while `document.pointerLockElement` is set; click-and-drag must NEVER be the primary camera scheme (an unlocked-state fallback is fine)
- **Movement** is WASD + arrow keys via `keydown`/`keyup` on `document` with a held-keys Set — canvas focus isn't guaranteed, key repeat isn't reliable
- **Escape belongs to the host** (first press releases the mouse, second exits) — don't bind it
- Don't call `requestPointerLock()` from click handlers — the host already requests it from the first trusted click
- **HUD overlays** are `pointer-events: none` unless they're real buttons

## Testing

`FormattingPromptTests` pins the load-bearing phrases (`movementX`, `pointerLockElement`, the click-and-drag prohibition, `Do not bind Escape`, `pointer-events: none`) so the contract can't silently drift out of the prompt while the host-side capture code keeps assuming it.

Full gate green: `make build` ✅ · `make lint` 0 violations ✅ · baseline shrank ✅ · `swift test` 774 tests / 126 suites ✅

**Note:** this fixes newly generated worlds. Existing 3D artifacts were authored with drag controls baked in — regenerate them (ask the agent to "update the world to use pointer-lock mouse look") to pick up the contract.

author: damian1000
body:
## What

Render the quote eyebrow and the symbol picker as DOM nodes with `textContent`
instead of assembling HTML strings.

## Why

Two `innerHTML` assignments interpolated strings that come from the upstream quote
provider, not from us, with no escaping:

```js
`${q.name} · ${q.exchange} · ${q.currency} ` + ...        // eyebrow
`<option value="${s.symbol}">${s.name}</option>`          // symbol picker
```

`name`, `exchange` and `currency` are Yahoo's `longName`/`shortName`,
`fullExchangeName` and `currency` fields. A value carrying markup was rendered as
markup, and the `option value="..."` case sits inside a quoted attribute, which is
the easier of the two to break out of.

This is not a hypothetical about a malicious upstream so much as a boundary the
page should hold regardless: the browser should never be asked to decide whether a
third party's instrument name is text or markup.

## What was deliberately left alone

Four `innerHTML` sites remain and are correct as they stand:

- `tape-empty` is a static literal with no interpolation.
- The tape and both ladders interpolate only `price2(...)`, `qty(...)` and
  `time(...)`. `price2` is `parseFloat(s).toFixed(2)`, `qty` is
  `toLocaleString` on a number, and `time` formats an epoch millisecond value —
  each produces a numeric string regardless of its input, so no provider text can
  reach them.

Churning those to nodes would add ceremony without closing anything, so the diff
stays on the two paths that actually carry foreign text.

## Testing

- `./gradlew --no-daemon spotlessCheck clean build` — BUILD SUCCESSFUL, including
  the Prettier and ESLint pass over the web assets.
- `node --check app/src/main/resources/web/app.js` — parses.
- `replaceChildren` accepts a mix of strings and nodes (strings become text
  nodes), so the eyebrow keeps its exact previous layout: plain text, a
  `pos`/`neg` span for the move, then plain text.

author: kevinlourd
body:
## Why now

brand-service's `staging` has **retired the goal from the declared-funnel payload** and **renamed the four funnel keys** (brand-service#434, migration `0054`). Promoting it to prod as it stands takes the Sales Funnels settings card down.

Verified on both sides:

| | this app, `origin/main` (= prod) | brand-service `origin/staging` |
|---|---|---|
| `goal` | `z.string()` **required** | **removed** |
| `currentGoal` | `z.string()` **required** | **removed** |
| `funnelKey` | enum of the 4 old keys | renamed to `sales_meetings_from_conversation` / `sales_meetings_from_website` / `website_purchases` / `form_magnet` |

Three simultaneous mismatches → `safeParse` throws → the card dies.

`lib/sales-funnels.ts` already carried both key spellings and `normalizeSalesFunnelKey`. **This file kept its own private list of the four old keys** and never got them — the same two-lists drift the retirement exists to end, one module apart.

## What changes

- **`funnelKey` accepts both spellings and normalises in** — on the declared-funnel reader *and* on `FunnelBudgetRowSchema`. A per-funnel budget row is keyed on the funnel too, so the rename reaches it; leaving the old keys pinned there drops every budget row on promote day. That one is easy to miss — it is 350 lines from the funnel reader.
- **`goal` / `currentGoal` become `.optional()`.** Nothing branches on them, so tolerating their absence costs nothing. Delete them outright once no brand-service in any environment still sends them.
- The runtime import of `normalizeSalesFunnelKey` does not create a cycle: `sales-funnels.ts` reads this module with `import type`, which is erased, so the edge only runs one way.

## Ordering — this wave is the other direction

The earlier waves of this migration were **additive**, so the producer could ship first and consumers caught up (that is how #3219 and brand-service v0.63.0 went). This one **removes fields**, so it inverts: every reader has to tolerate their absence *before* the producer promotes.

**features-service is the other blocker and is NOT ready** — `src/lib/declared-funnels.ts` reads `funnel.goal` then `funnel.currentGoal` and throws `UnknownFunnelGoalError` with neither, on `origin/main` *and* `origin/staging` (zero drift between them). brand-service#434's own body flags it: goal-arbitration 502s, and campaign-service fail-softs, so the visible symptom is the Strategy ranking rather than stopped campaigns. That needs its own PR before the promote.

## Blast radius

None today. brand-service prod still sends the old shape and it still parses.

189 test files / 2151 tests green, `tsc` clean apart from the one documented pre-existing `TS1501`.

Refs #3214 · brand-service#434

author: kurokouji
body:
Builds on #19 (wired LAN). Merge that first.

## Summary

Publish the vendor camera runtime's already-encoded frames over RTSP **without re-encoding**:

```
iCamera_app -> libvideo-hook.so (LD_PRELOAD) -> v4l2loopback -> v4l2rtspserver -> client
```

- `atomcam2-video-hook`: preloaded into `iCamera_app` only, intercepts `local_sdk_video_set_encode_frame_callback` and mirrors frames into the loopback device before handing them to the vendor callback
- `atomcam2-v4l2loopback`, `v4l2cpp`, `v4l2rtspserver`: Buildroot packages (video only — this kernel has OSS, not ALSA)
- `atomcam2-video-loopback`: loads the module from `atomcam2-pre-run`, before the vendor runtime starts
- `RtspServer` GenServer + `atomcam2-rtsp-server` script: opt-in through `/data/atomcam2-rtsp/auto-start.conf`, follows the vendor camera runtime and stops when it does

## The memory fix worth reviewing

v4l2loopback derives `sizeimage` from raw geometry even for compressed formats, so 1080p reserved **7.91 MiB per buffer** for frames that are tens to hundreds of kilobytes. That size lands twice: v4l2loopback allocates `buffer_size * max_buffers`, and v4l2rtspserver assigns it to live555's `OutPacketBuffer::maxSize`, which every sink and filter then allocates. On this 87 MiB board it exhausted memory as soon as a server attached — the whole userspace went unresponsive.

`0002-honour-compressed-sizeimage.patch` lets a writer that knows its own bitrate bound the allocation. Callers leaving `sizeimage` at zero are unaffected.

## Hardware verification

- **1920x1080 H.264**, `rtsp://<camera>:8554/video0_unicast`, ~18 fps, ~950 kbps, verified by decoding the received stream (IDR 14 + non-IDR 262 over 15 s)
- 640x360 H.265 on `/dev/video1` also verified
- Starts automatically at boot after the vendor runtime comes up; stops automatically when the vendor runtime stops
- Vendor runtime stays healthy throughout (`result=running`, zero encoder errors)
- RSS with all three running: BEAM 30.5 MB, `iCamera_app` 20.5 MB, `v4l2rtspserver` 4.2 MB

## Notes for reviewers

- **Only create the loopback nodes you publish.** Three nodes (two at 1080p) exhaust memory; the example README says so explicitly
- `RtspServer` has 6 tests covering start, wait, follow-the-vendor stop, disable, and non-looping start failure
- `precheck` reports loopback availability but does not block — RTSP is optional
- `docs/20260802_RTSP配信メモリ制約_技術相談.md` records the diagnosis in full, including what did not work

body:
## Brief requirements addressed

- Ensure RSS/Atom podcast enclosures are actually usable by the asynchronous media worker.
- Support signed or extensionless enclosure URLs without forcing `yt-dlp` to interpret the feed URL again.
- Preserve SSRF, DNS-rebinding, duration, and output validation boundaries.

## Deliberately not addressed

- This PR does not add a new provider, credentials, queue service, or browser playback claim.
- It does not remove the `yt-dlp` fallback for podcast pages and sources without a resolver-marked enclosure.
- It does not change the public annotation or media API shape beyond the existing `provider`/`mediaUrl` fields.

## Implementation and migration notes

- `resolveSource` marks generic podcast HTML sources with `provider: "podcast"` when it extracts an embedded media URL.
- `resolveInput` passes a podcast provider enclosure directly to FFmpeg even when the URL has no media filename extension, after `parseSourceUrl` and `assertPublicUrl` validation.
- Direct-media URLs and non-enclosure provider sources retain their existing paths.
- No migration or API version change is required.

## Validation

```text
node --test test/source-processing.test.js                    # 12 pass
for file in test/*.test.js except api-acceptance.test.js      # 65 pass, 1 explicit integration skip
npm run build                                                  # passed
npm run package:extension                                     # passed
node --check server/*.js src/*.js extension/*.js test/*.js scripts/*.js  # passed
git diff --check                                               # passed
```

The full local suite had already passed on the PR41 parent. On this PR, the
loopback API acceptance invocation was retried twice but the managed sandbox's
escalation reviewer timed out before launching it; the source/media and all
non-loopback tests passed. Hosted Node CI remains the complete clean-checkout
validation gate.

## Local setup

```bash
npm ci
npm run dev:server
```

Resolve an RSS/Atom source through `/api/sources/resolve`, publish a podcast
annotation, and configure the production `YTDLP_BIN`/FFmpeg runtime as described

author: iecg
body:
Follow-ups to #10, which shipped busy-awareness built only on the phone's calendar and recorded three limitations rather than fixing them.

## What was actually broken

**Refusing calendar access broke the intimacy propose screen.** Not degraded — broke. `suggestWindows` was fed only the device calendar, so with no permission the screen returned zero suggestions and showed a grant button. That reads as a broken app rather than a declined permission, and I under-described it last time as "no busy awareness".

**A `proposed` time was invisible to everything, including the app that proposed it.** `BOOKED` is `['scheduled']` on purpose — a time nobody has agreed to should not land in a shared calendar or fire a reminder — but the calendar was the only thing either app consulted. The one window most worth protecting from a double-booking was the one nothing knew about.

**Trip marks conveyed nothing.** Conflicts were judged over a plan's whole span, so a 14-night trip overlapped everything in the chip range and a single dentist appointment marked all fourteen days.

## Three sources, and why separating them matters

| Source | Needs permission? | Sees the other app? | Gated? |
|---|---|---|---|
| The app's own plans (already in `usePlans`) | no | no | never |
| The device calendar (`readBusyBlocks`) | yes | incidentally, neutral-labelled | never |
| The `plan_busy_times` view (new) | no | **yes** | in 2-2-2 only |

The first is free — both screens already hold their plans in a query — and it is most of the fix on its own. That leaves the view earning its place for exactly one thing: the other app's plans without calendar permission, which is precisely the crossing worth asking about.

## The view

```sql
create view public.plan_busy_times with (security_invoker = on) as
select couple_id, starts_at, ends_at from public.plans
where starts_at is not null and ends_at is not null
  and status in ('proposed', 'scheduled');
```

The schema's first view, so three things needed getting right and each fails silently in a different direction: without the grant it is unreadable (the default ACL hands out no SELECT and `auto_expose_new_tables` is off); without `security_invoker` it runs as its owner and sails past `plans_select_member`, handing every couple's schedule to everyone; with one column too many it stops being a redaction. All three are asserted in `tests/rls/`.

`createBusyRepository` **cannot take a domain** — not by convention but because there is no domain column to take one. Widening it means changing the view, in a migration, in review. That is a stronger guarantee than invariant 2 asks for, and `CLAUDE.md` now records it as the one deliberate exception.

It also deliberately does **not** join the realtime publication: views can't, and closing that would mean subscribing to `plans` — the exact thing #10's domain filter exists to prevent.

## The gate is asymmetric, and lives on the door

2-2-2 reads the feed only behind a device-local setting that starts **off**. Unlike the calendar path, a server feed shows occupied windows to a phone whose owner refused calendar access, and 2-2-2 is the app you'd hand to a friend. The intimacy app reads it unconditionally — what it discloses in that direction is that a date night is booked, and that app is behind the lock.

The gate sits inside the hook that owns the repository, not on a screen. My first pass put it in the screen; the guard test caught that a second consumer could forget it, so it moved. Even switched on it reveals times and never what fills them.

## Departure-day conflicts

Moving the departure day moves the whole window, so a clash on night six travels with it. The clash a different chip can actually fix is the one on the day you leave. Date nights are hours, not nights, so nothing changes for them. `rangeFor` still produces what gets saved — a chip can never disagree with the booking.

## `BOOKED` is untouched

Adding `proposed` to it would have been the obvious move and was wrong: `sync.ts` shares that constant between calendar-writing and reminder-scheduling, so it would fire notifications about times nobody has agreed to. `BUSY_STATUSES` is its own set in `windows.ts` precisely because occupying time and earning a calendar entry are different claims.

## Verification

- `npm run lint`, `npm run typecheck` — clean
- `npm test` — **252 passed**, including new `busyFromPlans` and busy-repository suites plus i18n parity
- `npm run db:test` — **88 passed** against the real migrations; this one genuinely exercises the change, since the view is schema

New guards in `tests/guards/standalone.test.ts`: free/busy never rests on the device calendar alone, the 2-2-2 side is gated where the repository is built, the intimacy side is *not* gated, and no app names the view directly.

Not covered by automation: the simulator walk. Worth checking a refused-permission propose screen, a proposed window marking in 2-2-2 only after the toggle is on, and a 14-night trip marking only its departure days.

author: patrick-steve
body:
A CCA head sets how many people may book one interview slot. Default 1 — which is exactly today's behaviour, so this is inert until a head types a bigger number.

## The design

Occupancy is **derived, not stored**. The slot carries `capacity`; seats taken are the count of `CcaApplication` rows pointing at it. The slot's `bookedByUserID` / `bookedApplicationID` / `bookedAt` scalars are **deleted**.

That collapses a mirror rather than adding to one. The application pointer was already maintained alongside those scalars inside the same `withCcaLock` section, so this removes a source of truth instead of introducing a third. Two properties fall out:

- **"One application holds at most one seat" is structural** — the pointer is a single scalar and cannot be counted twice, so re-booking a slot you already hold is idempotent for free. The alternative design needed a unique index to buy this.
- **Every stale reader is a compile error**, not a silent "free" on a full slot. That's why the scalars are deleted outright rather than left unused.

Rejected alternatives, the full edge-case list and the settled decisions are in `docs/plans/cca/01-group-interview-slots.md`.

## Rules worth naming

| | |
|---|---|
| Lowering capacity below occupancy | refused — an edit never evicts anyone |
| Raising capacity | always allowed, re-opens a full slot immediately |
| Cancelling a group slot | reverts **every** occupant, one audit row |
| A partially filled slot | is not "free", never bulk-cleared |
| Residents see | seat counts + a "Group interview · up to N" label, never who else booked |

The occupancy helper projects `interviewSlotID` and nothing else, so no other applicant's row is loaded on a resident path. Over-booking is prevented by the existing per-CCA advisory lock — the same guarantee the single-seat claim already relied on.

## Migration — read before merging

`scripts/remediation/backfill-slot-capacity.mjs`, dry run by default, full pre-image backup, verifier alongside it (`verify-interview-slots.mjs`).

**It refuses to `--commit` while `cca.applications.enabled` is on.** The script snapshots both collections up front, so a reject landing mid-run would strand a seat that no re-run could detect or repair. Quiescing closes the window; `--allow-live` overrides and prints what it is risking.

Live dry run against production:

```
cca.applications.enabled: "on"  <- LIVE
CcaInterviewSlot: 34   canceled: 24   carrying claim FIELDS: 31   real claim: 1
CcaApplication:   78   with a slot pointer: 1
[1] slot <-> application agreement: 0 disagreement(s)
[2] capacity := 1 — to write: 34
[3] terminal applications holding a live future seat: 0
[4] $unset booked* — 31 (by $exists, the same predicate the statement uses)
projected occupancy: 1 slot occupied, 1 seat claimed, none over capacity
```

Deploy order: quiesce → dry run → `--commit` → `prisma db push` → verify → deploy → un-quiesce. **`prisma db push` has not been run**; it has silently dropped a non-schema index in this repo before, so the script prints both collections' index lists for diffing.

## Review

Three adversarial review rounds by an independent agent. Round 1 found a **critical** defect: the migration was destructive on a second `--commit` — after step 4 removed the claim scalars, a re-run reclassified every terminal application as a reject-orphan and nulled its pointer, with the gate unable to see it. Confirmed by hand against production data before fixing. Round 2 verified the fix by fault injection the implementer's own harness couldn't perform, and found that the fix converted a recoverable miss into a permanent one — which is where the quiesce guard came from. Round 3 items are all closed.

The application code was verified sound throughout: state machine transition by transition, lock placement on all four count-then-write paths, resident-path privacy, the authorisation chain on all six head procedures, capacity-edit guards.

`tsc --noEmit` clean, `next lint` clean. No tests — the repo has no test harness; the migration's idempotence was proved against an offline fixture reproducing production's exact census, which is not a substitute for the dry run above.

## Second commit

Two one-off remediation scripts, both already applied to production, kept for the same reason the rest of `scripts/remediation/` is. Note `fix-leia-duplicate.mjs`: it deletes by ObjectId and refuses `deleteUserCascade`, because the broken row stored the *other* account's `userID` — the cascade helper deletes bookings and memberships by that string, so the routine repair would have destroyed the real account and then removed both rows.

author: mashkovd
body:
## What

Adds `.github/workflows/pr-validation.yml`: a `tests` job that runs the
existing suite on every PR and on pushes to `main`, plus a Docker smoke build
gated behind it.

## Why

**This repository has 234 tests and nothing runs them.** `.github/workflows/`
contained only `claude-review.yml` and `release-please.yml`, so a change could
break the entire suite and still merge green. Of everything surfaced by the
recent architecture review, this was the highest-severity finding — higher
than the language question that prompted the review.

Verified locally before writing the workflow: `pytest -q` → **234 passed in
4.71s**. The suite is healthy; it was simply never wired to CI.

## Scope

Deliberately narrow — run the tests that already exist, on the current
dependency set. No dependency file changes, no linter, no new style
requirements. Those are separate follow-ups, so that a red run here is
unambiguous about its cause rather than a mix of "the tests broke" and "the
linter has opinions".

## Notes on specific choices

- **pytest is installed inline.** It is not in `requirements.txt`, which pins
  only the runtime harness. A follow-up moves both into a `pyproject.toml`
  dev dependency group with a lockfile, at which point this step becomes
  `uv sync --frozen`.
- **The Docker build is gated on the tests** (`needs: tests`) rather than run
  beside them. The image installs Node, the `gh` CLI and a ~210 MB SDK wheel,
  so it is far slower than the suite; this keeps fast feedback fast and skips
  a costly build when the tests are already red. It is a no-push smoke build —
  image publishing stays in mctl-gitops.
- **Actions are pinned by commit SHA**, matching `claude-review.yml` in this
  repository. It is public and handles GitHub App and OAuth tokens.
- **`cancel-in-progress` applies to pull requests only.** Runs on `main` are
  each the record for a distinct merged commit and should not be cancelled.
- **No Telegram notification.** Unlike `mctl-api`, this repository has no
  `TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN` or `TELEGRAM_CHAT_ID` secret (only `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`,
  `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN_2`, `GITOPS_TOKEN`), so the step would fail on its
  first use. Adding one requires provisioning those secrets and is out of
  scope. Worth noting it would only ever fire on `main` anyway — on PRs it is
  noise, since a developer may push several intermediate commits.

## This PR alone does not close the risk

Adding the workflow makes the tests *run*; it does not make them *required*.
Until the `tests` job is a required status check on `main`, a PR can still be
merged without it. That is a repository setting rather than a file, so it
needs a separate, explicit step — flagged here so it does not get lost.

## Verification

- [x] `pytest -q` locally → 234 passed
- [x] Workflow YAML parses; jobs resolve as `tests` and `docker-build (needs: tests)`
- [ ] CI green on this PR
- [ ] Deliberately broken test turns CI red (proves the gate actually works)
- [ ] `tests` set as a required status check, and merge blocked when it is
      failing **or skipped**

author: nickgrant
body:
## Summary

- Add a canonical Dice Material Catalog containing 32 enabled materials.
- Restrict the complete roster to the four currently active sizes: d4, d6, d8, and d10.
- Explicitly exclude d12, d20, and all other sizes from material eligibility, generation, migration, Codex presentation, inventory filters, and combat assumptions.
- Define rarity, allowed sizes, effect timing, stacking caps, valuation, salvage, tags, starter identity, and legacy-affix disposition for every material.
- Establish the standard material rarity profile after size-first generation: 60 Common, 25 Uncommon, 10 Rare, 4 Epic, and 1 Legendary relative weight.
- Define 8 Common, 8 Uncommon, 7 Rare, 5 Epic, and 4 Legendary materials.
- Preserve Peach Pit and Glass as prominent material identities while broadening the roster across offense, defense, healing, statuses, roll control, economy, timing, survival, and chaos.
- Make Cardboard the explicit neutral default material, valid on d4, d6, d8, and d10 with no special effect.
- Make Cardboard d4 the starter die identity while preserving Cardboard as the baseline option for every active size.
- Activate 32 material Codex pages and raise the complete current Codex from 67 to 99 canonical keys.
- Reconcile combat order, status sources, die rewards, Gold reward markers, and dice-inventory UX with the material model.

## Size coverage

| Size | Materials |
| --- | ---: |
| d4 | 15 |
| d6 | 24 |
| d8 | 24 |
| d10 | 15 |

The difference in pool breadth does not change size frequency because generation remains size-first.

## Material highlights

- **Baseline:** Cardboard is neutral, explicit, valid on every active size, and never represented by missing material data.
- **Healing:** Peach Pit, Bloodstone, Worldroot.
- **Risk-reward:** Glass, Lead, Porcelain.
- **Roll control:** Copper, Clay, Rubber, Voidstone, Star Metal.
- **Status interaction:** Amber, Salt, Sporewood, Moonstone, Rusted Iron.
- **Explosive and chaos effects:** Powder Keg and Chaos Shard.
- **Survival:** Phoenix Ash and Living Bone.
- **Economy:** Gold creates capped, deterministic, victory-only Teeth markers.

## Legacy affix disposition

- `atk_plus` → Bone
- `guard_plus` → Iron when size-compatible
- `bulwark_plus` → Lead when size-compatible
- `precision_plus` → Brass when size-compatible
- `execute_below_half` → Butcher's Tooth on d8/d10
- `explode_once` → Powder Keg on d4/d6

Starter and explicitly neutral legacy dice migrate to Cardboard while preserving their active size. Incompatible material mappings use deterministic same-rarity fallbacks. Multi-affix dice do not retain hidden secondary behavior.

## Impact

Documentation only. No frontend, backend, schema, migration, seed, or runtime behavior changes.

## Validation

- Roster contains exactly 32 unique material keys.
- Rarity distribution is 8/8/7/5/4.
- Every material has an explicit non-empty allowlist using only d4, d6, d8, and d10.
- Cardboard is Common, supports all four active sizes, has no special effect, and is the only default material.
- Every active size has Common through Legendary coverage.
- Starter, Codex, combat, reward, status, and inventory documentation use the same target model.
- Branch is based directly on the merged dice-material identity model on main.
- Automated repository checks run through the pull request workflows.

author: ollehillbom1
body:
**Reported from real use**: after deleting the app and re-adding it to the home screen, there was no obvious way to sync again.

Sync was never broken. The way back was placed where nobody looks — the same shape as most of tonight's findings: a working mechanism with no reachable path.

## What a returning user actually met

**Onboarding**: `Already use Cortex? Restore from sync` rendered only on the **last** step, as the third button below *Start training* and *Back*. So the path is: four intro screens → type a name → tap the obvious primary action → you have just created an empty profile. After that the option is gone from onboarding entirely.

**Profile**: the only entry point was a button labelled **Enable sync**, described as *"Choose a strong passphrase … it is the only key to your data … it cannot be recovered if lost."* That is the language of creating a new secret. Nothing suggested that the very same button rejoins an existing group and brings the history back — which is exactly what `enableSync` does when the passphrase already has a group.

## Changes

- restore entry on the **first** welcome screen, not only the last
- Profile entry renamed to **"Set up sync, or rejoin with your passphrase"**, with a line addressed to this case: *reinstalled the app, or setting up a new device? Enter the passphrase you already use and this device rejoins that group — your profiles and history come back*
- the dialog now explains both outcomes: a known passphrase joins that group and brings its data here; a new one starts a new group
- enabling sync reports **what arrived**: *"Restored 2 profile(s) from your other devices"* instead of a bare *"Sync is on"*

## Evidence

```
npm run verify        # 192 unit tests, lint, types, build — PASS
npx playwright test   # 26/26 — PASS
```

New e2e pins the path the user actually tried: fresh install → first screen → restore → the profile is there.

**On verifying it honestly**: my first mutation check stashed the source and re-ran e2e — 3 passed, apparently proving the fix was pointless. That was wrong: `next start` serves the last *build*, so the test ran against a build that still contained the fix. Rebuilt without the change, the new test **times out on the missing button**. Worth remembering for any future e2e mutation check in this repo.

## For the affected user, before this merges

The capability is already live at https://ohillbo.se:9922 — **Profile → Enable sync → enter your usual passphrase** restores everything. The button is only named wrong.

author: devemberx
body:
## Summary

Four PRs (#34, #35, #36, #37) widened what the `config` segment reads off disk, and the
obvious next step — `doctor` listing hooks and MCP servers by the file that declared
them — is the one that should not be taken. Nothing written down said why, so the rule
goes in the list before somebody builds it.

The line it draws:

- A file Claude Code reads is a fair source. A count taken off it can be checked against
  that same file, which is what makes the number trustworthy.
- Rebuilding Claude Code's own resolution to publish a view it never shows is not. It
  answers a question `grep` already answers, and bets every undocumented key name and
  path this program guesses — `installed_plugins.json` layout, `enabledMcpjsonServers`,
  manifest hook paths, managed-settings locations, the 5-hop import rule — on the next
  Claude Code release.

It does not weaken the rule above it: a config *problem* still names the file that
declared it. A healthy config gets no tour.

## Type of Change

- [ ] Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)
- [ ] New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)
- [ ] Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to change)
- [ ] Refactor (no functional changes, code quality improvement)
- [ ] Test update (adds or corrects tests, no production behavior change)
- [x] Documentation update
- [ ] CI / packaging / dependency update

## Changes

- Four PRs widened what the config segment reads, and nothing said where reading Claude Code's files stops being the job
- Add non-negotiable rule: report what Claude Code loads, never rebuild its resolution to publish a view it never shows

## Testing

- Docs only, no code touched: `go test -race ./...`, `gofmt -l .` (silent),
  `go vet ./...` all still clean on this branch
- Read the rendered list to check the new bullet does not read as contradicting the
  `Origin` rule it sits under

## Notes for Reviewers

Deliberately not a ban on reading disk — `git`, `tokens`, `caveman` and `config` all
report things the stdin payload never carries, and that is the point of them. The test
is whether the output can be checked against the same file it came from.

author: meapy
body:
Tourism now touches the rest of the city rather than only hotels: visitors spend money in shops, and a preserved historic district draws them without needing a landmark dropped into it.

Published as 1.4.0, id [153543](https://mods.paradoxplaza.com/mods/153543).

## Historical buildings add to city attractiveness

City attractiveness is the sum of `AttractivenessProvider.m_Attractiveness` across every building carrying one (`TourismSystem:95-97`). In the base game that is parks, attractions and signature landmarks — an ordinary building contributes nothing, however beautiful. A preserved old quarter therefore draws nobody unless a landmark happens to sit inside it, and tourism ends up bolted onto a handful of placed buildings rather than emerging from the character of a district.

`HistoricAttractivenessSystem` reads `BuildingFlags.Historical` — the flag the player already sets from the building panel to preserve a level — and grants each such building a small value.

Reading the player's own flag rather than inferring one from zone or asset names means it works for any building, in any zone, from any asset pack, and it puts the decision where the player already expects to make it. My first attempt matched on old town zone prefab names; the flag is strictly better and removed the `PrefabSystem` lookup, the name matching and a per-zone cache along with it.

Deliberately small per building, default 3. One old house is worth very little; a whole preserved quarter is worth travelling for.

### Scope

This raises the tourist target, and improves how destinations on those streets score (`CitizenPathfindSetup:87-91`, which reads road-edge attractiveness into the target score). It does **not** make the historical buildings themselves visitable — that would require them to be leisure providers, which affects citizen behaviour well beyond tourism and is a separate decision.

So visitors end up *in* the district and pick the cafés and hotels among it. They do not queue at the townhouses.

### Behaviour

- Never lowers an existing value, so a signature building marked historical keeps its authored attractiveness.
- Setting to 0 removes the component rather than leaving a stale contribution, so it can be switched off without reloading.
- Walks 512 buildings per pass on a 4,096-frame cadence, resuming where it stopped, so a large city is swept gradually rather than in one spike.

## Mod page

The description now covers **tourist shopping**, which shipped in 1.2.0 and was never explained on the listing, and adds a section for historic districts. Both are written to match the existing sections: name the base-game defect plainly, then what changes, in player language.

`ShortDescription` was trimmed to 171 characters — Paradox rejects anything over 200 outright rather than truncating, which failed the first publish attempt. Noted in the XML and added to the PUBLISHING.md checklist.

## Fixed

`BuildingFlags` is ambiguous between `Game.Buildings` and `Game.Prefabs`, which carry unrelated values — the latter is the `LeftAccess`/`RightAccess` set used for lot fitting. Fully qualified at the use site. Worth knowing the collision exists, since an unqualified reference could compile elsewhere and silently mean the wrong thing.

## Risk

`HistoricAttractivenessSystem` is new and lightly tested. The failure mode is benign — attractiveness simply does not move — and the feature is off at 0, but it has not been verified over a long session.

Everything else here is documentation and a compile fix.

author: afafalguera-blip
body:
Permite marcar en el calendario un evento que dura del día X al día Y — Semana Santa, colonias, festivos largos — en vez de tener que crear un evento suelto por cada día.

## Modelo

Se añade `events.end_date`: el último día del evento, **inclusivo**.

- Un trigger la iguala a `event_date` cuando llega `NULL`, así toda fila tiene siempre un rango consultable y el código que solo manda `event_date` sigue siendo válido.
- `CHECK` que rechaza rangos invertidos (`end_date < event_date`).
- Índice `(event_date, end_date)` para el solape.
- Backfill de las 69 filas existentes: todas quedan como eventos de un día, sin cambio de comportamiento.

## El fallo que evita

Las consultas por mes filtraban solo por `event_date`, así que un evento del 27/03 al 05/04 **desaparecía al mirar abril**. Ahora se consulta por solape de intervalos:

```
event_date <= fin_mes AND end_date >= inicio_mes
```

Verificado contra producción: con la lógica nueva el evento aparece en ambos meses; con la antigua, la consulta de abril devolvía 0.

## Interfaz

- Formulario: campo "Fecha fin" opcional, con `min` en la fecha de inicio, validación antes de guardar y arrastre del fin si mueves el inicio por detrás.
- Rejilla admin: el rango se pinta como una barra continua (esquinas redondeadas solo en los extremos) con el título únicamente el primer día, para que se lea como un bloque y no como ocho chips repetidos.
- Listado admin y detalle público: muestran `inicio — fin` cuando el evento dura más de un día.
- Próximos eventos: un evento en curso sigue siendo "próximo" hasta su último día, no hasta el primero.

La lógica de rango vive en `src/utils/eventDates.ts` y la comparten admin y público, comparando cadenas `yyyy-MM-dd` para evitar el desfase de zona horaria de `new Date('yyyy-MM-dd')`.

author: baldborne94
body:
## Il difetto

```js
const pagesLeft = displayed.total - displayed.page;
const chapterLeft = pagesLeft * speed * pages;   // pages = 2 in doppia pagina
```

`speed` è la mediana del tempo **fra un cambio pagina e l'altro**, e in doppia pagina un cambio ne avanza **due**. Le pagine rimaste andavano quindi **divise** per il foglio, non moltiplicate: sbagliando verso, la stima usciva **quattro volte** più lunga del vero — «più di un'ora» per dieci minuti di lettura, esattamente come segnalato.

## La correzione

Si contano i giri che restano, non le pagine:

```js
const turnsLeft = Math.ceil(pagesLeft / Math.max(1, pages));
const chapterLeft = formatLeft(turnsLeft * speed);
```

Ogni giro avanza `pages` pagine e costa `speed`. A pagina singola (`pages = 1`) il conto è identico a prima.

## Verifica

`npm run build` verde. Confronto fra vecchio e nuovo calcolo:

| caso | prima | adesso | vero |
|---|---|---|---|
| doppia, 30s a foglio, 40 pagine rimaste | 40 min | **10 min** | 10 min (20 giri) |
| doppia, 45s a foglio, 24 pagine rimaste | 36 min | **9 min** | 9 min (12 giri) |
| doppia, 30s a foglio, 6 pagine rimaste | 6 min | **2 min** | 2 min (3 giri) |
| singola, 30s a pagina, 20 rimaste | 10 min | 10 min | 10 min (20 giri) |
| singola, 20s a pagina, 1 rimasta | meno di un minuto | meno di un minuto | (1 giro) |

Il fattore 4 in doppia pagina è confermato; a pagina singola nulla cambia.

**Nota su cosa la stima resta:** `speed` è la mediana degli ultimi 14 intervalli fra i cambi pagina, scartando quelli sotto i 2,5 secondi e sopra i 4 minuti. È quindi la tua velocità reale recente, pause di lettura comprese — non una media teorica di parole al minuto. Resta una stima: se leggi un capitolo fitto dopo uno scorrevole, arriverà tarata sul precedente finché non accumula nuovi intervalli.

## What changed

- Emit bundle-provided MCP app-server overrides as bare dotted keys such as `mcp_servers.host_mcp.command`.
- Cover command, arguments, working directory, and non-secret environment overrides with a regression test.

## Why

Codex CLI 0.146.0 treats quotes in `-c` dotted key paths as literal MCP server-name characters. The broker currently emits paths such as `mcp_servers."host_mcp".command`, so Codex attempts to register a server named `"host_mcp"` and rejects it against `^[a-zA-Z0-9_-]+$`.

This prevents bundle-provided stdio MCP servers from starting even though their manifest names are valid. MCP names accepted by Codex use characters that are also valid in TOML bare keys, so the quotes are unnecessary.

body:
**Bug crítico achado ao validar a v0.4.3 contra a base real do Gustavo.**

`renderDrawer` lia `c.infoclient.pessoais` direto, e todo contato criado pela **extensão de WhatsApp** chega sem `infoclient`. Como os **47 contatos da base dele** têm `origemCadastro:'extensao_whatsapp'`, o efeito prático era **nenhum contato abrir**: clicar no card ou na linha estourava `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'pessoais')` e o drawer não renderizava.

Bug **pré-existente** (não veio do reskin), mas bem no caminho de uso.

## Fix

`normContato()` preenche o que falta — `infoclient`, os arrays (`recs`/`eventos`/`planos`/`interacoes`), textos ausentes viram `—`, numéricos viram 0. Aplicado em três pontos:

| Ponto | Cobre |
|---|---|
| `carregar()` | base local no boot |
| `lpcCarregar()` | o que vem do Supabase depois do merge |
| `renderDrawer()` | cinto e suspensório, contato por outro caminho |

Normaliza **em memória** e não força `salvar()` — assim a correção não dispara um push da base inteira pro Supabase; o próximo save real leva os campos junto.

## Verificação

Base real reproduzida (contatos sem `infoclient`, um em cada funil): os dois **abrem**, sem `undefined` na tela, **console limpo**, e salvar `1.250,00` no valor do negócio grava `1250` → **PA 15.000**.

author: semx
body:
## Summary

`cosign initialize --root-checksum` rejects a correct checksum when it is written in upper case.

`hex.EncodeToString` always emits lower case, and `pkg/blob/load.go:107` compares it to the user-supplied value with `!=`. Hex is case-insensitive, and plenty of sources publish digests in upper case, so a user holding a perfectly good checksum is told it is wrong.

Reproducer against the real sigstore root:

```console
$ curl -sO https://tuf-repo-cdn.sigstore.dev/12.root.json
$ shasum -a 256 12.root.json | awk '{print toupper($1)}'
5FE1E509A47277183A004745942C0A116379297DA9F1CCA529774320F1A5DFAB

$ cosign initialize --root 12.root.json \
    --root-checksum 5FE1E509A47277183A004745942C0A116379297DA9F1CCA529774320F1A5DFAB
Error: incorrect checksum for file 12.root.json: expected 5FE1E509A47277183A004745942C0A116379297DA9F1CCA529774320F1A5DFAB but got 5fe1e509a47277183a004745942c0a116379297da9f1cca529774320f1a5dfab
```

The error message gives it away: expected and got are the same digest.

## Why this is more than cosmetic

`LoadFileOrURLWithChecksum` has exactly one caller, `cmd/cosign/cli/initialize/init.go:59`, and that is the TUF root of trust. So the person who hits this is doing the right thing: pinning a root they fetched out of band. What the tool tells them is that the root does not match. The nearest way out is `--force-skip-checksum-validation`, which is exactly the habit this flag exists to prevent.

## Change

`strings.EqualFold` instead of `!=`. Wrong checksums stay wrong: a `DEADBEEF`-prefixed digest is still rejected, and the prefixed forms (`sha256:`, `sha512:`) behave the same as before apart from case.

## Testing

Added upper-case sha256 and sha512 cases to the existing `TestLoadURLWithChecksum`. They fail on main and pass with the fix; the existing cases are untouched. `go vet ./pkg/blob/`, `gofmt` and `go build ./...` are clean.

Also ran both binaries end to end against sigstore's `12.root.json`:

| build | checksum | exit |
|---|---|---|
| main | lower case | 0 |
| main | UPPER CASE | 1 |
| fix | UPPER CASE | 0, initialization completes |
| fix | `sha256:` + UPPER CASE | 0 |
| fix | `DEADBEEF...` | 1, still rejected |

## Release Note

`cosign initialize --root-checksum` now accepts upper-case and mixed-case hex digests.

## Documentation

NA

author: chloeb276
body:
## Summary
Vercel logs (`Logs` tab, filtered to `/api/drill-feedback`, POST 502) showed the real error behind the recurring "Failed to generate drills":

```
Error [AI_RetryError]: Failed after 3 attempts. Last error: GatewayRateLimitError
```

Not a code bug in the request path — it's the AI Gateway's rate limit. Firing all 4 difficulty tiers' searches simultaneously via `Promise.all` bursts past it. The AI SDK already retries each call 3x internally with backoff, so the extra manual retry I'd added around the final write-up call (in #31) was actively making things worse — it added more requests on top of an already rate-limited burst instead of helping.

## Changes
- Difficulty tiers now search one at a time (sequential `for` loop) instead of all at once, so at most one request is in flight against the Gateway from a single generation.
- Removed the redundant manual retry on the final write-up call.

## Trade-off
This will be somewhat slower than the parallel version per request (tiers no longer overlap), but a slower response that succeeds beats a fast one that 502s. If it's still noticeably slow after this, the next lever would be asking Vercel/the Gateway dashboard what the actual rate limit ceiling is, rather than guessing further.

## Test plan
- [x] `npx biome check` / `npx tsc --noEmit` pass
- [ ] Retest live after deploy — check the Vercel logs again if it still fails, same as this time

author: qazuor
body:
## What

WB0-2 of HOS-369: a shared client-side store (`apps/web/src/store/favorites-store.ts`) that resolves favorite status for every `FavoriteButton` island on a page with **one** `POST /user-bookmarks/check-bulk` per entity type.

## Why

Favorite status is per-user, so it cannot be baked into an edge-cacheable HTML document. Wave B0 removes the SSR bulk check from the listing pages — without this store, de-personalizing a 24-card listing would trade one server-side bulk call for 24 client-side `/user-bookmarks/check` calls, one per heart.

## How

- **Batching.** Islands register the entity they display; registrations arriving within a 50 ms window are grouped by entity type and resolved in one bulk request. The window exists because `client:visible` islands hydrate across several frames as a grid scrolls into view, not in a single tick.
- **Session resolution lives in the store**, cache-first via `@/lib/auth-cache`. A guest issues no favorites request at all — every registered entity settles locally as "not favorited". Consumers therefore do not carry, and cannot forget, an auth gate of their own.
- **Per-key listeners.** Resolving 24 entities notifies each island about its own entity instead of re-rendering all of them 24 times.
- **Shared writes.** `setFavoriteStatus` publishes a toggle to every island showing that entity, so a listing card and its map popup never drift apart.
- **Failure degrades to settled, never busy.** A failed, partial, or thrown bulk check resolves the affected hearts to "not favorited" and clickable; the toggle itself remains the authoritative operation.
- **SSR renders the anonymous variant** (`getServerFavoriteStatus`), per D-11.

## Scope

No consumer yet, deliberately. `FavoriteButton` adopts the store in **WB0-3**, which also removes its SSR-prop gate (`FavoriteButton.client.tsx:236`) and makes the store its single source of truth. Half-wiring it here would leave two sources of truth — local state plus the store — for exactly one PR cycle. The spec orders `WB0-2 → WB0-3` for this reason (§12.3).

author: euphorialux
body:
## Purpose

* **A member can pay for Premium and have no way to tell they got it.** Found by walking a real SumUp payment on staging: the checkout succeeded, the membership went `active` and a coach was assigned — and the UI said nothing. `sumup_payment_return` drops a generic *"Payment completed successfully!"* and redirects to the Connect hub, where the only difference for a paying member was **one line of hero copy**. Nothing said Premium, and the hub never named the coach — the thing actually being sold.

* **3DS runs on domains CSP had never heard of.** The same payment reported framing violations for `test.ppipe.net` and `test.oppwa.com` — ACI Worldwide, SumUp's payment backend, **not** `sumup.com`.

## Does this introduce a breaking change?

```
[ ] Yes
[x] No
```

## Pull Request Type

```
[x] Feature
[x] Bugfix
```

## How to Test

```
git fetch origin
git checkout fix/premium-status-visibility
.venv/Scripts/Activate.ps1
```

```
pytest crush_lu/tests/test_crush_connect_hub.py crush_lu/tests/test_crush_connect.py crush_lu/tests/test_crush_connect_beta_phase.py --create-db
```

155 passed, exit 0. `ruff`, `manage.py check`, and the `crush_lu` design-token linter all clean.

## What to Check

* **The predicate matters more than the markup.** The badge keys off `has_active_premium` (the entitlement), **not** `is_receiver`. Those diverge: `is_receiver` is *(entitlement AND the phase lets them receive)*, so during the beta a member who has **paid** but is not a hand-picked tester has `is_receiver` False. Badging on `is_receiver` would show someone who just handed over money no sign at all that they are Premium — recreating this bug exactly where it costs most. Pinned by `test_premium_badge_shows_during_beta_even_when_not_a_receiver`, which asserts the precondition (`is_receiver is False`) so it can't silently stop testing the thing it's named for.

* **The coach is named.** `premium_coach` comes from `profile.assigned_coach`, which `PremiumMembership.confirm()` is the sole writer of. The hub previously never told a member who their coach was.

* **⚠️ The CSP addition narrows the 3DS caveat but does not close it.** Sandbox exercises ACI's own *demo* connector; a live challenge can still hand off to the card **issuer's** ACS domain, which is per-bank and cannot be enumerated. `form-action` is also still `CSP.SELF`. Both noted inline — walk a real 3DS payment under an *enforcing* policy before switching `SECURE_CSP_REPORT_ONLY` to `CONTENT_SECURITY_POLICY`.

* **Apex and wildcard are both listed** (`oppwa.com` + `*.oppwa.com`, `ppipe.net` + `*.ppipe.net`) because a CSP wildcard does not match the bare domain, and the live hosts drop the `test.` prefix.

## Other Information

* **A trap worth knowing, caught by the new test rather than by review:** Django's `{# … #}` is **single-line only**. The multi-line version I first wrote rendered the developer comment onto the page for every visitor — the test asserting *"Premium member" not in body* failed because the comment mentioning it was being served as literal text. Now `{% comment %}`.
* Benign noise seen alongside these violations and not a bug: `SumUp create_customer failed: 409 Conflict` is expected on a repeat purchase (the customer already exists) and is caught by the view. The `400` on ACI's `?action=ACI3DS2AccessControlServer&acsRequest=METHOD` is on their sandbox demo connector, and the payment completed regardless.
* Related: #769 (purchase allowlist), #770 (silent confirmation failure), #771 (widget overlay + initial CSP).

author: bendrucker
body:
## Why

Found while writing a spec for a `bin/` script in #592. Six examples stubbed `gum` by prepending a directory to `$PATH`, the way you would for a bash script. They passed locally and failed on both CI platforms.

The cause is that `bin/` scripts use a `#!/usr/bin/env zsh` shebang, and zsh sources `~/.zshenv` on every invocation including non-interactive ones. `zsh/.zshenv` runs `eval "$(brew shellenv)"`, which puts `$HOMEBREW_PREFIX/bin` ahead of the stub directory. The real command then wins and the stub never runs.

Reproduced directly:

```
$ env -i HOME=$HOME ZDOTDIR=<dotfiles>/zsh PATH=<stub>:/usr/bin:/bin zsh -c 'command -v gum'
/opt/homebrew/bin/gum

$ env -i HOME=$HOME ZDOTDIR=<empty> PATH=<stub>:/usr/bin:/bin zsh -c 'command -v gum'
<stub>/gum
```

## Why it deserves a note rather than a comment in one spec

It passes on a developer machine and fails in CI. `HOMEBREW_PREFIX` is already exported in an interactive shell, so `brew shellenv` emits no `PATH` line and the stub keeps its lead. A fresh CI environment has no such luck.

Prepending to `$PATH` is the ordinary way to stub a command, and it works for a bash script, so the habit carries over and breaks without any obvious reason. This applies to every zsh-shebang script in `bin/`, including `dotfiles-upgrade`, `dotf`, `dotfiles-sync`, and `worktree-prune`.

The spec that found it went away with #592, so without this the finding is lost.

Docs only.

## Summary

- add execution, tool-run, and patch-checkpoint SQLite persistence
- add exclusive workspace write leases with renewal, takeover, and token-protected release
- add guarded file read/search/create/patch/delete and Git status/diff tools
- enforce persisted Executor tool policy, filesystem access, file size, patch size, and tool-call limits
- add idempotent `workflow.execute` durable handler with crash recovery and final-attempt failure transition
- snapshot workflow, plan, workspace, agent-settings version, provider, and model for each execution
- add SHA-256 patch checkpoints and changed-file metadata
- register a deterministic scripted executor that performs read-only Git inspection
- expose read-only execution, tool-run, and checkpoint APIs
- show latest execution status and tool-call count in the OpenTUI Jobs screen
- document execution safety boundaries and update the development backlog

## Safety

- canonical workspace-relative paths only
- absolute paths, traversal, `.git` mutation, symlink escape, special files, recursive directory deletion, oversized files, and oversized patches are rejected
- Git commands run without a shell and with a constrained environment
- tool permissions are checked in code against the persisted Executor policy
- write operations require a valid workspace write lease
- lease renewal failure cancels the active runner
- stale lease tokens cannot renew or release a newer lease

## API

```text
GET /api/v1/jobs/:jobID/executions
GET /api/v1/executions/:executionID
GET /api/v1/executions/:executionID/tool-runs
GET /api/v1/executions/:executionID/checkpoints
```

## Current executor scope

The registered `ScriptedRunner` is intentionally deterministic and read-only: it records `git_status` and `git_diff`, creates a durable checkpoint, and advances the workflow to checks. Autonomous LLM-driven mutations will build on this execution foundation in a later task.

## Validation

GitHub Actions run #171 passed:

- Go module tidy and verification
- gofmt
- `go vet ./...`
- race-enabled Go tests
- Biome lint and formatting
- strict TypeScript typecheck
- Bun tests

Tests cover canonical path validation, traversal and `.git` rejection, symlink escape, file create/read/search/patch/delete, policy and size limits, real Git status, write-lease acquire/renew/release/takeover, stale-token rejection, and typed execution API clients.

author: muqsitnawaz
body:
Cursor commands now land in **both** the IDE directory and the CLI skills format — **fix**, closes [RUSH-2083](https://linear.app/getrush/issue/RUSH-2083) (parent [RUSH-2079](https://linear.app/getrush/issue/RUSH-2079)).

**Replaces #1721**, which took the wrong approach. That branch could not be pushed forward (its local ref had diverged from the remote), so this is a clean branch off the same base carrying the corrected design. #1721 is closed with a pointer here.

## Why the original approach was wrong

RUSH-2083's premise is right: `cursor-agent` does not run custom slash commands — Cursor staff say so, quoted in `tests/fixtures/cli-command-spec.json`. #1721 acted on that by setting `capabilities.commands: false` so the existing `shouldInstallCommandAsSkill` predicate would route commands to skills.

That predicate is **either/or** — `!supports(commands) && supports(skills)` (`command-skills.ts:58-60`). But Cursor genuinely needs both surfaces: the **IDE** reads `~/.cursor/commands/<name>.md` and runs them as typed `/commands`, while the **CLI** only consumes skills. Flipping the flag made the CLI right by making the IDE wrong.

It also had a data-loss bug. `versions.ts:2780-2783` ran

```ts
if (commandsAsSkills && agentConfig.commandsSubdir) {
  removePath(commandsTarget);   // fs.rmSync(p, { recursive: true, force: true })
}
```

That branch was unreachable for cursor before, and the flag flip aimed it at `~/.cursor/commands/` — which is the live IDE directory (`~/.cursor` is symlinked to the version config path, `shims.ts:1256-1262`, `:1467`). A user with hand-authored IDE commands would lose them on the next `agents sync`. CI was fully green.

## What this does instead

- **Cursor keeps `capabilities.commands: true`**, so the four CLI management surfaces the flip would have broken (`agents commands install|remove`, `agents packages install`, the list/prune/drift paths, and `agents view`/`inspect` command counts) keep working unchanged.
- **New registry-driven `shouldAlsoInstallCommandAsSkill`** (`command-skills.ts`), deliberately separate from `shouldInstallCommandAsSkill` — that one means *instead of*, this one means *in addition to*. Driven by a `COMMAND_SKILL_DUAL_WRITE_TARGETS` table, not an `if (agent === 'cursor')` arm.
- **The unscoped `removePath(commandsTarget)` is deleted.** The orphan sweep is now manifest-scoped for dual-write targets: only names captured by the prior sync manifest are eligible for removal, so anything else in that shared directory is treated as user-owned.

## The run — real sync against Cursor 2026.07.23

A sentinel user-authored file was placed in the cursor commands dir, then a real `agents sync` was run with the installed dev build:

```
commands (18)
skills   (92)
```

The sentinel **survived** the sync, `commands/recap.md` matched its managed source, and `skills/recap/SKILL.md` carried the `agents_command: "recap"` marker — both surfaces written, nothing user-owned deleted. The sentinel was then removed.

```
Test Files  passed
Tests       passed
```

`bun run test:remote` could not start: `error: HCLOUD_TOKEN is empty after secret resolution`. Full CI covers it.

## Docs

`README.md` and `apps/cli/docs/00-concepts.md` capability rows updated to describe the dual-write behavior. `apps/cli/AGENTS.md:142` was already correct for `commands: true` and is deliberately left alone. The `registry_divergence` note is removed from the fixture, since the divergence it described is genuinely resolved — the CLI now gets the command, via skills.

## Related

[RUSH-2101](https://linear.app/getrush/issue/RUSH-2101) — separately, `cursor-agent` 2026.07.23 does have `--plan` (read-only), which the registry still denies. Sequenced after this PR since it touches the same capabilities block.

author: fpelliccioni
body:
The v1 node validates through flat-file blocks + UTXO-Z + the new mempool. The pre-v1 single-block acceptance path (`organize` → `validate_block` → `populate_block`, over the LMDB utxo_pool and reorg pool) and the LMDB **utxo / reorg / block / transaction / history / spend** stores it drove are no longer reachable from any live path. This PR removes them.

### blockchain
- Delete `validate_block` and `populate_block`.
- Stub `block_chain::organize(block)` → `not_implemented`; reimplementation on the v1 model is tracked by #563. `block_organizer` keeps only the block-pool `get_data` filter and the block-broadcast subscription — the direct single-block acceptance entry is gone.
- Drop `get_output` and the confirmed address index (`fetch_spend` / `fetch_history` / `fetch_confirmed_transactions`), which read the removed spend/history stores.
- `get_transaction_position` / `fetch_transaction` / `fetch_transaction_position` no longer read the removed transaction store; they report `not_found` until a lookup over the flat-file block store is added (#491), matching `fetch_block`.
- `populate_pooled` no longer consults the confirmed-transaction index.

### database
- Remove the dead stores from `internal_database`, keeping only `block_header`, `block_header_by_hash` and `properties` (headers-first sync + height tracking). Delete the six store `.ipp` partials and drop `data_base::prune_reorg`.

### c-api
- Remove the `kth_chain_{sync,async}_{spend,history,confirmed_transactions}` bindings that wrapped the removed queries.

### Safety
The new mempool is unaffected: prevout population already resolves through UTXO-Z and the mempool, not the removed stores. `database`, `blockchain`, `c-api`, `node`, `node-exe` and the `kth_*_test` targets all build locally.

Net: 25 files changed, ~3.6k lines removed.

  * Removed block organization, validation, reorganization, and population capabilities; block organization now returns a not-implemented status.

  * Confirmed transactions are no longer indexed for hash-based lookup.
