body:
## Overview

`make release` 가 3단계에서 항상 실패하던 문제를 고칩니다.

```
==> 3. Release 빌드 · 서명 · 패키징
Working tree has uncommitted changes. Commit or stash them before packaging.
 M HorongHorong.xcodeproj/project.pbxproj
 M project.yml
```

`release.sh` 는 1~2단계에서 `project.yml` 을 고치고 `xcodegen` 으로 `.xcodeproj` 를 재생성합니다. 그 상태로 3단계에서 `package-release.sh` 를 부르는데, 그 안의 «클린 트리» 검사가 **방금 자기가 만든 변경** 을 보고 막습니다.

dry-run 은 `--skip-clean-check` 를 넘기고 있어서 통과했고, **실제 릴리즈 경로는 구조적으로 항상 여기서 막혔습니다.**

## Change Log

- `build_and_package()` 가 항상 `--skip-clean-check` 를 넘깁니다. 클린 트리 검사는 이미 0단계 preflight 가 수행하며, 그 시점 이후 생긴 변경은 스크립트 자신이 만든 것뿐입니다.
- 조건부 인자 배열이 사라지면서, 앞서 고쳤던 bash 3.2 빈 배열 우회(`"${extra[@]+...}"`)도 함께 제거됐습니다.

## To Reviewer

**dry-run 과 실제 경로가 갈리는 구조가 문제의 근원이었습니다.** 이번 세션에서 같은 원인으로 두 번 깨졌습니다.

1. `extra[@]: unbound variable` — 배열이 dry-run 에서만 채워져서
2. 이번 클린 트리 검사 — 플래그가 dry-run 에서만 붙어서

이제 두 경로가 같은 인자로 `package-release.sh` 를 부르므로 이 종류의 차이는 없어졌습니다.

**검증**: 더러운 작업 트리에서 `--skip-clean-check` 로 패키징이 끝까지 도는 것을 확인했습니다(zip 48M / dmg 53M).

**여전히 미검증**: 9~13단계(CHANGELOG 확정, 커밋·태그 push, 릴리즈 생성, appcast, 백머지).

author: sirhartley
body:
Both entries were written about the wrong thing.

**Mind Flayer** described how it swam. It is a mind flayer; what it does with a mind is the entry:

> Nothing anyone has put in front of one has ever been eaten. Ratings quartered near one lose hours first, then names, then the knack of reading. The specimen gains mass.

The escalation is deliberate — time, then identity, then a learned faculty — and the last sentence says where it all went without saying it.

**Yellow King** was written about the colour. It now runs on Chambers:

> The markings resolve, given long enough, into a page of a pre-Collapse play set down in yellow script. The first act is harmless. Crews who reach the second are relieved of duty and stay relieved of it.

The play, the safe first act, the second act nobody comes back from — the conceit intact, with the fiction moved into the setting: it survives as a pre-Collapse text, and the consequence is stated as a personnel outcome rather than as madness. "Relieved of duty and stay relieved of it" is doing the work the original leaves unsaid.

Yellow King runs 202 characters, over the ~175 the rest of the table holds to. The three-beat structure needs the room and it is one of two entries in the file with a story to carry — happy to cut it back if you would rather the ceiling held.

author: johnneto
body:
## What changed

Two features in two commits:

### 1. Live search autocomplete (`feat(search)`)
Debounced Places Autocomplete (New) with separate place/city suggestion sections, a city-switch confirm card, and session-token reuse so autocomplete + the follow-up details call bill as one Google session.

### 2. Curation pipeline rework (`feat(spots)`)

**Gemini prompts** — structured prompt with an official-Google-Maps-name contract (local language, no translation), consolidated selection rules, rewritten per-mode instructions (typos and the Atlas Obscura reference removed), and a per-mode Places-type palette so bad `primaryType` hints stop hiding correct venues under `strictTypeFiltering`. `maxOutputTokens` 4096 → 8192.

**Official-listing resolution** — Text Search now fetches 5 candidates (billing is per request, so same cost) and `PlaceResolutionScorer` ranks them: 45% diacritic-folded name similarity, 30% rating-count popularity, 15% in-city proximity, 10% business status, minus a penalty for typeless/ratingless user-created dupes. It defers to Google's top result on near-ties (< 0.10) and logs every override via `AppLog.places`, so existing good matches can't silently regress. Bias radius follows the viewport instead of a hardcoded 5 km.

**Details correctness** — decodes structured `periods` + `utcOffsetMinutes` and computes open/closed **at render time in the place's timezone** (`OpeningHoursCalculator`). Fixes the 30-day-stale "Open now" pill, garbled split-shift closing strings, and device-timezone errors. Unknown rating/price/address now render honestly (no "★ 0.0 (0)", no fake "$"). Reviews show Google's relative time verbatim. The two `PlaceMapper` paths are unified, ending the raw `dyn_<slug>` cityId leak into user-visible copy.

**API cost** — bulk resolution drops `reviews`/`editorialSummary` from the search field mask (top-SKU fields); the full payload loads lazily via one Place Details call when a POI sheet opens (`Place.detailsFetchedAt` marker + merge preserving the curated rationale).

**Misc** — POI distance measures from the user when physically inside the browsed city, else "from center"; units follow device region settings. 404/`NOT_FOUND` maps to `placesNotFound` so deleted saved spots finally show the Remove button. Three dead view files removed. One-shot cache wipe (`spotsCacheClearedForDetailsV3`) so installs pick up structured hours immediately.

## Reviewer notes

- The scorer's anti-regression tie-break is the safety valve: Google's #1 result wins unless a challenger beats it by ≥ 0.10. Overrides are logged (`Ranking override for …`) — worth watching in Console during rollout.
- `Place` gained a tolerant `init(from:)` so any pre-wipe cached JSON still decodes; all new fields are optional.
- `Profile → metric units` toggle was already unread before this PR; distance units now follow the device region, so the toggle is decorative and could be removed in a follow-up.
- Mock seed places have no structured periods, so they show "No opening information available" — honest, but mock mode loses the open/closed pill.

## Testing

- 36/36 unit tests pass (`xcodebuild test … -only-testing:CitisenTests`), including new suites: `OpeningHoursCalculatorTests` (split shifts, overnight, Sat→Sun wrap, 24/7 sentinel, cross-timezone), `PlaceResolutionScorerTests` (official-beats-dupe, near-tie keeps Google order, diacritic folding, out-of-city rejection), wire decoding, mapper behaviors, and prompt content.
- Verified live in the iOS simulator: San Francisco Standard mode resolved 20/24 spots to official listings; POI sheet showed curated "Why visit", live "Closed · Opens 1:00 PM" computed from periods, hidden price row for a cathedral, and 5 lazily-fetched reviews with verbatim "3 months ago".

author: olemarkus
body:
## The bug

On the running build `Termostat hovedbad` was held by the daily budget and its Overview card read **"Turned off by PELS"** — a line that restated the bold `Limited` state word and the `0.00 kW` fact beside it, and named no cause at all. The correct sentence was sitting in the same snapshot: the runtime's own `statusMsg` said `Limited by today's daily budget`. Verified live at 2026-08-02T12:34:42Z.

## Why not just print the ceiling on the card

Which ceiling binds — hard cap, this hour's pace, today's budget — is **one house-level fact, identical for every device**. Printing it on N cards says the same sentence N times while the reader's actual question ("what would it take to run this?") goes unanswered.

So the split is:

- **The hero names the ceiling once**, in visible text on the Power-now subline: `Safe pace now 1.9 kW · set by today's budget`. It was tooltip-only before, which is unreachable in a touch WebView.
- **Each card states the kW that would actually admit that device**, reserves folded in: `Waiting to resume — 0.9 kW more needed`.

That kW is measured against the safe **pace**, not instantaneous draw. The pace is itself dynamic (remaining budget ÷ remaining time), so the gap closes as the pace recovers, not only when load is switched off — prod the same day shows it climbing 1.54 → 1.85 kW across consecutive cycles.

## Before / after

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Budget-held thermostat | `Turned off by PELS` | `Waiting to resume — 0.9 kW more needed` |
| Hero subline | `Safe pace now 1.9 kW` | `Safe pace now 1.9 kW · set by today's budget` |
| Stepped fairness | `Blocked by safety rule` | `Holding at 6 A — cannot increase while 2 devices are limited` |

## The number was being thrown away

`resolveDailyBindingReattribution` re-labels an insufficient-headroom hold as `dailyBudget` and returned a bare `{ detail: null }`, discarding `needKw`/`postReserveMargin`. That was deliberate on 2026-08-01, because the displayed gap was then `need − available`, which ignored the reserve stack. `73a474373` fixed that arithmetic the next morning, so the fold now carries the shortfall instead of dropping it.

**Two holds deliberately carry no number**, because the arithmetic in scope at their producers belongs to a *different* device: swap victims (the numbers are the device being swapped in) and startup reservations (a gap "through" the reservation resolves to the holder's block — with 2.5 kW free, a device needing 2.0 kW and a 3.6 kW holder, the card would have read "3.6 kW more needed"). Both name the other device instead.

**The kW is kept out of every comparable reason.** It tracks `softLimitKw − totalKw`, which drifts continuously, and that signature gates the per-device device-log ring buffer. A logged `statusMsg` for a budget hold carries no kW, so a 50-entry recorder would fill with textually identical rows and evict the real transitions. Same rule the repo already enforces for `shortfall` via `CODE_ONLY_REASONS`.

## One resolver instead of three

The three card variants each re-derived their own partial cause map, which is why they disagreed with each other *and* with the runtime. Replaced by one ladder in `planCardReasonLine.ts`:

1. budget-rescue copy (the hold with a "Let it run now" action)
2. the shortfall
3. non-power causes keep their own wording — a kW figure would be a lie, since freeing power would not start them (smart task, solar surplus, external off, stepped fairness, countdowns)
4. honest fallback

It also guards the snapshot boundary: an unknown reason code used to reach `formatDeviceReasonUserFacing`, whose exhaustive-switch `default` returns the reason *object* at runtime and rendered as a blank line.

## Simulation

Every line the ladder produces now has a hypothetical form. A hold is a PELS action even when the copy describes waiting, so `Waiting to resume — N kW more needed` reads `Would be waiting to resume … (simulation)`. This closes the numbered half of the open "simulation wait-lines read factually" TODO, and fixes a regression in this PR's own first draft where the temperature card — one of three variants — lost its hypothetical framing entirely.

## Log parity

The device-log event gains `cardReasonText` alongside `reasonText`, so a support session can reconstruct what the owner actually saw now that the card and the log differ by design.

## Also

- Closes five TODO entries on the stepped fairness rule. It read "Blocked by safety rule" (jargon; not a safety rule; "blocked" overstates a rule that only refuses *increases*) and elsewhere rendered `maxStep` — the invariant's cap, not where the device is, so prod showed "Limited to Low" for a device running at Medium.
- Deletes `resolveHeldStateActionLabel` and its five strings, now unreachable (knip can't see it — shared-domain is an entry point).
- **Log-string change worth noting for support playbooks:** `Blocked by safety rule` no longer appears in `reasonText` / the device activity log.

author: kaifahmad1
body:
## Summary

Hardens Semantica's CI/CD supply chain against the class of attack behind the March 2026 LiteLLM/Trivy incident — a compromised third-party GitHub Action with a mutable tag was used to steal a long-lived PyPI publishing token, after which malicious packages were pushed straight to PyPI without ever touching the source repo.

- **SHA-pin every third-party Action** across all 8 workflows (tag kept as a `# vX` comment for readability).
- **Add `verify-action-pins.yml`** — a new CI check that resolves each pinned tag via the GitHub API and fails if the SHA no longer matches, so the pins are continuously verified rather than just trusted by comment.
- **Scope `release.yml` permissions to the job level** (workflow-level default is now `contents: read`; `contents: write` / `id-token: write` / `attestations: write` only granted to the release job) and add a `concurrency` group so two tag pushes can't race the publish job.
- **Add SLSA build provenance** (`actions/attest-build-provenance`) for every released wheel, verifiable with `gh attestation verify`.
- **Fix a latent bug** in `security-scan.yml`: the PR-comment step was missing `pull-requests: write` and silently failing on every run; also bounded the uploaded scan-report artifact retention to 14 days.
- **Group Dependabot's `github-actions` updates** into one PR instead of many.
- **Document the resulting posture in `SECURITY.md`** (bulleted, not tabled) for auditors and anyone forking this repo for a regulated deployment — including what settings a fork must reconfigure for itself (branch/environment protection, Trusted Publishing trust) since those don't copy on fork.

Also applied directly via the GitHub API (not part of this diff, but relevant context for reviewers): created a protected `pypi` GitHub Environment with a required reviewer, restricted to `v*` tag deployments, and enabled branch protection on `main` (1 required review with stale-approval dismissal, required status checks, no force-push/deletion, required conversation resolution).

## Test plan

- [x] All modified/added workflow YAML validated with `yaml.safe_load` (no syntax errors)
- [x] `verify-action-pins.sh` run locally against the full `.github/workflows/` tree — all 39 pinned actions resolve to their stated tag
- [x] Confirmed via GitHub API that the `pypi` environment has exactly the intended reviewer and tag policy, and that `main`'s branch protection matches what's described above
- [ ] First real run of `verify-action-pins.yml` on this PR (will show in checks below)
- [ ] Next tagged release should be watched to confirm the `pypi` environment approval gate and provenance attestation step both work end-to-end

author: nickelliang
body:
## What

Mobile's extension map (`mobile/src/session/mobile-file-language.ts`) carried no HDL at all, so `.vhd` **and** `.sv` files rendered flat in both the file viewer and the diff review pane.

Companion to #12123, which fixes the desktop renderer. The two surfaces are independent: mobile has its own extension map and uses lowlight/highlight.js rather than Monaco, so neither change helps the other.

## How

Two things were blocking it, and both had to go:

1. The extension map had no HDL entries — now the same set the renderer uses.
2. `createLowlight(common)` — lowlight's `common` bundle carries neither `vhdl` nor `verilog`, so even a correct language id resolved to `plaintext` via the existing `lowlight.registered(...)` guard. Both grammars are now registered explicitly.

highlight.js has no separate SystemVerilog grammar, so `systemverilog` joins the existing alias table (alongside `shell` → `bash`) and folds onto `verilog`, which covers both languages.

## Dependency

`highlight.js` becomes a direct dependency of the mobile workspace. It was already in the tree at the same version (11.11.1) as a transitive dependency of `lowlight`, so `mobile/pnpm-lock.yaml` gains 3 lines and no new package is downloaded. The two grammars add roughly 20 KB to the bundle.

## Testing

`mobile/src/session/mobile-file-syntax.test.ts` gains coverage for the extension mapping, the `systemverilog` → `verilog` fold, and actual segment output for both languages (`always_ff` colors as a keyword; so does VHDL `when`).

`pnpm run test` green (383 files, 2862 pass, 3 skipped), plus `typecheck`, `lint` and `format:check`.

author: nitrotap
body:
Deployment has been manual until now. This makes it automatic and adds a gate on pull requests.

## Deploy

Runs on every push to `main`, and on demand via `workflow_dispatch`.

Lint → build → verify the export → publish `out/` to `gh-pages-next`, the branch GitHub Pages serves from. Publishing is the last step, so a bad commit fails the job without touching the deploy branch and the live site stays on the last good build.

It commits on top of `gh-pages-next` rather than force-pushing a fresh tree, so the branch keeps a record of what was live when. It also writes two files that are not build output: without `CNAME`, Pages drops the custom domain on the next publish; without `.nojekyll`, Jekyll ignores every path starting with an underscore — all of `_next/` — and the site loads with no CSS or JS.

Concurrency is `cancel-in-progress: false`. Cancelling a run that has already pushed would leave the site on a commit nobody chose.

## CI

The same gates on pull requests, so a broken build surfaces before the merge instead of after. Only `pull_request` — pushes to `main` already run these steps inside Deploy, and building twice is wasted work.

## scripts/verify-export.sh

A green `next build` means the compiler was happy, not that the site works. The assertions both workflows share:

- `out/` exists, is non-empty, and has `_next/`
- at least 50 HTML pages and 40 sitemap URLs
- the route-handler artifacts exist — `robots.txt`, `sitemap.xml`, `llms.txt`, `search-index.json`, `opengraph-image.png`, `favicon.ico`
- every indexable page carries a canonical link and an `og:image`
- no `localhost:3000` leaked into the output

Each assertion was tested by breaking the tree and confirming it fires, then confirming the restored tree still passes.

## Verified

- Both workflows parse; clean `lint` and `build` from this branch; verifier passes at 63 pages / 61 sitemap URLs.
- The publish step was rehearsed against a throwaway remote seeded with a stale `gh-pages-next`: stale files removed, `CNAME` and `.nojekyll` present, history preserved, commit message clean.

The rehearsal also published a `.DS_Store` from the local `out/`. A Linux runner will not produce one, but the publish worktree checks out `gh-pages-next`, so this repo's `.gitignore` does not apply there and `git add -A` would take it on a manual run from a Mac. The deploy now deletes those before copying.

## Note

`main` is four commits ahead of what is currently live, so merging this triggers a deploy that ships `/llms.txt` and the career summary update.

author: anai-guo
body:
## Problem

Closes #4386.

With the `fs` L2 adapter and `use_odirect: true`, a single rejected direct write kills the whole disk tier. `_write_with_odirect` re-raises, `_execute_store` marks the chunk failed, and nothing about the adapter's state changes — so the next chunk takes the same path and fails the same way. The result is what the issue reports: nothing is ever persisted to L2, the server keeps running and reports no fatal error, and the log fills with one `FSL2Adapter failed to store <path>` line per chunk for the lifetime of the process.

Whether `O_DIRECT` is usable depends on the file system, the device stack, and the alignment of the buffers handed to the adapter. None of that can be checked up front — `statvfs().f_bsize` at construction only tells us the block size to size-align against, not whether the kernel will accept the call.

## Fix

Catch `OSError` around the direct write, drop `O_DIRECT` for the rest of the process, and retry that chunk buffered:

- The adapter already has a buffered write path — it is used when the object size is not block-aligned — so this reuses it rather than adding one.
- Clearing `_use_odirect` also covers the load path, which reads the same flag (`_execute_load`), so reads stop attempting direct I/O too.
- The one-shot warning names the base path and the concrete errno, so an operator can tell `EINVAL` from `EACCES` without reading LMCache's source. `_write_with_odirect`'s existing `logger.exception` still emits the full traceback once.

Only the first chunk pays for the failed attempt; every store after it goes straight to buffered I/O.

This is deliberately about the *degradation*, not about which errno the reporter's md-RAID0 stack returns — the adapter should not depend on that being knowable to keep working.

## Tests

New `tests/v1/distributed/test_fs_l2_adapter_odirect.py`:

- `test_rejected_odirect_write_falls_back_to_buffered` — a rejected direct write (`OSError(EINVAL)`) still stores the chunk with the right bytes, later chunks store too, `O_DIRECT` is attempted exactly once, and `_use_odirect` ends up `False`.
- `test_successful_odirect_write_keeps_odirect_enabled` — the fallback does not fire when direct I/O works.

Verified on Linux against the real adapter:

```
# before the fix
1 failed, 1 passed

# after the fix (new file + existing tests/v1/distributed/test_fs_l2_adapter_delete.py)
11 passed
```

`ruff==0.11.7` (check + format), `isort==6.0.1`, `mypy==1.17.1 --config-file=pyproject.toml`, and the SPDX header check are all clean on both files; `mypy` was also green on the unmodified file beforehand, so nothing new was introduced.

> **Note on the base commit:** my fork's `dev` cannot be fast-forwarded (the sync touches `.github/workflows/*`, which my token is not scoped for), so this branch is cut from my fork's `dev` tip rather than upstream's. The diff against upstream `dev` is exactly the two files above and merges cleanly — happy to rebase if you'd prefer a fresher base.

author: eranroseman
body:
An audit of `scripts/` and `packages/` for file/folder organization. **Nothing moved** — the layout is sound and most of what looks irregular is load-bearing: the flat plugin root is forced by Obsidian's loader, the 1303-line `main.js` is the Obsidian-coupled half of a purity seam (the siblings are host-free and headless-testable), and the single-file installer is a published curl-able contract.

What the audit did find was four stale config lines, each of which silently shrinks the gate while reporting green.

## Fixes

| Fix | Evidence |
| --- | --- |
| shellcheck `files:` → `^scripts/` | Lint-ed **1 of 4** tracked shell scripts. Its second alternation named `scripts/install/`, deleted in #1322 — a regex matching nothing is a green hook. `scripts/dev/setup.sh`, the first command CONTRIBUTING gives a new contributor, was covered by **no gate at all**. Proof: injecting `echo "$fooo"` into it now raises SC2154. |
| ruff + ruff-format `files:` → `^(src/memoria_vault\|scripts\|tests)/` | `scripts/verify` is deliberately extensionless, so it matched none of the `\.py$` alternations — the 218-line file that *defines* what "verified" means was the one Python file exempt from both hooks, and pre-commit never reports an exclusion. Proof: injecting an unused import into it now raises 2 errors. Both hooks already declare `types_or: [python, pyi, jupyter]`; the file filter was re-encoding that and getting it wrong. |
| `pythonpath` `["src","scripts"]` → `[".","src"]` | With both the root and `scripts` resolving one file, `e2e_smoke` imported as two distinct modules with separate state. And the root arrived only as a side effect of `python -m pytest`'s cwd insertion: a bare `pytest` collected **976 with 102 errors**, now **4038 with 0**. Three import spellings and one dead `sys.path.insert` follow. |
| `MIN_NODE_TESTS` 49 → 55 | 55 tests actually pass; six of slack is exactly the room a gutted suite hides in. Measured on **both** node 22 (`mise.toml`, CI) and node 24. |

## schema.js

Its header claimed `// Generated by scripts/build.mjs from src/schema.js.` Neither artifact exists, and it contradicts `main.js:1` (`hand-authored (no build step)`). That sat on the file holding the privacy contract (`sanitizeItemId`, `validateEvent`), making "regenerate rather than edit" the most expensive wrong instruction in the package.

The replacement states the real relationship, and a new test pins it: **subset, never equality**. The JS narrows to what an Obsidian client can legitimately submit — `SURFACES` is `obsidian` alone, and `WORKFLOWS` omits `attention`, which only the server-authored `read-observed.v1` telemetry emits ([api.py:1201](https://github.com/eranroseman/memoria-vault/blob/main/src/memoria_vault/engine/api.py#L1201)). Adding it would let the plugin fabricate attention-read telemetry the engine authors itself. Nothing had pinned that relationship, so an engine-side rename would have stranded the plugin until a real user's event was rejected over the wire. Mutation-tested: renaming a JS enum value fails the test.

The 38 floor goldens change one line each — the `schema.js` digest, verified as the only changed line in each file.

## Considered and rejected

Splitting `main.js` (would relocate 29 unchanged `this.plugin.*` references and force a constants module or a CommonJS cycle); splitting or renaming the 2095-line `test.mjs`; renaming `packages/memoria-obsidian/scripts/` → `test/` (under `test/` node executes *every* `.js`/`.mjs`, so a helper dropped there silently inflates the count `MIN_NODE_TESTS` keeps honest); and moving `PSScriptAnalyzerSettings.psd1` to the repo root — a wrong `-Settings` path makes `Invoke-ScriptAnalyzer` exit 0 with no findings, so that refactor can permanently disable the only PowerShell gate with every check green.

## Verification

`python scripts/verify` → `verify: OK` (4011 passed, 27 skipped).

author: dereuromark
body:
Fixes the carve-rs half of markup-carve/carve#450.

A `:::` written inside a code fence or a comment block, inside a container, closed that container. The real closer, the rest of the body and every block after it reparsed one level out - and under exact-length closers the leftover `:::` opened a fresh div, so the tail of the document moved into it.

````
::: note
```
:::
```
body
:::
after
````

The container body collector already copies opaque spans through verbatim rather than letting the block parser see their contents. It got the span's *extent* wrong: it tested every line against the closer pattern including the opener line, and an opener with no info string is closer-shaped - a bare ` ``` `, a bare `~~~`, a `%%%`. The span ended on the line it started on, and its contents went back to the block parser after all.

The opener is now consumed before the first closer test, in one helper both branches call. The other copy of this scan, `find_colon_container_end`, always did it that way - which is exactly the drift the issue predicted between the two copies.

The issue reports this against comment blocks only, and that is why: `%%%` never carries an info string, so the comment path failed every time, while the fence path failed only for a bare fence. Both are fixed here.

Six cases pinned in `tests/opaque_span_in_container.rs`: bare backtick fence, bare tilde fence, info-string fence, comment block, a non-bare container opener inside a fence (load-bearing under exact-length closers, since it would otherwise push a nesting level), and a well-formed comment block to catch the opposite error - swallowing a line past the closer.

Output now matches carve-js on all six. carve-php was already correct on all of them.

Corpus cases for these belong in the spec repo and will follow there.

author: jay-sahnan
body:
## What this fixes

Contact discovery decided whether someone works at a company from a single line: their LinkedIn headline. Most people do not name their employer there, so almost everyone came back `uncertain`, and `uncertain` still attached them to the company at confidence 0.2, rendered identically to confirmed staff.

Measured on Browserbase before this branch:

```
[contact-filter] Judging 39 candidates for "Browserbase" (0 name-matched headlines)
uncertain: 39 of 39
```

That is how six people who actually work at Chronicle Labs, Okta, Box, Hashgraph, Amazon and Stash ended up in a Browserbase campaign, each with a pattern-guessed `@browserbase.com` address that read as confirmation.

## The change

Exa already returns the profile page text on those same searches (100% coverage, measured, with dated experience blocks) and we discarded it. The judge now reads that text and the page's date, and can reach two verdicts it could not before:

- `former_employee`: a dated stint at the company that has already ended
- `rejected`: a full experience listing that names other companies and never the target, which is positive evidence of absence rather than missing evidence

Both detach. A deterministic staleness guard downgrades any `verified` resting on a snapshot older than 120 days.

Measured after, with the shipped code (`pnpm probe:affiliation`):

```
verified 34, uncertain 3, former_employee 2, rejected 1   (of 40)
```

Erik Dominguez caught as departed (Oct 2024 to Mar 2026). Chris Kim rejected, naming Box. Victor Lue lands in `uncertain` because the staleness guard catches his March snapshot saying Browserbase while his live headline says Anthropic.

Cost: the page text is already paid for at the Exa call. The larger judge prompt adds roughly $0.012 per discovery call on Haiku. Net spend is down, because unconfirmed contacts no longer consume email-provider credits.

## Also in here

- The three genuinely unresolvable contacts get a "Needs review" section with Confirm and Not here, wired to the affiliation endpoints that already existed
- A human's "Not here" is recorded as `user_rejected` rather than erasing the provenance, so the queue terminates instead of re-adding the same person on the next run
- Email discovery is gated on the send threshold in all three batch paths, so we stop minting company-domain addresses for people we cannot place at the company
- Person enrichment keeps each source's date and stops overwriting a correct title with a stale one when sources conflict
- `pnpm probe:affiliation [Company] [Title...]` re-runs the measurement above against production code, read-only

## Requires a migration

`supabase/migrations/20260802000000_affiliation_detach.sql`. Additive: widens the `affiliation_source` CHECK and adds a nullable `affiliation_detached_from` column.

**Apply it before the code ships.** The pre-existing CHECK permitted six values and did not include the new sources, so without the migration every detach raises SQLSTATE 23514.

## Review found five blockers, all fixed

The first nine commits built the feature; a four-dimension review (correctness, security, UI, test quality) found five blockers and the rest of the commits fix them. Worth knowing, because each was invisible to a passing test suite:

1. **The CHECK constraint above rejected every detach**, and `recordAffiliation` never destructured its update `error`, so it failed silently. The feature had never worked outside the test fakes.
2. **A rejection about company B detached the person from company A.** `organizationId: null` meant "detach from wherever you are", so a correct verdict that someone works at Box detached them from Box. Detaching writes now carry the org that was judged and no-op otherwise.
3. **The detach was irreversible.** A row at weight 0.8 with a null org could never be re-attached by any machine source to any company, including the right one. Attaching a detached row is no longer measured against the detaching weight, except at the company that rejected them.
4. **The review queue never terminated.** "Not here" nulled the provenance, which scored below a bare search stamp, so the next run re-added them.
5. **The test fakes did not model the query layer.** `select()` returned whole fixtures regardless of the column list and `eq()` was a no-op, so nine reverts of production code passed the entire suite, one of them failing unsafe. The fakes are now unified in `src/__tests__/helpers/supabase-fake.ts`, project only requested columns, and throw on reading an unselected one. All ten mutations are now caught.

## Verification

- 577 tests across 68 files, clean typecheck
- The judge measured against live Exa data with the shipped prompt, not a copy
- `recordAffiliation` exercised against real Postgres for the detach, the scope check, the re-attach and `user_rejected` stickiness

Not yet done, and worth doing before merge:
- The migration has only been applied locally
- Nothing has been clicked in a browser; the review-queue UI is verified in jsdom only
- Discovery to detach to review queue has not been run end to end against the deployed app

## Deliberately out of scope

Contacts already stored at 0.2 are not backfilled. Re-running discovery only re-judges people the search returns again; the review queue is what surfaces the rest for a human. A bulk re-judge is a follow-up once the mismatch rate is known to be sane.

author: jedwards1230
body:
The roster's group headers and the status panel already contract a cwd under `$HOME` to `~/…` (gofer#337). The identity header two lines above them did not — so the same directory appeared on one screen under two different names:

```
gofer v0.7.1
gpt-5.6-sol · /Users/justin/orchestration/repos/gofer     ← header
0 awaiting input · 0 working · 9 idle · 0 completed

~/orchestration/repos/gofer                               ← group header
```

`identityHeaderLines` now renders `meta.Cwd` through `displayHome`, the same helper `cwdLabel` and the status panel use. That function is the header **every** screen opens with — the overview, and via `attachHeaderLines` the attach transcript, its approval prompts, and the command panel — so one call site covers both views.

## Why nothing caught it

`GoldenMeta`'s `Cwd` is the literal string `"~/orchestration"` — already contracted. `displayHome` returns a path with no `$HOME` prefix unchanged, so **every golden renders byte-identically whether or not the header contracts anything.**

`TestAppHeaderOnEveryScreen` asserts `"claude-sonnet-5 · ~/orchestration"` and passes with or without this fix: the tilde it matches came from the fixture, not from the code under test. A fixture that pre-bakes the transformation cannot test the transformation.

## Test

`TestIdentityHeaderContractsHome` builds an absolute path under `os.UserHomeDir()` and asserts both directions — the contracted form present, `$HOME` absent — at a width wide enough that `truncate` cannot be what removes the prefix.

**Mutation-verified.** With the `displayHome` call reverted the tree still builds and the named test fails on both assertions:

```
--- FAIL: TestIdentityHeaderContractsHome
    header context "gpt-5.6-sol · /Users/justin/orchestration/repos/gofer"
      does not contain the contracted cwd "~/orchestration/repos/gofer"
    header context ... still spells $HOME ("/Users/justin") out in full
```

## VHS

`overviewCwdHomeScene`'s meta carried no `Cwd` at all, so `roster-cwd-home.tape`'s before/after `HOME` swap could not show the header line. It now seeds an absolute one and rides the same pair — no new tape, and the existing one gains the header alongside the group headers it already covers.

## Gates

`go build` · `go vet` · `go vet -tags workerbench` · `go test ./...` · `golangci-lint run` (0 issues) — all green.

author: arming-afk
body:
Phase 4's agent: prompt, context, client, loop, and the entry point that chooses between it and the state machine.

Independent of #15 — the agent core imports nothing from `lib/agent/golden/`. They can merge in either order.

## Nothing changes for anyone on deploy

`agent_enabled` defaults to **false**. Three routes back to the deterministic path, all of them wanted:

| Condition | Why |
|---|---|
| Shop has not opted in | Deploying changes nothing until someone sets the flag on one shop deliberately. Clearing it reverts within one message, no deploy. |
| No `AGENT_API_*` configured | A deployment without keys keeps working exactly as before. |
| **Model did not answer** | The one that matters in production. |

A free tier's real failure mode is rate limiting, and it arrives **precisely when a shop is busiest**. An outage degrades to last month's behaviour rather than to silence — the argument `CLAUDE.md` makes for gutting `dispatch.ts` into a fallback rather than deleting it.

## Tool gating: `dispatch.ts`'s own switch, re-aimed

Instead of deciding *for* the model, `switch (order.status)` now decides what the model may choose *between*.

| Status | Tools offered |
|---|---|
| no order | 7 — the only place `create_order` exists |
| `pending_payment` | 7 |
| `verifying` | **4** |
| `paid` | 5 |

Twelve become ~5. That's a per-round token saving on every message forever, but **the larger win is accuracy** — a tool that is not offered cannot be picked wrongly, and small models degrade as options multiply. Gating drops the tool from the list rather than refusing it at call time, so the model never learns it exists.

- `create_order` — only with no live order. Two live orders is two QRs for one purchase.
- `verify_payment_slip` — withheld in `verifying`; a second run would race the first over one order's payment state.
- `save_shipping_address` — only after payment.
- `search_products` / `get_shop_info` / `escalate_to_human` — **every status.** A customer mid-payment still asks about colours, and R7 says keep talking through `verifying`.

## The prompt is for usefulness, not safety

Everything in it is a preference the model can ignore, and the design assumes it sometimes will. Prices come from the catalog because no tool accepts one; consent is re-read from the transcript; payment claims are caught by `guardReply` afterwards.

**If a line in the prompt were the only thing preventing a bad outcome, it would be in the wrong place.**

It is also short on purpose: a long list of prohibitions reads to a small model as a list of things worth attempting, and every line competes with the tool descriptions that actually decide the turn.

## Context

Capped at 30 messages. History multiplies with rounds, so an unbounded window makes a shop's chattiest customer its most expensive without limit.

- **Tool rows are stored but never replayed.** A stale price in an old tool result looks exactly like a fresh one and the model cannot tell them apart.
- **Images become a marker.** Slip verification is a bank API call, never a visual read — and a model that could *see* a slip is one that could be talked into an opinion about it.

## client.ts has no provider abstraction, on purpose

Typhoon's tool calling is OpenAI-compatible down to honouring `additionalProperties: false`, so the twelve Phase 3 schemas transfer untranslated and switching provider is three env vars. A `ProviderRegistry` would be infrastructure for a problem that priced itself away.

**No retries, no failover, no circuit breaker.** That is policy about when to give up on a provider, it needs to be observable, and a retry hidden inside the function that makes one HTTP request would silently double every slow turn with nothing upstream able to see it.

## The loop

Round cap **6**. Rounds are the largest multiplier on turn cost, and a model that wants more is looping — the cap turns "expensive forever" into "one truncated turn".

Both bad-input cases come back to the model as a *result*, not an exception:
- hallucinated tool name → told which tools exist (cheaper than another wasted round)
- unparseable arguments → told to resend as JSON. **Defaulting to `{}` is how a malformed call quietly becomes an action.**

Canonical copy is sent **before** the model's prose, so a payment instruction never arrives after a chatty aside about it.

## Worth reviewing closely

- **`entry.ts`'s fallback catch is narrow** — only `ModelUnavailableError`. A genuine bug still throws and reaches the webhook's per-event handler, rather than being papered over as an outage.
- **The lease contract.** `handleIncomingEvent` must run inside `withConversationLease`; `webhook.ts` does. `create_order`'s read-then-act depends on it and nothing enforces it.
- **`guardTripped` is logged, not persisted yet.** A rising count is the signal to turn the flag off — it wants somewhere better than stdout.

## Verification

`tsc`, `eslint`, `next build` clean. **293 tests with the emulator** (272 on this base + 21 new).

The test worth reading: a model calling `mark_as_paid` — a tool that does not exist — costs one wasted round and the turn still ends in a sentence, with nothing recorded as executed.

author: danielhanold
body:
↩ [**Change 0192 — opencode support for profile-routed Docket builds**](https://github.com/danielhanold/docket/blob/docket/docs/changes/active/0192-opencode-profile-routed-build-support.md)

Registers **opencode** as docket's fourth first-class agent harness, alongside Claude, Cursor, and Codex. Unlike change 0169 (Codex), which shipped defaults into an existing substrate, this builds the substrate too: harness registration, a native emitter, and dispatch wiring, plus the complete sixteen-agent shipped default block.

## What changed

- **Registration** — `opencode` joins `DOCKET_GI_HARNESS_TOKENS` (the canonical roster, which also feeds `VALID_HARNESS_TOKENS` and the managed `.gitignore` block), `HD_KNOWN_HARNESSES`, and `HD_SHIPPED_HARNESSES`. The sidecar validator now requires a complete sixteen-agent `opencode:` block in both directions.
- **Shipped defaults** — a complete `opencode:` block in `agents/harness-defaults.yml`. Three models, chosen for cheap high intelligence: DeepSeek V4 Flash on every volume row, Kimi K3 on the judgment rows and the ladder top at two efforts, GPT-5.6 Luna as the family-diverse auto-groom critic. All OpenRouter-prefixed. `review-deep` equals `build-max`, preserving the cap-rung invariant.
- **Native emitter** — `emit_opencode_md` writes `.opencode/agents/docket-*.md` with `mode: subagent`, the resolved model verbatim, and the resolved effort as `reasoningEffort:`. It gets its own named emitter rather than inheriting the Claude-shaped default — the `*)` fallback is exactly how the Cursor defect (change 0135) shipped.
- **Dispatch** — the committed project-root `AGENTS.md` dispatch block becomes harness-neutral and is now **shared** by Codex and opencode, which read the same file. `sync_codex_agents_md_dispatch` → `sync_agents_md_dispatch`; the block is stripped only when the *last* dispatch harness is de-listed.
- **Surfaces** — a singly commented mirror block in `.docket.example.yml` with round-trip evidence, a new `docs/opencode/setup.md`, and the maintained harness enumerations across the README and the agent-layer reference.
- **Guards** — three guards that hard-coded `claude cursor codex` now derive their population from `$HD_SHIPPED_HARNESSES` with anti-vacuity floors, so a future fifth harness arms them for free.

`REGISTERED_RUNNERS`, the `docket-build` controller's routing, the shared task-worker contract, and the Claude/Cursor/Codex mappings are all unchanged.

## Verified against opencode 1.18.11

Probed with `opencode debug agent`, which prints the fully resolved config. This settled the spec's one open question — the effort-passthrough spelling:

```json
{
  "name": "docket-build-economy",
  "mode": "subagent",
  "model": { "providerID": "openrouter", "modelID": "deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash-0731" },
  "options": { "reasoningEffort": "medium" }
}
```

opencode has no first-class effort field; it forwards unrecognized agent-frontmatter keys to the provider as model options, so `reasoningEffort` is a real per-agent effort. All three shipped model IDs were confirmed present in the live catalog (`opencode models`, 360 entries).

Two plumbing checks saved work: `.gitignore` needed no separate edit (the managed block generates per-harness entries from the roster token), and `link-skills.sh` needed none either (opencode resolves skills from `~/.agents/skills/`, which it already populates).

## Build evidence

<!-- docket:build-evidence:start -->
command:  for test in tests/test_*.sh; do "$DOCKET_BASH_PATH" "$test"; done
result:   green
head_sha: eb5e92821da231c77dc4775867cae92067ba09cd
ran_at:   2026-08-02T16:31:47Z
<!-- docket:build-evidence:end -->

75 test files, 0 red. Built with `docket-build`: six plan tasks at standard ×4 / premium ×2, no escalations. The gate went red once — the added table row pushed `agent-layer.md` past its enforced size budget — and was repaired at the premium rung by a prose slim with the budget left untouched.

## Review

Reviewed at the **deep** rung (highest profile routed was premium; the 1785-line diff independently qualifies). **0 blockers**, so nothing was auto-fixed. The findings below are left for merge-time judgment.

**Important**

1. `docs/codex/setup.md`'s de-list note is now false — it still says de-listing Codex removes the `AGENTS.md` block, but with the block shared, de-listing Codex from a repo still targeting opencode leaves it in place. The opencode doc got the correct "last harness" caveat; the codex doc did not.
2. No test exercises two dispatch harnesses at once. The central property — a repo targeting both gets the block exactly once, and de-listing one while the other remains leaves it in place — is unasserted, and both new fixtures pass against the *old* codex-only predicate.
3. The opencode emitter test asserts only frontmatter. If body extraction or the skills preamble regressed to empty, the definition would carry no prompt and the suite would stay green. Both sibling emitters guard this.
4. The effort-drop-when-no-model rationale is stated as verified behavior but the model-less case was never probed. Unlike Cursor (which must drop it, since effort is encoded inside the model string), opencode has an independent key. The unverified claim currently ships in three places.

**Minor** — the shared block's head claims defaults "on every harness it supports", overreaching past the shipped set to the unpinned `agents`/`kiro`/`windsurf` tokens; two new guards key on enumerated spellings rather than shape and grep the whole file rather than the marker-bounded block; the `--check` diagnostic hand-lists "(codex, opencode)" instead of interpolating the variable; and the agent-layer table's opencode cell holds a full path where its three siblings hold a bare extension.

## ADR

**ADR-0036** received a dated `## Update` rather than a new ADR — this change reverses and replaces nothing, and its two decisions (the block is committed; it is machine-neutral) stand verbatim while only their scope widens.

## Merge-gate checks for a human

Recorded in [the results file](https://github.com/danielhanold/docket/blob/feat/opencode-profile-routed-build-support/docs/results/2026-08-02-opencode-profile-routed-build-support-results.md). The model IDs are **external truth** — every mirror assert compares generated output against the sidecar that generated it, so both sides move together and no in-repo test can ever detect a wrong ID:

- Confirm the three OpenRouter IDs resolve under your credentials (catalog presence is not entitlement).
- Live-certify the standard and premium rungs (economy was certified during the build).
- Run one real end-to-end opencode dispatch — everything certified so far is resolved config, not an executed run.

Waived deliberately, per the spec: the max rung, the three review rungs, automatic classification, and the single-escalation path.

## Plan deviations

Four worth knowing, detailed in the results file: a plan-supplied `sed` was unanchored and would have corrupted a fixture's indent regexes; three plan-supplied asserts were vacuous or violated the repo's own guard rules and were replaced with stronger forms; the documentation update set was larger than the plan listed; and a **latent defect** was found and fixed — `ex_slice`'s `sed` address broke on slash-bearing model IDs (opencode's are the first shipped values containing `/`), silently yielding an empty slice rather than a visible error.

author: antoine-teston
body:
## Le défaut

Le hub le dit lui-même : **Rockstar prolonge parfois un événement.** Ce kind est donc le seul du dépôt dont le contenu mute après publication — et toute la chaîne était bâtie sur l'hypothèse inverse.

`factDiscriminant` hache `source_url + claim`. Une prolongation change la fin de fenêtre → le claim → le discriminant → l'`id`. Au lieu de corriger le compte à rebours, on écrivait une **seconde entrée chevauchant la première**.

Et côté app, `currentEvent(at:)` faisait `events.first { isActive }` sur un tableau **sans ordre garanti** (`ContentMerge.merge`, pas un tri). La fenêtre affichée était tirée au sort entre deux dates, avec un résultat capable de changer d'une synchronisation à l'autre sans que la donnée bouge.

## Le correctif

- **`windowDiscriminant`** : l'identité tient à la source, au jeu et au **début** de fenêtre. Un début ne bouge pas — une semaine qui a commencé a commencé — donc la fin redevient une donnée révisable. Corollaire voulu : la phase 2 d'un événement de deux semaines a son propre début, donc sa propre entrée.
- **Révision au lieu d'ignorance**, annoncée champ par champ (`RÉVISE (PUBLIÉ) … [endsAt]`). Une entrée publiée garde son statut : un compte à rebours faux en ligne doit se corriger en ligne. La révision arrive dans le diff d'une PR, où un humain peut la refuser.
- **`currentEvent(at:)`** : le plus récemment **commencé** gagne, départagé jusqu'à l'`id`. Un ordre partiel aurait laissé le même indéterminisme un cran plus bas. `latestEvent()` garde son tri sur la **fin** — c'est « ce qui vient de se terminer » qu'il cherche — mais devient total aussi.

## Deux étages de propriété, et c'est un test existant qui les a imposés

Ma première version révisait toute entrée non-squelette. Un test a refusé : un squelette **rédigé à la main voit `needsRewrite` supprimé**, donc mon code le prenait pour une entrée machine et écrasait la rédaction.

D'où la séparation :

- la **fenêtre** appartient toujours à la machine — `content-editor.md` interdit explicitement à l'agent d'y toucher ;
- **le reste** ne se révise que si la machine est l'unique auteur, reconnaissable à un `needsRewrite: false` *présent*.

## Vérifié

- **Une prolongation simulée sur l'entrée publiée de la semaine** : `endsAt` révisé, statut intact, aucune duplication, changement annoncé
- 150 tests Node (11 neufs sur la mutation) ; 13 tests du modèle dont **4 neufs qui échouaient avant le correctif** — chacun vérifie les **deux ordres d'arrivée**, sans quoi il ne prouverait rien
- `TEST SUCCEEDED` sur la suite iOS complète, `validate` 632/632, `check-publishable` 632/632

Dernier changement d'`id` de cette entrée : les débuts de fenêtre ne bougent pas.

body: Plugin failures could leave operators with opaque, stale, or unrecoverable states, while restart exhaustion and delivery overflow made recovery and logs unreliable. This change persists sanitized bounded diagnostics, makes retries authoritative and deadlock-safe, rate-limits overflow logs, and covers desktop/mobile recovery paths with tests and docs. ## Important Changes - Persist bounded, timestamped plugin diagnostics with redaction for bearer tokens, PATs, labeled secrets, and host home paths. - Keep restart exhaustion and concurrent manual Enable safe by releasing the manager mutex before waiting for process shutdown; aggregate ring-buffer overflow warnings per plugin. - Show diagnostics and recovery actions on desktop and phone settings surfaces, refetch failed Enable results, enforce 44px phone targets, and wrap long messages. ## Validation - `go test -race ./internal/plugins/...` — 493 tests passed. - `make -C apps/backend test` and `make -C apps/backend lint` — passed. - `go vet ./internal/plugins/...` — passed. - Focused web Vitest suites — 75 tests passed. - Web typecheck, lint, i18n check, and i18n ratchet — passed. - `make build-backend build-web` — passed. - Focused desktop and mobile Playwright plugin recovery tests — 3 tests passed. - Public docs validation — 58 tests and 41 published pages passed. - `git diff --check` — passed. ## Screenshots ![Desktop plugin recovery row](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/kdlbs/kandev/8d1a501d55a821b278c3131eaea8195920e98e90/desktop-plugin-recovery.png) ![Mobile plugin recovery row](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/kdlbs/kandev/8d1a501d55a821b278c3131eaea8195920e98e90/mobile-plugin-recovery.png) ## Checklist - [ ] I have performed a self-review of my code. - [ ] I have manually tested my changes and they work as expected. - [ ] My changes have tests that cover the new functionality and edge cases. - [ ] If my change touches UI files (`apps/web/`), I have added or updated Playwright e2e tests in `apps/web/e2e/` and verified them with `make test-e2e`. - [ ] I checked whether this affects public docs in `docs/public/**` and updated them or noted why no docs change is needed.

author: tzervas
body:
`.vscode/mcp.json` is tracked in this repo. Editor state is per-developer and shouldn't be committed.

This isn't only tidiness. A committed `.vscode` is exactly how `memory-gate` ended up with a VSCode autocomplete cache in its history that indexed **Trivy's and TruffleHog's own secret-detection test fixtures** — 40-character strings labelled `aws_secret_access_key`. GitHub Push Protection then blocked every branch of that repo during the org migration. The credentials were fake (they're scanner test data), but the block was real and cost a history rewrite to clear.

Changes:
- remove `.vscode/` from tracking
- add `.vscode/` and `.idea/` to `.gitignore`, matching the standard already used in `gha-runner-ctl`

**History is not rewritten.** The file is removed going forward only, so existing clones and SHAs are unaffected. Only one commit ever touched `.vscode` here and it carries nothing credential-shaped (469 bytes, a single `servers` key), so a rewrite isn't warranted.

Anyone with a custom OpenAI-compatible endpoint configured who opens the `/model` picker: each custom endpoint gets a live `/models` probe, and `fetch_api_models`'s default timeout is 5s connect. `test_custom_providers_uses_live_models_for_multi_model_endpoint` (added on main after this PR's base) pins the exact kwargs of the probe call; with the timeout now always explicit the pinned shape gains `timeout: 5.0`. One-line assertion update.

- Monkeypatch-seam sweep: all `fetch_api_models` test seams use `**kwargs`-tolerant fakes (`lambda *a, **k` / `def fake(...,**kwargs)`) — no breakage

Capacitor's iOS template ships the placeholder `PRODUCT_BUNDLE_IDENTIFIER = com.getcapacitor.App`. Signing tools match a provisioning profile to a target **by bundle id**, so with the placeholder in place the profile created for `com.weddingandco.app` matched nothing and the archive failed with:

in the Signing & Capabilities editor. (in target 'App' from project 'App')

`scripts/ios-patch.js` now rewrites every `PRODUCT_BUNDLE_IDENTIFIER` to the `appId` from `capacitor.config.json`, so the generated project always carries the real bundle id — locally and in CI.

Once #761 merges and step (c) re-runs (install + bootstrap, documented runbook), this PR is the next step: mergeable on approval at that point.

## What

Slice 4 (TRADE) of the standalone momentum pipeline (renquant-model design `doc/design/2026-08-02-momentum-pipeline-architecture.md` §3, model#195; build-order amendment model#197): the `momentum_residual_v0_shadow` entry added to `ranking.panel_scoring.shadow_models` in **both** `configs/strategy_config.json` and `configs/strategy_config.golden.json` (byte-identical entries; prod/golden parity asserted by test).

```json
{
  "name": "momentum_residual_v0_shadow",
  "kind": "momentum_residual",
  "artifact_path": "artifacts/momentum/momentum_artifact_ledger.jsonl"
}
```

plus two narrative keys: `_2026_08_02_momentum_shadow_lane` (role; cites model#195 + model#197 + orch#757; "data collection, no verdict claimed; promotion via the standard gates") and `_2026_08_02_pending_first_artifact` (the resolution reality below).

## The artifact_path decision (verified convention)

- Base convention mirrored from the surviving blend-leg entry: relative refs resolve **strategy_dir-first** through the canonical resolver (`renquant-pipeline kernel/artifact_resolver.py`: absolute -> strategy_dir -> repo_root), strategy_dir = `RenQuant/backtesting/renquant_104` `[VERIFIED — resolver source + orch#757 progress doc's serving-root ground truth]`. No absolute path, no `..` (the config-artifact-path-gate incident class).
- The orch#757 weekly job publishes `artifacts/momentum/<cutoff>/momentum_residual_v0.json` (artifact kind `momentum_residual_v0`) **plus** the append-only digest-chained ledger `artifacts/momentum/momentum_artifact_ledger.jsonl` `[VERIFIED — wrapper OUT_ROOT + model tools/momentum_train_run.py LEDGER_BASENAME]`.
- The entry pins **the ledger** — the one cutoff-stable file in the publish set. The `<cutoff>` component changes weekly and the FIRST cutoff (the first post-grant Saturday firing date) is unknowable in a PR that must be frozen under review and merged untouched inside the batch; a dated pin would also demand a weekly config-PR cadence nobody designed. The ledger exists from run 1 onward, every weekly run appends, and each row's `artifact_content_sha256` chain transitively pins the dated artifact beside it `[VERIFIED — model src/renquant_model_momentum/ledger.py]`. Serving-handler contract (declared in the narrative key): read the verified ledger tail row, load the dated artifact it names, verify its self-carried `content_sha256`.

## Resolution reality (stated honestly, per model#197)

Until the slice-5 batch installs the job and the first artifact + ledger publish, this path resolves **nowhere** — which is exactly why this PR merges only inside the batch. No test in this repo resolves the path against the operator's disk (that test would be red or vacuously green per machine); the static resolve gate is umbrella CI at pin-advance time. Instead a **bounded pending guard** (the launchd-manifest `PENDING_INSTALL` idiom): `tests/test_strategy_configs.py::PENDING_FIRST_ARTIFACT = {"momentum_residual_v0_shadow"}` with a test asserting the set of shadow entries declaring a pending-first-artifact key equals exactly that named set — an unnamed pending entry cannot ride in, and the post-batch follow-up PR must delete the key and shrink the set together.

## Tests

- Exact `shadow_models` pin updated to the two-lane state (blend leg + momentum); prod/golden parity pin unchanged and passing.
- +2 tests: the bounded pending guard; the momentum entry pins the ledger path, repo-relative, no `..` escape.
- Suite: before 93 passed / 1 failed / 1 skipped; after **95 passed / 1 failed / 1 skipped** `[VERIFIED — make test in the worktree]`. The 1 failure (`test_config_drift_cli_exposes_repo_root`) is pre-existing and environmental (spawns the system python3.9 which lacks renquant-common; fails identically on the untouched main checkout at its current branch). Zero new failures.

## Findings the batch must clear BEFORE step (e) — surfaced, not solved here

- **F-1 (pipeline)**: kind `momentum_residual` is not registered in the pipeline model registry (origin/main 2026-08-02: xgb / patchtst / hf_patchtst / regime_router / blend only). After pin advance, the shadow task would emit a daily load-fault health record for this lane (soft-fail; primary unaffected) until the pipeline-side handler slice lands. Sequence that slice before or with (e), or accept the fault as the designed reminder.
- **F-2 (umbrella gate identity layer)**: `scripts/check_config_artifact_paths.py` requires every shadow entry's resolved artifact to carry inline `trained_date` + `config_fingerprint` and fails closed otherwise. The momentum artifact carries neither (`trained_at_utc` / `cutoff_date` / `content_sha256` instead), and the ledger is JSONL (no loadable inline metadata). Step (e) fails this gate for the momentum entry regardless of which publish-set file is pinned, until the umbrella gate learns a momentum-aware rule. Owner: umbrella-side; out of this repo's write scope.
- **F-3 (umbrella gate CI topology)**: the gate's verify-pinned-paths job resolves against the committed umbrella tree; the blend-leg artifact passes because it is git-tracked. The momentum publish set is job-written machine state that nothing commits — the batch design must reconcile this at (e).

## Scope

2 config files (one shadow entry each) + 1 test file + `doc/progress/2026-08-02-momentum-shadow-lane-config.md`. No src/ change; no production input, job, artifact, or machine state touched; merge-inert by ordering (nothing reads the entry until the batch's pin advance, and this PR does not merge until step (d)). Shadow = data collection; no capital-admission gate added or tightened.

Fixed the creator_id cookie disappearing 1-2 seconds after login on Vercel production.

Root cause: logout links in all shell components (creator, admin, account, affiliate) used Next.js <Link> which prefetches visible hrefs by default. Since logout routes are GET endpoints that clear auth cookies, the prefetch silently wiped the session cookie right after page load.

Changes:

- - changed sameSite from "strict" to "lax" on creator login API route for consistency with other login routes

Potential fix for [https://github.com/Alpha-Panel/AlphaPanel/security/code-scanning/21](https://github.com/Alpha-Panel/AlphaPanel/security/code-scanning/21)

The safest fix without changing intended functionality is to **escape option text before inserting it into HTML strings**. Here, `i.buttondown_txt` is intended as button label text, not markup, so HTML escaping preserves visual behavior while blocking injection.

In `alpha-panel/web/httpdocs/public/themes/default/app-assets/vendors/js/forms/spinner/jquery.bootstrap-touchspin.js`, add a small internal HTML-escape helper inside `D.fn.TouchSpin` scope, then use it where `i.buttondown_txt` is concatenated into `n` (both button markup branches shown). This keeps existing plugin behavior (string-built markup, same classes/structure) while neutralizing unsafe characters (`& < > " ' \``) in label text.

No external dependency is required; a local helper is sufficient and minimally invasive.

author: valstan
body:
## Summary

Заказ владельца 2026-08-02: «все сервисы вмалмыже должны работать на https», и отдельно — «пользователь Радара после входа должен попадать в свой личный кабинет».

### 🔴 Петля на `радар.вмалмыже.рф` — Радар не открывался у всех, кто вошёл

Домен отвечал бесконечной цепочкой `/` → `/radar` → `/`. nginx-блок создан 18.07 с `location = / { return 302 /radar; }`, когда Радар жил на `/radar`; 26.07 интерфейс переехал на корень, и приложение стало отвечать на `/radar` редиректом на `/`. **Две копии одного решения разошлись.**

Аноним петли **не видел** — его на первом же шаге уводило на страницу входа. Поэтому баг прожил неделю незамеченным и бил ровно по настоящим пользователям Радара, то есть по тем, кто уже вошёл. Воспроизведён прогоном цепочки редиректов **через nginx с живой сессией** (мимо nginx, прямо на `:8000`, не воспроизводится вовсе).

Лечение: маршрутизация внутри приложения живёт только в приложении; nginx этого решения больше не дублирует.

### 🔒 https на всех поддоменах

`вход.`, `радар.`, `валентин.` получили тот же редирект, что и `сарафан.` Для входа это не косметика: сессионная кука `Secure`, по голому http она не сохраняется — **вход на http-адресе молча не работал**, человек по кругу возвращался на «войдите».

Редирект ограничен **GET/HEAD**: server-to-server POST соседей (`/oidc/token`, `/api/gateway/`, `/api/ecosystem/`, `/api/classifier/`) 301 бы сломал — клиенты на редиректе часто превращают POST в GET и теряют тело. Условие — явное `= "http"`, режим отказа описан в `config/nginx_maps.conf`.

### Что расконсервировало включение https

Service Worker и Push API живут только в secure context: на голом http браузер молча отклонял регистрацию, `.catch(() => {})` это проглатывал, и дефекты PWA были невидимы. Всплыли три, все починены:

1. **`/sw.js` отдавал 403** роли `radar` — путь не был публичным, а поблажка для радар-хоста написана на точное `/`. Следствие неочевидное: `initPush()` показывал кнопку-колокольчик и **вис навсегда** на `navigator.serviceWorker.ready` (промис без регистрации не резолвится и не отклоняется, поэтому `.catch` не срабатывал).
2. **`sw.js` кэшировал жёсткий `/radar`**, хотя на своём домене кабинет живёт на корне. Cache API отказывается класть redirected-ответ → `install` падал целиком. Теперь оболочка выводится из scope регистрации, кэш `v6`.
3. **Кука состояния ВК-входа была host-only**, а callback всегда приземляется на issuer → первая попытка после каждого выхода падала в «Сессия ВК-входа истекла». Больнее всего по ВК-only аккаунтам, у которых пароля нет вовсе. Теперь кука на всю зону `.вмалмыже.рф` (blob подписан HMAC, TTL 10 минут), удаление — с тем же `domain`.

Плюс `/api/radar/` разрешён гостю на хосте сарафана — регрессия [#422](https://github.com/Valstan/setka/pull/422): установленные PWA помнят старый адрес `сарафан.вмалмыже.рф/radar`, оболочка поднимается из кэша SW, и её запросы данных упирались бы в 403. Навигация по-прежнему уводит на `радар.вмалмыже.рф`.

### Конфиги nginx сведены в git

`config/nginx_*.conf` сняты с прода и сверены. Лежавшая в репозитории версия `setka.conf` была **годичной давности** — `listen 80` без TLS и закомментированный редирект: скопировавший её на бокс снял бы HTTPS с технического домена. Тот же класс разъезда копий, который породил петлю на радаре.

### Карта доменов

Новый [`docs/ops/HOSTS.md`](docs/ops/HOSTS.md) — что где раздаётся, кто имеет доступ, какие правила уже ломались и чек-лист перед правкой. Ровно то, о чём просил владелец: «у нас много чего нацеплено на разные поддомены, надо не сломать случайно новыми разработками».

## Test plan

- Полный прогон **2016 passed** (+2: публичность `/sw.js` на всех хостах; данные Радара со старого адреса на хосте сарафана).
- `pre-commit run --all-files` — black / isort / flake8 passed.
- На проде до правки: цепочка редиректов с живой сессией через nginx — 8 витков без завершения (петля подтверждена). После деплоя — перепроверка той же командой.
- Поток Радара прогнан на проде с реальной сессией смоук-аккаунта: кабинет на своём хосте 200, статика 200, заход с хоста сарафана уводит домой, выход из сессии работает со всех трёх хостов.

## Применение на проде

`git pull` + `systemctl restart setka`. nginx — **строго по порядку**: сначала `setka_maps.conf`, `nginx -t`, затем серверные блоки, снова `nginx -t`, и только потом `reload`. Блок без карты не стартует вовсе («unknown variable») — ляжет всё, включая публичную витрину.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

author: sanketsudake
body:
Consolidates the outstanding RFC-0028/0029 work into one branch. Supersedes **#3639**, **#3640** and **#3648**, which are closed in favour of this — they were touching the same chart templates and the same `test/helm/portdrift_test.go`, so keeping them parallel meant re-resolving the same append/append conflicts on every rebase. That churn was the main source of review noise.

Every commit is preserved, so the individual pieces stay reviewable in isolation.

---

## 1. Auth material: provision the master in-cluster (RFC-0029 §10)

The chart previously minted the internal-auth master **in the template**, which makes it a function of render inputs rather than cluster state — a re-render with different inputs silently rotates it, and every derived key with it.

- `internalAuth.existingSecret` — point the install at a Secret you already manage. Resolution now happens in **one place** (`fission.internalAuthSecretName`); previously each consumer re-derived the name, which is the kind of duplication that drifts silently and then 401s at runtime.
- `internalAuth.autoGenerate` — a pre-upgrade hook (`cmd/preupgradechecks/generateauth.go`) generates the master in-cluster if absent. It `get`s first so a re-run reuses the existing master rather than rotating every derived key with no dual-accept window.
- The namespace set is supplied by the **chart**, never derived in Go. Under dynamic/cluster tenancy the master stays in the release namespace: tenant namespaces get controller-owned derived keys, and a master there would defeat the isolation end state.

### The RBAC bug this consolidation surfaced

The generation Role granted `["get","create"]` under a single `resourceNames` fence. **RBAC matches `resourceNames` against the name in the request path, and a POST carries the name in the body** — so the authorizer sees an empty name, the rule never matches, and generation fails Forbidden. The fence did not tighten the grant, it voided it: `autoGenerate` was dead on arrival for anyone who enabled it. CI never caught it because CI supplies `internalAuth.secret` directly and never exercises the path.

`get` keeps its fence; `create` drops it, because RBAC offers no way to keep it. This is the exact inverse of the CRD ClusterRole next door, which *does* keep `resourceNames` on `create` — server-side apply PATCHes a named path, so create is authorized against that name. Switching generation to apply would recover the fence and is deliberately not done: apply takes ownership of `.data` and would rotate the master, the one thing this hook must never do.

The chart guard asserted that *every* rule carried exactly one `resourceName` — it encoded the bug, so it could never have caught it. It now pins both halves separately and fails on the old fenced form.

## 2. Fixed-name inventory (RFC-0029 phase 2)

NetworkPolicies address workloads by a bare `svc:` pod label. A policy naming a label no workload carries does not error — it silently drops the traffic. `TestNetworkPolicySvcLabelsResolveToRealWorkloads` renders the chart and requires every `svc:` selector to resolve to a real workload.

Also `TestBuildermgrCanRollBuilderDeployments`: buildermgr rolls a drifted builder Deployment (#776), which needs `update` on `apps/deployments`. The Role granted only list/create/delete, so the feature would have shipped inert.

## 3. `spec apply` idempotency

A second `fission spec apply` of an unchanged spec rewrote Function package stamps, minting spurious RFC-0025 versions. The stamp is now driven by what this apply actually wrote (`ras.Created`/`ras.Updated`) against live stamps, so an untouched package keeps its existing reference. Covered by `test/integration/suites/common/spec_idempotency_test.go` — which previously existed as a `t.Skip` documenting the bug, and is now unskipped.

## 4. Two CI flakes that were reddening main

**`TestEngineLinearPipeline`** asserted exactly-once *delivery*. `execute()` sets `X-Fission-Workflow-{Run,Attempt}` precisely because delivery is **at-least-once**; what is exactly-once is the recorded outcome (W1/W2). A redelivered attempt re-runs the function and its append loses the result guard — log correct, call counter one high, which is exactly what CI showed (the run succeeded, output was the *first* call's response, all invariants passed). Exact assertions move onto the log via `attempts(log, state)`; the counter becomes a lower bound. The retry-budget and "4xx never retries" cases keep exact expectations, now against `attempts`, and still fail on a policy regression (mutation-verified).

**`TestRunLocalWatch*`** wrote the source file as soon as the first specialize was observed — but `runLocal` specializes inside `launch()` and only *then* calls `serveAndWatch`, where the fsnotify watch is registered. A write landing in that gap is lost for good, which is why the symptom was a full-timeout miss. Now rewrites on every tick, with the tick above the 250ms debounce so a faster loop cannot keep `drainBurst` from draining.

Plus `if-no-files-found: ignore` on the skip-level upgrade leg's artifact upload, so a designed skip does not annotate the run.

---

## Testing

`make code-checks` and `make license-check` exit 0. `go build ./...` clean. `./test/helm/...`, `./pkg/workflow/...`, `./pkg/fission-cli/cmd/function/...`, `./pkg/fission-cli/cmd/spec/...` all pass; workflow and watch suites additionally verified under `-race -count=20` / `-count=8`.

All new guards are mutation-verified: each was confirmed to fail on the defect it targets and pass on the fix.

1. **`000-docs/005-AT-ARCH`** — the `AUTOGEN:live-stats` block, regenerated by `bin/teamkb-systemmap.sh` during the 2026-08-02T10:33Z backup run. The block is machine-owned and marked *"do not hand-edit between the markers"*; this carries only what the script wrote.
2. **`.beads/*.jsonl`** — the export for epic `compile-then-govern-39z` ("Make the brain a living model of current truth") and its 10 children, plus evidence notes on `.2` and `.6`.

The stats block is the repo's only committed record of live brain state — letting it drift means the system map silently stops describing the system. The beads export is the durable record of the epic, since the Dolt DB is git-ignored and the JSONL is what travels.

The regenerated numbers carry a signal worth having in history:

```

decision           62 → 68

convention         47 → 53
troubleshooting   341 → 345
```

Recent growth is landing **entirely in the high-value categories with reference flat.** That corroborates the finding recorded in bead `39z.3`: the 93%-reference mass was **one bulk import on 2026-07-16** (16,201 of 16,221 reference rows, `source=import`), *not* ongoing over-capture by the daily loop — so the originally-planned capture bar would have governed the wrong path.

author: mykytastel
body:
## Summary

Add exact path-sensitive taint tracking for static non-negative array indexes and index-aware array destructuring.

Closes #346.

## Type of change

- [x] Feature
- [x] Precision improvement
- [x] Tests
- [x] Documentation

## What changed

- recognize JavaScript/TypeScript `subscript_expression` nodes as access paths
- normalize static indexes such as `items[0]` to internal exact paths such as `items.0`
- preserve dotted nesting: `payload.items[0].command` becomes `payload.items.0.command`
- reject dynamic, negative, floating-point, and call-based indexes
- collect array destructuring bindings by zero-based path
- support nested object/array patterns and default-value assignment patterns
- prevent whole-RHS fallback from re-tainting a binding whose exact source path is explicitly clean
- add unit tests for normalization, clean overrides, exact tainted indexes, and sibling isolation
- add differential review-zoo safe/unsafe fixtures
- add a changelog fragment

## Behavioral contract

### Clean exact index

```ts
const items = req.body.items;
items[0] = "safe";
const command = items[0];
```

`command` is clean.

### Sibling isolation

```ts
const items = req.body.items;
items[0] = "safe";
exec(items[1]);
```

`items[1]` remains tainted and produces canonical `taint.exec`.

### Exact tainted index

```ts
const items = ["safe"];
items[0] = req.body.command;
exec(items[0]);
```

The exact index is tainted.

## Scope and non-goals

Included:

- static non-negative integer indexes
- nested property/index paths
- exact clean and tainted overrides
- sibling isolation
- contiguous array destructuring

Not included:

- dynamic indexes such as `items[userIndex]`
- negative or floating-point indexes
- sparse array-pattern hole precision
- array rest-element provenance
- collection mutation methods
- heap alias analysis
- interprocedural propagation

## Public contract

- [x] Existing canonical `taint.*` signal kinds are reused
- [x] No JSON, SARIF, Action, MCP, baseline, or finding-ID changes
- [x] Changed-line sink gating is unchanged
- [x] Unknown indexes remain conservative rather than guessed

## Verification

The execution environment could not resolve GitHub for a local checkout, so CI and CodeQL are the compile/test source of truth.

- [x] `cargo fmt --check`
- [x] `cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`
- [x] full Rust test suite
- [x] `cargo test --test review_zoo`
- [x] release-contract checks
- [x] CodeQL
