author: oscharko
body:
## What

Adds a second, phrasing-independent deduplication stage that runs after the existing exact-marker check, and fixes two independent causes of the doubled incomplete-review notice.

**1. Phrasing-independent dedup (`src/publish/similarity.ts`, new).** A candidate finding is now suppressed when an existing **open** conversation this reviewer authored (same App identity — the marker stage's authorship check, reused, since spoofing an open conversation is exactly as dangerous as spoofing a marker):
- anchors the **same file path**,
- has a **line range overlapping** the candidate's within a small tolerance (±2), and
- is **conservatively similar** — a shared quoted code snippet, or overlap-coefficient token similarity above a tuned threshold with a minimum absolute shared-word floor.

A **resolved or outdated** conversation never suppresses, for *either* dedup stage now (`ownMarkers` in `publisher.ts` was updated too, so this is consistent rather than a special case). Resolution state comes from a new best-effort GraphQL lookup in `github/client.ts` (REST has no notion of thread resolution); a failed lookup degrades to today's behaviour — it never gates the review itself.

**2. The doubled notice (two independent contributing causes, both fixed):**
- The notice's marker excluded `head` from its hashed material (`marker.ts`), so a notice for a since-superseded head could alias the notice a fresh run for the *current* head still needs to publish.
- `settleIncomplete` only checked head staleness on one of its four call sites. A run that settled incomplete via an unclassified path (found in seconds) or an engine failure (found only after the engine's multi-minute run) could still publish a notice bound to a commit the pull request had already moved past. The guard now lives inside `settleIncomplete` itself, so every caller is protected uniformly (`review.ts`).

**Incidental, zero-behaviour-change fix:** `marker.ts`'s join separator was a raw embedded NUL byte instead of the `"\0"` escape sequence `review-cache.ts` already uses for the identical anti-collision reason (a path may contain a space; joining without a NUL-shaped delimiter risks two differently-split field sets hashing identically). Replaced for source hygiene — same byte value either way, confirmed by the full existing marker suite passing unchanged.

## Why

Production evidence from `oscharko-dev/Keiko#2926` — the first PR this reviewer ran on alongside CodeRabbit and Codex on identical heads:

```
codingContextRoutes.ts:236  "Restore the route's fallback connector construction."        keiko-for-quality:v1:845d23c1…
codingContextRoutes.ts:236  "Restore the route's default connector construction when …"   keiko-for-quality:v1:0b1968f6…
codingContextRoutes.ts:236  "Keep the fallback port construction for route requests."     keiko-for-quality:v1:a5705d5b…
```

The same finding, three markers, because the exact-marker fingerprint hashes normalized finding **text** — a model that rephrases the same defect on a re-run changes the hash and the marker check has nothing to compare against. The same pattern recurred on `containerRunner.ts:386/387` and `update-remediation.ts:337/338`; roughly a quarter of the PR's 29 inline comments were paraphrase duplicates. Separately, two byte-identical incomplete-review notices (marker `092f3566…`, anchor `ADR-0117…:1`) were published against the same head — investigation (below) found two independent, provable root causes in the notice publication path, not a guess.

## Failure-first proof (both defects)

Per the repo's regression-test discipline, each defect's test was run against the pre-fix code (via `cp` aside + `git checkout HEAD -- <file>` + restore, not `git stash`) to confirm it fails, then restored to confirm it passes.

**Defect 1 — paraphrase dedup** (`publisher.ts` reverted to HEAD, `similarity.ts` removed):
```
× publishFindings > paraphrase deduplication (similarity stage) > suppresses a rephrased repost of the same finding at the same location
  → expected { published: 1, suppressed: +0, …(3) } to match object { published: +0, suppressed: 1 }
× publishIncompleteNotice > publishes independently for a fresh head even when the reason and anchor repeat
  → expected [ { …(3) } ] to have a length of 2 but got 1
× publishIncompleteNotice > does not suppress once the earlier notice's conversation is resolved
  → expected [ { …(3) } ] to have a length of 2 but got 1
Test Files  1 failed (1) | Tests  3 failed | 21 passed (24)
```

**Defect 2a — missing staleness guard** (`review.ts` reverted to HEAD):
```
× staleness guard on every settleIncomplete path > abandons an unclassified-path settlement once the head has moved on
  → expected 'incomplete' to be 'abandoned'
× staleness guard on every settleIncomplete path > abandons an engine-failure settlement once the head has moved on
  → expected 'incomplete' to be 'abandoned'
Test Files  1 failed (1) | Tests  2 failed | 10 passed (12)
```

**Defect 2b — head-independent notice marker** (`marker.ts` reverted to HEAD):
```
× fingerprint > optional head field > changes the fingerprint when supplied and different
  → expected '4a05f63…' not to be '4a05f63…'
× fingerprint > optional head field > differs from the head-omitted fingerprint of the same otherwise-identical input
  → expected '4a05f63…' not to be '4a05f63…'
× publishIncompleteNotice > publishes independently for a fresh head even when the reason and anchor repeat
  → expected [ { …(3) } ] to have a length of 2 but got 1
```

All three reverts were restored and the full suite (`npx vitest run` → 27 files, 430 tests) is green with every fix in place.

## Verification

```
npm run verify
```
— `typecheck`, `lint` (max-warnings=0), `format:check`, `test` (27 files, 430 tests), `build`, and `check:bundle` all pass. `dist/index.js` is rebuilt and committed.

Not run (calls the paid model per `AGENTS.md`): `npm run corpus`, `npm run corpus:real`.

## Reuse / no-duplication

- Reused the marker stage's own author-identity check rather than inventing a second authorship rule.
- Reused `review-cache.ts`'s documented NUL-separator pattern for `marker.ts`'s own join, instead of leaving the pre-existing raw-byte version in place once it needed touching anyway.
- Extended the existing single `GitHubClient` with one more read (GraphQL resolved-thread lookup) rather than adding a second GitHub client or a parallel dedup subsystem.
- Centralized the staleness guard inside `settleIncomplete` (the one function every incomplete path already funnels through) instead of bolting a fifth ad hoc check onto `performReview`.

## Known limitation (documented in README)

The similarity gate is a bag-of-words measure: it can occasionally score "the same defect, reworded" and "a different defect described in the same sentence template with one identifier swapped" the wrong way around, since the second case can share more words than a genuine paraphrase. Calibrated against the three real production paraphrases above; biased toward publishing over suppressing when uncertain.

Closes #38

author: ubugeeei
body:
Closes nothing on its own; this is the docs-site half of #3391.

`compiler.jsxCompat: "babel"` — the opt-in `@vue/babel-plugin-jsx` compatibility mode from #3391 —
is documented at the crate level (#3733, in flight) but had nothing on the docs site. The agent that
finished #3391 deferred it because `guide/jsx.md` (510 lines) and `guide/configuration.md` (434) are
both over the 350-line budget and may not grow, and a new page needs a navigation entry in a
599-line theme file. So: do the theme surgery first, then add the page.

## Part 1 — splitting `docs/theme/i18n/navigation.js`

The file carried four things at once: the supported-locale list and sidebar structure, five locales'
worth of sidebar labels, five locales' worth of chrome strings, and all the DOM behavior. It split
cleanly along the seam it already had — **structure vs. strings vs. behavior**:

| File | Lines | Holds |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| `docs/theme/i18n/sitemap.js` | 101 | supported locales, blog nav paths, nav groups, hidden-path patterns |
| `docs/theme/i18n/locales/en.js` | 88 | English labels (also the fallback for every locale, so the blog post titles live here) + chrome strings |
| `docs/theme/i18n/locales/{ja,zh-CN,pt-BR,fr}.js` | 69–70 each | one locale's label overrides + chrome strings |
| `docs/theme/i18n/navigation.js` | 220 | behavior only |

**Per locale, not per nav group**, because the per-locale strings were what actually made the file
big and what grows every time a page is added: one new page previously meant five edits inside one
599-line file, and now means one edit per locale file. The nav groups are one shared structure that
every locale keys into, so they stayed together in `sitemap.js`.

**The loading path is unchanged.** The docs site has no module loader — `docs/theme/background.ts`
`readFileSync`s each theme script and concatenates them into one inline `<script>`. The new files
are plain browser scripts that register on globals (`__vizeDocsSitemap`, `__vizeDocsLocales`), the
same trick `navigation.js` already used for `__vizeDocsNavigation`, and `SCRIPT_BASENAMES` lists
them ahead of `i18n/navigation`. No imports, no exports, no bundler, no new build step. Verified by
building the concatenated script and evaluating it as a single classic script in a browser-like
context (see the "commands run" section below).

One dead field went with it: `navGroups[].title` was never read — headings came from
`localizedUi[locale].groups[groupIndex]`, i.e. by array position across five locales. Groups now
carry a stable `key` and each locale's `ui.groups` is keyed by it, so a group cannot silently shift
by one.

### On the 350-line budget

Worth recording, because the deferral note assumed otherwise: `docs/theme/i18n/navigation.js` was
**not** actually gated. `tools/moon/cmd/source_file_lengths` excludes any path containing an `i18n`
segment (intended for generated translation content), so the file could have grown freely. The split
is still the right shape — 599 lines is not a file anyone should have to add a locale to — but it was
not the blocker it was thought to be. The real blockers were real: `guide/jsx.md` and
`guide/configuration.md` are gated and over limit, so **neither is touched by this PR**, and the new
page is discoverable through the sidebar rather than through a cross-link from them.

## Part 2 — the page

`docs/content/guide/jsx-babel-compat.md` (161 lines), covering: what the mode is and how to enable
it; that it is opt-in, off by default and project-level with no per-component directive form, and
**why** (it changes module-level output shape, so half a module in compat mode would emit two
incompatible module shapes from one file); the mapping from each `@vue/babel-plugin-jsx` option to
its Vize entry point, including why `optimize` has no equivalent; the two deferred corpus rows
(`options/resolve_type_on`, waiting on the type resolution in #1497/#1502; `slots/dynamic_slot_name`,
waiting on dynamic-slot lowering); and why the Vapor and SSR lanes deliberately do not get the mode.

**No compatibility counts in the prose.** The page points at the oracle and
`crates/vize_atelier_jsx/tests/BABEL_COMPAT_INVENTORY.md`, whose totals are pinned by
`babel_compat_verdict_totals`, and says explicitly that it quotes none of them so they cannot rot.

**One accuracy note, please sanity-check it.** `jsxCompat` is read by the config loader
(`vize_carton`) and honoured by both the NAPI and WASM `compileJsx` bindings, but the bundler
plugins pass only `jsxMode` and `vapor` through to `compileJsx` (`npm/builder/vite/src/compiler.ts`,
`plugin/load.ts`) — nothing in `npm/` mentions `jsxCompat`. So setting the config key alone does not
yet change what a bundler emits. The page says so, in a status callout and in the "Enabling it"
section, rather than showing a config snippet that silently does nothing. If that wiring exists
somewhere I did not find, say the word and I will drop the caveat.

The page also uses no in-page anchor links, deliberately: translated headings would break
`#enabling-it`-style targets in four locales.

## Locales

All five, so the page is reachable in every locale the site ships.

**Sidebar labels are hand-written**, not machine-translated:

| Locale | Label |
| --- | --- |
| en | Babel JSX Compat |
| ja | Babel JSX 互換 |
| zh-CN | Babel JSX 兼容 |
| pt-BR | Compatibilidade com Babel JSX |
| fr | Compatibilité Babel JSX |

They are short technical noun phrases and I am confident in all five; none needed a machine.

**Page bodies:** `ja` is hand-written. `zh-CN`, `pt-BR` and `fr` are machine-translated through the
repo's own `docs/scripts/i18n/generate.mjs --accept-machine-translation --resume`, which is how every
other localized page on the site was produced, and they carry the standard
`<!-- Generated translation; source: ... -->` marker so they are not passing themselves off as
human-reviewed. I did not machine-translate the Japanese because the generator mangled it badly —
among other things it rendered "Vize" as "Vice" and turned "honoured by the `compileJsx` bindings"
into nonsense — and it is the maintainer's own language, so it is the one worth writing by hand.
I read the other three and they are consistent in quality with their siblings on the site; no product
names are mangled and all tables survived. **If a reviewer wants zh-CN, pt-BR or fr hand-written
too, that is a fair ask — say so and I will do those as well.**

## Tests

`tests/tooling/docs-navigation.test.ts` (new, and CI-gated via `test:scripts`). Every assertion is a
full-equality `deepEqual`; there is no `.includes()` on a structure and no spot check:

- `SCRIPT_BASENAMES` equals the complete expected script list, so a locale file that exists but is
  never concatenated fails rather than silently leaving the sidebar untranslated.
- The `i18n/locales/` directory listing equals the supported locale codes exactly, both directions.
- `supportedLocales` equals the complete list, and each entry is asserted present in
  `docs/vite.config.ts`'s `i18n.locales`.
- The nav group keys equal the complete ordered list, and the Project Setup group equals its complete
  ordered path list including the new page.
- Every sidebar path resolves to a content page **in every locale**.
- Every locale's label keys equal the English label keys (minus the English-only dated blog titles),
  key for key and in order — so a page added in one locale and forgotten in another fails here.
- The new page's label in all five locales, as one `deepEqual` over the whole map.
- It also shells out to `node --test docs/theme/*.test.*`, which nothing in CI ran before:
  `docs` is in neither `testedPackages` nor `checkedPackages`, so `docs/theme/navigation.test.js` and
  `background.test.ts` were dev-only until now.

`docs/theme/navigation.test.js` keeps its five existing full-structure `deepEqual` tests, unchanged
in expectation — they pass against the split files, which is the behavior-preservation evidence. Its
only edit is to

Added a `commentator` field to matches — the club's programmes name one alongside the umpire. It appears in the captain's match editor, on the fixtures tab, and in the PDF officials block directly under `UMPIRES`.

## Handicaps are hidden unless genuinely entered

This was a no-handicap tournament, which exposed a bug: `teamHandicap()` guards the per-player path against `Number(null) === 0`, but the stored-team fallback did not — so every unhandicapped team printed a spurious `0`.

The distinction matters in polo, where `0` is a real handicap and not the same as "unknown". Behaviour now:

| Case | Result |
|---|---|
| No handicaps anywhere | nothing shown |
| Team handicap cleared (`null` or `''`) | nothing shown |
| Field absent entirely | nothing shown |
| Stored team handicap of `4` | shows `4` |
| A genuine `0` entered | shows `0` |
| Player handicaps `2 / 1 / 0` | shows `3` |

Every clear path in the UI — the team handicap select, the per-team `HCP` input, the per-player `HCP` input — already stores `null`, so this single fix covers "entered or deleted" in both the PDF and the app. The live-scoring screen's "Team handicap" line was already conditional on non-null, so it now correctly disappears too.

## Two date bugs

**Fixtures spanning a month boundary.** `buildDateSubtitle()` stamped the fixture's own month onto every date it found, so the Whippet Trophy (`Thu 30 July – Sun 2 August`) came out as *"30th & 2nd July 2026"*, and that fed the PDF filename. Dates are now paired with the month that follows them → **"30th July & 2nd August 2026"**. Verified against every date string in `FIXTURES_2026`; same-month fixtures are unchanged.

**Ordinal day labels.** `\b(\d{1,2})\b` never matches `31` inside `31st` — there's no word boundary before the `st`. So `daySingleDate()` failed silently on every ordinal label and fell through to a branch that appends the year to the end of the whole string. With a plain `Friday 31st July` the result was accidentally correct; with any suffix it was not, and the header read *"31st July — Beach Polo 2026"*. The regex now accepts an ordinal ending.

## Also

- Removed `pdfprobe/`, `pdfprobe-dist/` and `pdfcheck.mjs`, committed by accident in the logo change — throwaway harnesses for driving the PDF generator headlessly. Added `.gitignore` rules so they can't come back.

## Demo data (live in Firestore, not in this diff)

**18 players across 6 teams** and **6 matches**, attached to the **Whippet Trophy** fixture as a single **Friday 31st July** day — the only day of that fixture it applies to. Ground is **Arena**: the evening was branded Beach Polo but played in the arena, so no fictional ground was added. The day is labelled "Friday 31st July — Beach Polo" so the theme shows in the app while the programme header stays a clean date.

Also populated the player database, the teams directory and the sign-up autocomplete cache.

One value I had to choose, since the card doesn't state it: **2 chukkas** per match, inferred from the 30-minute slots. Editable in captain mode. Handicaps are left unset throughout, as printed.

## Verification

Generated the programme from the live Firestore data and checked the rendered pages: 3 pages, opens on the matches, all six teams and eighteen players present, umpires and commentators on every match that has them, no phantom `0` handicaps, header "31st July 2026 / ARENA", filename `The_Whippet_Trophy_30th_July_&_2nd_August.pdf`. App builds and renders with no console errors.

author: cicalese
body:
Fixes #1426.

The MYSQL_PASSWORD heal added in #1423 never ran on the default `canasta start` path. Found while e2e-testing the 4.15.0 release candidate.

## What was wrong

`cmd_start` checked `_missing_db_password` only when `compose up` returned non-zero:

```python
rc = _helpers._run_compose(inst_id, inst, ["up", "-d"])
if rc != 0:
    if _helpers._missing_db_password(inst):
        return _helpers.FALLBACK
```

The comment justified this with "db exits immediately without it". It does not. MariaDB applies `MARIADB_ROOT_PASSWORD` only when it initialises an **empty** data directory; on a volume that already holds a database the stored password wins and the empty variable is ignored. So `db` comes up healthy, `up` returns 0, and the branch is never entered.

The condition the heal exists to catch is precisely the condition under which `up` succeeds — the check could only ever fire when `up` failed for some *other* reason and the password happened to also be missing.

Observed end to end, with `MYSQL_PASSWORD` deleted from `.env`:

```
Starting containers...
pod1_db_1
pod1_web_1
pod1_caddy_1
pod1_varnish_1
Waiting for web to become ready...
=== EXIT 0 ===
```

and the wiki serving:

```
HTTP 500
<title>MediaWiki</title>
Cannot access the database
```

Forcing the Ansible path showed the guard itself was correct and merely unreachable.

## The fix

Move the check ahead of `up`. The cost the old comment cited — an SSH round trip to read `.env` on a remote instance — does not apply: `cmd_start` already calls `_sync_compose_profiles`, which reads and parses `.env` one line earlier, on every start, remote included. It now returns that mapping, and `_missing_db_password` takes an optional pre-read env, so the check adds no I/O.

An empty mapping still means "no `.env`, or unreadable" rather than "missing password", so that separate fault keeps reporting itself instead of being routed to the heal.

## Verification

On the host that produced the 500 above, with the password still missing:

```
$ canasta start -i pod1
Starting containers...
Error: MYSQL_PASSWORD is missing from .../pod1/.env, and this instance already
has a database volume (pod1_mysql-data-volume). Generating a new password would
not reach that database — MariaDB only applies the root password when it first
initialises — so the wiki would be handed credentials the database does not
accept. Restore the value instead: 'canasta backup restore' brings back .env
from a snapshot, or copy MYSQL_PASSWORD from another copy of the file. ...
=== EXIT 2 ===
```

Restoring `.env` and starting again returned the wiki to HTTP 200.

## Coverage

The tests that came with #1423 asserted the Ansible task's structure — the refusal, its ordering, its message — but nothing asserted the fast path could reach it, which is why a dead check looked covered. The new tests drive `cmd_start` directly and assert compose is never invoked when the key is missing, that a healthy instance is unaffected, that an unreadable `.env` is not misread as this fault, and that the env is read only once.

`make test-unit` (2442 passed), `make validate`, `make lint` all green.

author: o-marsters-1997
body:
Closes #6.

`--addr` default `:8420` → `127.0.0.1:8420`, so the review server is not on the network by default.

## Why this is more than a default change

The old log line was `"http://localhost" + addr`, so changing the default alone would have printed `http://localhost127.0.0.1:8420`. Hence `browsableURL` plus listen-before-log: `serve` now `net.Listen`s first and logs the address the listener actually took. Side benefits — `--addr 127.0.0.1:0` prints the real assigned port, a taken port fails before anything is printed, and a malformed `--addr 8420` errors cleanly instead of printing a bogus URL.

## Verified against the built binary

Default binds `127.0.0.1:8420` only; `--addr :8420` still binds `*:8420` for the deliberate case. `just check` passes; new `TestBrowsableURL` table covers loopback, host-less, IPv4/IPv6 wildcard, IPv6 loopback, hostname and malformed input.

Docs, README and the `justfile` example updated — `just --list` was still advertising the wildcard form.

실기기(아이폰) 확인 결과를 반영합니다. 게임 로직 변경은 없고, 계측 패널의 색상 기준 한 줄과 문서입니다.

## 1. `OBJ` 경고 기준 150/400 → 600/1200

경고 기준 150은 **칸마다 Mesh를 만들던 시절**(1,000개 이상)에 잡은 값입니다. 청크 병합 이후 41×41에서 200~400이 정상 범위라, 정상값에 계속 노란 경고가 떴습니다.

## 2. 병합 판단을 실기기 수치로 확정

병합 직후 헤드리스(SwiftShader) 환경에서 FPS가 59 → 12로 떨어져 개악처럼 보였고, 그래서 "이론적 근거이며 실기기로는 검증되지 않았다"고 남겨 뒀었습니다.

**실기기 확인 결과 HIGH 프리셋에서 41×41이 59~60fps로 상한을 유지합니다.** GPU가 없는 환경은 삼각형 증가를 실제보다 훨씬 크게 손해로 잡는다는 것이 확인됐으므로, 그 편향을 경고와 함께 기록합니다.

## 3. "프리셋을 올린다고 항상 좋아지지 않는다" 기록

적응형은 **FPS만 보고 `renderScale`을 내립니다.** 더 무거운 프리셋을 고르면 그 대가로 해상도가 깎여, 실효 픽셀 밀도가 오히려 낮아질 수 있습니다.

아이폰 실측:

| | prCap | × renderScale | 실효 배율 | FPS |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| HIGH | 2.0 | ×1.00 | **2.0** | 59~60 |
| ULTRA | 3.0 | **×0.50** (하한) | **1.5** | 53~60 |

ULTRA는 광원이 11개라 절반 해상도로도 60을 못 지키고, 결과적으로 HIGH보다 흐리고 불안정합니다. `품질` 행의 배율이 하한(0.5)에 붙어 있으면 그 프리셋이 그 기기에 과하다는 신호입니다.

## 검증

4개 프리셋 콘솔 에러 없이 부팅, LIGHT 5/6/9/11 유지.

author: mfbernardes
body:
Works through the items deliberately left open during #140's review rounds. One commit per item, each with its own test.

Every fix was mutation-tested the way that branch established: reintroduce the bug, watch the new test go red, restore. Two of them needed that to find out the first attempt did nothing.

## What's here

**`pwa.screenshots[].src` could overwrite a tracked file.** `copy()` resolved its destination from the source's bare basename and only guarded against gen-schema's own writes, so a screenshot named `shots/sw.js` overwrote the tracked `public/sw.js` — and put that path in `.gen-manifest.json`, so the next build reconciled, i.e. deleted, tracked repo content. `copy()` now takes the same `isTracked` predicate `bundleFonts` already used, passed in rather than imported so the leaf module stays acyclic.

**The SVG sanitizer and `svgPrep` re-implemented each other.** `isSameDocumentRef`, `CSS_IMPORT_RE` and `CSS_URL_RE` existed twice and disagreed: the app-side `url()` pattern stopped at the first paren, so `url("a)b.png")` was not seen as a reference at all and the import wizard missed it. Both sides now read one copy from `src/lib/cssRefs.mjs`, in the `showIfSyntax.mjs` shape. Each module's element list is untouched — the sanitizer's allowlist and `ACTIVE_TAGS` answer different questions and differ by design; `dom.ts`'s stale "meant to agree" comment now says so.

**CI serialized the whole browser suite into one job.** `dist/` is uploaded once and the checks fan out into sibling jobs. `deploy` still gates on all of them.

**`defaultDesign` skipped the descriptor-driven type check.** `{"defaultDesign": 42}` reported "not one of the configured design ids" — a membership complaint about a value whose type was the actual problem. Routed through `applyTopLevelScalars` like the other top-level scalars.

**A dismissed dialog's overlay ate clicks.** Radix keeps a closing overlay mounted until `animationend` reaches the main thread, which first-render work delays well past the ~150ms animation; it sits at z-50 with `pointer-events: auto` over the parameter panel's resize handle. Dropping pointer-events once `data-state` is closed fixes it — but it has to be `!important`, because `DismissableLayer` sets the property inline. The version without the `!` type-checked, linted and built while having no effect at all.

**A doc block leaked onto the next parameter.** The scanner's `statementLines` branch never called `reset()`, so a comment above a non-parameter statement became the next parameter's label and help. The reset belongs per statement entry, not after the loop: `byEndLine` carries entries only on a statement's end line, so an unconditional reset wipes a multi-line statement's pending block before `pushParam` sees it.

**`sw.js` tested a suffix before the scope guard.** An out-of-scope path ending in `precache-manifest.json` was classified volatile — the same bug class the rule below it was already fixed for.

**No generated matrix for the parser scanner.** It was rewritten twice on #140 and both times the wrong shape was one nobody had thought to hand-write. `scad-shape-matrix.mjs` cross-products the constructs `scanTopLevelStatements` distinguishes over the separators between them: 3958 shapes, each validated against the pinned engine before assertion, each compared for equality against a list the generator derives on its own terms. Nothing asks `params.mjs` what the answer should be, so a leaked module local fails as loudly as a dropped parameter.

## Not here

Coverage collection (#140's item 8) was skipped by decision — the two defects that survived longest on that branch lived in files at 96% and 98% line coverage, so a percentage gate was not the useful version of it.

The `wrangler-dry-run` job was removed rather than repaired. Splitting the gates broke it: the redirected config wrangler reads is written to `.wrangler/deploy/config.json` in the repo root, outside `dist/` and gitignored, so a job that downloads only the dist artifact falls back to the root `wrangler.jsonc` — which deliberately carries no `assets.directory`. Repairing it meant shipping build state through a second artifact to re-derive what Cloudflare's own Workers Builds check proves on every push with a real build. `deploy` here publishes to GitHub Pages, so gating it on a Cloudflare config check was protecting nothing.

## Verification

`npm test` (1164), `tsc -b`, `lint`, `build`, `check:dist`, `check:svg`, `check:scad`, `check:studio`, `smoke`, `e2e:svg`, `vis` all green locally; rebased onto `main` at `752d1e3` and re-run after, since #142 touched four of the same files.

`renderHash`'s closure is unchanged — `src/lib/cssRefs.mjs` is not reachable from `worker.ts`, so no deployment's persisted geometry is evicted.

author: highbyte
body:
Fixes #87 (the contract itself; the issue's opt-in git-policy proposal remains recorded there as a possible follow-up).

Worker-spawned agents were never told what kind of session they are in. Left to defaults and user-level conventions written for interactive use, their behavior was nondeterministic — one live run ended blocked forever, asking for a branch-name approval no one could give; another under identical configuration silently skipped workspace isolation instead. A non-worktree run also received no commit instruction at all, leaving that outcome to the agent's habits.

## Changes

- **`WorkerPrompt.UnattendedContract`** — new preamble stating: unattended session, never pause for approval or confirmation, these instructions supersede interactive-session conventions, report blockers and end; workspace provenance (dedicated worktree with its branch name, or the prepared checkout); and git limits (no branches/worktrees/fetch/config/remotes, never push).
- **`WorkerPrompt.CommitInstruction`** — now explicit for non-worktree runs too: always "do not commit" there (the workspace is the shared checkout); worktree + `completion.commit: "agent"` keeps the explicit commit direction, and the contract's git limits are worded not to contradict it.
- **`WorkerPrompt.RunAddendum`** — single composition point (contract + commit expectation) used by all seven launch/resume/queued/preview paths, so they cannot drift. The execution-prompt renderer's parameter is renamed to match its payload.

## Validation

- 3 new/strengthened text-level tests; full suite 1568/1568.
- Live, on the private test repository:
  - The originally-blocked scenario re-run under identical interactive conventions: completed in one hands-off run — no approval wait, zero git mutations, straight to work and finish.
  - Failure path: a blocked run reported its blocker and ended cleanly instead of hunting or waiting.
  - `workspaceMode: worktree` + `completion.commit: "agent"` (with a codex execpolicy allowlist in place): the contract's commit variant composed correctly — the agent committed in the Wrighty-created worktree, finished, and the worker removed the clean worktree leaving the branch for integration.

author: copilot
body:
Adds a persistent `CodeStore` backed by Firestore so gift code state survives restarts. Previously the service used an in-memory store seeded from config; codes discovered at runtime were lost on redeploy.

## Changes

### `firestore/code_store.go` — new `CodeStore` implementation
- Stores codes in a `codes` collection, document ID = code value
- `Find`: fetch by doc ID; returns expired codes too so `AlreadyExpired` guard works
- `Add`: upserts with `is_active=!code.IsExpired()`
- `ActiveCodes`: queries `where is_active == true`
- `RemoveActive`: soft-deletes — sets `is_active=false` + `expired_at=now()` rather than hard-deleting, so re-submissions of the same code correctly return `AlreadyExpired` instead of re-hitting the API

### `service.go` — `NewWithCodeStore` constructor
Adds a constructor for injecting a custom `CodeStore`, leaving the existing `New` (in-memory) signature untouched.

### `cmd/discord/main.go`
Wires `firestore.NewCodeStore(store.Client)` into the service. The Firestore client is shared with `PlayerStore` — no second connection.

body:
### Motivation
- Ensure notification action URLs route to the correct book type path (format `/{type}/{id}`) by surfacing `bookType` in publication events or resolving it in the worker.
- Guarantee transactional atomicity for domain state changes and their matching outbox events so publishes cannot be lost or emitted incorrectly.
- Increase outbox worker throughput and multi-instance safety by using bounded batch claims, configurable concurrency, and a lease heartbeat.
- Make processing robust and idempotent via typed event contracts, validation, a handler registry, and correct broadcast accounting/statuses.

### Description
- Add `bookType` to the strongly-typed domain event payloads and include the slug when producing `BOOK_PUBLISHED` and `CHAPTER_PUBLISHED` events from book/chapter/scheduler services so `actionUrl` can be generated as `/{bookType}/{id}`. (see `outbox/domain-events.ts`, `books.service.ts`, `chapters.service.ts`, `scheduled-publishing.service.ts`).
- Make chapter updates and any related book counter/content updates and the `CHAPTER_PUBLISHED` outbox write execute inside the same Prisma transaction to enforce atomicity (see `chapters.service.ts`).
- Replace single-item polling with bounded batch claiming using `FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED`, add worker configuration (`workerBatchSize`, `workerConcurrency`, `leaseHeartbeatMs`), process claimed events with safe concurrency, and add a lease heartbeat/renewal while event batches are processed (see `notification.config.ts` and `notification-outbox.processor.ts`).
- Introduce a typed handler registry and payload validation per `eventType` + `eventVersion`, return invalid/unsupported events to a safe dead-letter path, and remove untyped `any` dispatch logic (see `notification-outbox.processor.ts` and `outbox/domain-events.ts`).
- Make broadcast processing idempotent and correctly accounted: compute `totalRecipients` separately, derive `processedRecipients` from persisted notifications, advance cursor only after successful batches, preserve `skipDuplicates`, and set broadcast `status` to `COMPLETED`, `PARTIALLY_FAILED`, or `FAILED` as appropriate (see `notification-outbox.processor.ts` and `notifications.service.ts`).
- Tighten types across notification APIs and utilities, remove `any` casts for payloads/metadata, and ensure persisted JSON uses Prisma JSON types (see `notifications.service.ts`, `notification.utils.ts`, `outbox/outbox.service.ts`, and `notifications.controller.ts`).

author: tcballard
body:
## Summary

Adds the bounded authenticated Responses API compatibility surface for #153.

## Scope

### Included

- `/v1/responses` and `/responses` on local and authenticated managed data-plane routers
- strict text and bounded multi-turn input normalization over the existing Chat Completions path
- explicit support for `model`, `input`, `instructions`, `stream`, `max_output_tokens`, and `temperature`
- normalized buffered response shape and input/output/total usage fields
- bounded Responses SSE events with one terminal `response.completed` or `response.failed` event
- explicit unsupported-field and unsupported-content errors rather than silent field loss
- input history, output, response-body, and upstream event bounds
- decision-only/dry-run preservation, route/auth/privacy/budget/accounting reuse, tests, ADR, and docs

### Excluded

- changes to the deterministic scorer or provider credentials
- tools, background jobs, stored conversations, previous-response references, or multimodal parts
- a second provider execution path or a Chat Completions contract change
- ChatGPT consumer-account access through OpenAI Platform credentials

## Product / Architecture Decisions

- Responses is an adapter boundary over the authoritative authenticated Chat Completions execution path, so routing, eligibility, privacy, budgets, failover, and accounting remain one implementation.
- The accepted field set is intentionally narrow and deny-unknown; unsupported features fail closed with `wayfinder_router_unsupported_request`.
- Text and message history are bounded before delivery; provider response bytes and streaming event/output growth are bounded during relay.
- Streaming emits `response.created`, ordered text deltas, and exactly one terminal event. Duplicate `[DONE]` markers and late upstream events cannot create a second terminal or second accounting operation.
- Provider usage is normalized only when present; missing usage is omitted rather than fabricated. Existing Chat Completions behavior remains unchanged.

## User-Facing Contract

### CLI / Human Output

No CLI command changes. OpenAI-shaped clients may POST to `/v1/responses` (or `/responses`) using the documented bounded text/multi-turn contract.

### JSON Output

Buffered success returns `object: response`, `status: completed`, a message output item, and normalized `usage` when the provider supplies it. Unsupported fields return `wayfinder_router_unsupported_request`; existing route headers and decision-only responses remain available.

### Exit Codes

No CLI exit-code changes.

## Verification

### Ran

- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings`
- `cargo test --workspace --all-targets --locked` (242 gateway tests plus all workspace crates and live Redis tests)
- `cargo +1.85.0 check --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --locked -p wayfinder-gateway`
- `cargo +1.85.0 test --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --locked -p wayfinder-gateway responses_ -- --nocapture`

### Covered

- buffered aliases and normalized provider usage
- fragmented SSE, ordered text deltas, duplicate terminal markers, and one terminal event
- bounded multi-turn translation and oversized history rejection
- strict unknown/unsupported field behavior
- dry-run/decision-only preservation for buffered and streaming requests
- existing Chat Completions, Redis, parity, concurrency, and provider behavior through the full suite

## Review Path

Stacked on #166 (bounded canary tripwires), targeting `codex/enterprise-canary-tripwires`. Review after #166.

## Notes For Reviewer

This is compatibility, not a claim of full OpenAI Responses feature parity. Tools, background execution, stored conversations, previous-response references, and multimodal content are intentionally rejected until each has an explicit bounded contract. The existing Chat Completions route remains the sole execution and accounting path.

author: ramoncoroso
body:
Node 18+ va contra OpenSSL 3, cuyo proveedor por defecto **no** incluye RC2 ni RC4. Las exportaciones antiguas de la FNMT usan `pbeWithSHA1And40BitRC2-CBC`, de modo que un `.p12` perfectamente válido —y con la contraseña correcta— falla al cargarse.

Lo que hacía la librería era envolver el mensaje de OpenSSL en un `CertificateError: Invalid certificate: Unsupported PKCS12 PFX data`, con el mismo código para los cuatro casos posibles. A quien solo tiene un certificado que «no funciona», eso no le dice qué hacer.

## Los casos son distinguibles

Medido en Node 22.22.1 / OpenSSL 3.5.5, con dos `.p12` generados sobre la misma clave y certificado:

| Caso | `err.code` | mensaje |
|---|---|---|
| heredado RC2-40 + contraseña **correcta** | `ERR_CRYPTO_UNSUPPORTED_OPERATION` | `Unsupported PKCS12 PFX data` |
| heredado + contraseña incorrecta | — | `mac verify failure` |
| moderno + contraseña incorrecta | — | `mac verify failure` |
| bytes que no son PKCS#12 | — | `not enough data` |

`mac verify failure` es **exclusivamente** contraseña incorrecta: el MAC se comprueba antes que el cifrado, y por eso hasta el heredado con la clave mala da ese error y no el otro. Tratarlos igual mandaría a reexportar el certificado a alguien que simplemente se equivocó de contraseña — y hay un test que lo impide.

## El mensaje

```
El certificado usa cifrado heredado (RC2/RC4), que OpenSSL 3 —el que lleva Node 18+—
no incluye en su proveedor por defecto. Es típico de exportaciones antiguas de la FNMT.
La contraseña es correcta: el problema es el algoritmo.

Opción A (recomendada) · reexportar con cifrado moderno:
  openssl pkcs12 -legacy -in certificado-antiguo.p12 -nodes -out temporal.pem
  openssl pkcs12 -export -in temporal.pem -out certificado-nuevo.p12
  shred -u temporal.pem     # rm -P en macOS. El PEM lleva la clave SIN cifrar.

Opción B (paliativa) · habilitar el proveedor legacy en TODO el proceso:
  node --openssl-legacy-provider app.js
```

Son tres pasos y no uno con tubería a propósito: el PEM intermedio contiene la clave privada **sin cifrar**, así que borrarlo es parte de la receta.

## El segundo hallazgo, que hacía inútil todo lo anterior

`validateCertificate` **no se invoca desde ningún punto del camino real**. El cliente llama a `getTlsOptions()`, y el PKCS#12 no se parsea hasta que `https.request` construye el contexto TLS — de forma **síncrona**, comprobado. El usuario recibía:

```
NetworkError: Request error: Unsupported PKCS12 PFX data
```

Un error de red por un problema de certificado, y todo el diagnóstico anterior inalcanzable. Ahora `sendSoapRequest` traduce también ese fallo síncrono, y hay un test que ejerce el camino completo con `submitInvoice`.

## Verificación

**971 tests** (+9). `tests/conformance/pkcs12.test.ts` **no mockea `node:tls`**: carga `.p12` reales.

Las fixtures van versionadas —con la excepción que ya existía en `.gitignore`— porque generar el heredado exige que el `openssl` de cada máquina tenga disponible el proveedor legacy, y un test de conformidad no puede depender de eso. Son autofirmados, la AEAT los rechazaría, y su `README.md` documenta el cifrado de cada uno y cómo regenerarlos. `scripts/generate-test-cert.sh` gana el flag `--legacy`.

**Reserva declarada:** probado en Node 22.22.1 / OpenSSL 3.5.5. CI lo ejecuta además en Node 18, 20 y 22.

Closes #29

body:
Ein Anbieter statt drei. Teil des Rückbaus aus [platform#1680](https://github.com/achimdehnert/platform/issues/1680).

## Was sich ändert

Die CI-Workflows kommen jetzt aus [`iilgmbh/shared-ci@v1.1.0`](https://github.com/iilgmbh/shared-ci) — statt aus `achimdehnert/platform` (oft ungepinnt auf `@main`), aus `achimdehnert/shared-ci` (heute versehentlich entstanden) oder aus einem alten `shared-ci`-Tag.

## Warum

**Es gab nie zwei Anforderungen, nur zwei Pflegestände.** Ein Vollzensus über alle 72 Repos der vier Owner-Namensräume zeigte: dieselben Jobs, dieselben Schritte, unterschiedliche Action-Versionen. `v1.1.0` vereinigt beide Linien auf dem neueren Stand.

| Action | vorher | jetzt |
|---|---|---|
| `actions/checkout` | v6 | **v7** |
| `actions/setup-python` | v6 | **v7** |
| `docker/metadata-action` | v5 | **v6** |
| `aquasecurity/trivy-action` | **`@master`** | **v0.36.0** |

Der letzte war ein ungepinnter Verweis auf einen beweglichen Branch — in jedem Docker-Build, seit zwei Monaten.

Entfernt wurden zwei Sonderwege ohne fachlichen Grund: `skip_external_verify` (gebaut für ein Repo, das gar keinen Deploy hat) und `ghcr_push_token` (das Package war längst mit dem Repo verknüpft; der Standard-`GITHUB_TOKEN` reicht — am 2026-08-02 mit einem echten Build belegt).

## Wenn hier etwas rot wird

Der Rückweg ist ein Revert dieses PRs. Bitte **nicht** mergen, solange die CI rot ist — der Sinn der Welle ist, dass jedes Repo einzeln beweist, dass der Wechsel trägt.

author: psychollama
body:
## TL;DR

An endpoint id is a 32-byte public key. Nobody guesses one, so holding it is already the grant — which made the accept/decline handshake built on top of it a second lock on the same door, and one that could only ever be less strict than the first. It was built ahead of the thing that would have justified it and nothing was leaning on it, so this takes it out: −1,127 net lines, no feature left behind it.

## What went

- **`ContactTrust`** (`invited` | `trusted`) and every guard reading it. Shares now send and land on the strength of the link alone.
- **The `accept` wire message**, the sagas that sent one and believed one, and the direction check that decided whether to believe it.
- **`network/requests.ts` whole** — the session dismissal set and the request queue — along with `PairingRequest` and the banner that stacked outstanding requests over every `/beam/*` route.
- **`ContactDirection`.** Once the above went, its only surviving reader was one row on the contact page, and "who dialled whom" isn't worth a persisted field on its own.
- **`PeerState.awaiting`**, which meant "linked but not yet accepted" and now describes nothing.

## What stayed

The beam link and its QR code. Under this model, handing out the endpoint id *is* the pairing step, so it's the one part that matters more than it did before rather than less. Setup's second step keeps its `pairing` name too — it asks the device to go meet somebody, which is still exactly what it does.

## Renames

`sagas/pairing.ts` is `sagas/messages.ts`, and `pairing-log.ts` is `peer-log.ts`. With trust gone, what makes a peer legible in a log line is whether we'd met it before, so `pairingContext(id, contact)` became `peerContext(id, known)`.

## Pros

- The security story is one sentence instead of two mechanisms that had to agree. There is no longer a state where a device is reachable but not allowed to speak, so there's no longer a way for those two answers to disagree.
- Connecting is one step. Open a link, share — nothing to accept in between, and no way to end up waiting on a device whose owner never saw the prompt.
- `flushSharesSaga` had a trust guard that was load-bearing precisely because the queue filled before the peer answered. Both halves of that are gone.
- The address book means one thing now: a record of who you've met, not a permission table.

## Cons

- **`receiveShareSaga` no longer refuses anything.** Text from an endpoint that isn't in the address book lands in the log instead of being dropped with a warning. That follows directly from the premise, but it's the one behavior a user could notice, and the place to look first if the premise turns out to be too strong.
- **No revocation story.** Forgetting a contact drops the record; it doesn't stop them reaching the device, because nothing ever did. That was true before — an `invited` peer could still connect — but the trust ladder made it *look* otherwise.
- **One commit.** The split that would compile either way is trust-then-direction, but they're one decision and the second half is a handful of lines living inside the first half's hunks.
- Schema v4 lands on a store that only just reached v3, so anyone with local beam data migrates twice in short order.

## Recommended followups

- **If unsolicited shares turn out to be a problem**, the answer is rotating this device's endpoint id rather than reinstating the ladder — that's the revocation primitive the key already implies, and it's one mechanism rather than two.
- **`InviteDialog` is now misnamed.** With no invite lifecycle it's a link/QR handoff. Cheap rename once this settles.
- **`platform/iroh.ts`** is still 455 lines over two subjects (the vault-backed key and the endpoint plumbing) — carried over from the last PR's followups, untouched here.
- **The contact page is thin now**: a name, a key, and a date. Worth a look at whether `lastSeenAt` should surface there, since it's recorded and nothing renders it.

body:
## Summary

- keep required CI deterministic by moving live LLM agent regressions to the nightly workflow
- retain live RDS tool coverage and add the missing offline fuzzy-location grader check

PR #39's code graders were deterministic, but required CI invoked the stochastic agent again on the merge commit. One otherwise-correct I-95 response failed a raw trace assertion after the PR run had passed, making main CI probabilistic.

This also addresses the three late review threads on PR #39: the over-broad pricing-tool prohibition, stale nightly artifacts, and the failed report in curated evidence.

Required PR CI now gates deterministic checks and live RDS tools. Stochastic agent quality checks still run nightly without blocking merges.

body:
### Motivation

- Replace scattered static content imports with Sanity as the single source of truth so Studio-managed edits (publish/unpublish, ordering, activation) immediately update the public site. 
- Provide typed GROQ projections and a server-side CMS gateway to normalize fields (slugs, images, alt text, ordering, references) and avoid leaking Sanity internals into components. 
- Preserve the existing public content and media by seeding the CMS with deterministic IDs and verified asset uploads, and provide a safe migration/fallback policy while migration is in progress. 
- Enable live published-content refresh on the public site while keeping the embedded `/studio` layout free of `SanityLive`/visual editing wrappers.

### Description

- Added a complete typed query layer in `sanity/lib/queries.ts` (homepage, clients, solutions, products, service categories, services, industries, stories, case studies, testimonials, events, FAQs, CTAs, video embeds, navigation, footer, site/contact settings, general pages, sitemap inputs) and a small `sanity/lib/typegen-queries.ts` helper for TypeGen. 
- Introduced a server-only CMS gateway `lib/cms.ts` that uses `sanityFetch` (from `sanity/lib/live.ts`) to fetch published content, normalize images/alt/metadata, merge deterministic legacy fallbacks while migration runs, and expose typed getters such as `getHomepage`, `getSolutions`, `getClients`, `getGlobalContent`, `getDocument`, and `getSitemapDocuments`.
- Implemented live updates using `defineLive` in `sanity/lib/live.ts`, and rendered `SanityLive` inside a new public route-group layout `app/(site)/layout.tsx` so the public site refreshes on publish while `/studio` does not include live wrappers. 
- Refactored public pages and components to consume CMS data: replaced `lib/content.ts`/`lib/catalog.ts` runtime imports with `lib/cms` calls (homepage, solutions/products/industries/success-stories/case-studies/services listing & detail, client marquee, header/mega-menu, footer, contact, general pages, sitemap). Client marquee now accepts a typed `clients` prop (`components/client-marquee.tsx`). Key files: `lib/cms.ts`, `sanity/lib/queries.ts`, `sanity/lib/client.ts`, `sanity/lib/live.ts`, `sanity/schemaTypes/index.ts`, `app/(site)/*`, `components/site-header.tsx`, `components/site-footer.tsx`, `components/internal-page.tsx`, `components/client-marquee.tsx`, `app/sitemap.ts`.
- Strengthened Studio schemas and type surface: added `serviceCategory`, required image `alt` validations, `order` defaults/ordering, specialized fields for `faq`, `testimonial`, `event`, `videoEmbed`, `cta`, `contactSettings`, `footer` columns/legal links, `homepage.sectionContent`, previews and Studio structure/singletons in `sanity.config.ts` and the schema files.

- Added a small test suite `tests/cms-pipeline.test.mjs` that asserts query coverage, marquee prop-driven usage and ARIA handling, that public routes use the CMS gateway and that `SanityLive` is isolated to the public `(site)` layout.

## Summary

- `tests/hermes_cli/test_models.py`: new `TestFormatPricePerMtok` covering standard prices, zero→free, invalid→`?`, the promo price, and the one-cent boundary.

author: goedelsoup
body:
Closes #1458.

The Findlay WPCC screened at **0.37:1** against a *derived* Blanchard 7Q10 of 8.67 cfs (LP3 at USGS 04189000). Two facts in the published record disqualify that gage as this plant's denominator — either sufficient alone, and **neither is in the issue body**:

1. **It sits below the outfall it was screening.** Gage `41.05589 / −83.68799` vs outfall 2PD00008001 at `41.049722 / −83.667778` on a westward reach; Straub 2001 places it *"2.0 mi west of Findlay, 3.0 mi downstream from Eagle Creek."* The plant's own effluent was in its own denominator.
2. **It is regulated.** Straub's REMARKS for the station, verbatim: water is diverted upstream into Findlay Reservoir and *"is available for low-flow augmentation."*

Where the Blanchard is **unregulated** it publishes ~nothing — 0.03 cfs at USGS 04188337 (SIR-classified Unregulated, WY2008–2020), 0 at Eagle Creek 04188496, and 0 at 04188300, which is *one of the two gages the fact sheet itself names as its basis*. Ohio EPA's 0.21 cfs at RM 56.42 is consistent with that; 8.67 was never the river's own low flow.

**The screen now reads 0.009:1** — same violation band, four orders of magnitude apart.

## Two corrections to the issue's premises

- **"SIR 2024-5075 drops 04189000 because it is regulated" is refuted.** That report *lists* regulated gages with full statistics (Gilboa 04189131 and Ottawa 04189260 are both `Regulated` **and** published). 04189000 is absent from table 1, 1.1 and 2.1 despite a continuous NWIS daily record since 1923, with no stated reason → `[open]`. The regulation finding survives on Straub's REMARKS instead, which state it outright.
- **The SIR PDF's own cover and both appendix CSV headnotes print report number "2024-5057"** while the publication, DOI (`10.3133/sir20245075`) and suggested citation are 2024-5075. Recorded as a publisher discrepancy, not normalized.

## Mechanisms added (both general, not Findlay-shaped)

**A fact-sheet low flow is permit-scoped, not river-scoped.** `lowflow._normalize` strips `at …` by design, so every reach of one river collapses to one key — name-keying can never hold Findlay's 0.21 cfs (RM 56.42) beside Ottawa's 7.78 cfs (RM 22.1). A `low-flow-7q10.yaml` entry may now declare `permits:` (suffix-stripped, so `2PD00008*VD` → `2pd00008` and the value stays bound across renewals), and `build_screen_lookup()` returns one `ScreenLowFlows(by_name, by_permit)` object so a new call site can't silently get the weaker index. `build_low_flow_lookup` (name-only) survives for the routed-network solver: a **reach** is not a permit.

**A gage a cited third party calls regulated demotes its own derived entry.** `mainstem-gages.yaml` gages gained optional cited `published` / `regulation` / `cross_check_gages` blocks; `_cited_annotations()` copies them into the emitted derived entry and sets `confidence: low` with a reason. The committed derived file was re-emitted **through its own writer with no NWIS call** (existing streams merged with the annotations), so the LP3 numbers are untouched — and a test pins the committed blocks to the curated source, which is what makes a touched regenerated file safe.

## Also

- **Sources now in-corpus**: `data/reference/usgs/low-flow/` — Straub 2001 (WRI 01-4140) and SIR 2024-5075 on LFS, both appendix CSVs byte-preserved (`.gitattributes` `-text`, so the publisher's CRLF survives), README with sha256s and the traps. New catalog entry `usgs-published-low-flow`.
- **`findlay-ottawa-comparison.yaml` rewritten.** The shared-denominator finding — *"downstream position confers essentially no assimilative advantage"* — was two **regulated** gages agreeing with each other, and is removed rather than softened. The 37× between the two fact-sheet values is stated as **not** decomposable into position vs method: different gages, non-overlapping records (1970–77/1923–97 vs 1921–51).
- `basin-network.yaml` + the Findlay bundle regenerated; prose, profile comments, `docs/NETWORK.md` and catalog notes updated. No contract-version bump (no feed or schema change).

## Left out deliberately, flagged in-file

- **Ottawa (OH0026921) still reads `no_receiving_water`** in the computed screen — ECHO carries no receiver and there's no curation-overlay entry (Findlay got one under #1460/#352). Its cited 7.78 cfs is committed regardless; wiring it needs a live ECHO re-pull, so it belongs to the Ottawa thread (#1420/#1422).
- **Only the Blanchard gage is annotated.** SIR publishes a Regulated/Unregulated classification for most of the other derived gages (Mad River near Urbana, Greenville Creek, Stillwater, Maumee near Defiance, Ottawa River at Lima are all `Regulated`) — a mechanical read of one committed CSV, but demoting those denominators' confidence moves other sites' committed artifacts and belongs in its own reviewed change. An un-annotated gage means "not yet read against the published record", never "unregulated".

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] `low-flow-7q10.derived.yaml` carries the published/cited values with provenance; the derived 8.67 is demoted (`confidence: low` + `confidence_reason` + `regulation` + `cross_check_gages`), never a silent default
- [x] `_FINDLAY.plant_receiving` populated from the fact sheet (landed in #1460; comment re-based here)
- [x] `findlay-ottawa-comparison.yaml` re-run on instrument-grounded denominators, with the at-gage/at-outfall mixing caveat stated explicitly — plus the weaker trap it still contains
- [x] `basin-network.yaml` / basin-screen hold-out for OH0025135 reconciled
- [x] `mise run check` green (3109 passed / 4 skipped) · `mise run //web:check` green · catalog reconcile + `audit --apply` run

Local-only failures, both environmental and both passing once scrubbed: the object-store settings test (ambient `WATERMARK_DOCUMENTS_OBJECT_STORE_*`) and `askEval.live.test.ts` (gated on `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, skipped in CI).

author: alexkroman
body:
## What broke

A tau2-bench run against a deployed agent died mid-word:

```
10:24:46.093  Tick 1006 completed          ← healthy
10:24:47.306  ERROR run_tick (tick=1009): Not connected to AAI host
10:24:47.307  WARNING Simulation loop exited with an exception
```

Across all 12 sessions in that run, **nothing lived past 300.2s**:

```
task_6  300.2s  ← "Not connected"
task_5  299.7s
task_9  297.6s
task_9  271.3s     ← nothing else above 268s
task_1  267.8s
```

Three sessions piling up against the same ceiling from different wall-clock
start times rules out container scaledown — that would align to container
idleness, not to each session's own start. And no `idle_timeout` event appears
anywhere in the wire logs, so it wasn't our watchdog either.

## Two defects, one masking the other

**1. Modal's default 300s function timeout.** A WebSocket is [one Modal input](https://modal.com/blog/websocket-launch)
for its whole lifetime, so the function timeout bounds **call duration**, not
request latency — and [it defaults to 300s](https://modal.com/docs/guide/timeouts).
Neither service set it.

Blast radius is narrower than it looks: browser voice sessions dial the guest
sandbox's tunnel directly and never touch this path. It's `?host=1` sessions,
which run *in* the server process, that were exposed. The sandbox layer hit the
same trap first and already documents it in `modal-sandbox-env.ts` ("Modal's own
default (5 minutes) is far too short") — the web service just never got the same
treatment.

**2. `idle_timeout` never closed the socket.** `session-core` emitted the event
and left the connection open. But the event retires nothing — `aai-ui` routes it
to its `default:` branch and waits for a close, with a comment asserting *"the
server closes the socket itself."* It did not. The only paths that closed a
socket in `ws-handler.ts` were start failure, resume takeover, and client close.

So Modal's 300s cap had been silently doing the idle-reaping job. Fixing #1
alone would have extended every abandoned host-mode connection from 5 minutes to
4 hours, each holding a Modal input slot against `MAX_INPUTS=150`, a live
session, and its provider sockets.

## The fix

| | |
|---|---|
| `packages/aai/host/session-core.ts` | Close the client socket after emitting `idle_timeout` |
| `packages/aai-server/modal_deploy.py` | `timeout=4h`, matching `DEFAULT_SANDBOX_TIMEOUT_MS` |
| `packages/aai-studio-server/modal_deploy.py` | `timeout=30min` — longest input is a cold-sandbox Publish |

The two timers measure different things, which is why both are needed. Modal's
is wall-clock from connect and can't distinguish a busy call from an abandoned
one. `idleTimeoutMs` re-arms on every inbound audio frame (`resetIdle`), so it
measures *silence*. After this the cap is a backstop and the watchdog is the
policy.

Closing runs the existing retirement path (sink `close` → ws close listener →
`endSession`) — the same one resume takeover already uses.

## Testing

Two new tests in `session-core.test.ts`, both watched failing first:

- `closes the client connection after emitting idle_timeout` — failed with
  `expected [] to deeply equal [ 'idle timeout' ]`
- `emits idle_timeout before closing, so the client learns why` — failed with
  `expected [ 'event:idle_timeout' ] to deeply equal [ 'event:idle_timeout', 'close' ]`

Ordering matters: the event has to precede the close or the client learns only
that it was disconnected, not why.

Full suite green (`pnpm check` via pre-push). `aai-server` failed once during an
early `check:local` and did not reproduce across four subsequent runs; I don't
have that error's text.

## Not verified

Modal's docs state that a WebSocket is a single input, and separately that the
default execution timeout is 300s. They never state the interaction directly —
the link between them is inferred, corroborated by the hard 300.2s empirical
ceiling. The studio's 30min is precautionary headroom, not a fix for an observed
failure.

## What & why
Stage B, first unit. Two **concrete professional methods** — MET-01 Brainstorming and MET-02 5W1H — implemented on the existing PM-001..004 method foundation. **No rebuild, no schema change.**

## Architecture reused (no fork)
Each method is a code-backed `ProfessionalMethodDefinition` + deterministic `ProfessionalMethodValidating` validators, assembled by the one new `Method/Catalog/ProfessionalMethodCatalog` into the method + validator registries the generic `ProfessionalMethodLifecycleEngine` already consumes. No second run store / lifecycle / registry / validation / Claim-promotion authority.

## Professional-truth enforcement
- **Brainstorming** — typed proposal items only; its output contract allows *no* findings, so the conformance gate rejects any fact promotion, and the validator blocks an item flipped to accepted-for-workflow inside the method (promotion is a separate reviewed path). Anchored to the case context by a required evidence link.
- **5W1H** — six slot nodes; the validator blocks a slot answered without supporting evidence unless it is explicitly marked *unknown* (no fabricated answers); each answered slot is confirmed through a required **human** review.

Both drive the generic engine end-to-end: create → start → anchor evidence → items/slots → validate → review → complete → reopen.

## Tests
14 authored (PM005ConcreteMethodTests 8 + PM005MethodCatalogBoundaryTests 6). Full local suite **2794 / 2792 passed / 2 skipped / 0 failed**. No schema change → migration floor stays 263; executed-test floor 2762 → 2776.

body:
### Motivation
- The mobile Expo app lost all user state on restart (language, base currency, wallet balances, favorites, recent picks), which breaks UX and blocks features depending on durable state.

### Description
- Add AsyncStorage-backed persistence to the mobile `AppContext`, including a versioned `STORAGE_KEY` and a `parsePersistedState` validator to safely restore only well-formed values.
- Hydrate state on mount and defer rendering until hydration completes using a `hasHydrated` flag, preventing initial defaults from overwriting restored user data.
- Persist subsequent changes (language, base currency, wallet balances, favorites, recent currencies) to storage and cap recent list length to 5.
- Make persistence resilient: corrupted or unexpected stored data is validated and ignored without crashing the app.

### Testing
- Ran `pnpm --filter @workspace/mobile typecheck` and it completed successfully.
- Ran workspace `pnpm typecheck` and it completed successfully across projects.
- Ran code formatting and fixed issues with `prettier --write`, then verified `git diff --check` showed no problems.

author: achimdehnert
body:
Ein Anbieter statt drei. Teil des Rückbaus aus [platform#1680](https://github.com/achimdehnert/platform/issues/1680).

## Was sich ändert

Die CI-Workflows kommen jetzt aus [`iilgmbh/shared-ci@v1.1.0`](https://github.com/iilgmbh/shared-ci) — statt aus `achimdehnert/platform` (oft ungepinnt auf `@main`), aus `achimdehnert/shared-ci` (heute versehentlich entstanden) oder aus einem alten `shared-ci`-Tag.

## Warum

**Es gab nie zwei Anforderungen, nur zwei Pflegestände.** Ein Vollzensus über alle 72 Repos der vier Owner-Namensräume zeigte: dieselben Jobs, dieselben Schritte, unterschiedliche Action-Versionen. `v1.1.0` vereinigt beide Linien auf dem neueren Stand.

| Action | vorher | jetzt |
|---|---|---|
| `actions/checkout` | v6 | **v7** |
| `actions/setup-python` | v6 | **v7** |
| `docker/metadata-action` | v5 | **v6** |
| `aquasecurity/trivy-action` | **`@master`** | **v0.36.0** |

Der letzte war ein ungepinnter Verweis auf einen beweglichen Branch — in jedem Docker-Build, seit zwei Monaten.

Entfernt wurden zwei Sonderwege ohne fachlichen Grund: `skip_external_verify` (gebaut für ein Repo, das gar keinen Deploy hat) und `ghcr_push_token` (das Package war längst mit dem Repo verknüpft; der Standard-`GITHUB_TOKEN` reicht — am 2026-08-02 mit einem echten Build belegt).

## Wenn hier etwas rot wird

Der Rückweg ist ein Revert dieses PRs. Bitte **nicht** mergen, solange die CI rot ist — der Sinn der Welle ist, dass jedes Repo einzeln beweist, dass der Wechsel trägt.

## Summary

- upgrade LangChain and the OpenAI SDK and migrate model initialization to their current typed APIs
- collect all LangChain text usage with `get_usage_metadata_callback()`
- capture exact `gpt-4o-mini-tts` token usage from OpenAI speech SSE events while writing audio atomically
- merge text and speech usage into one run-level ASCII cost table grouped by provider, model, and modality
- add configurable model pricing, snapshot aliases, unknown-cost handling, documentation, and an environment toggle
- preserve machine-readable glossary-eval JSON by emitting its usage report to stderr

## Why

Model calls were split between LangChain text generation and the direct OpenAI speech API, so a run had no single view of token consumption or estimated cost. This adds one project-level report while keeping provider billing authoritative and making missing or incomplete pricing explicit.

## Impact

The exposed model-calling commands now print an estimated-cost report at the end of the run, including failure paths. Pricing is maintained under `llm.usage_reporting` and reporting can be disabled with `USAGE_REPORTING_ENABLED=false`.

Non-SSE speech models keep the existing binary response path and are shown with incomplete usage rather than an invented estimate.

## Validation

- `uv run pytest` — 300 passed
- `uv run ruff check scripts tests`
- `uv run mypy scripts/ --config-file mypy.ini`
- `git diff --check`

## Summary
- add optional `download-smoke inspect` quality gates for FASTA N50, record count, fragmented multi-record signals, and WGS/scaffold/contig header keywords
- keep default inspection behavior descriptive-only unless the operator supplies gate flags
- expose download-smoke prepare/inspect through AI-facing command catalog/render/plan metadata

## Safety
- no datasets execution, network access, provider contact, manifest mutation, or strict-deliverable promotion
- quality gates are bounded smoke acceptance criteria only

## Summary

Fixes the remaining non-protocol CodeQL finding after Security Hardening Pass 1 by removing the scheduler worker-port conversion from an environment-parsed integer into `uint32`.

The worker port calculation keeps the same deterministic FNV hash behavior, but computes modulo in `int64` after range clamping instead of converting the range to `uint32`.

Refs #395

## Security Alert

- [CodeQL #11 - go/incorrect-integer-conversion](https://github.com/bunny-lab-io/Borealis/security/code-scanning/11)

author: jancoo2013
mlengmark
body:
Addresses #78. Second and final part — #100 shared the wording, this builds the panel on it.

## What's here

`PanelContent` renders the shared data with Avalonia; `PanelWindow` hosts it; the tray icon's click opens it. **Every figure comes from `PanelStatistics` and every sentence from `PanelText`** — nothing here computes or words anything, so the two panels can't disagree.

Two things the panel forced into the shared layer:

**`PanelPalette`** — the panel's colours, with their reasoning. Those hex values are *measured*: the accent pair clears 4.5:1 against white label text while staying separable from both panel surfaces, and the categorical series were validated for colour-vision separation against the exact tile backgrounds. A second copy carries the colour but not the constraint. The WPF `PanelTheme` now reads from it and drops 140 → 70 lines.

**`PortalThemeSource`** — `IThemeSource` for Linux, deferred from #74 because it needs D-Bus. Portal first (cross-desktop); `gsettings` only as a fallback, since it reports nothing useful on Plasma. Linux exposes **one** colour scheme, so both surfaces get the same answer — unlike Windows, where they're genuinely two settings.

## Not a docked flyout

Per ADR-0013. SNI can't report where its own icon was drawn, and Wayland clients generally can't position their own surfaces. The panel centres rather than approximating docking badly — a panel that lands in the wrong place every time reads as broken, a plainly centred one doesn't.

## `--panel-samples`

Renders the panel offscreen to PNGs, mirroring the WPF head's `--popup-samples`. This is what lets layout and legibility be judged from images by someone who isn't the tester, before anyone installs anything.

**Two bugs it caught, by looking at the output rather than trusting it:**

- Reusing one control across samples silently produced **eleven copies of the first image** — layout is cached against the tree, so re-populating and re-rendering returns what was already arranged. Every file was a plausible-looking 2,254 bytes.
- Shutting down from inside framework initialisation tore the lifetime out from under itself.

Both would have shipped invisibly if I'd only checked that files appeared.

## Verification

**416 tests pass** (332 Core, 72 App, 12 Linux). Solution builds clean.

**All 12 panel samples render distinctly and were inspected.** Confirmed in the images:

- the `~` marker on an approximate weekly reset (`Resets in 3d 4h · ~Mon 18:00`)
- `excludes claude-brandnew-9 (no published rate)` under both 31-day tiles
- `N of 31 days recorded`, and the `Est.` prefix throughout
- **the rule 6 case** — no-data shows `unknown` rather than `0%`, empty bar tracks with no fill, `Reset time unknown (no reset observed yet)`, and an **empty graph** rather than a row of zero-height bars

**ADR-0013's Windows guarantee holds**: no Skia, HarfBuzz, Avalonia or Tmds in the Windows publish. Both Linux RIDs still publish self-contained.

## Not verifiable from here

How the panel positions itself on a real desktop, whether it's legible at real DPI, and everything about Wayland. Those need a session — `--panel-samples` exists to make that round trip shorter, not to replace it.

body:
## What changed

**Documentation only.** Corrects the five stale *"P3 is planning-only / gates unsigned"* claims that `P3-a0` escalated rather than edited, and records two follow-up debts a0 surfaced.

`P3-a0` held the narrow **D3** terminal-packet exception, which permits writing **only** the lead block and `## Next Safe Step`. Five live claims sat outside those two locations, so a0 correctly listed them for the owner instead of exceeding its authority. This packet is the authorized correction.

## The five claims

| File | Section | Was |
|---|---|---|
| `MASTER_HANDOVER.md` | `## Open Decisions` | *"P3 is the only one left and is planning-only — Gate 0 and Gate 1 are both unsigned"* |
| `MASTER_HANDOVER.md` | `## Blockers` | *"P3 must not start before Gate 1, and Gate 0 is unsigned too"* |
| `ACTIVE_DEVELOPMENT.md` | `## Current Objective` | *"**P3** … is **planning only**: Gate 0 and Gate 1 are both unsigned"* |
| `REFACTOR_PLAN.md` | owner-review status table, P3 row | *"**planning only** with Gate 0 and Gate 1 both unsigned"* |
| `REFACTOR_PLAN.md` | owner-review status table, overall row | *"P3 must not start while Gate 0 and Gate 1 are unsigned"* |

Each was **doubly wrong**: the gates *were* signed, and then the arc was terminated.

## The state each now records

- Both gates **signed 2026-08-02**.
- **`P3-a0` shipped** — PR #280, squash `cd93480`.
- The owner **terminated the arc at a0**, after a0's nineteen-tool assessment priced `P3-a1` at **nine** new tools against the small deletion yield already accepted at **Q6**.
- **`P3-a1` … `P3-e` carry no residual authorization.** Reopening requires a new owner decision.

`ACTIVE_DEVELOPMENT.md` also gains a fact worth stating plainly: **no production CSS was ever touched.** a0 was read-only with respect to `static/css/**`, so the arc ends with `theme-dark.css` byte-identical to where it started.

The two lead-block scope notes that named these sections as knowingly-stale now record them as **corrected**, so the files no longer point at a defect that is fixed.

**No dated historical entry was rewritten.** Every edit is in a live section.

## Two follow-up debts recorded — neither reopens P3

**P2.5 — the CI visual gate certifies a broken-icon state.** `base.html:16` loads FontAwesome from a CDN with **no local fallback**, unlike the Bootstrap link one line above which falls back to jsdelivr. It never resolves on the CI runner, so **every icon renders as a magenta placeholder square** in the committed Linux baselines. It is identical before and after the #281 regeneration, so it did **not** block that recovery. The consequence is what matters: the gate compares one broken-icon render against another, so **no icon regression can ever fail it**. Same "gate that cannot fail" class as the `occurrences <= 1` assertion and `measure.verify_blind_spots()`.

**P2.6 — `j_known_live_mutation.mjs` pins a Linux-incompatible digest.** It reads with `readFileSync` (untranslated bytes) and hashes them, so its pinned `EXPECTED_INPUT = e54818bf…` is the **CRLF** digest. With `core.autocrlf=true` and **no `.gitattributes`**, the committed blob is LF and hashes to `3ab06083…` — exactly **574 bytes** smaller, one `CR` per line. The control **runs on Windows and refuses to run on Linux**. `P3-a0` surfaced it and hit the identical hazard in its own contract file, where CI caught it.

## Scope

4 documentation files, 38 insertions / 25 deletions. No source, test, config, CSS or snapshot file is touched.

author: jm-cloud-apps
body:
## What

An app can now own a `schedule` (`ScheduledJob`) — a launchd timer job that runs with no server and no port, so the port poll behind Start/Stop can't see it. Those get their own switch on the tile and in the menu bar.

**InventoryForge's `Background scans` is the one that ships with it.** Every collector run pops a real Chromium window (patchright headed is the only way past Cloudflare), so being able to silence it without reaching for `launchctl` is the point.

## Why it's built this way

- **State lives in launchd, never in apps.json**, so the switch can't drift from what's actually scheduled. `Shell.scheduledLaunchdLabels()` re-reads it on each 2.5s poll — flip the job from a terminal and the switch follows.
- **A label counts as on only when it's *loaded* (`launchctl list`) AND *not disabled* (`launchctl print-disabled`).** Loaded-only would read a job as on that launchd will refuse to bootstrap after the next login; disabled-only would read one as on that was simply booted out.
- **Both launchctl verbs are needed in each direction.** Off is `bootout` + `disable` — `bootout` alone lets the agent load right back at login. On is `enable` + `bootstrap` — a disabled override makes `bootstrap` fail.
- **`AppConfig.backfillNewFields`.** The apps.json merge matches by name, so an existing InventoryForge entry already counted as "known" and would never have picked up the new field — the toggle would have shipped **dead** on any install that had already run. New fields on defaults now get copied onto saved entries where they're nil.

## Verification

`./build.sh` is clean, and the toggle was driven from the real UI:

| action | `launchctl list` | override db |
|---|---|---|
| switch off | label absent | `=> disabled` |
| switch on | label present | `=> enabled` |

Launch Deck logs its own `SCHEDULE OFF/ON` lines alongside the server output. The backfill was confirmed against the live `apps.json`.

## Note on scope

This also folds in the tile-density and grid-sizing work that was already sitting uncommitted in the tree. It can't be separated: the toggle attaches to the InventoryForge default app and extends the seeded-ledger merge, and **neither exists in `main`**. That work is 4 default apps (PlantForge, Elevator Clicker, Housing Calculator, InventoryForge), the `seeded.json` ledger so a deleted default stays deleted, compact icon-only buttons, and a 900×560 default window.

Version: 1.3.0 → **1.4.0**.

author: chris-fixportal
body:
## What

The PR review-signal sweep has been costing **7.4x the GitHub GraphQL budget** since it shipped, and the failure mode is silent.

Measured from production logs over three consecutive hours:

- **1,537 points per sweep** across 29 repos (~53 each)
- 150s cadence = **24 sweeps/hour = 36,888 points**
- Budget is **5,000 points/hour**

The observed hourly cycle:

| Time | Event | Remaining |
|---|---|---|
| 16:38:13 | window opens | 5000 |
| 16:39:58 | sweep | 3461 |
| 16:42:26 | sweep | 1924 |
| 16:44:56 | sweep | 387 |
| 16:47:24 | dies part-way, 7 of 29 repos | 16 |
| 16:47 - 17:38 | rate-limited, ~51 min | 0 |

`ReviewSignalEnrichmentWorker` converts rate-limit errors to last-known-good by design, so the board looked healthy while **22 of 29 repos served stale pills for most of every hour**.

GitHub meters GraphQL **per user identity, not per token**, so `DASHBOARD_GH_TOKEN` shares one 5,000/hour pool with any human running `gh`. An exhausted hour blocks the CLI too — which is how this surfaced: an estate deploy failed with `unable to determine default branch ... API rate limit already exceeded for user ID 28714804`.

## Changes

- **Cadence 150s -> 900s.** Production sets no `ReviewSignals__RefreshSeconds`, so the compiled-in default is the deployed value.
- **`pullRequests` cap 50 -> 25.** GraphQL prices by connection fan-out, so the outer cap multiplies every nested connection — halving it roughly halves the whole query.

Together: ~4 sweeps/hour at ~27 points per repo, about **3,100/hour**, leaving headroom rather than spending to zero.

## Why not trim the nested caps

`reviewThreads(100)`, `reviews(50)` and `contexts(50)` are deliberately untouched. Trimming those buys the same points while silently dropping threads and check runs, and **none of them carry a `hasNextPage` warning** — so an over-cap PR would report a confidently wrong pill rather than a missing one. The outer cap is the only one whose overflow is observable.

## Verification

- `dotnet build`: clean, 0 warnings
- `dotnet test`: 258/258 passing
- New test pins the cadence against the budget arithmetic, since reverting it re-creates the outage
- The worker already logs true cost per sweep, so the new figures are checkable in Log Analytics after deploy rather than taken on trust

## Follow-up not in this PR

Giving the dashboard its own identity (a GitHub App installation token) would stop it contending with human `gh` use at all. Worth doing, but it does not replace this change — at 36,888 points/hour the worker did not fit in a dedicated bucket either.
