## Summary
Follow-up polish to the (now merged) #46 work on the "Apply {template}" existing-resume dialog. Three commits that improve the resume picker's rows.

## Commits

### 1. feat(templates): show ATS score and target level on each apply-dialog row
`ApplyTemplateDialog.tsx` — each row now shows an ATS score chip (Gauge icon, color-coded with the same ≥70 / ≥40 / <40 buckets as the ATS page, "ATS not scored" fallback) and a target-level label from RESUME_TYPES. No extra network calls (values already on ResumeListItem).

### 2. perf(templates): lazy-fetch full resume data per row in apply dialog
`ApplyTemplateDialog.tsx` — each ResumePreviewThumb now fetches its resume's full data only when the row scrolls near the viewport (useInView, once), replacing the parent-level Promise.all that fetched every resume up front. 1 list request + only the full-data requests for rows actually scrolled to. 'failed' guard prevents retry storms; AbortController cancels on close.

### 3. feat(templates): enlarge-on-hover preview in apply dialog
`ApplyTemplateDialog.tsx` — hovering a row's thumbnail shows a floating enlarged peek (~150px, ~2.1x) of the same resume in the target template. Reuses the memoized preview (no extra renders), pointer-events-none so it never blocks the apply click, 250ms hide-grace so it stays readable while moving toward it.

## Validation
Each intermediate commit passed `eslint` and `tsc --noEmit` before being committed; final working tree is clean.

author: prince-pokharna
body:
## Summary
Fixes the indefinite-loading bug described in #23. A crashed Celery worker
(OOM kill, unhandled exception in Prophet) previously left task_id returning
PENDING forever with no user feedback. This PR fixes it at all three levels.

## Root Cause
When a Celery worker is killed before writing its result, the task ID never
transitions from PENDING to FAILURE in Redis. The frontend polled indefinitely
with no timeout and no backoff.

## Fixes

### `celery_worker.py` — task timeouts + reliability config
- `task_soft_time_limit=120` / `task_time_limit=150`: guarantees FAILURE state is written even on OOM
- `task_acks_late=True` + `task_reject_on_worker_lost=True`: re-queues killed tasks instead of silently dropping them
- `result_expires=3600`: cleans up Redis after 1 hour
- `SoftTimeLimitExceeded` caught in task body with user-readable message

### `api.py` — structured `/task/{task_id}` response
- Returns `error` field on FAILURE state (previously returned None for both success and failure)

### `frontend/src/lib/pollTask.ts` — new polling utility
- Exponential backoff: 2s → 3s → 4.5s → ... → 10s cap
- 90-second client-side timeout with clear actionable error message
- `onProgress` callback for live elapsed-time display

### `frontend/src/app/page.tsx` — wired error state
- `trainingError` state displayed with dismiss button
- `pollingStatus` updates with elapsed seconds during training

Closes #23

author: mattbutlerengineering
body:
Closes #3629

## Summary

`selectZoneSpreadBatch` (ADR-023) was inert on this repo's real backlog: `issueZone()` only derived a zone from the conventional-commit **title** scope, which misses (a) infra scopes like `ci`/`build`/`docs`/`chore` that map to no workspace package, and (b) every `/decompose`-generated `[Feature] ...` title (non-conventional-commit format, no scope at all). Measured: 21/22 ready issues resolved to `<global>`, collapsing `selectZoneSpreadBatch({ maxWorkers: 3 })` to a batch of 1.

## Fix

`issueZone()` now:
1. Keeps title-derived zone estimation as the first, higher-precedence check (unchanged behavior for conventional-scoped titles).
2. When the title yields no zone, falls back to paths named in the issue **body** — preferring a `## Files to Modify/Create` section (the shape `/decompose` emits) and otherwise scanning the whole body — resolved through the same `zoneForPaths()` merge-train-lock.mjs already uses (imported, not reimplemented).
3. Still returns `null` (global) for genuinely cross-cutting bodies (paths spanning >1 zone) or when neither title nor body yields anything.

Path extraction is anchored to a recognized workspace root prefix (`apps/`, `packages/`, `services/`) so prose like `main`, `CI Gate`, or `origin/main` can never be mistaken for a path — bounded, non-nested-quantifier regex, no ReDoS surface.

author: hassanhabib
body:
Pillar 3 — closes the security-critical gap left by PR #206/#207: the **streaming** path (`GenerateStreamAsync`) is the primary one, and it was still sending PII to the brain in the clear when `.Redact()` was on. Now it doesn't.

- **Input** is redacted before the generator is asked to stream — the brain (and any host) sees only `{{LABEL_N}}` tokens on this path too.
- **Output** is rehydrated as it streams, with a small hold-back buffer so a placeholder **split across chunks** (`"…{{EMA"` then `"IL_0}} now"`) is reassembled and restored to the real value — never emitted half-tokenized. The `{{` opener is grouped so a chunk boundary can't split the braces.
- **Zero cost when off:** with no redaction rules the vault is empty and tokens pass straight through — byte-identical to before, no buffering, no added latency. Every existing streaming test is untouched.

Together with #206/#207, **`.Redact()` now protects both the buffered and streaming brain boundaries.** Remaining follow-on: the Judge/verifier boundary (a remote judge still scores the rehydrated answer) — same tokenization, applied there next.

FAIL→PASS: `ShouldRedactPiiBeforeBrainAndRehydrateStreamedReplyOnGenerateStreamAsync` (token echoed split across two chunks; brain sees `{{EMAIL_0}}`, stream yields the real address). Category: MEDIUM FOUNDATIONS. 276 unit + 10/10 conformance green.

body:
## Qué cambia

La pantalla de planes dentro de la app mostraba los precios sueltos en USD, sin la oferta que sí aparece en la web. Ahora usa **los mismos números** que `home-client` y las landings por país, con el precio anterior tachado y la etiqueta **-50% hoy**:

| Plan | Mensual | Anual |
|---|---|---|
| Esencial | ~~$48~~ **$24** | ~~$38~~ **$19** (total $228) |
| Pro | ~~$98~~ **$49** | ~~$78~~ **$39** (total $468) |

## Moneda local

Se reutiliza el hook `useMonedaLocal` que ya usaba la web — detecta el país con `/api/geo` y convierte con sus tasas. Así se ve:

```
US   Esencial: $48 USD → $24 USD /mes       anual: $38 → $19 (total $228 USD)
MX   Esencial: $816 MXN → $408 MXN /mes     anual: $646 → $323 (total $3,876 MXN)
CO   Esencial: $201,600 COP → $100,800 COP  anual: $159,600 → $79,800
PE   Esencial: S/180 PEN → S/90 PEN         anual: S/143 → S/71 (total S/855)
```

Mientras `/api/geo` responde se muestra USD, en vez de pintar un precio local que después cambiaría solo.

## El cargo sigue siendo en USD

Stripe cobra en dólares (como quedó tras el PR #46). Por eso, debajo del precio local aparece el importe exacto que se va a cargar:

> Precio de referencia. El cargo se hace en dólares: US$24/mes.

En la web el precio local es orientativo y no pasa nada; **esta es la pantalla donde el usuario da clic y paga**, así que ver MX$408 y que el banco le cobre otra cifra sería un problema. La línea evita ese reclamo sin quitarle fuerza a la oferta.

- Conversión probada en US, MX, CO y PE (salida arriba).

author: mxinden
body:
Set the `ConnectionParameters` default for `max_pto` to 7, turning on the black-hole detector added in #3662 by default instead of leaving it opt-in.

A connection that sees 7 consecutive unacknowledged PTOs is almost certainly black-holed. Closing it then (`Error::TooManyPtos`, sent on the wire as `NO_VIABLE_PATH`) lets the application recover on a fresh path or another protocol rather than hanging until the idle timeout. At a 20ms RTT the 7th PTO fires around 2.5 to 5.7s, well inside the 30s idle timeout.

I plan to enable this on the Firefox side soon, so it is worth running neqo's own unit tests with the detector on by default already.

author: davidmjacobson
body:
A relay fetch page can be several megabytes. On an iPhone the whole HTTP request was bounded by a fixed 15-second wall clock, so on a weak connection — ship Wi-Fi, a busy port — a big page could not finish in time no matter how well it was actually moving. The resulting failure looked like an ordinary network error rather than "that page was too big", so the next pass asked the same relay for the same window from the same cursor and failed in exactly the same place. Nothing behind those rows was delivered until they expired.

## What changed

**The iPhone waits on progress, not on the clock.** `ios/CruiseMesh/Relay/RelayClient.swift` used a single `DispatchSemaphore.wait(timeout: connectTimeout + 5)` around the whole request, which is a total-time budget. That wait is now a loop: each slice that expires without the task finishing asks the response delegate whether anything arrived meanwhile, and as long as the byte count keeps moving the download is left alone, however long it takes. The delegate keeps a lock-guarded progress counter bumped on the response head and on every data chunk. Connecting stays bounded exactly as before — `URLRequest.timeoutInterval` is still `connectTimeout`, and URLSession applies it as its own inactivity timeout — and a transfer that genuinely goes quiet is still cut off.

**A body that stops part-way now shrinks the page instead of failing the pass.** Both shells already halve the row limit and retry the same cursor when a page is too big to *decode*; a page too big to *move over this link* is the same permanent stall and now takes the same recovery. Both errors share a common type — `RelayPageTooBigError` (iOS) / `RelayPageTooBigException` (Android) — so the retry loop cannot be wired up for one and forgotten for the other. On Android this is a reclassification only: its read timeout was already per-read inactivity rather than total, and `readBounded` now reports a `SocketTimeoutException` mid-body as `RelayResponseStalledException`. A timeout *before* the response head says nothing about page size and stays an ordinary transport failure on both platforms.

**Status is now checked before size.** `android/…/relay/RelayClient.kt` and the iOS `didReceive response` precheck both classified any large body as oversize before looking at the status code. A captive portal notice or a gateway error page can be any size, so one would be mistaken for an oversized page: the fetch would walk the entire shrink ladder — nine round trips — on a request that was never going to succeed, and a 429 lost the `Retry-After` the server asked for. Non-2xx responses now take the HTTP error path regardless of size, and only a 2 KiB preview of the error body is read (`readAtMost` on Android; a reduced accept budget in the iOS delegate), so an unbounded error body still never lands in memory.

**The server's page byte budget now has its floor pinned by a test.** `MAX_FETCH_PAGE_SEALED_BYTES` is exactly 16× `MAX_ENVELOPE_SEALED_BYTES`, and that is load-bearing for phones already in the field: they ask for 16 rows and treat any short page as the end of the mailbox, so a budget below that could truncate their ask and silently hide everything newer. Neither constant is changed — the new test just makes the coupling impossible to break by accident, with a note on when it can be retired.

Also: `RelaySyncEngine.kt`'s comment claimed the reduced fetch limit was "kept for the rest of this pass" when it is a function local, and so is per-mailbox. Corrected to match reality and the iOS comment; no behavior change.

## Tests

- `relayd`: `the_page_budget_can_never_truncate_a_sixteen_row_ask`.
- Android: a stalled body maps to the shared page-too-big type and carries the bytes it got; a 502 with a large body surfaces as an HTTP error after exactly one request rather than nine; a 429 with an oversized `Content-Length` keeps its `Retry-After`; the error-preview reader stops at its limit instead of failing.
- iOS: a page that stops arriving mid-body is retried at half the limit from the same cursor; a timeout with no response at all is *not* treated as a page problem; a large 502 surfaces by status with only a preview of the body kept; a 429 keeps its `Retry-After`. The mock URLProtocol grew a `stallAfterHeaders` mode to drive these.

Honest note on coverage: the iOS timing change itself — that a slow-but-progressing download is no longer killed at 15 seconds — is not directly unit-testable here, since the mock protocol delivers instantly. What the tests pin is the classification and recovery around it; the loop restructure is compile-checked by CI and reviewed by reading.

`cargo fmt --all`, `cargo test -p cruisemesh-core`, `cargo test -p cruisemesh-relayd` (54 lib tests green; the pre-existing `ws_live_push_after_connect` failure on this machine is the local VPN, not this change), and `:app:testDebugUnitTest` (450 tests) all pass. No exported core signatures changed. iOS compiles on CI.

body:
Closes #71

## What changed

- `canManageAllPortForwards()` (`backend/src/routes/admin.js`) now returns `isAdmin || userHasPermission(userId, 'can_manage_firewalls')` instead of reading `users.can_manage_firewalls` off the row.
- The `canSeeSensitiveFields` check in `GET /api/admin/firewalls` (`backend/src/routes/admin.js`) goes through `userHasPermission` the same way, so role-holders get `host`/`port`/`vdom`/`wan_interface`/`verify_tls`/… back instead of a blank Firewalls page.
- `PERMISSION_KEYS` in `backend/src/utils/permissions.js` now carries an explicit warning: never read these columns directly, always use `userHasPermission`/`effectivePermissions` (or `requirePermission`).
- Extracted the role-vs-column precedence rule into a new DB-free module `backend/src/utils/permissionRules.js` (`resolvePermissionCheck`, `resolveEffectivePermissions`); `permissions.js` now delegates to it. **No behaviour change** — the admin bypass still short-circuits before the role lookup, and `effectivePermissions` still deliberately does not fold in `is_admin`.
- New static regression guard `backend/src/utils/permissionColumnScan.js` — a pure `scanForLegacyPermissionColumnReads(path, contents)` plus a one-entry allowlist for the sanctioned `provision.js` read.

**`backend/src/routes/provision.js:134` was verified and left alone** — the issue is right about it. It selects `can_provision` *and* `role_id`, and `loadProvisioner()` immediately re-derives `can_provision` from `getRolePermissions(user.role_id)` on the next lines, so the role does win there. The allowlist entry pins that: it requires the matched line to mention `role_id`, so the exemption evaporates if that query ever stops selecting it.

## Tests

```
cd backend
node --test src/utils/permissionRules.test.js src/utils/permissionColumnScan.test.js
```

**Result: 22/22 pass.** Two new files:

- `backend/src/utils/permissionRules.test.js` — the precedence rule: a role grant counts while the column is `0` (the bug), a role that omits the key denies even when the column is `1`, no-role fallback to columns, `=== 1` strictness, admin bypass, missing user, multi-key OR, and the effective-map variants including "`is_admin` is not folded in".
- `backend/src/utils/permissionColumnScan.test.js` — unit tests for the scanner (bug shape, lowercase SQL, aliased table, comments and unrelated tables ignored) and the allowlist, then a walk of the real `backend/src` tree asserting the only match left is `routes/provision.js`, plus a check that `provision.js` still folds the role back in.

Verified the guard actually catches this bug: running the scanner over `git show HEAD~1:backend/src/routes/admin.js` reports 2 unsanctioned reads (lines 60 and 1433); over the fixed tree it reports 0.

Pre-existing sibling tests still pass — `node --test src/utils/vipName.test.js src/utils/vlanAccess.test.js src/utils/certSlots.test.js src/utils/taskProgress.test.js src/utils/wsClose.test.js src/utils/backupTask.test.js` → **56/56 pass**. `node --check` clean on every changed backend file.

## Notes / not done

- The tree walk skips `*.test.js` files (they hold example SQL, not authorization code) and matches per line. The multi-line user-listing query at `admin.js:176-188` is therefore not flagged — that one legitimately selects every `can_*` column for the admin user-management UI to display and edit, and is not an access decision.
- No frontend changes, so no `npm run build` was run.

대표 확정(2026-08-03): *"DB로 유어딜에 활동할 인플루언서 및 대행사에게 **제휴 제안을 보낼거야**. 출구는 내가 알아서 해."*

정면으로 충돌합니다. 그대로 두면 다음 세션이 그 문장을 읽고 **발송에 필요한 필드·필터·내보내기를 방치하거나 정리합니다** — `opted_out` · `email_status`(반송/스팸신고) · `contacted_at` · `status` · 엑셀 내보내기는 **제안 발송의 전제**입니다. 오늘 하루 낡은 문서로 오판한 게 여러 번이라(CF 토큰 건이 대표적) 같은 클래스를 미리 막습니다.

⚠️ 다만 **발송 자체는 대표가 한다**고 명시했습니다 — 세션이 콜드 발송을 자동화하지 않습니다. 방향이 아니라 법·평판 문제이고, 대표가 직접 판단할 자리입니다.

```
전체 43,995 → 이메일 6,107 → 거부제외 6,097 → 카테고리 5,887 → 개인 5,801
```

⚠️ **44,012 같은 총계로 진척을 보고하지 말 것** — 87%는 이메일이 없어 지금 쓸 수 없습니다.

그리고 이 지표로 재보니 **② 카테고리는 병목이 아니었습니다** — 발송 가능 리드의 **96.5%**(5,887/6,097)가 이미 카테고리를 갖고 있습니다. 병목은 ④ 연락처 하나뿐이고, 측정 수율(블로그 28.7% · YT 45%)이 그걸 증명합니다.

author: barakatammre84
body:
## Why

`apiRequest` is the only place the **401 → `/login`** redirect is wired ([queryClient.ts](client/src/lib/queryClient.ts)). 17 authenticated call sites went around it with a raw `fetch`, so when the session expired those surfaces just rendered an error or an empty state while the user was actually logged out — whether they got bounced to `/login` depended on which endpoint happened to notice first.

Third finding from the client data-flow audit, after #271 and #275.

## What changed

Converted every call whose endpoint is **server-side gated** (`isAuthenticated` / `requireRole`) — I checked each one against its route definition rather than converting on sight:

deal-team + available-staff queries · notification read/read-all · predictions · affordability · autopilot snapshot + admin metrics · presigned-upload request · staff-invite redemption · prequal / pre-approval / MISMO / adverse-action downloads.

### Deliberately NOT converted

These are wrong to convert, and the guard test now documents why:

| Left raw | Reason |
|---|---|
| `/api/track`, `/api/client-errors` | public, fire-and-forget — routing telemetry through the thing that throws and navigates risks a loop |
| `POST /api/auth/logout` (×3) | session teardown; a 401 is the expected end state, not an expiry |
| rates, articles, faqs, geocode, agent search, invite validation, waitlists | public — no session to expire, and each owns error copy that apiRequest's `"<status>: <body>"` throw would replace for no benefit |

## `ApiError`

`apiRequest` now throws `ApiError`, carrying `status` alongside the **unchanged** `"<status>: <body>"` message. Two sites branch on 403 to keep their specific copy ("MISMO export is restricted to internal staff…"), which previously required reading `res.status` directly. Keeping the message format identical means `friendlyApiError` and every existing consumer are unaffected.

## One behavior change worth reviewing

Because `apiRequest` throws instead of returning a response, the staff-invite redemption's error branch moved. The server's specific copy ("this invite has already been used") now arrives in the `catch`, which previously swallowed it behind a generic message — so that catch unwraps it with `friendlyApiError`. Without this the change would have been a quiet UX regression.

## The ratchet

[`tests/apiRequestConvergence.test.ts`](tests/apiRequestConvergence.test.ts) scans client source for raw `fetch` to `/api/` and fails with `file:line` unless the file is on an allowlist carrying its reason. A second assertion fails if an allowlist entry *no longer* has a raw fetch, so the list can't rot into blanket permission for a future one.

I verified the guard actually bites by reintroducing a converted call as a raw fetch — it failed with the exact file:line, then passed again on revert.

## Verification

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `pnpm check` (tsc) | clean |
| Unit lane | 1364 passed (103 files, +1 new) |
| Client lane | 77 passed |
| `pnpm guard:tokens` | at baseline |

**Live, against a seeded borrower:** killed the session server-side while sitting on `/dashboard`, then clicked "Mark all read" — the app redirected to `/login` instead of failing silently. That is the bug.

Document downloads confirmed unchanged: identical `200 application/pdf`, valid 4.5KB blob under apiRequest's exact request shape.

author: davidalcoba
body:
Wires each deployment target to its own Neon branch so no preview can ever read
from — or, since the build runs `prisma migrate deploy`, migrate — production.

## What changed in the repo

- **`scripts/migrate.mjs`** — logs `[migrate] target: <neon-endpoint-id> (via DATABASE_URL|DIRECT_URL)`
  at the top of every build. Prisma prints the full host, but Vercel redacts it in
  build logs because it matches an env var value; the first DNS label is the Neon
  endpoint id, is not a credential, and survives redaction. Without it there is no
  way to tell from a build log which Neon branch a deployment actually migrated.
- **`ai-instructions/context/ARCHITECTURE.md`** — new "Databases (Neon)" section:
  the branch-per-target table, the Vercel env var layout, why there is deliberately
  no generic `preview` `DIRECT_URL`, the free-plan 10-branch cap and its fail-closed
  behaviour, and the SQL-over-HTTP tooling note (port 5432 is blocked by the network
  policy).
- **`CLAUDE.md`** / **`.env.example`** — index entry and `DIRECT_URL` documented.

## Configuration changed outside the repo (Vercel project env vars)

| Key | Target | `gitBranch` | Points at |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `DATABASE_URL` | `production`, `development` | — | Neon `main`, pooled |
| `DATABASE_URL` | `preview` | `preview` | Neon `preview`, pooled |
| `DIRECT_URL` | `preview` | `preview` | Neon `preview`, direct |
| `DATABASE_URL` | `preview` | — | Neon `preview`, pooled — safety net |

The generic `preview` `DATABASE_URL` previously held the **production** URL, which
meant any preview that missed the Neon–Vercel integration's per-deployment injection
would have connected to and migrated production. It now points at the shared
non-production `preview` branch.

## Verification status

Production and feature-branch previews are verified — their build logs show their
own Neon endpoint. The one open point is the `preview` git branch itself: the
`[migrate] target:` line does not exist on `preview` yet, so merging this PR is what
makes that check possible. After the merge, a `preview` deployment should log
`ep-wild-bonus-alkflucu (via DIRECT_URL)` (the Neon `preview` branch);
`ep-green-tooth-alfoy7me` would mean production and would need fixing.

author: michaelayoade
body:
## Summary

Kernel-adoption slice **E2**, re-derived from scratch on current main against the released **`dotmac-kernel==0.1.0a8`**. The earlier E2 attempt (85ceff47, branch `feat/kernel-adoption-e1`) was blocked on the a7 wheel's floors and is superseded by this PR — nothing was merged from that branch.

### Exact pin + resolution success

- `[[tool.poetry.source]]` **forgejo** (`https://registry.dotmac.io/api/packages/dotmac/pypi/simple/`, `priority = "explicit"`) — URL only, **no credential in the repo**; poetry reads auth from its own store under the source name.
- `dotmac-kernel = {version = "0.1.0a8", source = "forgejo"}` — exact `==`-pin, no range, **no python marker**: a8 widened its floors (`fastapi>=0.111,<0.116`, `pydantic>=2.7.4,<3.0`, `pydantic-settings>=2.2,<3.0`, `python>=3.11`), so ERP's existing pins (fastapi 0.111.0, pydantic 2.7.4, python `>=3.11,<3.13`) resolve cleanly with **zero ERP pins loosened**.
- `poetry lock` delta adds only three packages: **dotmac-kernel 0.1.0a8**, **pydantic-settings 2.14.2**, **typing-inspection 0.4.2**. No removals, no version moves.
- **No extras installed**: a8's extras split means `[testing]` would add only httpx and `[licensing]` only cryptography — both are already ERP main dependencies (httpx 0.27.0, `cryptography>=44.0.1` above the kernel's `>=42` floor).

### 13 canaries — all RUNNING, zero skips

`tests/architecture/test_kernel_compatibility.py`. The blocked attempt's skip machinery is deleted entirely: a missing or wrong-version kernel is now a hard failure, never a skip.

1. `test_kernel_is_pinned_to_one_exact_version` — `==`-exact pin, gate synced to `0.1.0a8`
2. `test_kernel_resolves_from_the_named_private_index` — named source, `priority=explicit`, no userinfo/token in URL
3. `test_consume_pure_list_matches_e1_allowlist` — this file cannot drift from the E1 guard's allowlist
4. `test_import_dotmac_kernel_needs_no_database_url` — from-scratch no-DB subprocess env
5. `test_installed_distribution_is_the_pin_and_ships_py_typed` — wheel version == `0.1.0a8`, PEP 561 marker
6. `test_every_consume_pure_module_imports_without_db` — full consume-pure surface **including the `dotmac_kernel.testing` subtree**
7. `test_consume_pure_imports_are_all_kernel_supported_modules` — no known-omissions carve-out remains
8. `test_money_is_exact_and_rejects_float` — Decimal-exact, float refused, cross-currency refused
9. `test_composition_contract_types_are_constructible` — FeatureManifest / CapabilityCatalogue / ProductAssemblySpec / DeploymentProfileSpec
10. `test_licence_verifier_is_importable`
11. `test_fake_licence_signer_works_via_erps_own_cryptography` — see below
12. `test_app_import_loads_no_kernel_module` — subprocess proof importing `app.main` loads **zero** `dotmac_kernel` modules
13. `test_app_boot_mounts_no_kernel_route_or_middleware` — no kernel-served route, no `/platform/auth` prefix, no kernel middleware

### Inverted defect assertions

The old E2 pinned the two a7 release defects red-sensitively; a8 fixed both (kernel CHANGELOG "0.1.0a8 — Fixed"), so the tests now assert the **fixed** behavior:

- `dotmac_kernel.testing` (incl. `fakes`/`licensing`/`provisioning`) imports in a no-DB subprocess — the eager `harness → deps → db` engine build is gone; a DB-bound testing kit is now a regression that fails canary 6.
- `dotmac_kernel.profiles` **is** in `SUPPORTED_MODULES` — asserted explicitly in canary 7.
- Extras/cryptography decision: ERP installs the kernel with no extras, and since `cryptography>=44.0.1` is ERP's **own** main dependency, the honest assertion is that `FakeLicenceSigner` **constructs and signs successfully** (not `VerificationUnavailableError`). Canary 11 first proves the provenance (pyproject declares cryptography) so the claim cannot silently rot if ERP ever drops that dependency.

### App unchanged / E1 guard intact

`app/` is untouched in this slice. The E1 import-boundary guard (`test_kernel_import_boundary.py`) passes unchanged, and canaries 12–13 prove booting the app touches no kernel code.

### Ledger

`docs/PLATFORM_ADOPTION_LEDGER.md`: E2 status block rewritten for a8 (install unblocked, lock delta, defects fixed with CHANGELOG reference, extras decision), classification heading bumped to 0.1.0a8, `dotmac_kernel.testing` row updated.

### Validation

- `poetry lock` / `poetry install` clean; `poetry show dotmac-kernel` → 0.1.0a8
- `pytest tests/architecture/` → **40 passed, 0 skipped** (kernel file: 13 passed, 0 skipped)
- `ruff check` + `ruff format --check` clean on touched files
- `mypy app/ --ignore-missing-imports` → no issues in 1409 files

author: csguth
body:
## O que

Garante que um pedido da loja só possa ser **pago/capturado** quando a entrega for para a Holanda — respondendo ao pedido de "validar o formulário para que somente Netherlands seja possível".

O seletor `shippingCountry` já escondia o checkout para não-NL, mas isso era só uma dica de intenção escolhida pelo próprio comprador. Como o formulário "Debit or Credit Card" é hospedado pelo PayPal e o comprador controla o endereço lá dentro, adicionei validação real do país (defense-in-depth), tudo **client-side** (sem backend, mantendo a arquitetura zero-build da loja).

## Como

- **`onShippingChange`** (1ª camada): rejeita um endereço de entrega não-NL ainda dentro do popup do PayPal/cartão, **antes** de qualquer autorização — o PayPal mostra o próprio aviso de "não é possível enviar para este endereço".
- **`onApprove`** (2ª camada / guarda real): relê a ordem aprovada com `actions.order.get()` e só chama `actions.order.capture()` (a cobrança de fato) quando o país de entrega/cobrança é `NL`. Se não for, **não captura** (nenhum valor é cobrado; o PayPal anula a aprovação) e exibe uma mensagem de erro localizada.
- **`onCancel`/`onError`**: handlers adicionados para não deixar o carrinho num estado inconsistente e logar erros inesperados.
- Nova string i18n `checkout_country_error` em **en/nl/pt**, renderizada por um novo bloco `<template x-if="checkoutCountryError">` (i18n compile-time, como o resto do site).
- Constante `ALLOWED_COUNTRY = 'NL'` centraliza o país permitido.

## Ressalva

Sem backend, toda validação roda no navegador do comprador (a captura é client-side via PayPal JS SDK). Isso cobre muito bem o caso real de merch de banda, mas não é uma trava criptográfica server-side. O país de **cobrança** do cartão no formulário hospedado do PayPal não é 100% travável pelo Smart Buttons (exigiria Advanced Card Fields); por isso a checagem antes de `capture()` usa o endereço de entrega com fallback para o de cobrança.

## Verificação

- `hugo --gc --minify` builda sem erros (só warnings de deprecação pré-existentes); as 3 páginas `/{en,nl,pt}/shop/` renderizam o bloco de erro e a frase traduzida.
- `node --check static/js/shop-page.js` OK.

author: teamleaderleo
andtii
body:
Closes #571 (part 3 — parts 1+2 landed in #602). The last phase of rfc-server-v3: request-value disposal, deferred from v1 because "disposed when the response has flushed" could not be made true on WinterCG — `createFetchHandler` settles its scope at the shell while `useData` fetchers keep resolving into the stream. This implements §2.6's sketched design exactly, plus the pieces it left open.

**The API:**
- `perRequest((rq, onDispose) => …)` — the setup's additive second parameter registers teardown. Disposers run LIFO, each awaited, throws logged and swallowed; disposal clears the memo. Register synchronously before the first `await` (late registration still registers, dev-warned).
- `disposeRequestValues(rq)` — public root export: the trigger for stores nothing owns (`fn.with({ context })`, detached calls — dev-warned at registration).
- `__SIGX_SERVERFN_SCOPE__.keepAlive(until)` — optional seam extension (docs/seams.md updated): extends the current scope's disposal past `run()`'s settle. The fetch handler registers it before returning a streamed Response, resolved by `chunksToBytes`'s new `onSettled` on whichever ending the body reaches (close/error/cancel). Feature-detected on both sides — an old package beside a new renderer (or vice versa) degrades to pre-disposal behavior, and the stamp also patches `keepAlive` onto an already-stamped seam object for dev's dual-module copies.

**Ownership — claim-based, first-claimer-wins, per store** (the open design question, now decided): the endpoint claims its context before opening a scope (so it owns with or without ALS); `runInScope` claims any unclaimed store it enters — a nested same-request merge reuses the enclosing (claimed) bag, so only the outermost entry disposes, and the documented pre-seed recipe gets disposal for free. Disposal releases ownership (a deliberately reused bag is claimed afresh next entry) but leaves `disposed` sticky until that claim, so a straggler from the dead request — a fetcher settling after a client cancel — runs its disposer immediately instead of parking forever.

**Endpoint wiring:** disposal hangs off the WORK promise's real settle — never the `timeoutMs` race (the old losing-work swallow is absorbed by the settle hook) — so a 504 disposes only when the still-settling handler finishes. Streams take ownership at `streamResponse` entry: every terminal (empty generator, normal end, mid-stream throw, unserializable chunk, client cancel) disposes AFTER the generator's `return()` settles, so a `finally` reading a per-request value never races its own teardown; pre-Response failures dispose in the same order before rethrowing to the buffered catch; a stream that lost the timeout race has its body cancelled at work-settle, driving the same chain.

**Tests (41 new):** `disposal.test.ts` (drain semantics, registration rules, scope ownership + keepAlive accumulation/drain-loop/nesting/pre-seed, endpoint settle paths incl. THE timeout pin, all stream terminals + the ordering pin) and `disposal-keepalive.test.tsx` — **the motivating pin as a real cross-package integration** (real `@sigx/server` seam, real ALS, real `useData` fetcher): a streamed edge response is NOT disposed at the shell and IS disposed after the body is read, plus cancel/shell-error/Node-twin cases. Also chunks-to-bytes `onSettled` once-per-ending, the serverfn-scope version-skew no-op pin, and node-adapter buffered + stream disposal over real `node:http`.

**Docs:** seams.md contract row; rfc-server-v3 §2.6 marked shipped with the decided rules recorded + phase 5 proofs listed; rfc-server §2.1's withdrawn `onDispose` claim un-withdrawn in its landed form; README `perRequest` section rewritten (incl. the workerd `ctx.waitUntil` note and the upgrade-together version-skew note) + the rate-limit section's concurrency-cap release now points at `onDispose`; CHANGELOGs for both packages, with a `Changed` entry naming the observable pattern per the return-value rule (a locals bag reused across sequential scoped renders now re-runs setups after disposal).

Verification: `pnpm typecheck`, full `pnpm test` (3483 passed), `pnpm lint`, `pnpm build`, `pnpm test:edge` all green. Perf: sequential quiet-machine `bench:ssr:quick` runs show no regression attributable to this change (flagged rows vary per run and appear identically on untouched main); the bench-ab job's same-runner table is the authoritative check.

body:
Dictating an answer while an agent was waiting on a question showed the level meter and the recording indicator, then produced no text at all. The same silence hit `@` file mentions, slash commands, skills and stash insertion whenever a question was pending.

The answer field is the main composer in a different mode, and it is controlled. A programmatic write reaches the change handler one render before Lexical holds the new text, and the handler focused the editor immediately. `focusAt` re-emits the editor value through `onChange`, so it echoed the stale text straight back into the same handler and overwrote what had just been written, in the same tick. Typing was unaffected because Lexical already holds the new text, so the mismatch that triggered the focus never fired.

The focus is now deferred by a frame, matching what the ordinary composer branch already does, and it refuses to focus an editor that still lags, which is precisely when the echo does damage. The logic moved into `pendingAnswerFocusSync` so it can be tested without rendering `ChatView`. A dictation write rejected by the concurrency guard now raises the same Dictation stopped toast used for transport errors rather than disappearing.

author: faviann
body:
Follow-up to #33, which introduced both problems.

`skills/engineering/domain-modeling/CONTEXT-FORMAT.md` is byte-identical to `upstream/main`,
so its rules bind here. Two of them were broken:

> **Be opinionated.** When multiple words exist for the same concept, pick the best one and
> list the others under `_Avoid_`.

`_Avoid_` holds *other words for the concept*. `pilot Frontier` qualifies and stays.
`Frontier mid-sentence` doesn't — it's a casing rule in the field's clothing. Removed.

> **Keep definitions tight.** One or two sentences max.

The entry had grown to four. Now two.

The casing note is **dropped rather than relocated**. `CLAUDE.md` already carries the rule,
and it loads into every session in this repo while `CONTEXT.md` is read on demand — so the
glossary copy was the less reliably seen of the two, and it cost the sentence budget.

The longer explanation of the two scoped uses stays in **Flagged ambiguities**, which has no
length rule.

### The same rule, two more entries

An audit of every entry against the same cap found two more over it — **Map** at three
sentences, **Not yet specified** at four. Both are fork-added, by `9ddba21`. Upstream's own
four entries (**Issue tracker**, **Issue**, **Decision ticket**, **Triage role**) are all
compliant, so every violation in this file is ours.

Nothing is lost, because the overflow restated the skill that owns the term:

| dropped from | already in |
|---|---|
| the fog test | `wayfinder/SKILL.md:88` |
| "coarser than a ticket… several tickets, or none" | `wayfinder/SKILL.md:91` |
| the in-scope boundary | `wayfinder/SKILL.md:86` |
| map/children/blocking/frontier are tracker-specific | `wayfinder/SKILL.md:25` |

**Not yet specified**'s dropped exclusions are entailed by its own first sentence — *in
scope* excludes out of scope, *not yet sharp enough* excludes a live ticket, *you can tell
are coming* excludes already decided. **Map**'s dropped pointer to
`docs/agents/issue-tracker.md` is still reached from `CLAUDE.md:45`, which is always loaded.
(An earlier draft of this description claimed `wayfinder` reaches it too — it does not.
Per `CHANGELOG.md:63`, wayfinder was deliberately changed to stop pinning the literal path
and to resolve the tracker doc through `CLAUDE.md`'s `### Issue tracker` block. One route,
not two.)

All 12 entries now sit at or under the cap. Upstream's destroyed-word count for this file
holds at 1, unchanged. Its `## Language`, `## Relationships` and `## Flagged ambiguities`
sections are upstream's own — not fork additions — and are untouched.

### Review finding, fixed in `a35032a`

A review of this branch found that `882259f` hit the two-sentence cap on **Frontier** by
**rewriting** its second sentence rather than deleting around it: 35 fork words destroyed
where 20 — the casing note — were the only intended deletion.

The replacement wording tracked `8244a95`'s *pre-resolution* phrasing, undoing
`8cc0b6a` — a commit from the previous day whose title is the verdict it installed,
*"Resolve the frontier flag: two scoped uses, not a conflict."* `git log -S "Two scoped uses"`
names it in one line; `CLAUDE.md` requires that check before rewriting a sentence and it
was not run. Neither the commit message nor this description disclosed the rewrite.

Sentence 2 is restored verbatim. Destroyed words drop 35 → 22: 20 the intended casing
deletion, 2 the punctuation and case forced by folding *"See **Flagged ambiguities**"* into
the clause before it. The cap never required the rewrite.

### The `_Avoid_` line is dropped, not relocated (`30c141c`)

The review flagged that `_Avoid_: pilot Frontier` named no chosen alternative. Looking
closer, the problem is upstream of that: **it was filed under a headword it doesn't serve.**
`_Avoid_` rejects synonyms *of the headword* — upstream lists *backlog manager* under
**Issue tracker**, *ticket* under **Issue**. Nobody wrote *pilot Frontier* meaning *"the work
takeable right now"*; they wrote it meaning the frontier published now under staged
calibration, which `STAGED-CALIBRATION.md` calls the **immediate frontier**.

Moving it to **Staged calibration** would be the same misfiling one entry over. That left a
headword of its own, or removal. Removal chosen: the drift is corrected in all four files
that carried it, and `CLAUDE.md` now carries the trigger that catches a rename, so a
glossary entry for a term used in one reference file would cost per-session context for a
guard that already exists.

The rejection stays on the record in `3be96c7` and #33 — which is where someone asking
*"was pilot considered?"* would look — since the changeset carrying it is consumed at
release.

### Note

The `_Avoid_` violation was written by #33's `8244a95` — the commit that added the trigger
meant to stop vocabulary drift. The length violation on **Frontier** is older: `9ddba21`
shipped it at three sentences and `8244a95` took it to four, so the tidy
"the drift-prevention commit caused the drift" reading is only half right. Nothing routes someone editing `CONTEXT.md` to `CONTEXT.md`'s own
format spec, which is the same shape of gap one level up. Not fixed here; worth a pointer
from `CONTEXT.md` to `CONTEXT-FORMAT.md` if it recurs.

No changeset — `CONTEXT.md` is repo governance and ships in no plugin.

author: nazmi02551
zook-bot
body:
Executes the port planned in su-xkmq.1 (PR #41), landing the
`claude/ios-voice-transcription-review-9ss6cj` transcript-core rewrite
(`27c20ed`) on top of post-PR#37 main. Base is `32f341f`, which already
contains both prerequisites: the plan (#41) and the Xcode 26 runner upgrade
(#42).

**Nothing in this PR has been compiled.** There is no Swift toolchain and no
Xcode on the Linux worktree this was written in. That is expected and planned
for — §6 schedules the operator's Mac gates as named steps — but it means the
test-plan section below is an honest account of what was *written*, not what
was *verified*. Please read it before merging.

---

## What changed, and why

### Deleted: the obsolete scaffolding, including the set git would not have flagged

`AudioPipeline` and `SpeechTranscriber` are modify/delete conflicts git reports.
The dangerous three are the **silent set** — `FileTranscriber` (+97),
`TranscriptReconciler` (+143) and `TranscriptStitcher` (+101), plus their two
test files. PR#37 *added* these; they did not exist at the merge base
`a3437ce`, so the rewrite never saw them, never deleted them, and a merge
reports no conflict. Left alone they merge in clean and ship as live,
compiling, wrong code. The plan called this the single most likely way the port
ships wrong, so it is done deliberately and early (Stage 2).

They are obsolete rather than merely redundant: with SpeechAnalyzer there is no
duty cycle, so no ~50 s task-rotation seam is left to stitch, and the live
transcript is authoritative, so there is nothing to repair from a second
offline pass over the `.m4a`. `SessionRecord.transcriptIsReconciled` and
`SessionRecovery.reconcilePendingTranscripts` go with them.

Deleting the app's own `SpeechTranscriber` class is also what makes the rewrite
compile: `SpeechTranscriber` is an Apple iOS-26 SDK type that `AnalyzerEngine`
and `AssetEnsure` both use, and the same-named app class shadowed it.

### `SessionController` re-derived in one pass

All four workstreams land in this file. A textual three-way merge produces
garbage — both sides rewrote it (+820 / +798) — so the rewrite's 1101-line
version is the skeleton and PR#37's surfaces are re-applied by hand.

Carried forward, each of which the re-derivation would otherwise have silently
deleted: **generation-token fencing** (`31dba3c`), the ambient analyst, session
modes, coverage presets, `sessionCost`, typed `SessionErrorKind`, the
IntentBridge wiring, the candidate-pool fast path, and the `#if DEBUG`
capture-seam call sites.

The fencing is worth calling out: the rewrite had regressed it to
`isRunning`-only, which is precisely the insufficient check `31dba3c` replaced.
Stop a session and start another inside one in-flight request and `isRunning`
is `true` again while the reply belongs to the previous conversation. The
transcript seam did not make it redundant — it fences model replies, which are
a network round-trip, not transcript delivery. `sessionGeneration` +
`isCurrent(_:)` now guard **every** model-reply completion, including the
rewrite's two.

### The analyst rides the transcript seam, on a monotonic basis

`CandidatePool` anchors candidate freshness to a character offset and expires
on `currentPosition - anchorPosition > maxDrift`, which is meaningful only
while `currentPosition` never decreases. `store.fullText` includes **volatile**
segments, SpeechAnalyzer revises those in place, and a revision can be
*shorter* — so drift goes negative and candidates stop expiring exactly when
the transcript is churning.

This is not hypothetical: anchoring by character offset into a mutable string
is one of the two load-bearing reasons the rewrite exists, and PR#37
re-introduced a second such anchor in the analyst, months later.

Fix: `TranscriptStore.finalizedText`, mirroring `fullText` exactly but for
`state == .final`, cached beside it on the same store event. **Both** analyst
call sites move to it together — `tick` and
`candidate(for:transcriptLength:)` — because one basis per `CandidatePool` is
the whole invariant. Splitting them either over-states drift (fresh candidates
dropped at the moment they would be spoken) or makes it negative (nothing ever
expires); both compile and both are silent. `askNow` and `checkCoverage`
deliberately stay on the live text. `CandidatePool` itself is unchanged.

### Interruption handling and the TTS sink re-homed

`CaptureController` owns the audio graph and handles the interruption *event*;
the session's *response* is still the host's. PR#37's `handleInterruption`
did five things and the controller replaces only two, so `onState` → `.paused`
now drives the rest: cut the clip, **close the open listener segment at the cut
point**, release the floor, park the turn machine.

The listener close matters because the open segment's end is an *estimate* set
at append time — without it the record claims the companion said words it was
cut off before speaking, and on a long interruption that estimate lands
arbitrarily far from any audio that exists. `lastFloorReleaseMs` is set from
wall-clock `nowMs()`, not `audioNow`: the audio clock stops with the engine and
the two diverge by exactly the interruption's length.

`AudioPipeline` owned the TTS player node; deleting it took the sink with it,
and without it the mic hears the app's own voice. `CaptureController` now
conforms to `TTSPlaybackSink`, and **every** engine-rebuild path re-attaches
the node — route change, configuration change, media-services reset, resume.
Missing any one of those is a permanently silent companion mid-session.

Its `pause()` also now clears the VAD window, which it did not. `AudioPipeline.
suspend()` was explicit about why: *"VAD state so a half-formed onset doesn't
survive the gap."* Without it, `inSpeech` carried across a five-minute phone
call fires a hangover-driven speech-end the instant audio returns. It is done
as a `resetVADOnNextBuffer` flag rather than a direct write, mirroring the
existing `proveResumeOnNextBuffer`, because those fields are written from the
audio thread and `pause()` cannot make `start()`'s "no tap exists yet"
argument.

### One migration covering both shipped shapes, and a silent data-loss path closed

Three shapes exist: base (pre-PR#37), PR#37 (current main), and V2. **V1 is
declared at the PR#37 shape**, not the base shape as the rewrite had it — both
PR#37 fields are lightweight-inferrable from the true base, so one V1 opens
both shipped stores. The rewrite's V1 described a shape matching no device that
ran a current-main build.

`costUSD` is **carried into V2** (the rewrite's V2 omitted it; dropping it
voids the cost readout for every past session). `transcriptIsReconciled` is
**dropped** — a destructive change, which is why the stage must be `.custom`.

The data-loss path: `TranscriptCore.StoredEntry` had no `startMs`/`endMs`, and
`JSONDecoder` ignores unknown keys — so a PR#37-era blob decoded through it
*successfully* and dropped its timings, with no exception and no log line.
Every session recorded on current main would have migrated replay-less,
permanently. Fixing `StoredEntry` alone changes nothing observable, because the
migration does not go through `segments(from:)` — it runs
`materializeLegacySegments(in:)`, which hardcoded the zeros. **Both** halves
are fixed, and the read-path fallback and the materializer now agree by
construction.

**Documented approximation:** PR#37's `startMs`/`endMs` are wall-clock ms from
`clockOrigin`; V2's ranges are canonical fed-samples audio seconds. They agree
except across an interruption. Carrying them is strictly better than zeroing —
the conservative alternative loses working replay on every existing session to
avoid drift on the subset that was interrupted. Recorded on the migration
stage's doc comment.

### `project.pbxproj`, done by hand

Both sides edit the same config blocks, and PR#37's blocks are where the
capture seam's Release exclusions live. Merged: the `TranscriptCore` product
(four places), `IPHONE

author: homesignalg
body:
Follow-up to #553, from the first run that actually reached the end instead of being cancelled at the 6 h cap.

**The leak fix worked**: run `30762637599` terminated in **1 m 39 s** instead of burning six hours. But it failed — with `SyntaxError: Unexpected end of JSON input` inside `loadDevReports` — exposing a **second, independent defect** that the cancellations had been hiding.

### This job has never been able to load its own input

The read pulls `development_reports` rows whole, including the entire `sites` array — and those rows now reach **~19.6 MB each**. A large page drops mid-stream, so the response arrives **200 with a truncated body**, and `res.json()` throws.

The adaptive page-size ladder sits immediately below and handles exactly this condition — but only for `!res.ok`. A body failure escaped the retry logic entirely instead of halving the page the way a non-200 would.

### Fix

A truncated body is the *same signal* as a rejected request — the page is too big — so it now takes the same path: halve the page size, reset the clean-page counter, continue; at floor size, back off and retry up to three times before failing loudly.

### Worth noting

This was **not** introduced by #553. It was only reachable once the job stopped being cancelled before it got that far — which is the general hazard: **a broken instrument that never finishes hides its own defects.** The same reason the 6 h cancellations never surfaced as anything but a billing line.

Suite 72 files, all green. Throughput still to be measured on the first run that completes end to end.

author: tonylampada
body:
# Description

Dictate into the board through a Siri Shortcut and the phone stays silent for the rest of the page's life — the ▶ previews in notification settings make no sound, TTS says nothing, and only a reload brings audio back. The microphone taking the audio session leaves the `AudioContext` permanently dead in a way #96 could not reach: `resume()` resolves, `state` reads `running`, and not one sample ever comes out of it again. A context you cannot resume back to life is a corpse, so this stops asking the state field — which lies — and asks the clock, then does what the reload does and builds a new one behind the same graph.

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking)

## How has this change been tested?

- New automated tests added: the corpse verdict as a pure function over state and clock, a rebuild that has to come back with the volume and the whole graph on it, a healthy context that must survive any number of gestures untouched, and the captain's actual morning — a context that ran, then died, and a ▶ that has to sound on the first tap.
- Needs the captain's own verdict on his phone: dictate through the Shortcut, come back, press ▶ — no reload.

## Any specific deployment considerations

- None — browser-side only, no server change.

author: willkhinz
body:
## Summary

Wires up the clip merged in #7 as an ambient loop behind the hero copy.

## Encoding

The source was 3840×2160, 15s, 5.3 Mbps, with an audio track — none of which a muted background loop needs.

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Source | 9.6 MB, 4K, H.264 + AAC |
| `hero.mp4` | **724 KB** — 1280×720 H.264, no audio, faststart |
| `hero.webm` | **592 KB** — 1280×720 VP9, no audio |
| `hero-poster.webp` | 27 KB |

VP9 is listed first because at matching quality it came out *smaller* than the H.264; Safari and iOS fall through to the mp4. Worth noting a first VP9 attempt landed at 788 KB — larger than the mp4 — which would have made it the worse choice for every browser that preferred it. Re-encoded rather than shipped.

## Scrim

Tuned to this clip rather than guessed. It averages ~59/255 luma with highlights around 180, so the copy side needs roughly `.78` effective cover while the rest stays light enough for the footage to actually read. The two gradients multiply, which the values account for.

The video also runs 160px up behind the header — that header is transparent until stuck, and without the overlap the top of the video cut against the black band above it as a hard horizontal seam.

## Also

- Staging now copies `assets/video`. The asset check caught this as missing before it could ship broken, which is the guard from #4 doing its job.
- The 9.6 MB source is dropped from the working tree. It stays in history at `5366058` and in the shared Drive folder, so re-encoding later is still possible.

- [x] Autoplay confirmed at 393×852 and 1280×900 — `paused: false`, 1280×720 decoded, no console errors or failed requests
- [x] Scrim checked against live frames at both sizes; headline legible over the brightest part of the loop
- [x] Header seam confirmed gone
- [x] Staging and asset verification simulated locally — 19 refs, none missing, 2.0 MB payload
- [ ] Confirm autoplay on a real iPhone

Note: `muted` and `playsinline` are both present — iOS refuses to autoplay without them. Playwright's Chromium has no H.264 support, so verification here ran against the VP9; the mp4 path is unverified in-browser and worth a look on your device.

## Premise correction

The task names two tests in `tests/test_proposal_genesis.py`
(`TestProposalGenesisPhaseF_API::test_win_loss_records_with_data` /
`::test_win_loss_lessons_with_filter`) as failing with "rows written but endpoint returns
count 0". **Neither fails.** That file is 202/202 green in a clean worktree — which is what
the `tsr-gov-01-d1` triage already recorded (`docs/testing/tsr-gov-01-d1-triage.md`,
"Correction to the task premise": proposal_genesis has 0 failures, win_loss has 2).

The real "win/loss records and lessons" failures are the two the triage lists under **P4 —
tables missing from the conftest fixture entirely**:

```
tests/win_loss/test_win_loss_engine.py::test_engine_run_inserts_analysis_run
    sqlite3.OperationalError: no such table: win_loss_analysis_runs
tests/win_loss/test_win_loss_engine.py::test_engine_high_impact_cross_registers_to_creative_gaps
    sqlite3.OperationalError: no such table: pg_win_loss_records
```

The fixture used is `_sql_compat`-shaped already; there was no bare-`sqlite3.connect`
translation bug to fix. The defect is a schema gap.

## Root cause

`pg_win_loss_records`, `pg_win_loss_lessons`, `win_loss_analysis_runs`,
`win_loss_feature_impacts` and `creative_feature_gaps` are all declared in
`tools/db/init_icdev_db.py` (so a seeded DB has them) but none was ever added to
`MINIMAL_ICDEV_SCHEMA` in `tests/conftest.py`. That is CLAUDE.md's new-module registration
checklist item #6.

## Why all six tables, not the two the tests read

`WinLossEngine.run()` writes the analysis run, the per-feature impacts and the
cross-registered gap in **one transaction** wrapped in a bare `except: rollback()`
(`tools/win_loss/win_loss_engine.py:57-110`). One missing table rolls the whole write back
and the engine still returns `success` — so the symptom is an empty table, not an error.
Adding only `win_loss_analysis_runs` would have left the test failing for a different reason.

`pg_win_loss_lessons` is the sibling written by the same R13 reflex and is included so the
pair the task names is complete.

`creative_feature_gaps` drops `init_icdev_db.py`'s `REFERENCES creative_pain_points(id)` —
that parent table is not in the fixture, and a dangling FK would bite the first test to
enable `PRAGMA foreign_keys`.

author: mikaelporttila
body:
Closes #32.

## What was wrong

Being **stopped** by a thing and **standing** on it are one question, and `MountController` answered them separately:

| | query | includes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| horizontal step test | `blockTop` | terrain + tree boles + structures |
| vertical clamp | `getHeight` | terrain only |

So a crate stopped a mount at its wall, and then — once the mount was on top of one — dropped it straight through the lid to the dirt. Refused at the side, unsupported on top.

Measured on a 1.96-unit crate in the Encampment, hero and rider at the same column:

| | y | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| on foot | 13.96 | resting exactly on the crate |
| mounted, before | 12.91 | **a metre inside it** |
| mounted, after | 14.87 | a saddle's height above it |

## Three queries, not one

The integrator is the one the screenshots show. The other two are the reason this is a three-line change rather than a one-line one:

- **`mount()`** — mounting up while standing on something dropped the animal to the dirt underneath. Same picture, one frame.
- **`dismount()`** — the step-off placed the hero inside whatever he got off beside. His own physics shoved him out on the next slice, so it never showed. That is exactly the one that would otherwise have been left behind to resurface later.

## Deliberately not changed

**Followers and enemies** keep the same split on purpose: stopped by a settlement (a beast's head poking out of a hut wall next to you reads worse than no collision at all) but keeping their footing on `getHeight`, so they walk up terraces and through trees. The note at `BeastActor.updateGrounded` states it. The mount differs only because a player is sitting on it.

**Flyers.** `floorFor` stays terrain-plus-clearance, so a cruising mount passes over roofs rather than being shouldered up by them. Whether a flyer should collide with a gable is a design question this issue doesn't ask — say the word and it's a separate change.

## Guard

`test-structures.mjs` grows a `mounted` section — the only case in that file that is not on foot. On the parent commit:

```
a ground mount sinks through it: rider 12.91 is 1.05 below the 13.96 it should be sitting on
```

It is a **pair at one column** deliberately: the hero resting *on* the furniture is what makes the mounted number mean anything, and asserting only the mounted half would pass in a world where nothing is solid at all. `riderY` is the rider, so it sits a saddle above the surface — on the crate it is over `structureTop`, through it, under.

## Verification

- `bun run build` — clean
- `bun run verify` — HEAD typechecks on its own
- `bun tools/test-structures.mjs` — exit 0, colliders 59/38/25 unchanged (exit 1 on the parent commit)
- `bun tools/test-zfight.mjs`, `test-npc.mjs`, `test-pause.mjs`, `test-menu.mjs` — exit 0

author: jackzampolin
body:
Fixes the three verified defects from #1001. All three live in the gap between the Lean slot model (persisted running rows) and the in-memory bookkeeping the model abstracted over, so the model was extended first, then the Rust brought into conformance.

## Lean (model first)

- **`Proofs/InferenceCall/ControllerBookkeeping.lean`** — models one call's path through `BackendAdmissionController::acquire` as a phase machine with per-phase waiter / in-flight / semaphore-permit contributions.
  - `permit_implies_in_flight` + `drained_no_outstanding_permits` + `replacement_preserves_capacity`: a drained controller holds no permits — including one assigned to a parked waiter — so installing a replacement preserves the capacity bound **only** when in-flight is counted from acquisition intent.
  - `late_admission_counting_unsound`: the pre-fix counting (increment after acquisition) is rejected by the model, not merely unmentioned.
  - `persist_error_releases_waiter` / `terminal_phase_releases_bookkeeping`: every terminal admission outcome — including queued-persist failure — holds no waiter or in-flight unit (the in-memory S9 analog).
- **`Proofs/Recovery/StartupOrder.lean`** — models the parent gate of `InferenceCall::recover_all`. `inference_before_request_leaves_call_live` states defect 2 end-to-end (wrong order ⇒ a running orphan keeps its slot after startup); `request_before_inference_converges` is the ordering contract the runtime now implements. The sweep cadence deliberately stays `.startup` — a periodic inference sweep would race the permit-drop's spawned terminal persistence and is not needed once the order is right.

`lake build` clean, zero `sorry`s.

## Rust

1. **Queue-waiter leak** (`admission/controller.rs`): `QueuedCallGuard` is constructed *before* the fallible `persist_call_queued` and arms terminal-persist-on-drop only once the row is durable. A persist error now releases the waiter unit instead of permanently shrinking the queue toward `QueueFull`.
2. **Crash-orphan recovery order**: new `startup_recovery` module runs the ordered startup sweeps (tool calls → requests → inference calls), consumed by startup's `log_recovery` (tool calls stay first so the #937 restart-disposition classifier still observes crash-time parent liveness). Crash-orphaned `running` rows now terminalize on the **first** restart.
3. **`is_drained()` race** (`admission/controller.rs`): `running` is replaced by an `in_flight` counter incremented at acquisition intent and released through an RAII guard on every non-admitted exit (handed off to `AdmissionPermit` on success). A permit in the acquire→resume window — including one assigned to a parked waiter whose task hasn't run — is never invisible to reconcile's drain check. SeqCst on the closed flag + counter closes the close/check vs. count/check-closed interleaving.

## Regression tests (each watched failing before the fix)

| Defect | Test | Pre-fix failure |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `admission::tests::queued_persist_failure_releases_queue_capacity` | waiter counter left at 1; asserts the counter and that queue capacity still admits |
| 2 | `conformance::startup_recovery_order_terminalizes_crash_orphaned_calls` | orphaned call left `running` after driving the real ordered sweep over a seeded crash state |
| 3 | `admission::tests::assigned_permit_is_visible_to_drain_detection` | `is_drained()` reported true while a parked waiter (noop-waker-driven) held an assigned permit |

## Gates

- `cargo test -p gents` — all suites pass (1194 lib, 326 conformance, all e2e)
- `cargo check --workspace --all-targets` — clean, zero warnings
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check` — clean
- `lake build` — clean, zero `sorry`s

One unrelated e2e failure (`panicking_background_tool_terminalizes_and_notifies`) occurred in a run that overlapped a disk-full window on the build host; it passed 3/3 reruns and in the final full-suite run.

Closes #1001

author: sunilparajuli
body:
#Thank you for your contribution to openIMIS!
#Please complete the sections below. Anything in comments is guidance and can be deleted.

# Description

This PR resolves a critical data corruption issue that occurred when submitting FHIR Claim payloads containing attachments (e.g., PDF bills).

When a base64 attachment was sent via FHIR, the underlying parsing library converted the valueAttachment.data payload into a Python bytes object (e.g., b'JVBERi0xLjcK...'). Because this bytes object was passed directly to the Django ORM to be saved in a text field, Python automatically invoked str() on it, which saved the literal representation of the bytes object (including the b prefix and single quotes) into the database, irreversibly corrupting the base64 string.


Fixes Implemented
Updated claimConverter.py -> build_attachment_from_value() to explicitly check if valueAttachment.data is a bytes instance.
If it is, we now explicitly call .decode("utf-8") on the binary data before assigning it to the document dictionary field.
This ensures the Django ORM saves the raw, pure base64 string directly into the database without the Python b'...' artifacts.

body:
Automated draft PR opened by the Claude queue worker for Agira item #1013.

Model: Sonnet
Job: #199

---

## Zusammenfassung

`Project` heißt jetzt `Vorgang` (Model, Feld, Admin) — Bestandsdaten bleiben per Rename-Migration erhalten. `Document.extraction_method` war bereits aus #1009 vorhanden und ist unverändert im Admin sichtbar; hier nur verifiziert, nicht neu gebaut.

## Änderungen

- `Project` → `Vorgang` (`apps/documents/models.py`): Model umbenannt, `verbose_name`/`verbose_name_plural` = „Vorgang"/„Vorgänge".
- `Document.projects` → `Document.vorgaenge` (n:n), `related_name="documents"` unverändert.
- Migration `0007_rename_project_to_vorgang.py`: `RenameModel` + `AlterModelOptions` + `RenameField` — kein Drop/Neu, Bestandsdaten und bestehende Zuordnungen bleiben erhalten.
- Admin (`apps/documents/admin.py`): `ProjectAdmin` → `VorgangAdmin`, `DocumentAdmin.autocomplete_fields` zeigt jetzt `vorgaenge`.
- `apps/documents/retrieval.py`: Filter-Parameter `project` → `vorgang` im `DocumentRetrievalService` (`_filtered_documents`, `list_documents`, `search`), damit der interne Query-Service dieselbe Terminologie durchzieht wie das Model.
- Tests (`test_retrieval.py`) auf `Vorgang`/`vorgaenge` umgestellt.
- `Document.extraction_method` (Werte `text_layer`/`ocr`/`vision`, Default leer) existiert bereits seit #1009 und ist im Admin (`list_display`, `list_filter`, `readonly_fields`) sichtbar — keine Änderung nötig.

## Warum / Entscheidungen

- **Rename-Migration statt Drop/Neu-Anlage**, weil das Akzeptanzkriterium „Bestandsdaten bleiben erhalten" verlangt und `Project`/`Document.projects` bereits produktiv befüllte Tabellen/Relationen sind; Django erkennt den Rename automatisch korrekt als `RenameModel`/`RenameField`, sofern man die Frage danach bejaht — kein manuelles SQL nötig.
- **Kein neues FK-Feld `Vorgang.department` hinzugefügt**, obwohl die Aufgabenstellung eine `related_name="vorgaenge"` dafür nennt: Im aktuellen Code hat `Project`/`Vorgang` nie ein `department`-Feld besessen (auch nicht vor #994), und die Akzeptanzkriterien dieses Issues verlangen es nicht. Ein neues Pflichtfeld hier ungefragt einzuführen hätte offene Fragen (nullable? Default für Bestandsdaten? Cascade-Verhalten) aufgeworfen, die nicht Teil dieses Tickets sind — nicht spekulativ hinzugefügt, weil das ohne Vorgabe zu Migrationsentscheidungen führen würde, die besser in einem eigenen Ticket geklärt werden.
- **`extraction_method` nicht neu implementiert**, weil es bereits vollständig aus #1009 vorliegt (Feld, Choices, Migration `0005`, Admin-Sichtbarkeit) — erneutes Anlegen hätte zu einer doppelten/kollidierenden Migration geführt.
- **Retrieval-Service-Parameter mitbenannt (`project` → `vorgang`)**, nicht nur das Model, weil sonst eine interne API mit `Projekt`-Vokabular neben dem umbenannten Fachbegriff stehen geblieben wäre; keine externen Aufrufer betroffen (nur intern in `apps/documents` verwendet).
- **Keine Kategorien/Ordner/Regale eingeführt** (Design-Notiz aus der Aufgabenstellung, keine Code-Änderung): Struktur entsteht bewusst über Absender, Vorgang, n:n-Tags und semantische Suche statt über eine zusätzliche Ablagehierarchie.

- `python manage.py makemigrations --check --dry-run` → „No changes detected" (Model und Migration sind deckungsgleich).
- `python manage.py migrate documents` gegen bestehende Datenbank angewendet — Rename lief ohne Fehler durch.
- `python manage.py test apps.documents apps.ingest apps.accounts` → 76/76 grün.
- `python manage.py test` (volle Suite) → 128/128 grün.

author: thomaspryor
body:
Closes the class behind all three dead arms in the 2026-07-30 pipeline health audit (dead 11 days, 16 days and 5 months, none of which raised an alarm).

Every zero-data guard in the repo was PER-RUN. None can see a cancelled run (no guard runs), a run that dies before its guard, or a monthly cron that gets five chances in five months. The signal only exists across runs.

**What landed**
- `scripts/lib/arm-yield.js` — pure judgement over a per-arm daily yield ledger. Two rules: SILENCE (consecutive zero days, thresholded from the arm's own longest quiet gap) and COLLAPSE (still producing, at a fraction of its demonstrated peak — the orchestrator's real record has stray successes that reset any consecutive-zero counter).
- `scripts/lib/arm-registry.js` — 7 workflow arms + 11 outlet arms.
- `scripts/record-arm-yield.js` — writes `data/audit/arm-yield-ledger.jsonl` from sources that already exist, so it is backfillable and replayable. Never writes a zero for a day it could not observe.
- `scripts/check-arm-yield.js` — one digest alert per arm per incident via owner-alert-router; resolves on recovery.
- `.github/workflows/check-arm-yield.yml` — daily 12:25 UTC, listed in CRITICAL_CRONS so the detector is itself watched.
- Root cause (b): `scripts/lib/cron-stale-streak.js` + `scripts/update-cron-health-state.js` track consecutive stale DAYS (the state file recorded which crons were stale, never for how long) and escalate at 3 days to a dispatched card.

**Acceptance**
Replaying real history as of 2026-07-30 fires on all three audit arms — orchestrator collapsed to 12% of peak, sweep-we-aggregators 16d silent, scoring-audit dead beyond the ledger — plus scrape-westendtheatre, while nysr (the sparse-arm control, 8-day publishing gaps) stays healthy. 31 unit tests.

**Reviewed**
Codex adversarial + gpt-5.4-mini alert-copy review; findings verified individually, then fixed in the second commit (one finding — timezone mixing — was refuted: all 650 sampled stamps are UTC Z). Ship-check verdict recorded.

author: amnibro
body:
## Silent crash on launch — root cause and fix

Since 3.33.0 the global `uncaughtException` "keep alive" handler swallows **async bind failures**: `server.listen` has no `error` listener, so `EADDRINUSE`/`EACCES` falls through to the keep-alive, gets one line in `crash.log`, and the process lives on **with no listening socket** — no banner, no exit code, nothing on screen. Worse, `Start Haven.bat`'s netstat readiness probe is satisfied by whatever stale process still holds the port, so it prints "Haven is LIVE" while the new server is a zombie. Every retry stacks another invisible zombie. To users this presents as *Haven silently crashing on launch* (several of us hit it after upgrading; my own `crash.log` had the swallowed `EADDRINUSE` twice).

**Fix:** an `error` handler on the main listener makes bind failures fatal and self-explanatory (which port, why, what to do) before `exit 1`; all other server errors keep today's keep-alive behaviour. The HTTP→HTTPS redirect listener (`PORT+1`) gets a warn-and-continue handler so it can't feed the same silent path.

**Also: Node 24 refusal.** `Start Haven.bat` hard-blocks Node ≥24 with "Haven requires Node 18-22" — but Node 24 is the current LTS that new users install, and better-sqlite3 12.10.0 ships working prebuilds for it (verified end-to-end on 24.14: install, boot, DB ops). The bat now verifies compatibility honestly — `node -e "require('better-sqlite3')"` after `npm install` — and only warns on ≥25. `engines` widened to `>=18 <25` (lockfile version also synced from stale 3.31.2).

Repro (before → after):
```
# terminal 1                      # terminal 2
node server.js                    node server.js
# ...HAVEN is running...          # before: prints startup lines, then hangs forever, port dead
                                  # after:  ❌ Haven could not start: port 3000 is already in use — ...
                                  #         exit code 1
```

## Braid themes + Braid Layout plugin (pure opt-ins, zero core-file edits)

Ports the Braid look from the Amni-Haven mobile app onto the rails this repo already ships:

- **`themes/braid.theme.css` / `braid-light.theme.css`** — the mobile BRAID / BRAID_LIGHT palettes (mint on slate / deep green on white) with the 1.6×-rounder shape language. Unpublished by default; admins opt in per server via **Settings → Custom Themes**, like any file theme.
- **`plugins/BraidLayout.plugin.js`** — a "two edges only" simplified layout: folds the server rail (including manage/sync) into a strip atop the sidebar, gives messages the full width, and tucks header extras into a kebab menu. **Every stock feature stays reachable** — the kebab proxies search/pins/gallery/channel-code/encryption/settings and adds People, Soundboard, Status bar, and app-download entries for the chrome it hides. A separate **variable-driven shape layer** (radii/blur/focus rings, no hardcoded colors) applies the Braid format on top of *any* active theme — Matrix keeps its rain and green, Nord stays Nord, just braided. `stop()` fully restores DOM, styles, listeners, and localStorage (verified through enable→disable→re-enable). The MutationObserver is childList-only and mutates only styles/attributes, so it can't observe its own writes. All sizes are rem so the interface Zoom slider scales Braid chrome with everything else; `prefers-reduced-motion` disables the motion layer.

## Validation

- `node --check` across all 58 repo JS files; `scripts/validate-locales.js` passes
- Fresh-server boot, admin registration, theme publish + picker injection, plugin enable/disable/re-enable — all exercised in a real browser on 3.39.0
- `Start Haven.bat` chain boots on Node 24.14 (`/api/health` verified)

## What changed

- make the Private Plugin credential test reuse the same endpoint normalizer as node execution
- normalize whitespace, full webhook URLs, trailing slashes, and Plugin Setting UUIDs consistently
- reject invalid credential values before a credential-test request is sent
- clarify Private Plugin setup requirements and the separate Account API credential scope
- document that the Account API requires a developer license and is not used by current node operations

## Why

The credential test previously used a separate inline expression that only checked whether the raw value started with lowercase `http`. That could behave differently from node execution, which trims and validates URLs/UUIDs in `normalizePrivatePluginEndpoint`.

The Account API credential is registered for future operations but is not currently requested by the node, which was easy to misinterpret in the credential picker.

## Impact

Users can enter either a full Private Plugin Webhook URL or a Plugin Setting UUID and get the same normalization during credential validation and workflow execution. Existing credential field names and stored values remain compatible. No Account API operations are added or removed.

author: keisuke58
body:
## What & why

Adds `research/SEMICON_CFRTP_APPLICATION.md` — a research memo connecting this repo's process-physics (residual stress, spring-in, delamination, crystallization) to a concrete **application motivation: semiconductor manufacturing equipment**.

The thesis so far frames the material via its *aerospace* use (the Daikin CFRTP dev report). This memo develops the semiconductor angle, which is arguably the larger and more natural home for a *fluoropolymer*-matrix composite.

## Contents

- **Why fluoropolymer in semiconductor**: requirement profile (chemical resistance, cleanliness/low ion+particle elution, heat, low dielectric) — all fluoropolymer strengths — plus the one thing neat PFA lacks: **stiffness & dimensional stability**. That gap is the CFRTP raison d'être.
- **Concrete application targets**: wafer carriers/baskets, chemical piping/valves/pump housings, wet-process jigs (where neat fluoropolymer is used today and CFRTP could stiffen/replace); and Daikin's stated new uses (cleanliness applications, low-loss high-heat PCB).
- **The physics bridge** (the key section): the same residual-stress model that means *strength/fatigue* for an aircraft part means **dimensional tolerance + cleanliness** for a semiconductor part —
  - residual-stress warpage → flatness / wafer-positioning tolerance,
  - spring-in → assembly-angle tolerance (ties directly to the L-bracket deck #23),
  - delamination / microcracks → particle & elution risk (cleanliness),
  - crystallinity (cooling-rate dependent) → dimensional & chemical stability.
- **Application story** reusing existing tooling (residual-stress FE, B-5 inverse design, cohesive delamination, field-prediction GNN/DeepONet).
- **Open/needs-Daikin-data** items and public **sources**.

Every claim is tagged 🟢 fact (with source) / 🟡 inference / 🔴 needs Daikin data, so nothing reads as overclaimed.

## Notes

Docs-only change (one new Markdown file); the L-bracket content already landed in `master` via #23, so the diff here is just the memo.

author: yunidbauza
body:
Builds story 032 — the left rail's Work panel. Closes HIVE-18.

`WorkPanel` → `TicketCard` → `TicketSessionRow` / `TicketPrRow`. The same fleet the projects panel groups by repo, grouped by work item instead.

## The selector was wrong, and it was hiding a PR

`useTicketPrs()` filtered the global `prs` list by the ticket's session ids. The spec says PR state and findings come from that list **"falling back to the session's own `pr` field"** — there was no fallback, so any PR the global list had never heard of vanished.

That is not hypothetical. Fixture PR **#31** lives only on the `ecs-scaling` session; the global list does not contain it. Ticket **GRAC-2954 rendered no PR section at all** before this change. The selector now walks the ticket's sessions and resolves each PR against the global list, falling back to the session's copy.

Both halves are load-bearing and both have a fixture proving them:

- **#219** is `approved` in the global list but still `open` on the `webhooks` session — the global list wins (single source of truth).
- **#31** exists only on the session — the fallback fires.

## Worth a reviewer's eye: the selector cannot use `useShallow`

My first version did, and every render blew up with `Maximum update depth exceeded`. `useShallow` compares an array's **elements** by identity; this selector builds new objects rather than handing back store-owned ones, so no two renders ever compared equal and React looped until it bailed. It now subscribes to the three stable store slices and memoises over them, with the resolution extracted as the exported pure function `resolveTicketPrs()` — which is also what the story asked for ("tested as a pure function").

Every other selector in the store returns store-owned references, so this is the first one where the distinction bites. It is commented at the call site.

## One deliberate reading of the spec

**PR #495 (`dark-tokens`) is in the global `prs` list but does not appear on GRAC-3005.** The spec gates the section on "≥1 linked session has a PR", and the `dark-tokens` session's `pr` is `null` — so the card shows no PR. This matches the concept's own logic (`renderVals()` iterates `t.sessions` and tests `e.pr`) and the spec's wording exactly, but it does mean the PRs panel (052) will list a PR the work panel does not. Flagging it as a conscious reading rather than an oversight — say the word and I'll invert the gate.

## Verification

- `pnpm lint`, `pnpm type-check`, `pnpm build`, `pnpm verify:boundaries` (16/16) — clean.
- `pnpm test` — 272 passing (up from 242).
- `pnpm test:coverage` — 99.41% statements, 98.61% branches, 99.31% functions, 100% lines (gate 80%).
- **Driven in real Chrome at 1440×900.** All 8 cards render in fixture order; GRAC-3010 shows both `nplusone` and `e2e-quote`; dividers appear on exactly the four cards that have PRs and nowhere else; **#219 renders `approved`** and **#31 renders `merged`** — the two cases above, confirmed end to end. `⚠ 2` on #482 with `2 open findings` for screen readers. State colours computed green/brand/subtle per the shared rules. No horizontal overflow at 268px. Zero console errors.
