body:
Missing projection labels were created lazily with whatever color GitHub assigned. This gives them deliberate defaults and a config surface, and folds color into the existing drift-healing model. - Lazy label creation now carries a deliberate color: `tasks-axi:in-flight` orange `FF8C00`, `tasks-axi:blocked` red `D73A4A`, `tasks-axi:held` purple `8250DF`. - Colors are configurable next to the label names in `.tasks.toml`'s `[github]` table (`in_flight_color` / `blocked_color` / `held_color`), validated loudly as 6-digit hex; a leading `#` is accepted and stripped in both the config layer and the `GithubStore` constructor. - Color drift heals like name-projection drift: every write and `render` end with a color-heal step (one `tasks-axi:`-prefix-filtered label query, then a repaint of any managed label whose color disagrees with the configured/default value). Human unprefixed labels are never touched, and a heal failure degrades to a warning without failing the task mutation. - Reads stay one memoized GraphQL query per process; the label query runs only on the write path. - Tests cover lazy-create colors (client and store), heal on render and on any write, human-label preservation, degraded-heal warnings, and loud invalid-hex validation; the README's GitHub-backend section is updated accordingly. ## Pipeline Updates from [git push no-mistakes](https://github.com/kunchenguid/no-mistakes)
✅ **intent** - passed ✅ No issues found.
✅ **Rebase** - passed ✅ No issues found.
🔧 **Review** - 1 issue found → auto-fixed ✅ - 🚨 `src/backends/github.ts:172` - The required criterion says a leading `#` is accepted and stripped during both config and `GithubStore` constructor validation. The constructor copies option values verbatim and validates them with a regex that rejects `#`, so `labelColors: { held: "#8250DF" }` fails instead of normalizing. Strip the optional prefix before constructor validation and storage. 🔧 Fix: Normalize prefixed GitHub label colors in constructor ✅ Re-checked - no issues remain.
✅ **Test** - passed ✅ No issues found. - Inspected `git diff 4d775f0^..2391bf0` for implementation, configuration wiring, tests, and README behavior. - `pnpm exec vitest run test/backends/gh.test.ts test/backends/github.test.ts test/config.test.ts -t "label colors|lists repository labels with colors|repaints a label color|configured label color|malformed label color" --reporter=verbose` - `pnpm exec vitest run test/backends/gh.test.ts test/config.test.ts -t "creates missing projection labels and retries once|resolves defaults for the label names" --reporter=verbose` - Ran the real CLI command `tasks-axi add demo-1 "Demonstrate deliberate label colors" --start --json` against a controlled GitHub API executable. - Introduced managed-label drift and an unprefixed human label, ran `tasks-axi render --json`, and inspected persisted API calls and label state. - Simulated a REST repaint failure, ran `tasks-axi update demo-1 --title "Mutation succeeds despite color heal failure" --json`, and verified the warning, successful response, and persisted mutation. - Ran the real CLI with `blocked_color = "red"` and confirmed `VALIDATION_ERROR` with exit code 2. - Verified cleanup with `git status --short`; no worktree changes or transient build outputs remain.
✅ **Document** - passed ✅ No issues found.
✅ **Lint** - passed ✅ No issues found.

author: brunobertolini
body:
Meta on both halves: the pixel in the browser, the Conversions API on the server.

## Verification evidence

ADR-0004 gates this merge on evidence that the events arrived, not on a passing suite. Both were
produced from the **built** library loaded over HTTP in a desktop Chrome, never a headless one.

**The outgoing browser request**, for a purchase carrying a deduplication id:

```
https://www.facebook.com/tr/?id=<pixel-id>&ev=Purchase
  &cd[transaction_id]=TL-TRACK-1&cd[value]=69.9&cd[currency]=BRL
  &cd[contents]=[{"id":"SKU-1","quantity":1,"item_price":49.9},{"id":"SKU-2","quantity":2,"item_price":10}]
  &eid=TL-TRACK-1
```

**The outgoing server request**, same conversion:

```json
{"event_name":"Purchase","event_time":1785694643,"action_source":"website",
 "user_data":{"em":"8e43ca37…","ph":"a8691779…","fn":"24d4b96f…","ln":"8c26ccec…",
   "external_id":"user-42","client_ip_address":"…","client_user_agent":"…","fbp":"fb.3.…"},
 "event_id":"TL-LIVE-1","event_source_url":"…",
 "custom_data":{"value":69.9,"currency":"BRL","order_id":"TL-LIVE-1","contents":[…]}}
```

Meta answered `{"events_received":1,"messages":[],"fbtrace_id":"…"}`.

**Meta's own report.** Events Manager listed every browser event as processed (PageView,
ViewContent, AddToCart, InitiateCheckout, Purchase, and the custom one), showed the event id on
the purchase, and then attributed the purchase itself to **both** sources: integration "Várias",
event match quality 8.0/10, with the detail panel naming "da API de Conversões (servidor)" and
"para o pixel (navegador)". Meta separately warned about `fbc` coverage "por meio da API de
Conversões", which is it acknowledging the server channel unprompted.

**Hashing was checked rather than trusted.** `'ANA@Example.COM '`, padded and mixed case, produced
the SHA-256 of `ana@example.com`; the formatted phone produced the digest of its digits alone.

## What verification decided, and tests could not

**`fbq('track')`, not `fbq('trackSingle')`.** `trackSingle` addresses one pixel, which is tidier on
a page carrying two. Meta publishes no signature for it carrying the `{ eventID }` object that
deduplication depends on. The placement worked when captured live — and an undocumented shape that
works today can stop working with no error and no symptom, the failure being both halves counting
the same conversion. The browser factory therefore takes no pixel id: `track` reaches every pixel
the page initialised, so a parameter there would promise what the command cannot deliver.

**`revoke` queues, it does not drop.** Not in Meta's pages. An `AddToCart` fired while revoked sent
nothing for three seconds, then left the instant a later `grant` arrived, without being fired
again. A visitor who declines, browses and accepts later delivers the declined stretch to Meta at
the moment of acceptance. The page says so, and points at keeping Meta out of `providers` when the
policy is that a declined period must never arrive.

**One false alarm, chased down.** `PageView` appears as a custom event in Events Manager. Firing
Meta's own `fbq('track', 'PageView')` with the library out of the path produces exactly the same
label, so it is their table's wording and not our translation.

## Not in this PR

The other providers stay out. LinkedIn, PostHog, X and TikTok have no verification evidence yet,
and by the same ADR that is what keeps them from merging.

author: ruckus000
body:
Follow-up to #74, which ran the experiment this comment had been waiting for.

## What was observed

[PR #74](https://github.com/Ruckus000/SaidThat/pull/74) touched only `AGENTS.md` — the first PR since this workflow was rewritten to match neither `apps/mobile/**` nor `mobile-tests.yml`. On [run 30763145904](https://github.com/Ruckus000/SaidThat/actions/runs/30763145904):

| Observation | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `dorny/paths-filter` log | `Filter mobile = false` |
| `test` job | `status=completed`, `conclusion=skipped` |
| `test` on the checks page | appeared — did **not** hang pending |
| Run conclusion | `success` |

That is what the header paragraph predicted, and the opposite of the failure mode it warned about: a workflow skipped by a top-level `on:` path filter leaves its check pending forever, while a job skipped by `if:` reports and completes. The filter is in the right place.

## What is deliberately still marked unproven

The comment now splits the claim in two, because only one half was tested.

GitHub reports the conclusion as `skipped`, **not** literally `success` — #74 confirmed that exact wording, which the original comment had already anticipated. The docs then say a skipped *required* check is treated as passing. **That** half is still resting on documentation rather than observation: #74 showed the check reports at all, not that a required check would accept it. This repo's plan has no required checks to configure, so it remains untestable here.

Overstating it as fully verified is precisely the ambiguity the rest of this comment block exists to prevent.

## Note on ordering

This had to be a separate PR. Editing `mobile-tests.yml` inside #74 would have matched the filter, run the `test` job, and destroyed the experiment — so the observation had to land first and be recorded second. This PR does touch the workflow, so `changes` reports true again and the full mobile suite runs, as expected.

author: atillasaadat
body:
## Summary

Repo-wide sweep replacing `std::acos`-based angle computations with the well-conditioned `atan2` forms. `acos(clamp(a·b))` loses half its significant digits near 0 and π (derivative → ∞); the `atan2` forms are uniformly well-conditioned over the full range. Zero `std::acos` remains in production code (`lib/`, `sim/`, `flight/`, `tools/`).

## Conventions enforced (now a house rule)

| Quantity | Form |
|---|---|
| Angle between two vectors | `atan2(‖a×b‖, a·b)` |
| Quaternion rotation angle | `2·atan2(‖q_v‖, \|q_0\|)` |
| Colatitude from a unit vector | `atan2(hypot(x,y), z)` |
| Law-of-cosines scalar ratios | `sqrt`-based rewrite (robustness only) |

Rule documented in `lib/README.md`, `sim/CLAUDE.md`, and design doc §3.3, with the Kahan (2016) cross-product-angle citation in `docs/refs.bib`.

## Changes

- 12 call sites converted across 9 files in `lib/` and `sim/` (frame geometry, quaternion angle metrics, occlusion/keep-out cones, sun/nadir separation angles, IGRF colatitude path).
- `lib/environment/igrf.cpp`: `fieldSphericalTrig` now passes sin/cos through directly so the pole-conditioning benefit survives (no `cos→sqrt` round trip); golden outputs bit-identical.
- New `tests/unit/angle_conditioning_test.cpp` (6 tests) including an IEEE-754 conditioning demonstration: for θ ≤ 5e-9 the dot product rounds to exactly 1.0 and `acos` returns 0, while the `atan2` form recovers the angle to full precision (1e-8 case asserted by magnitude — 0.05 ulp from a libm tie).
- Test-side independent `acos` cross-checks intentionally retained as verification diversity.

## Verification

- 541 unit / 29 integration / 4 golden / 30 component-UT — all green
- Python: 126 collected — 124 passed, 2 skipped
- MC accuracy figures bit-identical pre/post sweep; SITL 4/4 including both lockstep bit-identity gates
- Docs build clean (`-E`), requirements gate passed; pre-commit clean

author: aadisaraf
body:
The same cat on Windows: same art, same tuning, same modules. Native C#/.NET 8 with a
Win32 layered window — not a wrapper around the Mac binary.

## What's shared, and why that was already true

`assets/` is loaded **verbatim** by both builds. Neither has a pixel offset or a
behaviour constant compiled into it — that was already architecture rule 1 in
`CLAUDE.md`, written down long before there was a second platform, and this is the
thing it was written down for. Retuning the cat is still a JSON diff, and it retunes
both.

The file layout mirrors `Sources/LoafCat` one-for-one (`Rig.swift` ↔ `Rig.cs`,
`Modules/*.swift` ↔ `Modules/*.cs`), so a change to a feature can be made by reading
the two files side by side. All twelve modules ported.

## Three places the platforms genuinely differ

Each because doing the same thing would have been worse.

**Click-through is free here, and better.** `spikes/RESULTS.md` records that macOS has
no per-pixel click-through — a transparent `NSWindow` takes every click regardless of
alpha, and the only thing that works is polling at 120Hz over a *dilated* mask
(97% vs 88%). A layered window is hit-tested by the window manager against the alpha
we just handed it, synchronously, before delivery. So the polling toggle is **not**
reproduced and clicks use exact alpha. The dilated mask survives as the definition of
`CursorOnCat`, which is a proximity question and wants to stay generous.

**Keystroke counts are inferred, not read.** There is no `counterForEventType`, so the
guarantee is rebuilt from two APIs that each individually cannot leak anything:
`GetLastInputInfo` (entire payload: one `DWORD` tick count) and a mouse-only hook
(payload: `MSLLHOOKSTRUCT` — cursor position, wheel delta, timestamp; no field that
could carry a keystroke). If the input tick moved and it is not the tick the mouse
fired on, a key was pressed. This is strictly **less** information than the macOS build
gets, which distinguishes key events from scroll events at the source.

**Per-monitor DPI awareness v2**, so Windows never bitmap-stretches the window — a 150%
display would otherwise resample the cat with bilinear filtering, which is exactly the
mush the art pipeline exists to prevent. The cost is that first run has to pick a
starting scale from the monitor's DPI.

## Privacy is enforced on both platforms now

`scripts/check-privacy.sh` scans `.cs` and `.ps1` and blocks `WH_KEYBOARD_LL`,
`GetAsyncKeyState`, `GetKeyState`, `GetKeyboardState`, `ToUnicode`, `MapVirtualKey`,
raw input, journal hooks, `SendInput`, `GetWindowText` and screen capture. I verified it
bites by feeding it a file that uses them, rather than trusting that it passes.

`GetAsyncKeyState` was in an earlier draft for one thing — "is the left button still
held", the safety net for a lost mouse-up. It is now read from the mouse hook instead,
so the API could be banned outright rather than by argument about its parameter.

## Verification — and what is *not* verified

**I have no Windows machine.** The macOS rule is "`./build.sh` succeeds AND the app was
launched and looked at"; the second half could not be done. Rather than quietly dropping
it, the properties a human would have been checking are asserted mechanically:

`--selftest` (gates CI, all three themes):
- the atlas loads from the same files the macOS build reads
- the hit mask is a real silhouette, not empty and not the whole canvas
- the composed frame is **opaque on the cat and alpha-0 in the margin** — literally what
  the window manager hit-tests for click-through
- **3× is byte-for-byte the 1× frame with every pixel tripled** — the pixel-art claim
  stated as an equation; any fractional transform that leaked in would break it
- 240 frames of ambient motion compose without throwing

`--demo-drag` (gates CI): the scripted grab-hold-shake-release through the same entry
points real mouse events use, failing the build if the cat has not come completely to
rest 3s after release. This is the check that the ported springs and pendulum behave
like the original rather than merely compiling.

**Still needs a person at a Windows machine** — listed in full in `windows/README.md`:
whether it *looks* right at 2×/3×, click-through in practice, the tray icon against a
light/dark/wallpapered taskbar, hooks not slowing a real Claude Code session, mixed-DPI
multi-monitor, and whether SmartScreen behaves as documented for both install routes.
The macOS quarantine asymmetry was *measured* (0 vs 183 files); the Windows equivalent
is documented behaviour I have not observed.

## Shipping

`irm https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aadisaraf/loafcat/main/install.ps1 | iex` — the
exact mirror of `install.sh`, and for the same reason: Windows attaches its mark of the
web based on *what downloaded the file*, and `Invoke-WebRequest` does not attach one.

The `.ico` comes from `tools/generate_icon.py` like everything else, **drawn** at each
Windows tray size rather than resampled (20px and 24px are the 125%/150% tray sizes and
are whole multiples of nothing we had), and it is byte-compared by `check-assets.sh` —
Pillow's ICO writer would otherwise LANCZOS-resample every frame it derives, and a
blurred tray icon is subtle enough to ship unnoticed. The generator asserts this by
reading the file back.

author: zinackes
body:
## Why

App Store reviews was the one source whose URL no domain can produce, so it waited on
the user pasting an `apps.apple.com` link — on competitors whose store badge we already
read off their homepage every day (`competitors.metadata.mobileApps`, written by
`recordMobileApps` since the mobile-apps work).

The app id we already have now provisions the monitor itself.

## What

- **Detection seeds the source.** `seedAppStoreReviews` (workers/lib/mobile-apps.ts)
  creates the `appstore_reviews` monitor with the canonical listing URL
  (`apps.apple.com/<country>/app/id<appId>`), weekly, and enqueues the first scrape.
- **New bucket `DETECTION_SEEDED_SOURCES`** in `@outrival/shared/sources/defaults`:
  same stored preference and same settings card as the blind-seedable sources, but it
  never widens `resolveSeedSources` — no detected app, no row.
- **Settings → General → Monitoring defaults** gets an "App Store reviews" row
  (checked by default, lock badge under pro). `GET/PATCH /api/settings/sources` now
  offers and stores it (`seedableSources` → `selectableSources` on the wire).

Four guards: an existing monitor is never re-created (a source turned off stays off),
never on a self-competitor (reviews aren't scraped for self), never below pro, never
when the org unticked it.

Seeding is retried on **every** capture that knows an app, not only the one that
discovered it: the gates move on their own (an upgrade, a ticked box) long after the id
was written, so competitors whose app id is already in the DB get the source on their
next homepage scrape (≤24h) and an upgrade opens it by itself. No backfill script.

## Verification

- `pnpm typecheck` — 8/8 green
- `pnpm test` — 12/12 tasks, 0 fail (2 API assertions updated, 3 new shared tests)
- No worker test: `apps/workers` has no DB harness, same as `seedDetectedSources`
  (status/changelog), which this mirrors.

📄 `docs/architecture/pipeline.md` updated (seeding section + mobile-apps step).

author: zeroliu
body:
Fixes logancyang/obsidian-copilot-preview#258

_Cross-repo `Fixes` did not register a closing reference on this PR (`closingIssuesReferences` is empty), so the issue needs a manual close on merge._

## Problem

The Agent Mode composer renders chat's placeholder verbatim — `"Your AI assistant for Obsidian • @ to add context • / for custom prompts"`, hardcoded at the `LexicalEditor` mount in `src/components/chat-components/ChatInput.tsx`. It is wrong on its face for Agent Mode, where `/` opens skills and commands, not chat's custom prompts. It also wastes the one screen where a new user is deciding what to ask an agent: Agent Home's landing rotates a greeting (`landingGreetings.ts`) but never shows a prompt worth stealing.

## Fix

An empty landing composer now types out sample prompts one at a time — type in, hold 5s, delete, next — and Tab commits the one on screen into the real input.

The design decision that carries the PR is **where the rotation lives**: it is mounted as Lexical's `placeholder` slot. Lexical renders that slot only while the editor is empty (`Placeholder` returns `null` when `useCanShowPlaceholder` is false, `@lexical/react` 0.34), which buys three requirements for free:

- The first keystroke unmounts the component, stopping the animation and clearing its pending timer — there is no editor-value subscription anywhere in this diff.
- Clearing the composer remounts it, so suggestions come back.
- IME composition hides it, because Lexical passes `isComposing` into that check.

That slot also renders *inside* `LexicalComposer`, so the same component can register `KEY_TAB_COMMAND` — which is why one component owns both the frames and the key binding instead of a plugin/renderer pair passing state between them. Holding the per-character state there confines a ~22fps re-render to that leaf rather than re-rendering `ChatInput` and its 20-plugin editor tree on every character.

Rejected: driving the rotation from `AgentChatInput` state and passing the text down as a prop. It is the obvious shape, and it re-renders the whole composer tree 22 times a second.

Tab is claimed only while a suggestion is visible and unmodified, at `COMMAND_PRIORITY_LOW` — below the typeahead menus' `HIGH` binding — so `@`/`/` selection and the Shift+Tab mode cycler are untouched, and Tab in the beat between two prompts falls through to its default. Accepting routes through the existing `INSERT_TEXT_WITH_PILLS_COMMAND` rather than `setInputMessage`: it reuses the mounted `TextInsertionPlugin`, resolves `[[note]]` links to pills, and leaves the caret at the end (`ValueSyncPlugin` rebuilds the root without setting a selection).

## Scope

`Budget gate: PASS — 11 files, +887/−225.` Read that with `-w`: **673 added, 11 removed**. The 214-line gap is one reindent — `AgentChatInput.test.tsx` had seven top-level `describe` blocks before this PR and review asked for one, so its existing groups were renamed and nested with no test-body edits (`git diff -w` on that file: +45/−6).

Of the real additions, 371 are tests. The production surface is three new files (the pure frame machine, the leaf component, the prompt pool) plus two optional pass-through props; the mechanism lives in `chat-components` and the copy in `agentMode`, so nothing generic learns about Agent Mode. The gate's own trim removed the duplicated "referentially stable" prop docs — the rule is now stated once, on the component that enforces it.

## Changes

- `utils/promptTypewriter.ts` — pure frame machine (`typing → holding → deleting → gap`) with no timers or React, so the cadence is directly testable. `delayMs` precedes the frame it is paired with, which is what puts the 5s hold on the completed prompt rather than its second-to-last character.
- `PromptSuggestionPlaceholder.tsx` — the leaf: self-scheduling `setTimeout` chain, the Tab binding, and a `⇥ Tab` hint rendered only during the hold (without it the affordance is undiscoverable). Honors `prefers-reduced-motion` by rotating whole prompts instead of animating characters — the rotation loops for as long as the landing is open, which is exactly the case that preference exists for. The animation is `aria-hidden`, but since Tab is bound from the first typed character it also renders a stable `sr-only` description ("Suggested prompt: … Press Tab to insert it.") that the composer points at with `aria-describedby` — otherwise the ordinary focus-navigation key silently inserts text a screen-reader user was never told about.
- `docs/agent-mode-and-tools.md` — the user-facing behavior: what rotates, Tab to insert (it does not send), typing to dismiss, clearing to bring it back, and the reduced-motion variant.
- `agentMode/ui/agentPromptSuggestions.ts` — 12 vault-capability prompts, deliberately free of any assumption about how a vault is organized, plus the Agent Mode-accurate static line.
- `ChatInput.tsx` / `LexicalEditor.tsx` — two optional props; the previously inline placeholder string becomes `DEFAULT_PLACEHOLDER`, so chat mode is byte-identical.
- `AgentChatInput.tsx` / `AgentHome.tsx` — pass the existing `isLanding` down and offer the pool when it is true. No emptiness check: the placeholder slot only exists while the composer is empty.

## Verification

- `npx jest src/agentMode src/components/chat-components` — 134 suites, 1750 tests, all pass. New coverage: the machine's full cycle, wrap-around, reduced-motion path and zero-length prompt; the component's per-character render, the 5s hold boundary, Tab mid-type vs. holding vs. in the gap, modifier rejection, and timer teardown on unmount; and `AgentChatInput`'s landing gate including the clear-and-resume case.
- `npx tsc --noEmit`, `npm run lint`, `npm run format` — clean.
- Manual: exercised by the author in a live vault, which is how the one behavioral bug in this PR was caught — an earlier revision latched "user has typed" and so refused to bring the suggestions back after a Tab-accepted prompt was cleared. The latch is gone (a net deletion) and the case is now a test. I have not personally watched the animation run in Obsidian; the timing constants are asserted in tests, not eyeballed.

author: franciscuo
body:
## 1. Context

`main` had no branch protection, no commit-message enforcement, and no written record of how a
release is decided. `.github/workflows/release.yml` runs on every push to `main` and ends in
`npx semantic-release`, which publishes to the public npm registry — so the commit message is the
only thing standing between a push and a version other people install.

## 2. Problem

The release decision is invisible. Unlike a changesets repo, where an absent decision is a missing
file a reviewer can see in the diff, here it is a string in a commit message that is already
written by the time anyone looks.

That has already produced a wrong release. `f9fab4b`, subject `fix(demo): add metric sparkline
cards with full history`, also changed five files under `src/` — it added `recordEvents?: boolean`
to `CadenceConfig`, the exported type `KeystrokeEvent`, and `events?: KeystrokeEvent[]` on the
result. A new public option and a new public type shipped as **1.4.1, a patch**, under a changelog
entry about the demo. Nothing errored.

## 3. Possible flows

Every path by which a change reaches npm today, and which of them this PR closes.

| Path to `main` | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Direct commit on `main`, then push | allowed | refused by `pre-commit` locally; PR required on GitHub once the org ruleset lands |
| Commit with a non-conventional subject | allowed, silently treated as non-releasing | refused by `commit-msg` |
| `feat:`/`fix:` on a diff with no `src/` change | allowed, publishes a version containing nothing | refused by `commit-msg` |
| Force-push or delete `main` | allowed | refused by ruleset `protect-main` |
| Release job pushing `chore(release):` back to `main` | allowed | still allowed — CI is exempt from the hooks, and the ruleset carries no rule that blocks it |

## 4. Solution

Three things, in order of how much they change.

**`lefthook.yml`** gains a `pre-commit` check refusing commits on `main`, and a `commit-msg` check
validating the Conventional Commit subject. The third check is the one worth having: `feat:`,
`fix:` and `perf:` are refused when nothing under `src/` is staged, because those types publish.
Both are exempt when `$CI` is set — otherwise the release job's own commit on `main` would be
refused after npm had already published.

**`.claude/`** carries three advisory agents (`cadence-core`, `browser-expert`, `api-steward`),
four commands under `/cadence`, and five skills. `releasing/SKILL.md` is the release contract and
`public-api/SKILL.md` is the export contract. `CLAUDE.md` holds the repo-level rules;
`.claude/CONTEXT.md` is the domain glossary.

**Not done here:** no library code changed, no dependency added, no CI workflow changed. The
`commit-msg` check is a shell regex rather than commitlint, so nothing new is installed.

## 5. Before vs after

| | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Commits on `main` | 29 of 42, direct | refused locally |
| Commit subject format | convention, unenforced | enforced |
| `feat:` with no `src/` change | publishes | refused |
| Force-push / delete `main` | allowed | refused |
| PR required to merge | no | pending the org ruleset, see below |
| Release contract | undocumented | `.claude/skills/releasing/SKILL.md` |
| Runtime dependencies | 0 | 0, unchanged |

## 6. Example

The check that matters, run against this branch:

```
$ git commit -m "feat: add hook config"
refusing: 'feat' publishes a version, but nothing under src/ is staged.

  staged: lefthook.yml

A release whose diff ships no library change reaches real installers
with a changelog entry describing something else. Use chore/docs/test/ci,
or stage the src/ change this message is really about.
```

And what this PR itself releases, by the same contract: `chore(claude):` and `ci:` are both
non-releasing types, so merging this runs `release.yml`, finds nothing to release, and publishes
nothing.

---

Ruleset `protect-main` is already active on `main` with `deletion` and `non_fast_forward`. The
`pull_request` requirement is not on yet: GitHub only allows a bypass actor for the GitHub Actions
app on an **org-level** ruleset, and without that bypass `@semantic-release/git` would be rejected
when it pushes `chore(release):` — after `@semantic-release/npm` has already published. It needs
`gh auth refresh -h github.com -s admin:org` before it can be created.

Five findings came out of writing this and are recorded but not fixed here: the `<3KB gzip` claim
is false (`dist/index.js` gzips to 3454 bytes), the gaussian and replay bot fixtures score above
the human classification threshold, `npm run test:coverage` fails on a missing `@vitest/coverage-v8`,
ring-buffer and event-log dwells disagree under rollover, and the held-Backspace correction defect
is pinned by a passing test.

author: rubentipparach
body:
Several rounds of work on the interface, then two on the simulation.

## The 1080p rescale and the repaint fixes

- Moved the design space from 1600x900 to 1920x1080 and rescaled the layout constants, content margins and font size with it. Texture margins deliberately did not scale: those describe art baked at 2 pixel blocks, and 1.2 times 2 is not a whole number, so scaling them would resample pixel art at 1.25 and soften every border in the skin. Content margin is layout, texture margin is art.
- Set canvas texture filtering to Nearest. It had never been set, so the project default of Linear was smearing the plates. That plus a `grit()` fleck landing inside a nine patch stretch centre is what the blurry red dot was; `grit()` now takes an avoid box derived from `MARGINS`.
- Buttons now use the button plate rather than the panel plate.
- Leaf redraw guards in `box_strip.gd`, `ssd_control.gd`, `sys_line.gd` and `subsystem_panel.gd`.
- The four planet SubViewports and the hull view render `UPDATE_ONCE` and ask for a frame when something changes, instead of re-rendering every frame forever.

## The vertical station strip

The strip was a 3 by 2 grid of wide icon and text buttons above the panel it opens; it is now a 60 pixel column of vertical stencils standing beside that panel.

- Each station gained a `mark` in `data/stations.json` (SHLD, RCTR, SENS, TRAC, MRNE, SHTL, RPR, LIFE, CRGO, LAB). `label` stays and is what the tooltip says.
- The panel beside it is 296: 360 for the column, less 60 for the strip, less the 4 between them, written into the scene rather than left to a container per CLAUDE.md 6.4.
- The icon and the mark are authored child nodes rather than the Button's own `icon` and `text`. A Button reserves horizontal room for its icon even when `vertical_icon_alignment` puts the icon above the text, so the rect a 60 pixel button clips its text to is 22 pixels, which trimmed every four letter mark to two.
- They are painted together through a new `Paint.stencil`, for the same reason `BUTTON_SLOTS` is one list.

## A skin belongs to a faction

`ui_skin` was a single key naming the build's one skin. It is now `ui_factions`, a map from faction to skin.

- The Federation flies **steel** (gunmetal chassis, cool glass) and the Kthaari fly **verdant** (oxidised bronze, green phosphor).
- Every hull in `data/ships.json` names its faction. `Session.faction()` reads it off the hull the player is flying and `main` wears that deck, so flying a captured Kthaari cruiser puts you behind a Kthaari console without a line of code knowing that is what happened.
- Both halves of a skin move together or the interface lies, so the generators emit one plate set and one theme per faction and `Palette.theme_path()` names the theme built from the same skin its roles come from.
- Rose is unassigned and therefore not built. Its note records why it is kept: its chassis face and its glass panel are the same palette entry, which loses every panel frame.

## The settings panel

A gear opens one fixed 460 by 212 panel over a dimmed screen: the debug overlay switch, and quitting. It is on the top bar and on the station strip, so it is reachable during a battle, which is what pausing to change a setting needs.

- `SelectCard` gained an authored delete button, hidden by default. Four callers, one card.
- **The corner DEBUG button is gone.** It sat on top of the skirmish screen's tonnage readout. The overlay is a CanvasLayer above every screen and it survives a screen change. F3 and the three finger touch still work.
- The switch is `BoxStrip` at a capacity of one. Clicking the lit box picks one less, which is zero, so the control the reactor allocation and the tractor bid already use is a toggle with no special casing, and the game gains no switch widget it would wear nowhere else.
- Two things a CanvasLayer breaks, both fixed rather than worked around: it is not a Control, so the theme main sets on the screen root does not reach the panel (main hands it the deck through `wear()`, and it follows a faction change); and the skin's plate has a glass centre meant for a HUD over space, which let the fitting screen show through the settings text, so the panel has an opaque backing painted from the palette.

## Saved designs belong to the shipyard

Designs were briefly in settings, which was the wrong room: a design is a shipyard object, not a preference. They now live on the fitting screen beside the hull list.

- `src/sim/design_store.gd` is deliberately the same shape as `replay_store.gd`: a directory under `user://`, a chronologically sorting filename, a listing newest first, a describe for a row. Reading a design rebuilds from the hull's defaults and overwrites slot by slot through `ShipFit.set_slot`, so an old design still loads and a since-illegal slot is refused by the fitting validator rather than by a second check. An unknown hull returns null and the row is skipped.
- Discarding is a trash button on the ship display rather than one per row, so the button always throws away the design that is actually on screen.

## CLAUDE.md section 6.5

A new binding rule: menus name things, they do not explain them. A row is a label and a control, not a paragraph about the control. Applied to the settings panel, which lost every explanatory line it had been given.

## The ship display shows the ship

- `tools/gen_wireframes.py` reads each committed hull `.obj`, finds its crease edges and writes a ribbon mesh per hull, so the wireframe is a committed model like everything else (CLAUDE.md 2). OpenGL line width above 1 is unsupported on most drivers and Godot's `.obj` importer ignores the `l` element, so a line list was never an option.
- `SsdRingControl.fit_inside` is the one place that knows how much room is inside the shield band. The shipyard's painted hull and the combat readout's wireframe both ask it rather than each keeping a copy.
- The hull integrity percentage that used to sit in the middle of the ring is gone. The same number is already printed as boxes in two other panels.

## Facings are letters

`Sectors.facing_mark` gives A at the bow, then B to F clockwise, and every screen labels a facing through it. A tactical screen is full of numbers already; shield strength, box counts, bearings, ranges and power are all numbers a captain compares, and a facing is none of those. "Shield D at 19 of 24" does not make the reader work out which of three numbers is an identifier.

## The disruptor overload

An armed disruptor reads the falloff table at half the distance and hits twice as hard. That is the same rule at a different scale rather than a second damage path: `weapon_model.gd` divides the shot's distance by the range multiplier before it looks the band up and multiplies the band's damage on the way out, so the fitting screen's projection and a live shot cannot disagree. Accuracy comes along with the compressed range rather than being a third number to tune.

- The multipliers are weapon character and live in `data/weapons.json`. What the shot costs is the same whatever is firing, so it lives in `data/tuning.json`: the whole battery, and four seconds during which the shield generators buy nothing and bank nothing. Handing that energy back afterwards would make the overload free.
- Arming is one shot, not a mode. The switch springs back when the weapon fires, so emptying the reserve twice takes two decisions.
- `fire_check` gains a `battery` reason, so an armed mount that cannot pay says why instead of quietly firing an ordinary shot.
- The order goes through `Battle.apply_command` like every other, so it is written into the battle log and a replay reproduces the heavier hit. The scripted replay battle now carries a disruptor and arms it, which is what proves that rather than asserting it.

**The control**, mocked up and approved before it was built, is one switch per weapon row in three states: dark where the mount has no overload, raised where it can be armed, lit where it is. It

author: acb-graphics
body:
…act/Reflection/Strengths structure

Same treatment as the previous seven rewrites: converts this page from its own full inline CSS copy to the shared styles.css link, and replaces the hero svg viewBox with the shared image. The three hand-built audit artifacts (button, menu-navigation, image-contrast) are kept as-is — they're genuine reconstructions, not placeholders.

Two terminology/framing issues get fixed throughout, not just once:

- "ADA AA standards" / "passed ADA's assessment" conflated a US civil-rights law (ADA) with a technical conformance level (WCAG's "AA"), which don't map 1:1 and would read as a domain-knowledge gap to anyone accessibility-literate. Replaced everywhere — headline, body copy, Outcome tiles, even the audit-source attribution labels — with accurate framing ("AA conformance level," "passed its accessibility assessment"). An editor's-note asks to confirm the specific WCAG version if it should be cited by number, since the source material didn't commit to one.
- "Flagged as non-compliant" reads as litigation/demand-letter language if that's what actually happened, which would be Carnival's legal exposure rather than portfolio material. Replaced throughout with the neutral "did not meet accessibility conformance requirements," per the flag, with an editor's-note asking to confirm the actual mechanism before publishing.

Also fixes the weak "3 audit categories" outcome tile (reads as limited scope) by swapping in the "5 user scenarios" figure the draft itself identified as more representative of the work, and drops the dead "the Carnival Cruise" link (the sentence needing it didn't carry into the rewrite). This is the first of the eight rewrites with a genuine binary, verifiable business outcome (the app failed, then passed), so the Outcome band leads with "Pass" rather than a placeholder or a fabricated number. The draft's closing "Flags" section and portfolio-sequencing note are omitted from the shipped page — the sequencing note isn't page copy.

author: yumetukushi
body:
Closes #166

`ADR-081` が採ると決めた三本柱の**一件目**の実装です。

## 根拠は一次文書

JERG-2-610C（2025年3月28日 C改訂）の用語定義:

> **検証**　客観的証拠を提示することによって、規定要求事項が満たされていることを確認すること（JERG-0-049D、ISO9000）

同標準の 6.4 検証プロセスは三つのアクティビティからなります —— 「(1) プロセス開始の準備　(2) 検証　**(3) 検証結果の管理**」。**この体系には (3) がありませんでした。**

## 実害が出ていました

2026-08-02、`plugin/scripts/_hookio.py` の実行ビットは**手元で 1036 件すべて緑、CI では落ちました**（`core.fileMode=false` により git の索引の mode が 644）。同じ試験・同じ commit・違う判定。

**「試験が通った」という主張が、どの環境の話なのかを持っていませんでした。** JERG の定義でいえば、客観的証拠の提示を伴っていないので、それは検証ではなく検証戦略でした。

## 足したこと

走行の末尾に `PROVENANCE:` の節。**実物の走行**:

```text
SUMMARY: 1054 run, 1054 passed, 0 failed, 0 error, 0 skipped
RESULT: PASS
PROVENANCE:
  python: CPython 3.12.13
  platform: Linux 6.18.33.2-microsoft-standard-WSL2
  plugin: 0.8.0
  core.fileMode: false
  commit: ba61644deeeb4e70bb80132ec5b6ed158f0f6b55
```

**`core.fileMode: false` の一行が、CI との食い違いを説明します。**

- 書式の正本は `SPEC-028` に**一箇所だけ**。lens 側は自分の `SPEC-007` が持ちます（二重定義しない）
- `TEST-028` + `test_meta.TestRunProvenance`（4件）。走者の証跡を刷る関数だけを別プロセスで呼び、全件を回さずに投影を検めます

## 制約（守ったこと）

- **保存しません。** 走らせた場のログが持ちます（導出値を保存しない。ADR-055）
- **統治対象の内容を刷りません** —— パス・作業ディレクトリ・統治木の名前（ADR-074 の許可制と同じ形）。**試験でそれを凍らせました**
- 取得の失敗で走行を落としません。`git` を `PATH` から外した走行で、終了符号 0 と該当項目の未取得を確かめています

## 却下したもの

| 案 | 却下の理由 |
|---|---|
| 判定を成果物として保存する | 第二の正本ができ、実体とのずれという欠陥面を作る。機密も入りうる |
| 環境の差を潰す（`core.fileMode` を強制） | 次に判定を変える性質で同じ驚きが起きる。**差を消すのではなく読めるようにする** |
| 監査に「証跡の無い判定」を検出させる | **監査は試験の走行を見ていない。** 見ていないものを見ていると書かないので、この受入条件は #166 から外し、保証限界に落とした |

## 残る限界（明記しました）

author: guillaume-osmo
body:
Fixes #302. Sending the diff since you said it should be simple — take it or reimplement it, whichever is less work.

An alkane stem followed by a lactone, lactam or sultone closes the ring onto the acid carbon, so that carbon is position 1 and the greek letters begin at 2, exactly as they do for a terminal suffix such as `-oic acid`. The greek locant assignment tested only for `TERMINAL_SUBTYPE_VAL`, so cycleformers fell to the `[locantNumber - 1]` branch and every greek locant came out one place too low.

```
gamma-decanolactone   C1(CC(CCCCCCC)O1)=O     four membered   before
gamma-decanolactone   C1(CCC(CCCCCC)O1)=O     five membered   after
```

PubChem gives gamma-Decalactone (CID 12813, CAS 706-14-9) as `IFYYFLINQYPWGJ-UHFFFAOYSA-N` and delta-Decalactone (CID 12810) as `GHBSPIPJMLAMEP-UHFFFAOYSA-N`; both now match. Before this, `delta-decanolactone` returned gamma-decalactone's structure, so the two names were shifted into each other rather than merely being wrong.

The change accepts `CYCLEFORMER_SUBTYPE_VAL` alongside `TERMINAL_SUBTYPE_VAL`. That group is `carbolactone, dicarboximide, lactam, lactim, lactone, olide, sultam, sultim, sultine, sultone` plus the imides, all of which attach at the same carbon.

### Verification

`mvn test` green: 682 core, 1057 integration, plus 8 new cases in `greekLactones.txt` covering gamma/delta/epsilon on both constructed and retained forms, and one lactam so the change is not silently lactone-only.

Scored against PubChem's own InChIKeys over the 142 greek-lettered lactone synonyms in `CID-Synonym-filtered.gz`:

| | correct | silently wrong | rejected |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2.9.0 | 47 | 30 | 65 |
| this | 61 | 16 | 65 |

Nothing newly fails and the rejected count does not move. The 16 that remain are the ones I broke down in the issue — four are PubChem synonyms that are themselves shifted, four are #282, four are names that never state where the double bond is, and four I did not chase.

Output over 500,000 PubChem IUPAC names is byte-identical to 2.9.0, which is expected rather than reassuring: Lexichem writes these as oxolan-2-ones and never uses the greek form, so a corpus of computed IUPAC names cannot exercise this at all. The whole defect lives in the synonym namespace.

Note the industry spelling without the linking `no` — `gamma-decalactone`, `delta-dodecalactone` — is still rejected outright. That is a separate gap and not addressed here.

Route-planner work bundling four related changes, plus the `v1.6.1` changelog.

### What's new
- **Turbo playback speed** — a fourth autoplay speed (`400ms`) alongside Slow / Normal / Fast, for a quick run-through of the sequence.

author: claudecollab7-alt
body:
## ⚠️ Required manual step before merging — apply this SQL migration first (Issue 5)

`dismissed_duplicates` is a new table this PR's code depends on for cross-device dismissal sync. Applying the code without the migration means every dismissal upsert queues and retries harmlessly (same graceful-degradation pattern the `accounts` table used before it existed), so it's not a hard blocker to functionality — but cross-device sync won't work until this is applied.

```sql
-- STEP 0 (read-only, run first): confirm the table does not already exist.
select table_name from information_schema.tables
where table_schema = 'public' and table_name = 'dismissed_duplicates';
-- Expected: 0 rows back.

-- STEP 1: create the table. No `id` column - (user_id, group_key) IS the primary key.
create table public.dismissed_duplicates (
  user_id uuid not null references auth.users(id) on delete cascade,
  group_key text not null,
  created_at timestamptz not null default now(),
  primary key (user_id, group_key)
);

-- STEP 2: enable RLS with the same auth.uid() = user_id shape every other table uses.
alter table public.dismissed_duplicates enable row level security;

create policy "dismissed_duplicates_select_own" on public.dismissed_duplicates
  for select using (auth.uid() = user_id);
create policy "dismissed_duplicates_insert_own" on public.dismissed_duplicates
  for insert with check (auth.uid() = user_id);
create policy "dismissed_duplicates_delete_own" on public.dismissed_duplicates
  for delete using (auth.uid() = user_id);

-- STEP 3 (the step this project has gotten wrong once before - the 42501 "accounts" outage
-- was a missing GRANT, not a missing policy): RLS alone is not sufficient without this.
grant select, insert, delete on public.dismissed_duplicates to authenticated;

-- STEP 4 (verify):
select relrowsecurity from pg_class where relname = 'dismissed_duplicates'; -- expect true
select policyname, cmd, qual, with_check from pg_policies where tablename = 'dismissed_duplicates'; -- expect 3 rows
select grantee, privilege_type from information_schema.role_table_grants where table_name = 'dismissed_duplicates'; -- expect authenticated: SELECT, INSERT, DELETE
```

## Summary

Root-caused and fixed a real production bug (screenshot: mobile showing 5 wallets including a phantom duplicate "Cash", Supabase table editor showing 4 correct rows) plus 4 related hardening issues raised alongside it.

### Issue 1 — accounts id-collision root cause (confirmed, fixed)
- `accountsReconciledOnce` used to be a single flag reset to `'false'` on every logout — deliberately, per PR #39, so a second user on the same device got their own first-contact reconciliation. But logout's `hardClearAllLocalDataNoSync()` also unconditionally reseeds local `accounts` to `defaultAccounts()`, so the **same returning account** re-ran the name-based reconciliation merge on every relogin, against fresh default wallets. Since the merge matched by **name only**, a locally re-seeded default (`{id:'acc_cash', name:'Cash'}`) never name-matched a cloud row that had been renamed (`{id:'acc_cash', name:'Cash in hand'}`) — so both survived into the merged array sharing one id. Postgres then rejects the whole upsert batch as a cardinality violation (`21000`, "ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE command cannot affect row a second time").
- To be precise about the user's framing: the rename does technically survive (the correctly-renamed cloud row stays in the merged array) — but it's accompanied by a spurious phantom duplicate under the old default name, which is the actual bug shape reported.
- Fixed both root causes:
  - `reconcileAccountsOnFirstContact()` now matches by **ID first** — a local record whose id already exists in the cloud is dropped outright (cloud wins), never merged in under it. Falls back to name-matching only for a local record with no id match at all (two genuinely different devices that each created a same-named wallet before ever syncing).
  - `accountsReconciledOnce` is now scoped **per user id** (same pattern as `duplicateDismissals`), not reset on logout at all. A genuinely different user on the same device still gets their own first-contact reconciliation (the original intent), but the same account relogging in never re-triggers it.
- Existing installs' legacy flat `'true'`/`'false'` flag gets treated as unset once (shape guard), causing one harmless extra reconciliation pass per account after this ships — safe now that the merge is id-first.

### Issue 2 — defensive dedupe before every upsert, all tables
- `dedupeRowsById()` runs immediately before every upsert in `runOp()`, for every synced table, so a duplicate key can never reach Postgres regardless of which local bug produced it. Any collision found is logged to the diagnostic store (table, which ids collided, which was kept).
- Two distinct *legitimate* records can never collide here: every id in this app is either a uuid or (post PR #49's composite-key fix) unique per user, and `dismissed_duplicates`' key (`group_key`) is unique per user by construction — a collision can only ever mean the same record made it into the array twice.

### Issue 3 — auto-repair for already-corrupted devices
- `dedupeAccountsById()` runs on every launch (inside `loadData()`, before a user is even attached), detects local `accounts` sharing an id, and merges each colliding group down to one record.
- Picks the winner via `pickAccountDedupeWinner()`: whichever name does **not** match `defaultAccounts()`'s literal hardcoded name for that id wins, since that's the reliable signal for "this is the user's real customization" vs. "this is a stray reseeded default."
- Reassigns any transaction referencing the losing record's name over to the winner's name first — exactly the same operation `handleRenameAccount()` already does — so a merge can never orphan a transaction (confirmed via test: a transaction logged against the phantom "Cash" wallet ends up correctly reassigned to "Cash in hand", not orphaned).
- Purges any stale queued `accounts` upsert built before the repair ran (same reasoning as the existing legacy-id-remap migration), then re-pushes the corrected state once a user is attached in `startAppForUserImpl`.

### Issue 4 — Integrity Check's blind spot for constraint errors
- Previously only RLS (`42501`) and FK (`23503`) violations were pulled out of the pending-write queue into the `permanentlyRejectedRecords` store that Integrity Check reads from — any other error (including `21000`) fell through to `throw error`, which got silently re-queued forever, invisible to both Integrity Check and the user.
- Generalized the rule: **any error Postgrest actually returns a response for** (as opposed to a thrown network exception) is permanent in the same sense — retrying an unchanged payload against an unchanged schema can only ever repeat the same rejection. A genuine connectivity failure never reaches this line at all; it throws before there's a `{error}` response to destructure, which is what the pending-write queue (now reserved purely for that case) already exists to handle.
- Answering the round's specific questions:
  - **Which codes are "permanent" vs "transient", and why**: no longer a hardcoded code list — permanent means "the server responded" (any resolved `{error}`), transient means "the request never got a response" (a thrown exception, e.g. offline/DNS/dropped connection). 42501/23503 keep their own explanatory copy in `reasonFor()` since they're common/named cases; everything else (21000 included) gets a generic "Server rejected this — retried automatically."
  - **Do Integrity Check and the logout warning share a source of truth?** Not literally the same store (by design — one is "still worth retrying," the other is "permanently isolated per-record"), but after this fix a server-rejected write no longer lingers in the pending-queue the logout warning reads, so the two no longer disagree about the same fact the way they did in the bug report.

author: slenz
body:
## Summary
This PR adds tabbed folder browsing to UltraFiler and introduces configurable video preview behavior to UltraCanvasMediaViewer. The preview pane now intelligently shows/hides based on selection, and the media viewer supports three video preview modes (autoplay, muted clip, or still frame).

## Key Changes

### UltraFiler App (v1.0.0 → v1.1.0)
- **Tabbed browsing:** Added `UltraCanvasTabbedContainer` to the center pane, with each tab hosting its own `UltraCanvasFilerWidget`. Tabs are closable (except the last), reorderable by dragging, and each maintains independent folder history and view settings.
- **Tab management:** New `FilerTabState` struct encapsulates per-tab state (filer widget, page container, navigation history). Added `AddNewTab()`, `HandleTabSwitched()`, and helper methods (`ActiveTabState()`, `IsActiveTab()`, `TabIndexOf()`).
- **New Tab button:** "+" button on the left of the navigation toolbar opens additional tabs showing the current folder.
- **Smart preview pane:** The preview pane now only appears when a previewable file is selected and the preview feature is enabled, giving the folder display the full width otherwise. Replaced `SetPreviewVisible()` with `SetPreviewEnabled()` and `UpdatePreviewPane()`.
- **Video preview mode dropdown:** New command bar control to select video preview behavior (Autoplay, 5s muted clip, or still frame).
- **Per-tab history:** Back/Forward navigation is now per-tab instead of global; each tab maintains its own history stack.

### UltraCanvasMediaViewer
- **Video preview modes:** New `VideoPreviewMode` enum with three options:
  - `Autoplay`: Full playback with sound (default, previous behavior)
  - `PreviewClip`: First few seconds muted, then paused (album hover-preview style)
  - `Still`: Prerolled first frame, paused
- **API additions:** `SetVideoPreviewMode()`, `GetVideoPreviewMode()`, `SetVideoPreviewClipSeconds()` (default 5s), and `StopPlayback()` to halt video/audio and pending clip timers.
- **Clip timer management:** New `StopVideoClipTimer()` and `ApplyVideoPreviewToCurrent()` handle the muted clip playback and auto-pause.
- **Immediate mode switching:** Changing the preview mode applies to a currently shown video without reloading.

### UltraCanvasSupportedFormats
- **New API:** `CanImagePipelineLoad(extension)` determines whether the raster/SVG image pipeline (libvips + built-in SVG renderer, including ImageMagick fallback) can decode a given file extension. Distinguishes between plugin-provided formats (CDR, XAR) and formats the image pipeline actually handles.
- **Refactored bitmap candidates:** Extracted `BitmapCandidates()` as a shared helper used by both format inventory and the new `CanImagePipelineLoad()`.

### UltraCanvasFilerWidget
- **Gated thumbnail decoding:** Thumbnail generation and delete-confirmation previews now use `CanImagePipelineLoad()` to avoid feeding unsupported vector formats (e.g., `.xar`, `.cdr`) to the libvips loader, eliminating spurious "not a known file format" warnings.

## Implementation Details
- Tab state is stored in a `std::vector<std::unique_ptr<FilerTabState>>` that mirrors the tabbed container's tab order, ensuring tab indexes remain consistent.
- The `filer` member pointer always references the active tab's filer widget, allowing existing navigation and command bar logic to work transparently.
- Preview pane attachment/detachment is now driven by `UpdatePreviewPane()`, which checks both the preview-enabled flag and whether a previewable file is selected.
- Video preview mode changes are applied immediately to a visible video player via `ApplyVideoPreviewToCurrent()`, providing instant visual feedback.

body:
🔗 **View agent run:** https://app.netlify.com/projects/delifekitchen/agent-runs/6a6f8ea2f207a936202184c3

🤖 **Agent:** Codex

💬 **Prompt:** The admin dashboard is showing all orders as Pending Payment.

Stripe payments are succeeding, but no Stripe webhooks are configured.

Please audit the Stripe integration and implement the missing webhook configuration.

Requirements:
- Create a Stri...

✅ **Result:** The Stripe payment flow was audited and the webhook handling was completed so successful payments update the existing Netlify Database order record instead of leaving it in “Pending Payment.” The signed webhook now handles `checkout.session.completed`, delayed Checkout success through `checkout.session.async_payment_succeeded`, and `payment_intent.succeeded` as a fallback. It matches orders using the order reference metadata and the stored Stripe session or PaymentIntent identifiers, validates the amount and currency, sets `orders.status` to `paid`, and records `paidAt` without overwriting the original payment time on retries.

Reporting required no separate write path because the existing sales report reads paid orders from `paidAt`; webhook updates therefore refresh order counts, revenue, fulfilment totals, and daily metrics automatically. Notification email delivery was moved out of the payment acknowledgement path so missing or temporarily failing email configuration no longer prevents Stripe from receiving a successful webhook response. The already-applied orders migration was left unchanged because it already contained every required field.

The production webhook URL to register in Stripe is:

`https://delifekitchen.com/api/stripe-webhook`

The required Netlify environment variable is `STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET`. Its value must be the endpoint signing secret shown by Stripe for that specific event destination, beginning with `whsec_`. It is not the Stripe API secret key and should not be committed to the repository.

In Stripe Dashboard, the endpoint should be configured from Workbench → Webhooks → Create destination. Select events on the account, select the account’s current API version, add `checkout.session.completed`, `checkout.session.async_payment_succeeded`, and `payment_intent.succeeded`, choose Webhook endpoint, enter `https://delifekitchen.com/api/stripe-webhook`, and create the destination. Open the new destination, reveal its signing secret, and store it as `STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET` in Netlify under Site configuration → Environment variables with the appropriate deploy context. After the updated site deploys, Stripe’s Event deliveries view should show HTTP `200` responses.

Test and live mode use different endpoint signing secrets even when the URL is otherwise identical. Sandbox testing should use a non-production Netlify deploy URL ending in `/api/stripe-webhook` and set that deploy context’s `STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET` to the sandbox destination secret. Production should use the live Stripe destination at `https://delifekitchen.com/api/stripe-webhook` and the live destination secret in Netlify’s Production context. The Stripe CLI listener secret is only for CLI-forwarded local tests and must not replace the Dashboard destination secret in production.

Existing successful orders are not retroactively changed merely by creating the destination. For recent payments, the corresponding successful event should be opened in Stripe and resent to the new destination after deployment. Stripe Dashboard supports manual resend for events created within 15 days; older records require a controlled reconciliation using Stripe data rather than changing order statuses without payment verification.

Focused tests were added for raw-body signature verification, Checkout Session mapping, PaymentIntent fallback mapping, and idempotent paid timestamps. All 11 project tests passed, and syntax checks passed for the modified webhook files.

author: isaacromayvida
body:
Closes #389. Implements ADR-002's remaining half: the fee rate becomes admin-editable without ever reintroducing the drift that caused P0-2.

## What changes

- `config/loanConfig.ts` — `getLoanConfigValues()` becomes async and reads `config/loan`. Three outcomes only: document absent → compile-time seed (0.3); present and valid → stored rate; anything else (read threw, malformed, out of bounds) → **throws**. There is deliberately no branch that returns a default, because silently substituting 30% would print a rate on a CONDUSEF-regulated contract that no admin approved.
- `config/loanConfigAdmin.ts` — `proposeLoanConfigChange` / `approveLoanConfigChange`. Two-person rule enforced on `uid`; TTL, single-use, and bounds are all re-checked *inside* the transaction, since each is a race otherwise. Both callables write append-only audit records in the same transaction as the change.
- Bounds (`MIN/MAX_ALLOWED_FEE_RATE` = 0 / 0.35) are compile-time constants with no Firestore representation — no API and no admin can widen them. A fat-fingered `3.0` is impossible, not merely unlikely.
- `index.ts` — `requestLoan` prices from the live read and persists `feeRate` **on the loan**, so a later config change can never reprice an already-signed loan.
- `firestore.rules` — explicit `match /config/{document=**} { allow read, write: if false; }`. The catch-all gives the same answer today; this is the document that prices every loan, so the deny is spelled out.

## Behaviour on deploy

No borrower-visible change. `config/loan` does not exist in production, so the read returns the seed — the same 30% in force today.

## Verification (run on this branch, not reported by a builder)

- `npm test` → **20/20 suites, 358/358 tests**, up from 349 with 9 failing.
- `npx tsc --noEmit` clean; `eslint --max-warnings 0` clean.
- The P0-2 source-grep guardrail was **strengthened, not relaxed**: it now asserts the fee is derived from the single async seam *and* persisted from the same value, and keeps the original `amount * 0.\d+` literal check. The regression test now drives the real config seam rather than mocking the module export.

## Reviewed and explicitly rejected

`super_admin` is **not** added to `adminClaims.ts`'s settable role enum. Doing so would let any `admin` self-promote and unilaterally reprice the book; the callables gate on `['admin','super_admin']` instead, with the reasoning recorded in-file.

## Known pre-existing issue, not introduced here

`authMiddleware.ts:79` lets any legacy `admin: true` token satisfy any admin gate. It already gates `setAdminClaim`, so this PR does not widen the blast radius, and the two-person uid rule still holds. Tracking separately.

author: devswha
body:
Fixes three related defects in the Claude ask path found by the post-v1.7.0 review (HIGH #2/#3/#4). Ordered so the gate only opens after the correctness fix.

## 1. Multi-question asks no longer produce a chat card (#4)
`findPendingRelayAsk` collapsed multiple questions into a single max-choice number, losing which question the TUI is currently showing. A displayed "Q1" card could deliver its answer to Q2 after the TUI advanced. It now returns `null` unless the ask carries exactly one question; multi-question asks fall back to the screen-derived interactive prompt, which always shows the active question.

## 2. Claude enabled in both transcript-ask gates (#2)
The v1.7.0 Claude transcript-choice implementation (parsing + key dispatch in `tmux-ask-selection.service.ts`) was unreachable: `loadPendingTmuxAsk` (server) and the `pendingRelayAsk` memo (client) both rejected `claude`. Both gates now include it.

The server intentionally rejects Claude multi-select toggling (`TMUX_INTERACTIVE_CHOICE_UNSUPPORTED`) until the real key sequence is verified, but the composer still accepted comma-separated numbers — every submission round-tripped into a 400. author: santiago1397
body:
The capture answered it. **`manage/<token>?action=display` keeps serving after a posting ends, and it is the whole ad.**

On the first one opened, `#postingbody` held **14,138 characters** — on a post whose public URL and edit form were both long gone.

So the copy is recoverable after all.

## What it does

`cl scan-ended` now opens each ended posting through its read-only `display` control and reads the title, body, picture list and numeric post id — reporting them as a `post_content` event. That's the same path hydration uses, which already writes the copy onto the posting and refuses an older read over a newer one.

## Selectors are observed, not guessed

| | |
|---|---|
| `#titletextonly` | title |
| `#postingbody` | body |
| `p.postinginfo` | `post id: 7944787606` |
| `img[src*='images.craigslist.org']` | the ad's photos |

That last one is scoped to the image host deliberately — the page also carries OpenStreetMap tiles from `map*.craigslist.org`, and counting those would file **map fragments as the ad's photographs**. Gallery URLs are requested at `_1200x900` rather than the `600x450` the page renders.

## Recovered postings are read-only

They arrive with `editable = false` and the dashboard now honours it. Otherwise the Edit button lit up the moment the copy landed, on an ad Craigslist will never offer a form for, and every attempt would have parked as `gone`.

`--limit` throttles how many are opened per account — each is a page load against an aged account.

32/32 pass, selectors pinned in `test_edit_guards`. Frontend typechecks and builds.

author: pjfo
body:
Polymorph previously rejected any mobject whose points live in submobjects, which ruled out Text, Tex, VGroups, and SVG imports. Since polymorph aligns arbitrary numbers of subpaths natively, flatten each keyframe's family into one multi-subpath path instead:

- collect subpaths per family member in draw order, so boundaries stay exact even when one member's path ends where the next begins
- collapse the animated mobject to a single flat VMobject during the morph, styled after its first drawn family member; style crossfade interpolates between those representative members rather than the (styleless) parents
- restore the target's full submobject structure on finish with snap_to_target, so Text/Tex targets end as real glyphs

Flattened text exposes how subpath-count mismatches are filled: with polymorph's origin-point padding, four letters of a five-letter word grow from nothing while only one morphs from the source shape. Add a fill_mode option to control this. The new default, share, clones the smaller keyframe's subpaths (cycling largest-perimeter first) so every subpath morphs from and to real geometry — one shape splits into every glyph of a word, and every glyph merges back into one shape. The previous behavior remains as fill_mode=grow, used explicitly by the demo's origin-growth showcase.

Per-submobject styling collapses to one style mid-morph; documented in the README limitations.

author: ofekuna10
body:
Follow-up to #1. Corrects URLs that were guessed wrong and adds the resilience needed for a first live run to be *diagnosable* rather than silently empty.

## Wrong URLs, now corrected

Bazaraki puts the neighbourhood in the path under its own slugs. The originals were guesses and would have 404'd:

| Area | Was (guessed) | Now (verified) |
|---|---|---|
| Mackenzie | `?q=Mackenzie` | `/apartments-flats/larnaka-makenzy/` |
| Finikoudes | `?q=Finikoudes` | `/apartments-flats/larnaka-finikoudes/` |
| Livadia | `?q=Livadia` | `/apartments-flats/livadia-larnakas/` |
| District | `district-larnaca` | `larnaka-district-larnaca` |

The crawl also sweeps the adjacent central quarters (Chrysopolitissa, Harbor, Skala) and lets the geo stage decide what falls inside the 10-minute ring. Scala's district fallback is corrected to `/property-for-sale/larnaca/`.

## Resilience

- **Automatic card detection** — when a portal's declared CSS selectors match nothing, the card element is inferred: find the nodes holding a price, walk up to the nearest ancestor that also owns a link, keep the largest group sharing a tag/class signature. A redesign now costs a warning instead of a dead scraper. Tested against markup with class names the scraper has never seen.
- **`--diagnose`** — one page per portal, reporting what parsed, which extraction layer worked, missing fields on a sample, and the specific next step. It distinguishes *blocked* (rerun with `--engine browser`) from *unreachable* (connectivity) from *loaded but nothing matched* (selectors drifted). Every normal run now ends with the same status table, so a dead portal is visible rather than counted as "no results".
- **`--enrich-details N`** — fetches advert pages for listings whose covered area is missing, recovering size, coordinates and build year. Those listings were previously dropped outright, since no size means no €/m².
- **Browser engine hardening** — realistic viewport/locale/timezone, `AutomationControlled` disabled, cookie-banner dismissal, auto-scroll for lazy loading, `networkidle` wait.
- **Two new portals** — `zyprus` and `offer.com.cy`, both with verified URL patterns.

## Bug found by the new tests

On whole-card text, `"Nice 2-bedroom flat € 210.000 85 m²"` parsed as **2** — the regex took the first digit run. A first tightening then merged price and size into `21000085`. Prices now anchor to the currency marker with a strict number grammar (`210.000`, `185 000`, `185,000.50`), and a bare number surrounded by prose needs four digits to count as a price. This would have silently poisoned every benchmark on live data.

## Testing

`python -m pytest tests -q` → **76 passed** (was 58). New coverage: auto card detection on unknown markup, JSON-LD completeness, coordinate extraction from four map/JSON shapes with a Cyprus bounding-box check, URL construction and area-hint round-tripping for all eight portals, and the price-parsing regressions above.

Still not verified against the live sites — this environment's egress policy blocks all of them (403 at CONNECT), which `--diagnose` now correctly reports as *unreachable* rather than blaming the selectors.

author: akarsh-hegde
body:
## Summary

While confirming PR #658 (`pre-main → main`) was ready to merge, CodeRabbit's latest review pass on it surfaced 4 genuinely new, unaddressed findings — on code that landed via other recent PRs (#659 `feat/db-repair-from-tray`, #662 `fix/provider-health-runtime-signal`), not the corruption-recovery work #661 already fixed. This PR closes those.

(Separately: that same review round also re-flagged 7 items as "raised previously and remains unaddressed" — those are stale. The review ran at 18:57 UTC, 8 minutes before #661 actually merged at 19:05 UTC. I verified all 7 directly against current `pre-main` and they're already fixed.)

### Fixed

- **`tray/src-tauri/src/lib.rs`**: the repair-outcome notice block ran *before* `app.manage(db_pool)`, contradicting the comment's claim that it runs after specifically so a failure there "must never be able to cost them the pool itself." Reordered so `app.manage` happens first; the notice block now reads `capture_pool` (already cloned) instead of the `db_pool` that gets moved into `app.manage`.
- **`src/db/repair/rebuild.rs`**: `ensure_checkpointed` collapsed every `stat` error on the `-wal` sidecar into "0 bytes held" via `unwrap_or(0)` — so a permissions problem or other I/O error would masquerade as a clean checkpoint on the one check standing between a corrupt swap and a sound one. Now only a `NotFound` error means "no WAL"; anything else fails loud with context.
- **`src/llm/runtime_health.rs`**: `record_success()` read and parsed the whole runtime-health JSON file from disk on *every* successful LLM call — the common, healthy-provider path — even though the read is only needed to catch a stale on-disk failure when the in-memory streak is already clean. Short-circuited so the disk read only happens when it can actually change the outcome; behaviorally identical, just skips the wasted I/O on the hot path.
- **`src/llm/runtime_health.rs`**: `most_recent_outcome()`'s `(None, None)` arm only ever fell back to the test result's outcome, so a runtime observation with an unparseable timestamp and *no* competing test silently returned `None` instead of the observation's own outcome. Added the missing fallback, plus a regression test (`an_unparseable_runtime_timestamp_falls_back_to_the_runtime_outcome`).

author: adamforrester
body:
Closes the **part A** half of #388 — the live defect. Part B (Styles/Foundations restructure, the Foundations → Primitives rename, specimen refresh, caption leading band) is unblocked now that #385 is on `main`, and follows separately.

## The defect

#384 locked the leading/tracking ladders in the engine. The dashboard was never told — the Foundations fields kept `min="0.8" max="3" step="0.05"` from when any value was legal:

```
line-height  compact = 1.30   arrow-key up   →  1.35   (the deliberate 1.30→1.40 gap)
engine       throws "not a step on the ladder"
rebuild()    catches, keeps the last-good theme
user         sees the field still showing 1.35
```

The value was rejected and the UI said nothing.

## Two defects met here, so both are fixed

**The control was the wrong verb.** A locked ladder means *bind to an existing step*, not *type a number*. The fields are now selects over `LINE_HEIGHT_LADDER` / `LETTER_SPACING_LADDER`, so an off-ladder value is unreachable rather than caught. Steps that would **cross a neighboring rung** render `disabled` with a title rather than being omitted — the ramp order is a real constraint, and showing it grayed teaches it, where hiding it would make the ladder look shorter than it is.

**The error surface was per-page.** It was rendered only inside `renderPrimitives`' paint closure, so an engine throw from *any other page* set `lastError` and displayed nothing. That shape is the bug: the next page added would have forgotten it too. The bar is now mounted once in the chrome and refreshed by `syncErrorBar()` on every apply.

## The trap this left, and how it was caught

Mounting in the chrome is not sufficient on its own — `build()` re-runs on every page-nav click and mints a fresh host. The first version hardcoded `globalErrHost.style.display = 'none'` there, which meant **the bar vanished the moment the user changed page** — reintroducing the exact hole it exists to close, one layer down. Verified in-browser: with a live error, nav to Layout showed `h=0`. `build()` now calls `syncErrorBar()` instead, so visibility is always *derived*, never asserted.

**A second silent-inertness, same PR.** The `.errbar-global` rule was written full-bleed (`border-radius:0`, no side borders) and placed **above** `.errbar` at equal specificity, so every declaration lost the source-order tiebreak and did nothing. Rendered, the plain `.errbar` card matches the mode bar it sits under, so the fix was to **delete the override, not reorder it** — the class stays as a marker with no rules. Confirmed by reading computed style, not source: `radius 7px / border-left 1px / margin-bottom 16px`, all inherited.

Also worth flagging: **#366's trap fired again** while writing that comment — backticks around `.errbar-global` terminated the stylesheet template literal, and `tsc` reported it as `Property 'errbar' does not exist` at a line ~300 below the edit. The comment now says so inline.

## Verification

End-to-end in a real browser against the **built** bundle, driving the actual controls rather than guessing at selectors. Two earlier attempts to force an engine throw failed silently because they never reached one — which reads identically to "the bar is broken". **The reliable route is Typography → Styles → shape `Compact` + the `titleFloor 16` toggle**: the shape cards trial-build and self-disable when they would clash, but the toggle does not, so it is the one control that can still drive the engine into a throw. Noting it here so whoever re-verifies this does not lose the same time.

| check | result |
|---|---|
| ladder selects on Foundations | 12 selects, **0** leftover number fields |
| enabled ranges | bounded by neighbors — `tight` → 1.00–1.15, `snug` → 1.05–1.25 |
| persistence | picked step round-trips through `localStorage` across a reload |
| bar with a live error | visible `h=62` on **all eight** pages |
| bar after undo | cleared, and still cleared after nav |
| page errors | 0 |

Gates: `regen` · `regen --check` (88 artifacts byte-match) · `test.ts` (1243 passed) · NB regression · `tsc -p web` · build · `lint-us-english` (91 files clean) — all green.

author: spencersmithsite
body:
The AI-backend banners paint themselves with the `*Container` colour roles, and every palette in this app is hand-built. A hand-built `ColorScheme` that omits those roles doesn't get sensible ones — Flutter falls each back to its base role — so `errorContainer` **was** the full-strength error red and `secondaryContainer` **was** the full-strength accent.

That's why the "no API key" banner filled its card with saturated red and the "running on this device" banner with solid accent: they grabbed attention by overriding the theme the reader chose, rather than by working within it. Same root cause as the progress bar in #75.

## The fix

Containers are derived from each theme's own accent, error and surface. The colour that catches the eye moves to the **icon** and a **hairline border**, which stay at full strength — so a warning still reads unmistakably as a warning.

## Both halves have to adapt, and the tests caught that

A fixed 20% tint plus a fixed text blend looked right on Tokyo Night and failed badly elsewhere. On Solarized the accent sits near the text in luminance, so tinting the surface moved the background *toward* the text and dropped a paragraph to **2.7:1**.

The tint now backs off until the text clears the bar. The bar is WCAG AA — except where the theme misses it on its own surface, since a few of these community palettes put their body text below 4.5:1 by design, and holding a banner to a standard the rest of the app misses would only bleach the tint out for no gain.

## Verified

Asserted across **every theme in both brightnesses** — 162 assertions — because the failure mode is silent: a banner that's merely ugly, or text merely hard to read, in one theme nobody screenshotted. The adaptive rule was written *after* the fixed one failed those tests, not before.

Checked on device in Tokyo Night: error state, success state, and the cloud-key disclosure. 326 tests pass, `flutter analyze` clean.
